round6_research.bug_semantics: Information leak through incomplete API-key redaction (CWE-200 / CWE-312). remove_api_keys() in src/backend/base/langflow/api/utils/core.py (originally src/backend/langflow/api/utils.py) scrubs serialized flow data before save/export, but its redaction predicate is extremely narrow: a template field is only blanked when has_api_terms(value['name']) is true ('api' in name AND ('key' in name OR ('token' in name AND 'tokens' not in name))) AND value.get('password') is set. Credentials stored under other key names (e.g. secret, passwd, authorization, private_key, connection_string, access_key), non-password-flagged fields, and values nested outside the node template all pass through unredacted, so flow exports / saved flows accessed via the 'flow using API' surface disclose live credentials. round6_research.bug_semantics: Broken access control / missing object-level scope (CWE-639 / CWE-284) in the pretix REST API check-in history endpoint: GET /api/v1/organizers/(organizer)/events/(event)/checkins/ (CheckinViewSet, registered on the event router). Its get_queryset ran `Checkin.all.filter()` with NO filter, so although the endpoint is documented and expected to return 'all check-in events within a given event', it returned every check-in row of the organizer (scan time, success/error result, matched position id, list, device). round6_research.bug_semantics: DNS-rebinding TOCTOU SSRF (CWE-367) in @fastgpt/service <=4.14.11: isInternalAddress() (packages/service/common/system/utils.ts) resolves the target hostname to IPs via node:dns/promises resolve4/resolve6 and compares them against private ranges at check time (T1), but the actual HTTP fetch (axios/http tool/serverRequest/plusRequest) re-resolves the hostname in a separate request at T2, so an attacker-controlled hostname (e.g. rbndr.us pattern resolving to a public IP for the check and to 169.254.169.254 for the fetch) bypasses the guard -> SSRF to cloud metadata / private network. Affected endpoints: getApiSchemaByUrl, mcpTools/getTools, mcpTools/runTool, workflow http468 node, readFiles. Advisory GHSA-cc8x-jrqv-hmwh (CVE-2026-42344) published 2026-04-28, no patched_versions field; npm @fastgpt/service <=4.14.11 affected.

round6_research.flaw_origin: The resolve-then-fetch TOCTOU: the guard and the fetch perform independent DNS resolutions, so the check result does not bind the connection target. A synchronous-only guard, or a check that pins the resolved IP into the request, would not be rebindable.
round6_research.reasoning: Minimum atomic introducer of the vulnerable resolve-then-fetch behavior is the async rewrite of isInternalAddress shipped in squash 76d6234de (V4.14.7); the parent commit provably lacks the async DNS-check code. round6_research.bug_semantics: Reflected XSS (CWE-79) via missing JSON parse error handling. The Express server mounts app.use(express.json({limit:3mb})) with no subsequent error handler for body-parser SyntaxError. On malformed JSON, express.json() throws a SyntaxError whose message embeds the raw user-supplied body; with no custom handler, Express's default error response reflects that input, so an attacker sending an HTML/JS payload as an unparseable JSON body gets it reflected back in the error response (XSS if Content-Type is not strictly enforced). Affects LibreChat up to v0.8.0.
round6_research.evidence: OSV CVE-2025-66452 (GHSA-q6c5-gvj5-c264, CWE-79): 'no handler for JSON parsing errors; SyntaxError from express.json() includes user input in the error message, which gets reflected in responses... XSS risk if Content-Type is not strictly enforced'; noted no fix at publication (2025-12-11). Fix commit 01413eea3 adds packages/api/src/middleware/json.ts handling body-parser SyntaxError with status 400 and 'body' in err, returning a static 'Invalid JSON format' JSON response, mounted in both api/server/index.js and api/server/experimental.js immediately after express.json(). Introducer traced via git log --follow -S 'express.json' -- api/server/index.js: first occurrence in 92860a1bb (server/index.js, initial express server, 2023-02-04). Parent-absence verified: numactl git grep -c 'express.json' 037a12a2 -- server/ exit 1. Fix is also ancestor of OSV last_affected b288d81f (version-derived metadata lag); fix tagged chart-1.9.4+.
round6_research.flaw_origin: First writer of the vulnerable behavior is commit 92860a1bb (Daniel Avila, 2023-02-04, 'adds express server'), which created server/index.js with a bare app.use(express.json()) and no parse-error handler; the pattern was carried through renames (server/index.js -> api/server/index.js via fca546af6) and copied into api/server/experimental.js. round6_research.reasoning: The vulnerable behavior — mounting express.json() with no handler for body-parser SyntaxError, so malformed user JSON gets reflected in the default error response — originates in the repository's very first express server commit (92860a1bb, Feb 2023), written by the project's human founder Daniel Avila before any AI-era tooling was in use, and persisted via straightforward file renames and copies. round6_research.bug_semantics: OS command injection (CWE-77) in the quick_capture MCP tool of the A-G-U-P-T-A wireshark-mcp server. pyshark_mcp.py builds a tshark command by f-string interpolation of the user-supplied MCP arguments and executes it through a shell: `cmd = f"tshark -i \"{interface}\" -c {packet_limit} -a duration:{duration} -T fields -e frame.number -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e _ws.col.Protocol"` followed by `subprocess.Popen(cmd, shell=True, ...)`. interface is only wrapped in double quotes (breakout via embedded `"` or `$(...)`/backticks, which expand even inside double quotes), and packet_limit/duration are interpolated with no quoting at all, so a malicious MCP client (or any prompt-influenced tool call) can achieve arbitrary OS command execution on the host running the MCP server. NVD rates CVE-2026-7785 CVSS 7.3 HIGH, CWE-77, published 2026-05-05 (GHSA-v798-39xf-8fg2, severity medium, same advisory), listing repo snapshots edaf604416fbc94a201b4043092d4a1b09a12275 and 400c3da70074f22f3cce7ccb65304cafc7089c89 as affected; rolling release, no version numbers.
round6_research.evidence: Class members verified by hash: ('CVE-2026-7785', 'GHSA-v798-39xf-8fg2') -> prefix of sha256 joined-sorted pair = class id; GitHub API confirms GHSA-v798-39xf-8fg2 = CVE-2026-7785 (published 2026-05-05, severity medium). Introducer edaf604 (root commit, no parents - git log -1 --format='%P' empty), author Arnab Gupta <arnabgupta91996@gmail.com>, body 'init' with no trailers: git show edaf604:pyshark_mcp.py line 764-767 shows the sink `cmd = f"tshark -i \"{interface}\" ..."` + `subprocess.Popen(cmd, shell=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)` and the interface/duration/packet_limit parameters are MCP tool inputs (@mcp.tool(name="quick_capture") at line 743). git diff edaf604 400c3da -- pyshark_mcp.py is empty, so the CVE's second named SHA carries the identical vulnerable code. Fix: 6e56043c74f1fa0bbd89539c6655695c43d42a5f (2026-07-20, Arnab Gupta, 'Ship a host-agnostic Wireshark MCP with novice setup docs.') restructures into the src/wireshark_mcp/ package: tools/capture.py quick_capture calls validate_capture_interface / validate_positive_int and tshark_runner.popen_tshark_capture which uses subprocess.Popen([...], shell=False); security.py + tests/test_quick_capture_security.py cover validation; grep of pyshark_mcp.py at HEAD shows no shell=True/Popen/os.system left. Marker scans: introducer message 'init' - no AI markers of any kind. The FIX commit 6e56043 carries the trailer 'Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>' - an AI-agent co-author - and its body mentions Cursor/Claude as MCP host clients; this is an AI-written remediation, not the origin of the flaw.
round6_research.flaw_origin: The vulnerable quick_capture function was present in the very first commit of the repository: edaf604416fbc94a201b4043092d4a1b09a12275 (2025-03-31, Arnab Gupta <arnabgupta91996@gmail.com>, message just 'init') authored the entire ~3000-line single-file MCP server pyshark_mcp.py, including the shell=True f-string sink (verified: git show edaf604:pyshark_mcp.py lines 764-767 contain the Popen(cmd, shell=True) sink). The second commit 400c3da (README, same day) did not touch the file (empty diff), yet is the other SHA named in the advisory. edaf604 is the repository root - it has no parent, hence no earlier commit could have written the vulnerable behavior (introducer_parent_absent trivially true, introducer_parent = null). No later commit modified pyshark_mcp.py until the fix; the vulnerable code shipped unchanged from 2025-03-31 to 2026-07-20.
round6_research.reasoning: Step 1: the vulnerability is OS command injection (CWE-77) in quick_capture via shell=True with unvalidated, quoted-only interpolation of MCP-supplied arguments, present in both advisory-named snapshots. Step 2: decomposition - the sink was authored in the repository root commit edaf604 (2025-03-31); no parent exists and no later pre-fix commit touched the file, so edaf604 is the minimum atomic introducer. round6_research.bug_semantics: Remote code execution via eval on JSON-RPC command-string parameters (CWE-95, critical): the openc3-api JSON-RPC layer accepts the string form of API calls such as cmd(); attacker-controlled parameter text (e.g. an array literal) is parsed with String#convert_to_value, whose array branch executes 'return_value = eval(self)' - arbitrary Ruby code execution as the api server user. Because the cmd code path parses the command string BEFORE calling authorize(), an unauthenticated attacker can trigger Ruby code execution even though the request ultimately fails authorization (401).
round6_research.evidence: Identity: member_map pin alias-10def964 -> CVE-2025-68271 + GHSA-w757-4qv9-mghp (published 2026-01-13, critical, CWE-95; rubygems openc3 >=5.0.6,<6.10.2, patched 6.10.2; advisory: JSON-RPC string-form API parses attacker text via String#convert_to_value; array-like inputs execute eval(); cmd path parses before authorize() -> unauthenticated RCE). BIC 320cb782 (2014-12-22, Ryan Melton <rmelton@ball.com>, 'Initial commit') creates lib/cosmos/core_ext/string.rb whose convert_to_value contains 'elsif self.is_array? / return_value = eval(self)' - this is the file-birth commit (git log --diff-filter=A --follow terminates at 320cb782); immediate parent 7a059f8b (repo root, 2014-12-19, 'Update README.md') has zero convert_to_value hits (git grep exit 1) and no core_ext/string.rb in its tree; single-parent commit, no trailer lines. eval logic untouched for 11 years (only path rename 4e6ced00 'rebrand', 2022-07-17). Reachable pre-auth chain per advisory: openc3/lib/openc3/api/cmd_api.rb cmd API -> openc3/lib/openc3/script/extract.rb:62 'cmd_params[keyword] = value.convert_to_value' (and script.rb:165), parsed before authorize(). Fix 01e9fbc5 (2025-12-14, Ryan Melton, single parent 24ca2102, no trailer lines) replaces 'eval(self)' with 'YAML.safe_load(self)', adds OBJECT_CHECK_REGEX + is_object? for {..} hashes, adds 'require yaml', and fixes the Python twin openc3/python/openc3/utilities/extract.py in the same commit; first contained in tag v6.10.2 (git tag --contains) matching advisory patched version; spec updates in openc3/spec/core_ext/string_spec.rb.
round6_research.flaw_origin: Applying Kernel#eval to an attacker-controlled String when the value looks like an array (is_array? regex /\A\s*\[.*\]\s*\z/), instead of a safe parser.
round6_research.reasoning: The vulnerable eval-on-array-string branch is atomic to the file-birth commit of the initial 2014 Ball Aerospace import: parent-absence proven against the repo root (README-only), and the eval line is present verbatim in the first revision of the file. BIC and fix are both authored by human maintainer Ryan Melton with no Co-Authored-By/Co-authored-by trailers naming AI tools (2014 BIC predates AI-assisted coding entirely). No AI signal on the flawed line or the fix -> NOT_AI.
round6_research.remaining_gap: Exploitability depends on deployment (openc3-api JSON-RPC endpoints exposed; eval payloads must satisfy is_array? after float/int/hex checks); advisory gives no concrete PoC payload, and the parse-before-authorize ordering was asserted in the advisory rather than re-derived from a full route trace here. YAML.safe_load introduces object-literal support but may change legacy array-string semantics in edge cases.

round6_research.bug_semantics: STARTTLS stripping via predictable-tag OK injection (CWE-392/841/636, CVSS 4.0 HIGH): Net::IMAP#starttls returns 'success' without establishing TLS when a MITM injects a tagged OK response before the client finishes sending the command. Root mechanism: Net::IMAP#send_command writes the command line to the socket BEFORE registering the caller's response handler (add_response_handler after put_line), and the receiver thread only invokes handlers while processing lines; get_tagged_response then returns the pre-stored tagged OK without the block ever running - so start_tls_session is never called and the connection stays plaintext. Affects net-imap 0.x (all versions before 0.6.4/0.5.14/0.4.24/0.3.10 backports).

round6_research.bug_semantics: WebSocket upgrade header smuggling (CWE-444): daphne reconstructs a raw HTTP request from Twisted's parsed headers and re-injects it into autobahn for WebSocket handshake processing. Twisted does not treat \x0b \x0c \x1c \x1d \x1e \x85 as header line separators, but autobahn decodes values to str and splitlines() splits on them: a parser differential allowing an attacker to smuggle extra headers (auth tokens, X-Forwarded-For, Origin, Daphne-Root-Path) into the ASGI scope. Fixed in daphne 4.2.2 by rejecting these bytes in any header value with 400 per RFC 9110 s5.5.
round6_research.evidence: OSV CVE-2026-44546/GHSA-xh68-hfp5-5x5m/PYSEC-2026-214: affected daphne ECOSYSTEM introduced 0 fixed 4.2.2; OSV GIT range introduced ce3e7f6 (v4.2.0 release), fixed c19f2f43 (v4.2.2 release bump; not the code fix). Clone .ai-slop/state/repos/django_daphne: git log -S 'Re-inject request' -- daphne/http_protocol.py -> only 88d47df2769e715b0ccc1fdcd5a2ae6c082b9d9d (root commit, no parent, Andrew Godwin <andrew@aeracode.org> 2015-12-23, no trailers). Fix commit 2628b7b2e6a196afff58defee3d77671a28de631 (Carlton Gibson <carlton.gibson@noumenal.es>, 2026-05-06, 'Fixed CVE-2026-44546: Prevent header injection on WebSocket upgrade path', 0 AI markers) adds INVALID_HEADER_VALUE_BYTES frozenset(b'\x0b\x0c\x1c\x1d\x1e\x85') in daphne/utils.py and rejects such header values in validateHeaders with 400; also adds regression tests. Release commit c19f2f43 bumps to 4.2.2.

Step 3: 88d47df is 2015 code by Andrew Godwin (Django Channels/daphne author) with zero AI markers — AI authorship is impossible for behavior introduced in the project's first commit, a decade before consumer AI code tools. round6_research.bug_semantics: CWE-770 (CWE-1333 ReDoS): Rack::Multipart mime-head parsing. MULTIPART_CONTENT_DISPOSITION = /Content-Disposition:(.*)(?=#{EOL}(\S|\z))/ni (lib/rack/multipart/parser.rb) is unanchored to line start; on crafted input containing many 'content-disposition:' occurrences and/or long comment/folded regions, the engine re-runs the greedy (.*) scan with lookahead from each candidate position, giving super-linear (quadratic) runtime -> DoS. Empirically reproduced: 200k repetitions of the literal 'content-disposition:' caused the old regex to run >180s (killed), while the anchored fix form is linear.
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-47m2-26rw-j2jw (github-reviewed, CVSS 4.0 moderate, aliases CVE-2025-49007, published 2025-06-05): ReDoS in Content-Disposition parsing of Rack::Multipart, similar to CVE-2022-44571, credited to scyoon via HackerOne; affected rack >=3.1.0 <3.1.16; references fix commits 4795831a and aed514df. Repository archaeology (git log -S across lib/rack/multipart/parser.rb): vulnerable regex string 'Content-Disposition:(.*)(?=' introduced ONLY by 51b0c26b (2023-04-28, Jeremy Evans); git grep shows zero occurrences at parent ab360dd5 (exit 1). Fix commit 4795831a (main, parent d1d30227) and aed514df (3-1-stable backport, parent 352650a6), both authored by John Hawthorn <john@hawthorn.email> 2024-08-13, message '[CVE-2025-49007]' + 'Co-authored-by: Matthew Draper <matthew@trebex.net>' (human); diff replaces MULTIPART_CONTENT_TYPE/DISPOSITION/ID with /^Content-(Type|Disposition|ID):#{FWS}?(#{HEADER_VALUE})/ni and adjusts a quoted-escapes test. Empirical ReDoS reproduction on ruby 3.2.3: head = 'content-disposition:' * 200000; old regex match exceeded 180s (process killed); anchored regex form is linear. No AI markers anywhere in chain (2011 origin file authored by Sam Woodard/Blake Mizerany; all subsequent edits by Jeremy Evans, John Hawthorn, Matthew Draper, Rodrigo Nascimento-era rack contributors are human).
round6_research.flaw_origin: 2023-04-28 commit 51b0c26b 'Add Content-Disposition parameter parser' (Jeremy Evans <code@jeremyevans.net>) replaced the previous disposition regex (Content-Disposition:[^:]*;\s*name=(VALUE), itself the CVE-2022-44571 fix ee25ab9a) with the vulnerable unanchored lookahead form while adding a hand-rolled parameter parser. The commit landed on main and first shipped to users in rack 3.1.0 (Dec 2024), matching the advisory range 'introduced 3.1.0' (the 3.0.x line never received it). f92e0563 (2024-07-06, Jeremy Evans) later narrowed Content-Type/Content-ID whitespace but left the vulnerable disposition regex untouched. The fix (4795831a/aed514df, John Hawthorn, Aug 2024) anchors all three header regexes to line start and allows FWS.
round6_research.reasoning: The exact vulnerable regex was introduced by a human maintainer (Jeremy Evans) in 2023 while repairing the fallout of the CVE-2022-44571 security fix; it shipped in 3.1.0 as first release containing it, which matches the advisory's introduced range. The fix was also authored by humans (John Hawthorn, co-author Matthew Draper) ahead of the coordinated release of 3.1.16. No AI co-author/trailer/bot markers exist on the introducer, fix, or interleaved commits. AI did not cause this flaw.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Insufficient Session Expiration (CWE-613): HAXCMS authenticates API calls with stateless, deterministic bearer tokens that are never revoked server-side. user_token = hmacBase64(value, privateKey+salt) with no expiry and no server-side state (getRequestToken); access JWTs carry a 15-min exp but logout() only clears the haxcms_refresh_token cookie client-side. Any endpoint validating user_token (e.g. getSkeleton, listSites, getUserData, skeletonsList) keeps accepting a captured token forever after logout: no blacklist, no server-side session record, no revocation.
round6_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-g5rc-4gpf-wx3w / CVE-2026-46401 (published 2026-05-12, reported by d6fault; PoC replays captured user_token against GET /system/api/getSkeleton after logout). v25.0.0 (72834e31) confirms vulnerable design: Operations.php skeletonsList/listSites/getUserData validate only via stateless validateRequestToken(user_token); logout() clears cookie only. v26.0.0 (ce406afc, 2026-05-12) does NOT contain the fix (logout still cookie-only). Fix landed in the 5wp5 wave: 0d0597767a (2026-07-28) added setRefreshTokenCookie/validateAccessTokenClaims + logout cookie-clear helper; 56b12f146a (2026-07-30) added revokeRefreshSession/validateRefreshSession/rotateRefreshTokenAndCookie server-side revocation, wired into routes/logout.php (revoke refresh-token family on logout) and systemRoutes/v1/session.php (reject revoked family, rotate cookie) - first release containing it: v26.0.1 (b4fc6242, 2026-08-14; v26.0.2/26.8.0 tags predate it, v26.8.1 contains it). Root commit 48d59b6641 (2018-07-19) already contains getRequestToken (deterministic HMAC, no expiry) and validateRequestToken; system/logout.php at root only unsets PHP_AUTH_USER - stateless never-revoked token design introduced at initial commit. All commits authored/committed by btopro (btopro@outlook.com / bto108@psu.edu), no Co-Authored-By/Assisted-by trailers or AI markers anywhere on introducer or fix chain.
round6_research.flaw_origin: introduced_by_feature/regression: design present from the initial commit. Root commit 48d59b6641 (2018-07-19, btopro) already contains validateRequestToken/getRequestToken/getJWT (stateless HMAC tokens, no revocation) and system/logout.php that only unsets PHP_AUTH_USER. The formal API refactor c540f86fb0 (#276, 2020-01-07, btopro) created the swagger API engine and the 'function logout' (cookie-clear only); the refresh-token cookie was added cb0c9a6b42 (#431 #284, 2020-01-08, btopro). round6_research.bug_semantics: GHSA-7pr5-w74r-jjj7 / CVE-2025-6050 (published 2025-06-17, CVSS v4 4.8 medium, CWE-79 Stored XSS): Mezzanine CMS admin XSS in displayable_links_js(). The view /admin/displayable_links.js serializes Displayable objects (blog posts/pages) into a JSON link-list consumed by TinyMCE. Since the 2015 TinyMCE-4 refactor it returns HttpResponse(json.dumps([...])) directly; json.dumps does not escape <, >, & (ensure_ascii only escapes non-ASCII), so a blog-post title containing e.g. '</script><script>...' survives raw into JS/HTML output. An authenticated admin can create a post whose title carries a JS payload and trick another admin into visiting /admin/displayable_links.js, executing the payload (stored XSS in admin context, but requires two admins: low intrinsic impact per advisory). Fix (898630d8, v6.1.1) wraps title in django.utils.html.escape() before serialization.
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-7pr5-w74r-jjj7 (GitHub API): summary 'Stored XSS in displayable_links_js', first_patched 6.1.1, references mezzanine commit 898630d8df48cf3ddb8b9942f59168b93216e3f8. mezzanine clone (blobless): git log -S 'displayable_links_js' -> 4fb15b88 only (introducer of view); git log -S 'getattr(obj,"titles",obj.title)' -> 4fb15b88 only; git show 82339b05: deletes templates/admin/displayable_links.js ('{{ title|escapejs }}'), rewrites view to HttpResponse(dumps(...)) — first occurrence of unescaped serialization (git log -S 'dumps' on views.py would show 82339b05 as sole relevant change); parent e9819d39 still shows template-rendered view at line 173 with escapejs template present => vulnerable behavior absent pre-82339b05. Fix diff: +from django.utils.html import escape; title = escape(getattr(obj,'titles',obj.title)); tag v6.1.1 contains 898630d8 (git tag --contains). Weblinks: github.com/stephenmcd/mezzanine/issues/2080 discussion.
round6_research.flaw_origin: Escaping of user-controlled Displayable titles was lost when the displayable_links_js view was converted from a Django template (admin/displayable_links.js rendering '{{ title|escapejs }}', served as text/javascript) to direct JSON output via HttpResponse(json.dumps(...)). The template path (introduced 4fb15b88, 2013) escaped titles with Django's escapejs filter; the TinyMCE 4 upgrade commit 82339b05 deleted that template and introduced raw json.dumps serialization with default content type and no HTML/JS escaping of title values. Vulnerable mezzanine/core/views.py: for url,obj in url_map: title = getattr(obj,'titles',obj.title); ... links.append((not page and real, {'title': str(title), 'value': url})); return HttpResponse(dumps([...])).

round6_research.bug_semantics: Rack::Multipart::Parser unbounded in-memory buffering (memory-exhaustion DoS): the parser loop appends all uploaded bytes to an in-memory buffer (@buf, later StringScanner @sbuf) while scanning for the multipart boundary (preamble) or a complete mime part header, with no size cap on the buffered data; a client that never sends a boundary/header terminator forces unbounded memory growth. Fixed in rack 2.2.19 / 3.1.17 / 3.2.2 by adding BOUNDARY_START_LIMIT (16KB) and MIME_HEADER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT (64KB) checks in parser.rb (actual limit the higher of these and the 1MB default buffer size).
round6_research.evidence:
Advisory GHSA-p543-xpfm-54cp / CVE-2025-61770 (github-reviewed/2025/09): Rack::Multipart::Parser buffers the entire multipart preamble (and mime part headers) in memory with no size limit, enabling memory-exhaustion DoS; fixed in rack 2.2.19/3.1.17/3.2.2; fix commits referenced 589127f4ac8b5cf11cf88fb0cd116ffed4d2181e (master, also in origin/3-2-stable), d869fed663b113b95a74ad53e1b5cae6ab31f29e, e08f78c656c9394d6737c022bde087e0f33336fd (release branches), all authored by Jeremy Evans (2025-09-15, 'Fix denial of service vulnerbilties in multipart parsing') adding BOUNDARY_START_LIMIT=16KB and MIME_HEADER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT=64KB raises. Class metadata repo field is rubysec/ruby-advisory-db (advisory-DB mirror); the vulnerable product repo is rack, analyzed here (clone rack). Introducer analysis: the unbounded buffering loop 'content = @io.read(...); @buf << content' inside 'until head && @buf =~ rx' was first written by 24d512531bd88f2d6ce94b3a3d9798fde8fbb713 (2011-05-02, Sam Woodard, 'refactor of multipart module') but was then bounded by @content_length (CONTENT_LENGTH header): 'content = @io.read(BUFSIZE < @content_length ? BUFSIZE : @content_length); @content_length -= content.size', so memory could not grow past the declared content length. The cap was removed by 6b23130e5122bb9d5240a08944ca2e21d7209958 (2012-09-16, Santiago Pastorino, 'Make multipart parser work when there is no Content-Length header', Closes #418): diff removes '@content_length = @env["CONTENT_LENGTH"].to_i' and makes the read unconditional ('@io.read(@content_length && BUFSIZE >= @content_length ? @content_length : BUFSIZE)') so without a Content-Length header (e.g. chunked requests) the loop appends to @buf forever with no cap - the exact unbounded buffering fixed by the advisory. round6_research.bug_semantics: Privilege escalation / broken access control (CWE-862, route-metadata abuse) in LiteLLM proxy key generation: the `key_type` field on /key/generate (and /key/update, /key/regenerate) lets a caller specify a preset route bucket. `handle_key_type` maps key_type=management -> allowed_routes=["management_routes"], which is written into the stored key AND bypasses the role-based route gate (RouteChecks.non_proxy_admin_allowed_routes_check). The caller-permission check `_check_allowed_routes_caller_permission` only inspects `data.allowed_routes` (the raw request body, which is empty when the caller uses key_type instead of allowed_routes), so an authenticated internal_user can create a key scoped to admin-only management_routes and thereby escalate to proxy_admin. Affected < 1.83.14.
round6_research.evidence: Identity: class hash verified sha256('CVE-2026-47101\nGHSA-qrc4-49gv-mv9m\n')[:24] == alias-157f1d498d17cb4c987f261d (pair recovered from GHSA-qrc4-49gv-mv9m page; repo-precise mapping assigns berriai/litellm). Advisory GHSA-qrc4-49gv-mv9m / CVE-2026-47101 (published 2026-05-21, from NVD, patched 1.83.14): 'LiteLLM allows an authenticated internal_user to create API keys with access to routes that their role does not permit... a key created with access to admin-only routes can then be used to reach those routes successfully, bypassing the role-based access controls... enabling full privilege escalation from internal_user to proxy_admin.' Fix chain (all in litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/key_management_endpoints.py): (1) d910a95661 (2026-04-09, jayden <git@jayden.email>) added _check_allowed_routes_caller_permission and called it in generate_key_fn / _validate_update_key_data on data.allowed_routes; (2) 2220f3076a (2026-04-24, Yuneng Jiang <yuneng@berri.ai>, 'fix: tighten caller-permission checks on key route fields') added the missed re-check in _common_key_generation_helper AFTER handle_key_type (since key_type can derive an elevated bucket e.g. management_routes not present in the original body), added _check_passthrough_routes_caller_permission for allowed_passthrough_routes (top-level + nested under metadata), extended checks to regenerate_key_fn, and added _NON_ADMIN_SAFE_ALLOWED_ROUTES_PRESETS frozenset permitting only llm_api_routes/info_routes presets for non-admins (management_routes still admin-gated); (3) 5190bd07eb (2026-04-24, Yuneng Jiang) extended caller-permission checks to service account key generation + hardened raw-body acceptance. Primary gate is 2220f3076a (direct_fix). Release v1.83.14-stable contains 2220f3076a (git tag --contains). Confirmed pre-2220 code calls handle_key_type at line 675 in _common_key_generation_helper but only checks _check_allowed_routes_caller_permission(data.allowed_routes) at 1287 in generate_key_fn and 1939 in _validate_update_key_data -> handle_key_type-derived value unchecked. round6_research.bug_semantics: SSRF protection bypass (cloud metadata endpoint disclosure): FastGPT's isInternalAddress() in packages/service/common/system/utils.ts blocks cloud metadata endpoints using a fullUrl.startsWith() check against a hardcoded URL list (169.254.169.254 AWS/Azure/Huawei, metadata.google.internal, 100.100.100.200, metadata.tencentyun.com). partial_wave.bug_semantics: SSH identification parsing accepted non-canonical client banners and did not bound pre-banner input (GHSA-76r6-x97p-67vr / CVE-2026-48108): russh/src/ssh_read.rs read_ssh_id() used one permissive path for both client and server - lines not starting with SSH- are treated as 'preliminary' pre-banner text and discarded in an unbounded loop (`ssh_id.total = 0; ssh_id.bytes_read = 0`), no line-count cap and no distinction that RFC 4253 section 4.2 only allows pre-banner lines from server to client. A remote client can hold server connection setup in the cleartext pre-auth phase with endless non-SSH lines (until app-level timeout), and the accept/discard behavior acts as a parser-state oracle for fingerprinting. Fix 22295fa5 splits read_ssh_id_inner(allow_pre_banner_lines) into read_ssh_id (banner-tolerant) vs read_client_ssh_id (strict) used by the server, adds SSH_ID_MAX_LINE_LEN=255 and SSH_ID_MAX_PRE_BANNER_LINES=20 caps, rejecting non-SSH client lines with Error::Version

round6_research.bug_semantics: Code injection (CWE-94) when generating Java specific classes from untrusted Avro schemas. The Velocity template lang/java/compiler/src/main/velocity/org/apache/avro/compiler/specific/templates/java/classic/record.vm (and enum.vm) interpolates attacker-controlled schema/field '[doc]' text RAW into the generated Java source inside Javadoc comments: '/** $schema.getDoc() */' and '/** $field.doc() */'. A schema doc containing '*/' closes the Javadoc comment early and the remainder of the doc text is emitted as Java code, so compiling generated classes from an untrusted schema yields arbitrary code injection into the generated source (which downstream tooling compiles). Affects avro-compiler 0-1.11.5 and 1.12.0; fixed 1.11.5/1.12.1.
round6_research.evidence: Identity: hash reversal over the plan pool -> {CVE-2025-33042, GHSA-rp46-r563-jrc7}; OSV GHSA-rp46-r563-jrc7 (aliases CVE-2025-33042, PYSEC-2026-26; Maven avro-compiler introduced 0/1.12.0, fixed 1.11.5/1.12.1) explicitly references the fix commit 84bc7322ca1c04ab4a8e4e708acf1e271541aac4 and PR #3150 (AVRO-4053). Introducer efd4e04a (2010-11-01): creates record.vm/enum.vm with raw '/** $schema.getDoc() */' + '/** $field.doc() */'; parent ba0a281 lacks the template files (verified cat-file 128) and its SpecifiedCompiler.java escaped docs via escapeForJavaDoc() - so the template port is the first writer of the unescaped-doc behavior. %B of efd4e04a is a plain svn-era message + git-svn-id trailer, no AI markers (commit predates AI coding by 13 years). No other commit between 2010-11-01 and the fix changed '$schema.getDoc()' count on either template path (file-scoped pickaxe across --all: only efd4e04a, 4631aef, 9403bef, plus two unrelated 2022/2023 github-actions docs-publish artifact commits). Fix 84bc7322 (2024-10-04, Oscar Westra van Holte - Kind, PR #3150, human, no AI trailers) replaces every raw interpolation with '$this.escapeForJavadoc(...)' in record/enum/fixed/protocol.vm, adds escapeForJavadoc/escapeForJavaString helpers to SpecificCompiler.java, updates TestSpecificCompiler + fixture; verified live in repo (fix diff and HEAD grep).
round6_research.flaw_origin: Introduced by efd4e04a (2010-11-01, 'Java: Use Velocity templates to generate specific code. Contributed by philz.', author/committer Douglass Cutting) which ported specific-class generation from hand-written Java string building in SpecificCompiler.java to Velocity templates. The pre-existing Java implementation ESCAPED doc text ('"  /** " + escapeForJavaDoc(doc) + " */"', SpecificCompiler.java:333-336 at parent ba0a281); the template port dropped the escaping, emitting '$schema.getDoc()'/'$field.doc()' raw in the new .vm files. Parent ba0a281 does not contain the .vm files at all (cat-file 128: path absent -> introducer_parent_absent=true). The raw interpolation survived byte-identical on both post-AVRO-647/Avro-716 file paths until the 2024 fix (file-scoped pickaxe -S '$schema.getDoc()' hits only the two module-move commits 4631aef/9403bef and the creating commit itself).
round6_research.reasoning: The vulnerable behavior - unescaped schema-doc interpolation into generated Java source - was first written in 2010 by Apache Avro's human founder (Douglass Cutting) porting the compiler to Velocity templates and dropping the escaping the replaced Java code had. The commit message/trailers show no AI markers, no AI coding tools existed in 2010, and the flawed template lines remained untouched for 14 years until a human-authored 2024 fix (no AI markers either). Closed causal chain, no AI authorship -> NOT_AI.

round5_research.bug_semantics: Vertical authorization bypass in Admin API order state transition endpoints (/api/_action/order/{orderId}/state/{transition}, order_transaction and order_delivery variants): the transition routes do not declare required server-side ACL privileges, so low-privileged authenticated users without order:update can change order states (CWE-862).
round5_research.evidence: Fix 86dff24ba5 (Lennart Tinkloh, Mar 18 2026 'fix: acl permissions on state transition updates') adds defaults: [PlatformRequest::ATTRIBUTE_ACL => ['order:update'/'order_transaction:update'/'order_delivery:update']] to the three transition Route attributes; released via v6.6.10.18/v6.7.10.1 (merge-back b570cc9217 carries the same hunk with '_acl' defaults). Advisory GHSA-F8Q6-3G5W-JJR6 references those release tags. Introducer a3f1ed1abd created the routes without ACL; parent f5e8fb0d lacks the controller entirely. The recorded ledger fix 94569f7e71e61de428f2ee5cc2f810c00bc8421d is an unrelated OAuth fix merge (ClientRepository/UserRepository) - metadata mismatch for this advisory.
round5_research.flaw_origin: First writer of the vulnerable behavior: a3f1ed1abd (NEXT-973 'Add state machine', Nov 19 2018) created OrderActionController with the transition_state routes (/api/v{version}/order/{orderId}/actions/state/{transition?}) carrying no ACL metadata. round5_research.bug_semantics: RSACrypt::decryptWithRSA15() (RSA1_5/RSAES-PKCS1-v1_5 key decryption) validates PKCS#1 v1.5 padding after RSADP and throws InvalidArgumentException as soon as the padding is malformed, without the implicit-rejection countermeasure required by RFC 3447 7.2.2/RFC 8017 7.1.2. From a JWE caller this yields a Bleichenbacher/Marvin padding oracle: padding-rejected, padding-valid-wrong-CEK-length, and padding-valid-full-AEAD ciphertexts all return the same false from JWEDecrypter but perform measurably different amounts of work, recoverable via timing (CWE-208).

round5_research.bug_semantics: urllib3 2.6.0 introduced partial (bounded) decompression in the streaming API, but two paths could still decompress an entire response instead of the requested portion: (1) the second HTTPResponse.read(amt=N) call on a Brotli(br)-encoded response when the official brotli package lacks output_buffer_limit (has_unconsumed_tail forces full decode of the buffered tail); (2) HTTPResponse.drain_conn() after decompression already started, because drain_conn called read() with decode_content=self._has_decoded_content, decoding all remaining compressed bytes in one operation. Result: client-side decompression bomb (CWE-409, high CPU/memory) from a small compressed body.
round5_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-mf9v-mfxr-j63j (github-reviewed 2026-05-11, CVE-2026-44432): introduced 2.6.0, fixed 2.7.0; two sinks: 2nd read(amt) on br with official brotli, and drain_conn after partial decompression. Introducer c19571de (author Illia Volochii, committer GitHub, 2025-12-05; single-parent squash 'Merge commit from fork') first added max_length to all decoders, has_unconsumed_tail properties, the read(amt) tail-decoding branch in src/urllib3/response.py, and kept drain_conn calling self.read(decode_content=self._has_decoded_content). Parent 816fcf04 (2.5.0-era) has zero occurrences of max_length/has_unconsumed_tail in response.py and drain_conn was plain self.read() with no decode_content flag semantics tied to partial decode - vulnerable behavior absent in parent. 2.5.0 tag response.py also has 0 hits for max_length|has_unconsumed_tail. Fix 2bdcc44d (author Illia Volochii, 2026-05-07, squash of PR: 'Avoid any decoding in HTTPResponse.drain_conn' and 'Fix full decompression on the 2nd small read from response using Brotli') changes drain_conn to self._raw_read() plus decoder cleanup, and adds 'and len(self._decoded_buffer) < amt' guard to the has_unconsumed_tail branch; it is an ancestor of tag 2.7.0 (9a950b92 Release 2.7.0). Recorded fix_sha d5df809a675471a67a576a7921820104153b9366 is the annotated v2.7.0 tag object (peels to 9a950b92d999f906b6020bb2d1076ee56cddd5d2), not a commit; direct fix is 2bdcc44d. No AI markers (no co-authored-by/copilot/generated/openai/claude/anthropic/chatgpt/llm) in introducer or fix commit bodies.
round5_research.flaw_origin: Commit c19571de34c47de3a766541b041637ba5f716ed7 (2.6.0 'Merge commit from fork' partial-decompression redesign) first wrote the has_unconsumed_tail machinery and the drain_conn -> read(decode_content=self._has_decoded_content) path. In read(amt), the new branch 'if self._decoder and self._decoder.has_unconsumed_tail: decoded_data = self._decode(b'', decode_content, flush_decoder=False, max_length=amt-len(self._decoded_buffer))' decodes the decompressor's whole buffered tail for brotli because the BrotliDecoder.decompress(max_length) falls back to full _decompress() when output_buffer_limit is unavailable (brotli<1.2.0), while has_unconsumed_tail returns True once can_accept_more_data() is False. drain_conn() retained read(decode_content=self._has_decoded_content), which with amt=None flushes the decoder fully.
round5_research.reasoning: The atomic first writer of the vulnerable partial-decompression behavior is c19571de, a human-authored squash merge by Illia Volochii (core urllib3 maintainer) implementing the 2.6.0 streaming decompression redesign; parent and 2.5.0 both lack the machinery, so parent absence is closed. The 2026 fix is also human-authored by the same maintainer. No AI-generation markers on the vulnerable-line writer. NOT_AI.

round6_research.bug_semantics: SQL injection (CWE-89) in LangGraph's SQLite checkpoint store (libs/checkpoint-sqlite/langgraph/store/sqlite/base.py, BaseSqliteStore/SqliteStore): filter keys passed to store search/list_namespaces operations were interpolated directly into SQL via string concatenation - e.g. json_extract(value, '$.' + key + '...') in _get_filter_condition and the filter loop - without validation or parameterization of the key. Because filter keys are also used for JSON-pointer-style path extraction with a trailing '.0' suffix appended, crafted keys can escape the json_extract path literal, inject arbitrary SQL, and bypass access controls (namespace/filter restrictions). Fixed by _validate_filter_key() enforcing ^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+$ on every filter key before query construction.

round5_research.bug_semantics: Buffer overflow in Zlib::GzipReader: zstream_buffer_ungets prepends caller bytes ahead of previously produced output but fails to guarantee the backing Ruby string has enough capacity before memmove shifts existing data, causing memory corruption.
evidence: Advisory rubysec gems/zlib/CVE-2026-27820.yml (GHSA-g857-hhfv-j68w, 2026-03-05): buffer overflow in Zlib::GzipReader via zstream_buffer_ungets failing to guarantee backing-string capacity before memmove; patched versions ~>3.0.1, ~>3.1.2, >=3.2.3; credit to reporter calysteon and patch by nobu.

git log -S'rb_str_capacity' reverse on ext/zlib/zlib.c: first writer is 5aa9cca1eadd2dcdc799db2b1c067a8e1f23c96c (2017-09-13 SHIBATA Hiroshi, Picked r58526 from ruby/ruby); diff changes zstream_buffer_ungets guard from 'NIL_P(z->buf) || RSTRING_LEN(z->buf) - z->buf_filled == 0' to 'NIL_P(z->buf) || (long)rb_str_capacity(z->buf) <= ZSTREAM_BUF_FILLED(z)', and changes zstream_expand_buffer_into to rb_str_modify_expand semantics.

Parent cd21420537e217faa5138b82b5c456b0fb2d1917 ext/zlib/zlib.c zstream_buffer_ungets has the safe RSTRING_LEN-based check and no rb_str_capacity use (grep count 0), confirming immediate-parent absence of the vulnerable capacity guard.

Direct fix 608d2be66fcbcb759cbe26c82e95f4381b8dd140 (Fix buffer overflow at ungetc, Nobuyoshi Nakada, 2025-11-26, on master; contained in tag v3.2.3) unconditionally calls zstream_expand_buffer_into(z, len) and removes the capacity-guard branch; test/test_zlib.rb regression test added. Branch backports 82d5d26993e9b7eafc79bb1b6be9f39c5db964f9 (v3.0.1) and 6cc139d87c498e60bcf38bc9e4f2ac0f2faa0eb1 (v3.1.2) carry the same hunk. Recorded fix_sha 2ce25b3cd8722250fd650c49bef96f8ce862aaf5 is the v3.0.1 tag merge commit.

Introducer author/committer SHIBATA Hiroshi <hsbt@ruby-lang.org>, empty body, no trailers/co-author markers. Fix author Nobuyoshi Nakada <nobu@ruby-lang.org>, committer Hiroshi SHIBATA, no AI markers. No AI indicators on either commit.
round5_research.flaw_origin: Commit 5aa9cca1eadd2dcdc799db2b1c067a8e1f23c96c (Picked r58526 from ruby/ruby, SHIBATA Hiroshi, 2017-09-13) first wrote the flawed guard in zstream_buffer_ungets: it replaced the safe 'NIL_P(z->buf) || RSTRING_LEN(z->buf) - z->buf_filled == 0' check with '(long)rb_str_capacity(z->buf) <= ZSTREAM_BUF_FILLED(z)'. Because rb_str_capacity can exceed the logical length, the expansion is skipped whenever capacity > filled even if capacity - filled < len, so the subsequent memmove(bufptr + len, bufptr, filled) and memmove(bufptr, b, len) can write past capacity.
round5_research.reasoning: The buffer-overflow mechanism is the capacity guard introduced in zstream_buffer_ungets by 5aa9cca1 in 2017, whose immediate parent used the safe RSTRING_LEN-based full-buffer check. The direct fix removes the flawed conditional and always expands the buffer. Both introducer (SHIBATA Hiroshi) and fix (Nobuyoshi Nakada) are long-time Ruby core human committers with no AI markers, so AI-written code did not cause this flaw.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Prototype pollution via dot-notation field names (CWE-1321) leading to instance-wide DoS: the Edit Fields (Set) node assigns output fields through a dot-notation path setter (lodash set) without restricting field names, so an authenticated workflow author can name a field after an inherited built-in method path (e.g. 'toString.call'). lodash baseSet reuses a value found at a path segment even when it is inherited, so the assignment writes onto a shared built-in object in the main Node.js process; that global is used on the request-authentication path, so every authenticated request then fails until process restart. Fixed by patching lodash 4.18.1 (pnpm patch patches/lodash@4.18.1.patch): baseSet only reuses a segment value when it is an own property (hasOwnProperty.call(nested, key)), so built-in-named segments are stored as plain own data; fixed in 1.123.67, 2.31.5, 2.32.1.
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-xwx6-jjhv-84p8 (2026-07-22): 'Prototype Pollution via Dot-Notation Field Names Leads To Instance-Wide Denial of Service' in Edit Fields (Set) node, fixed 1.123.67/2.31.5/2.32.1, references commit f69dfc6dd2. Fix tokens verified: git log --all -S 'Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(nested, key)' -- patches/ -> only the 4 bundle commits; git show 2222fe3a6c:patches/lodash@4.18.1.patch modifies _baseSet.js and bundled lodash.js changing 'newValue = isObject(objValue)' to 'newValue = isObject(objValue) && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(nested, key)'; bundle adds regression tests packages/nodes-base/test/lodash-set.patch.test.ts (set(obj,'toString.call','x') must not touch Object.prototype.toString.call) and Set v2 helpers/__tests__/utils.test.ts ('keeps built-in object prototypes intact' for assignment name 'toString.call'). Pre-fix code: git show 69c86333b:packages/nodes-base/nodes/Set/v2/helpers/utils.ts -> configureFieldHelper(dotNotation !== false) uses set(item, key, value) via lodash/set with raw assignment names. BIC: git show 9cb9804e:packages/nodes-base/nodes/Set.node.ts -> import { set } from 'lodash' with set(item.json, setItem.name as string, setItem.value) at lines 129/134/139; 9cb9804e is the repository initial commit (2019-06-23, Jan Oberhauser) with no parents; the vulnerable dot-notation setter pattern therefore exists from the first commit of the repo, matching the advisory's 'introduced: 0' range. Set v1/v2 split at 3a474552b2 (2023-09-19) created v2/helpers/utils.ts already importing set from 'lodash/set' (line 10) with the same unguarded calls.
round6_research.flaw_origin: Born at repository root: packages/nodes-base/nodes/Set.node.ts in the n8n initial commit already contains the vulnerable pattern set(item.json, setItem.name as string, setItem.value) with lodash and unvalidated user-controlled field names passed as dot-notation paths. round5_research.bug_semantics: Docker registry auth substring match forwards credentials to a different registry (CWE-522/CWE-346): when building X-Registry-Auth for a Docker registry API request, getDefaultOptions(forRegistry) iterates config.json auths and credHelpers and selects the first entry whose serverAddress merely includes the requested registry as a substring (e.g. registry 'evilregistry.example' matches stored auth for 'registry.example'), leaking credentials to an unrelated registry.
round5_research.evidence: Direct fix cb5a2f20 (PR #3964, 2026-05-05) rewrites lib/managers/docker.js credential selection with normalizeRegistryPath/buildRegistryAuthority/parseRawRegistryAuthority and exact host matching, replacing the two `!serverAddress.includes(forRegistry)` guards (auths and credHelpers loops). Introducer trace: the substring-match lines first appear in a3e1309a (PR #717 first commit, 'Update packages. Support for private docker registry', author Prabhu Subramanian <prabhu@appthreat.com>, 2023-11-20), which added getDefaultOptions(forRegistry) with `if (forRegistry && !serverAddress.includes(forRegistry)) continue;` in both the config.json auths and credHelpers loops (git show a3e1309a -- docker.js lines 109/141). Parent 0e65ee55 of a3e1309a lacks the pattern (git grep absent). The merged squash 97d1e48e was decomposed via fetched PR ref origin/pr717 into a3e1309a + 7e12e3da; the substring logic came from a3e1309a (7e12e3da 'use env based credentials first for docker' has no serverAddress.includes diff). No co-author/AI trailers on a3e1309a or 7e12e3da. The advisory's reviewed commit b1e17986 and affected-from v9.9.5 are consistent with this 2023-11 introducer being in release v9.9.5. Note: the fix commit cb5a2f20 itself carries Co-authored-by: copilot-swe-agent[bot] and Agent-Logs-Url trailers (AI-assisted fix), but fix authorship is separate from the vulnerable-line introducer, which is human.
round5_research.flaw_origin: Design flaw in credential selection logic: substring matching (String.includes) instead of exact host matching when correlating stored registry credentials to the requested registry.
round5_research.reasoning: The vulnerable substring-match credential-selection logic was written by project maintainer Prabhu Subramanian in 2023 with no AI markers on the introducer commits; the squash commit was decomposed to the atomic first writer via the PR head ref. AI-assisted authorship appears only on the 2026 fix (copilot-swe-agent co-author trailer), which does not establish AI origin of the flaw. Verdict NOT_AI.

round6_research.bug_semantics: SSRF (CWE-918) in spring-ai-bedrock-converse BedrockProxyChatModel: multimodal media content with user-supplied URLs is fetched server-side via URLConnection.getInputStream() with no destination validation. The only gate, URLValidator.isValidURLBasic, is a regex that checks protocol/shape but never blocks internal destinations and explicitly permits 'localhost'; the media.getData() instanceof URL branch performs no validation at all (direct url.openConnection().getInputStream()). An attacker can make the Spring AI server issue HTTP requests to internal or external destinations. The advisory references fix commit a7d3223bc (1.1.x) and versions 1.0.5/1.1.4 (affected since 1.0.0-M5).
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-mhrg-94vw-45c5 (published 2026-03-27): 'Spring AI: Insufficient Validation causes SSRF when processing multimodal messages with user-supplied URLs' in BedrockProxyChatModel, affects 1.0.0 before 1.0.5 and 1.1.0 before 1.1.4, references commit a7d3223bc11a010b93fbc40a17fa9b68c52a8118. round6_research.bug_semantics: CWE-266 incorrect privilege assignment: the rid-based futime ops (op_fs_futime_sync/op_fs_futime_async, exposed as Deno.FsFile.prototype.utime/utimeSync, earlier as Deno.futime/futimeSync) never consult the permission model. Unlike the path-based op_fs_utime_* (Deno.utime) which calls state.check_write(&path), the rid-based ops only resolve the file resource and call file.utime_sync directly - so a script executed with --deny-write=./ (or a file opened read-only with write:false) can still change atime/mtime of any open file handle, bypassing allow-write/deny-write enforcement.

partial_wave.bug_semantics: Heap-buffer-overflow (CWE-122) in the tiled-TIFF decode path of coders/tiff.c: the tile_pixels buffer extent is computed with the formula (samples_per_pixel+1)*MagickMax(rows*TIFFTileRowSize(tiff),TIFFTileSize(tiff)), while the decode loop writes 4 bytes per pixel for samples_per_pixel samples per row and advances p+=TIFFTileRowSize(tiff) for each of 'rows' iterations; a crafted TIFF whose tile rows/stride product exceeds the estimate under-allocates and the ImportQuantumPixels loop overruns the heap. Crash confirmed on 7.1.1-13 beta (2023-06-25).
partial_wave.evidence: Advisory GHSA-fff3-4rp7-px97 (CVE-2025-68469), published 2025-08-25, credits Hardik shah of Vehere (Dawn Treaders team), PoC 'magick poc.tiff /dev/null' crashes on 7.1.1-13 (2023-06-25 build). Flaw formula origin: blame at a531d28e3^ shows extent line at a854a0a8af (2022-06-21) then 309dfda112 (2022-06-29); earlier form '4*MagickMax(rows*TIFFTileRowSize,TIFFTileSize)' from the 2022 tree migration (c6de626f2c, itself imported from Mercurial-era history).

round5_research.bug_semantics: Windows path-form bypass of server.fs.deny: isFileServingAllowed/isFileLoadingAllowed in packages/vite/src/node/server/middlewares/static.ts matches the deny globs against the raw normalized URL path with no normalization of Windows alternate path forms. NTFS ADS suffixes (/.env::$DATA?raw) and 8.3 short names (ENV~1) are not rejected, and Windows resolves them to the denied file's default data stream, so contents of server.fs.deny files (e.g. .env, *.pem) inside fs.allow directories are returned to the browser (information disclosure; requires --host exposure).
evidence: GHSA-FX2H-PF6J-XCFF / CVE-2026-53571: server.fs.deny contents returned to browser on Windows via NTFS ADS (/.env::$DATA?raw) and 8.3 short names; affected if dev server exposed via --host and sensitive file in fs.allow dir on NTFS volume; fixed in 6.4.3 / 7.3.5 / 8.0.16 (advisory local file read).

git show 1a15460bf35325ab9a7c22aacdb1e0afd1703c52 (Anthony Fu, 2021-10-27, feat: server.fs.deny support (#5378)): adds the deny glob check to isFileServingAllowed: if (server.config.server.fs.deny.some((i) => match(file, i, _matchOptions))) return false. Path is normalizePath(cleanUrl(url)) with no Windows alternate-path handling.
Parent d5e51f4840e4e75756c55cc5af58673c07ff643c: packages/vite/src/node/server/middlewares/static.ts has zero 'deny' occurrences (grep -c deny = 0), confirming parent absence of the deny logic.

Function-history chain: c22c43de6 (2024) renamed isFileServingAllowed -> isFileLoadingAllowed (check inside sirv) and 242f550eb (Environment API, 2025) refactored fs.allow/deny handling into isFileLoadingAllowed(config, filePath); both preserve the raw-path deny match; git blame on the current isFileLoadingAllowed shows no ADS/8.3 handling before the fix.

Direct fix dc245c71e5007ea4d891a025e2d69ac96c736546 (fix: reject windows alternate paths (#22572), green@sapphi.red, 2026-06-01, first release v8.0.16; backport 96b0c1016 into v6.4.3): isFileLoadingAllowed now rejects isWindows && filePath.includes('~') (8.3 short names) and any ':' beyond the drive letter (NTFS ADS); adds playground fs-serve tests for .env::$DATA and 8.3 names; follow-up 02cffa9e2 (#23066) narrows the tilde check to the 8.3 shape to reduce false positives, preserving the fix.

round5_research.bug_semantics: Endpoint-security bypass via Docker Swarm service API: Portainer enforces seven EndpointSecuritySettings restrictions (privileged mode, host PID, device mapping, capabilities, sysctls, security-opt/Seccomp/AppArmor, bind mounts) on the standard container creation path, but POST /services/create applies only 1/7 checks (partial Mounts struct) and POST /services/{id}/update applies 0/7 (only generic restrictedResourceOperation RBAC ownership, no body inspection / fetchEndpointSecuritySettings call). A non-admin user with Swarm endpoint access can create/update a service with CAP_SYS_ADMIN or ALL plus a host bind mount, reaching host RCE, bypassing admin-configured restrictions (CWE-862).
round5_research.evidence: Real fix aef1d982c2eb2d067cdb5acc27566959417e8559 ('fix(docker): add missing restrictions for Swarm BE-12772 (#2226)', andres-portainer, Apr 18 2026) modifies api/http/proxy/factory/docker/services.go (extends PartialService to parse CapabilityAdd/CapabilityDrop/Sysctls/Privileges and VolumeOptions.DriverConfig.Options, adds rejection logic), transport.go (+10 lines to invoke fetchEndpointSecuritySettings/body checks on service create and update paths), plus containers.go and a 468-line services_test.go. Same hunk on LTS branches: 6b1b6ff99 (#2557), d40462b75 (#2561). Introducer 4c0d8ce73 added the policy check to /containers/create only. Parent e1cc4bc9a: no decorateContainerCreationOperation, no AllowPrivilegedModeForRegularUsers in proxy, services create/update unguarded (verified transport.go lines 247-272). Git log confirms 4c0d8ce73 is the earliest commit introducing AllowPrivilegedModeForRegularUsers enforcement in the proxy.
round5_research.flaw_origin: First writer of the vulnerable asymmetric behavior: 4c0d8ce73252a9e5a13ac739bc6f8a5f34b16f25 ('feat(containers): Ensure users cannot create privileged containers via the API (#3969)', Maxime Bajeux, Jun 30 2020). This commit introduced the first EndpointSecuritySettings enforcement (AllowPrivilegedModeForRegularUsers -> decorateContainerCreationOperation) on the container path (it switches /containers/create to decorateContainerCreationOperation and adds privileged-mode/CapAdd checks in containers.go), while leaving /services/create (bare replaceRegistryAuthenticationHeader, no body inspection) and /services/{id}/update (restrictedResourceOperation only) with no such checks. Immediate parent e1cc4bc9a192347fb003e22c97ab5cbaa2f5929b has no decorateContainerCreationOperation at all (git grep -l returned nothing in parent) and no AllowPrivilegedModeForRegularUsers anywhere in the proxy; parent services.go handling confirmed /services/create and /services/{id}/update pre-existed as unguarded paths, but the policy asymmetry (that makes those paths a security relevance) is first introduced by 4c0d8ce73. The svc create/update routes themselves date to 5523fc90 (2017, bare passthrough), but they only become a bypass once container-side policy enforcement exists while services remain unchecked.
round5_research.reasoning: The named behavior (Swarm service create/update escaping endpoint-security restrictions) is first expressible when those restrictions are first enforced on containers but not services, which is exactly 4c0d8ce73. Parent e1cc4bc9a has no endpoint-security policy enforcement anywhere in the proxy, so the asymmetry (and hence the bypass) is atomically introduced by 4c0d8ce73. The direct fix aef1d982c extends services.go/transport.go so service create/update enforce the same checks. Introducer written by a human in 2020 with no AI markers -> closed causal chain -> NOT_AI.

round5_research.bug_semantics: vLLM tool schema DoS: the /v1/chat/completions backend fails to validate malformed/unexpected 'pattern' and 'type' fields in tool JSON schemas before passing them to the xgrammar native json-schema/regex compiler, so a single crafted request crashes the inference worker (RuntimeError in json_schema_converter.cc / regex_converter.cc); worker stays down until restarted.
evidence: Advisory PYSEC-2026-2023 (GHSA-vrq3-r879-7m65, aliases CVE-2025-48944): tool schema with malformed 'type' or 'pattern' field crashes the vLLM inference worker via native json_schema_converter.cc / regex_converter.cc fatal errors; fix links PR vllm-project/vllm#17623.

Fix 08bf7840780980c7568c573c70a6a8db94fd45ff ([Bugfix] validate grammar and throw 400 error instead of crashing when xgrammar validation fails, #17623, Jason Cheng+Russell Bryant, 2025-05-12): adds try/except xgr.Grammar.from_json_schema(schema) in validate_xgrammar_grammar (backend_xgrammar.py) and adds validate_guidance_grammar call on auto-fallback, so a malformed tool schema now raises a 400 request error instead of crashing the worker; adds regression tests test_chat_completion.py/test_completion.py.

Its json branch only calls has_xgrammar_unsupported_json_features and returns without schema compilation validation.

Immediate parent 1e3598edeb694c1a6a1fdfac5e7d12697749561b has no vllm/v1/structured_output/ tree (git ls-tree shows only unrelated vllm/v1 subdirs), confirming the vulnerable validate module and its missing-schema-compilation behavior are absent in the parent.

round5_research.flaw_origin: Commit 80e9afb5bc53a5ca9f2b229e46c3cdead2704f5c ([V1][Core] Support for Structured Outputs, Aaron Pham, 2025-03-07) first created vllm/v1/structured_output/utils.py and wrote validate_structured_output_request, whose guided_params.json branch only ran has_xgrammar_unsupported_json_features(schema) and then returned, WITHOUT compiling/vouching the schema via xgr.Grammar.from_json_schema. round6_research.bug_semantics: IDOR in message deletion (CWE-862): DELETE /api/messages/:conversationId/:messageId lets any authenticated user delete any other user's messages. validateMessageReq middleware only checks that conversationId belongs to the requester, but the handler calls deleteMessages({ messageId }) with only messageId as the MongoDB filter, no user/conversation constraint. An attacker passes their own valid conversationId plus the victim's messageId to permanently delete the victim's message. Incomplete fix of CVE-2024-41703 (which added the middleware but left the model filter bare). Fixed in 0.8.4-rc1.

Introducer commit 7dc27b10f (parents db77163f) added the DELETE route + validateMessageReq middleware; parent's messages.js EXISTS but contains no deleteMessages call (grep count 0) - file pre-existed, vulnerable behavior absent (introducer_parent_absent=false). round5_research.bug_semantics: Git symlink injection leading to arbitrary file read: go-git Clone writes Git blob entries with mode 0o120000 as real OS symlinks (only .gitmodules is blocked); the clone output under the stack project path may therefore contain docker-compose.yml as a symlink to an arbitrary host path. GET /api/stacks/{id}/file reads the stack entry point with os.ReadFile (GetFileContent), which follows the OS symlink and returns the target file content.

Direct fix a33cc4886 (fix(git): forbid the usage of symlinks BE-12768 #2533, andres-portainer, 2026-05-04) wraps the clone worktree with NewNoSymlinkFS so Symlink() returns ErrSymlinkDetected and clone fails on any symlink; companion b28796175 (backport #2365, 2026-04-18). round5_research.bug_semantics: OpenAI API authentication bypass in vLLM: AuthenticationMiddleware derives the URL path from starlette's URL reconstructed from request scope (request.url.path in the original implementation, then URL(scope=scope).path after a refactor) and strips root_path from that reconstructed path. Because ASGI web servers can report a scope path that differs from what the router routes on (root_path handling), the proxy root_path stripping can be bypassed so a request path that does not start with /v1 escapes auth, allowing use of the OpenAI API without the configured VLLM_API_KEY or --api-key.
round5_research.evidence: Direct fix 2b94d1c0ca (PR #43426, 2026-05-22, Russell Bryant) changes vllm/entrypoints/openai/server_utils.py AuthenticationMiddleware from `url_path = URL(scope=scope).path.removeprefix(root_path)` to `url_path = scope['path'].removeprefix(root_path)`, closing the URL-reconstruction differential. The vulnerable URL-from-scope reconstruction first appeared in the AuthenticationMiddleware class created by 6e244ae091 (PR #19946, 2025-06-27) as a refactor of the original token-auth middleware introduced by 9c1352eb57 (PR #1106, 2024-01-23). The pre-refactor code in 9c1352eb57 used `request.url.path.startswith('/v1')`, which is the same starlette URL-from-scope reconstruction, so the required-vulnerable-behavior introducer is 9c1352eb57, where parent 7a0b011d has no token auth at all. 6e244ae091 preserves the logic (same URL(scope) reconstruction), so it is not a new atomic introducer. Introducer author Erfan Al-Hossami, no co-author/AI trailers.
round5_research.flaw_origin: Trust boundary flaw: auth decision derived from a reconstructed URL whose path can diverge from the actual routed path under proxy/root_path setups instead of the request scope path used for routing; CWE-287/improper auth.
round5_research.reasoning: The auth middleware that decides guarded-path eligibility via a starlette-reconstructed URL was written by human contributor Erfan Al-Hossami in Jan 2024 with no AI markers; the parent commit has no auth, so behavior absent in parent. The 2026 fix 2b94d1c0ca has a Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6 trailer, but AI-assisted fix does not establish AI origin of the flawed introduced logic. Verdict NOT_AI.

round5_research.bug_semantics: Multiple denial-of-service vectors in Scriban expression evaluation (CWE-400). Vector 1: string * int in ScriptBinaryExpression.CalculateToString loops unboundedly (for (int i = 0; i < value; i++) builder.Append(leftText)) with no LimitToString/LoopLimit guard -> OOM for e.g. 'AAAA' * 500000000. Vector 2: ShiftLeft in CalculateLongWithInt / CalculateBigIntegerNoFit does (BigInteger)left << (int)right with no cap (MaxBigInteger exists but is only used for Power) -> multi-MB BigInteger allocation for 1 << 2000000000. Vector 3: range operators .. and ..< yield lazy iterators (RangeInclude/RangeExclude) that builtin functions (array.size -> .Count(), array.join -> StringBuilder append) fully enumerate, bypassing LoopLimit -> CPU/memory exhaustion for (0..1000000000) | array.size.

Verified hunks in src/Scriban/Syntax/Expressions/ScriptBinaryExpression.cs and src/Scriban/Functions/ArrayFunctions.cs. Introducer 4605481: root commit, no parent (rev-parse 4605481^ fails), contains the unbounded string-mult loop at line 102 and integer RangeInclude iterators (git show 4605481:src/Textamina.Scriban/Runtime/ScriptBinaryExpression.cs). round5_research.bug_semantics: HtmlSanitizer allowLinkHosts()/allowMediaHosts() bypass via URL-parser differentials and <area> misclassification: UrlSanitizer::parse() parses input with league/uri UriString::parse following RFC-3986, while browsers follow the WHATWG URL Standard (normalizing backslash to slash before parsing authority of special schemes, etc.), so off-allowlist URLs can be smuggled past the host/scheme allowlist checks. Additionally UrlAttributeSanitizer only sanitized <a> href URLs, not <area href>, which browsers treat as a link target.
round5_research.evidence: Direct fix d506b556d3 (2026-04-17, Alexandre Daubois) adds to UrlSanitizer::sanitize() a backslash / triple-slash rejection (`if (false !== strpbrk($input, '\') || preg_match('~^(?:https?|ftp|wss?):(/[^/]|///)~i', $input)) return null;`) and extends UrlAttributeSanitizer::sanitizeAttribute to also sanitize 'area' elements (`in_array($element, ['a','area'], true)`). Introducer: the HtmlSanitizer component was created in 199e405fdd (2021-12-15, author Titouan Galopin) with UrlSanitizer using league/uri UriString::parse (RFC-3986) plus isAllowedHost() host-part matching, and UrlAttributeSanitizer handling only element 'a'. git show 199e405fdd^:...UrlSanitizer.php -> path does not exist in parent (parent 0d6e859d), so vulnerable behavior absent in parent (new component). No AI markers on the introducer commit message/trailers. The recorded fix sha 1c38fe68 is the v6.4.40 release tag carrier; actual security fix is d506b556d3 (merged via 6fccb4c1f5).

round5_research.bug_semantics: Integer overflow in the FreeType text-sizing path. When each glyph's advance is an exceeding large value (font-controlled), Pillow accumulates the advances into a 32-bit int position/advanced while tracking the current draw position, causing an integer wraparound (CWE-190). Fixed by widening position/advanced from int to long.
round5_research.evidence: Advisory CVE-2026-42308/GHSA-WJX4-4JCJ-G98J: integer overflow when processing fonts where glyph advances by an exceeding large amount; first_patched_version 12.2.0. Direct commit search: recorded fix 3c41c095064200a02672d89cc5ff629eaf4b0d4f is only the '12.2.0 version bump' (tag carrier). Real fix ec8272044d2adfc97a5f4b6e921c1a908318d9cb (2026-04-01, Hugo van Kemenade, co-authored-by Andrew Murray) changes src/_imagingft.c bounding_box_and_anchors to widen 'int position; int advanced' to 'long position; long advanced'; it is an ancestor of the 12.2.0 tag (git merge-base --is-ancestor -> yes) and present on main + 12.2.x/12.3.x remotes. Atomic introducer: git log -S'position += glyph_info[i].x_advance' yields ea0f1c6b06 (2019) but that traces to a77850564ae32c3b9ee289f1ebb9a5b8507025a0 (2016-02-16 shamsa 'Fix gitsize function.') which is the first commit making font_getsize accumulate glyph_info[i].x_advance (font-derived advance) into an int; parent 02d0bcbc6b97f39dde6ba7bc55f1d38be8422ecc still used x += face->glyph->metrics.horiAdvance in getsize (git show parent:_imagingft.c confirms), so parent absence verified. The vulnerable int-accumulation of font advance in size detection originates at this commit and persists through later refactors (x -> x_max -> position) until the long fix.
round5_research.flaw_origin: font_getsize in _imagingft.c accumulates font-derived glyph advances (x_advance / y_advance from raqm or fallback FreeType layout) into a 32-bit int position while computing the text bounding box; a crafted font with an extremely large per-glyph advance triggers int wraparound.
round5_research.reasoning: The vulnerable behavior (32-bit int accumulation of font-supplied advance values in the text-size path) was first written by human maintainer shamsa in 2016 commit a7785056, well before mainstream AI coding assistants and with no AI author/committer/co-author/trailer markers. The 2026 fix by Hugo van Kemenade (with a human co-author Andrew Murray) also carries no AI markup. Closed causal chain: atomic introducer found, immediate parent absence confirmed, direct fix mapped to the exact vulnerable function, no AI markers. verdict NOT_AI.

round5_research.bug_semantics: Child processes spawned by Renovate's exec() incorrectly inherit the full parent environment: lib/util/exec/common.ts passes execa(cmd, opts) with env=childEnv but without extendEnv:false, so execa's default extendEnv:true merges the sanitized childEnv into the complete process.env, exposing all Renovate process environment variables (including secrets/credentials) to every spawned tool/child process.
evidence: Fresh full-history clone of renovatebot/renovate at .ai-slop/state/repos/renovate (blob:none filter, git checkout main). Advisory GHSA-8WC6-VGRQ-X6CF: child processes spawned by Renovate have full access to environment variables; introduced 42.68.1, fixed 42.96.3/43.4.4.

Fix: 9b59ffda 'fix(exec): don't extend env (#41024)' (2026-02-09, Michael Kriese) adds extendEnv:false to the execa call in lib/util/exec/common.ts; commit is a cherry-pick of a825cac81 (same PR #41024) and is the fix shipped in 42.96.3 (git merge-base --is-ancestor 9b59ffda 42.96.3 = yes; a825cac81 is on mainline and not an ancestor of 42.96.3).

Introducer: e773b3243 (2025-12-30, PR #40212, Jamie Tanna) migrated exec() from node:child_process spawn to execa. Pre-migration: spawn(cmd, {...opts, env: childEnv}) - node child_process with an explicit env option does NOT inherit process.env (env replaces). Post-migration: execa(cmd, {...opts, env: childEnv}) - execa defaults extendEnv:true, merging childEnv into process.env and thereby exposing the full parent env to child processes.

env: childEnv was passed both before and after (lib/util/exec/index.ts getRawExecOptions returns env: childEnv; childEnv built by getChildEnv -> getChildProcessEnv which sanitizes only when exposeAllEnv is unset). The leak is purely the execa extendEnv default semantic change.
git merge-base --is-ancestor e773b3243 42.68.1 = yes; not an ancestor of 42.68.0. Matches advisory introduced=42.68.1 exactly.

AI markers: introducer e773b3243 (author Jamie Tanna <jamie.tanna@mend.io>, committer GitHub noreply) has no trailers/co-authors. Fixes a825cac81/9b59ffda (Michael Kriese) and test 01d2772b9 (Jamie Tanna) all have no AI trailers. No AI-authored code in the causal chain.
round5_research.flaw_origin: e773b3243 (2025-12-30, fix(util/exec): migrate to `execa` for command execution #40212, Jamie Tanna) replaced node:child_process spawn with execa in lib/util/exec/common.ts. node spawn with an explicit env option replaces the environment (no inheritance), while execa defaults extendEnv:true and merges the provided env into process.env, changing the semantics to full-env inheritance for child processes. This commit shipped in 42.68.1, matching the advisory introduced=42.68.1.

round6_research.bug_semantics: TOCTOU race condition (CWE-362/367) in Rack::Session::Pool: session is loaded at request start (prepare_session) and unconditionally stored back at request end (commit_session -> write_session -> @pool.store). A concurrent long-running request holding a session cookie can re-store (restore) a session that a logout/deletion request removed from the pool, letting an attacker retain illicit access after logout. Also delete_session generates a new sid without storing the empty session, so deletion is not atomically reflected in the pool.
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-vpfw-47h7-xj4g (published 2025-05-08, fixed in rack 2.2.14, vulnerable <=2.2.13, CWE-362/367, CVSS3 4.2): Rack::Session::Pool restores a deleted session; mitigation recommends invalidating sessions atomically. Fix commit c48e52f7c57e99e1e1bf54c8760d4f082cd1c89d (2025-05-06, Jeremy Evans code@jeremyevans.net, Co-authored-by Samuel Williams, squash merge from fork): write_session returns false unless get_session_with_fallback(session_id) present; delete_session now stores empty session for new sid. Vulnerable code in v2.2.13 lib/rack/session/pool.rb lines 55-71 (write_session unconditional @pool.store; delete_session generate_sid without store) and abstract/id.rb call flow (prepare_session at start, commit_session at end). Introducer 186ef7f1c785e613eadf00f7c7227c463164736d (2007-08-11, Scytrin dai Kinthra) created lib/rack/session/pool.rb with load_session/commit_session and unconditional @pool.store; parent cdab8c7376131a9f11a5207a19c2138bbc5ffce1 had only lib/rack/session/cookie.rb (no Pool, no restore-after-delete pattern). Same pattern carried by a76a3aaff53a4c44681710eb320f9f4a80aefed1 and 2d383fa25326b00969d8f30693571b38f2e2f4aa (2009-01, same author, added :drop and with_lock, kept semantics). No AI markers on introducer or fix (all human authors/committers; fix is a human maintainer merge).
round6_research.flaw_origin: Original Rack::Session::Pool design (2007): load_session reads cookie sid, commit_session unconditionally stores the session back (@pool.store) with no existence check; read-modify-write at request boundary makes any concurrent deletion reversible. The :drop deletion path and with_lock mutex (per-store serialization only, not across the whole request+app call) were added in 2009 but kept the restore-after-delete semantics.
round6_research.reasoning: The restore-after-deletion race originates in the 2007 design of Rack::Session::Pool (read session at request start, unconditionally write back at end) by human author Scytrin dai Kinthra, long predating AI coding tools. The 2025 fix by Rack maintainers Jeremy Evans and Samuel Williams is human-authored. No AI involvement anywhere in the causal chain.

round6_research.bug_semantics: SSRF (CWE-918) in Portkey AI Gateway proxy routes. The gateway determines the destination baseURL by prioritizing the value of the x-portkey-custom-host request header: getProxyPath() in src/handlers/proxyHandler.ts / proxyGetHandler.ts returns `${customHost}/${reqPath}${reqQuery}` when the header is set, and the server then performs an external fetch to that URL. An attacker can set x-portkey-custom-host to an internal address (e.g. 169.254.169.254 AWS metadata) and the gateway fetches it server-side. Patched in 1.14.0 by adding isValidCustomHost() validation (URL scheme/port checks, @ rejection, IP/private-host blocking) in the request validator and config schema.

round5_research.bug_semantics: Recursive container scanning (deep scan, --depth>0) fails to enforce the recursive size budget as a hard limit on compressed/archive inputs: single-stream decompressors (gzip/bzip2/lzma/xz) fully materialize decompressed content before the remaining budget is validated, and the recursive_scan continues when the residual budget is already negative; zip/tar/rpm multi-entry archives are checked only against the original per-entry budget rather than a shared cumulative budget, allowing many individually small members to exceed the aggregate limit. Exploitable by a crafted archive to force excessive memory/CPU consumption (CWE-400/CWE-409, DoS).
round5_research.evidence: introducer b3336a946a7c5e41bb797bd09b798d6c4d9bc373 (author Roman Babenko, 2022-07-12, single parent, no squash, no co-author/trailer AI markers); parent app.py data_scan grep count 0; commit adds data_scan() recursive container scan with per-entry zip budget check and recursive_limit default 1<<30. Git log -S'data_scan' confirms b3336a9 is the first written occurrence; later commits (4b764f8 gzip, e571ec9 tar/bzip2, c8ddb62 lzma, 0bd8fe56 refactor to deep_scanner) extend/relocate but introduce no new vulnerability pattern. Fix 8b9b111cb65e42410b6454665e172bdfe7869a37 (v1.16.0, #855, DeepScan refactoring) adds negative-budget guard 'recursive_limit_size -= data_size; if MIN_DATA_LEN > recursive_limit_size: return' to recursive_scan and structure_scan, plus limited/bounded read for gzip (and bzip2/lzma): direct fix verified.
round5_research.flaw_origin: atomic introducer b3336a946a7c5e41bb797bd09b798d6c4d9bc373 'ZIP archives scanner' (2022-07-12) first wrote app.data_scan() recursive container-scan in credsweeper/app.py; parent 4d09255ecd7140f8c1a3498423dd90a8332683c6 has zero occurrences of data_scan (grep count 0). round5_research.bug_semantics: Denial of service / disk exhaustion (CWE-400). The Evolver proxy HTTP server binds to 127.0.0.1 (reachable by any local process, container host-netns neighbor, or malicious postinstall script) and its parseBody() in src/proxy/server/http.js reads the entire POST body (req.on('data') -> chunks.push, Buffer.concat(chunks)) with NO size cap. Routes 'POST /asset/submit' and 'POST /mailbox/send' (src/proxy/server/routes.js) pass that attacker-controlled body through store.send/appendLine which fs.appendFileSync's the full body verbatim into messages.jsonl (src/proxy/mailbox/store.js). An unauthenticated local attacker can POST a multi-GB body to fill the disk and make the daemon OOM on restart (startup readFileSync over the huge JSONL).
round5_research.evidence: Direct code fix is commit 4a63e91ffb28c2c74e1b8d9ba934ad1e57d1e885 ('Release v1.70.0-beta.5', evolver-publish, Co-authored-by seikiko, Apr 27 2026), which reworks parseBody(req) -> parseBody(req, opts) in src/proxy/server/http.js: adds DEFAULT_MAX_BODY_BYTES=1*1024*1024 (tunable via EVOMAP_PROXY_MAX_BODY_BYTES), rejects declared content-length > cap with 413, destroys the request when the streaming count exceeds cap, with an explicit comment 'GHSA-7xp7-m392-h92c: cap request body at 1 MiB... /asset/submit and /mailbox/send write the full body verbatim into messages.jsonl'. round6_research.bug_semantics: Remote DoS (speculative-decoding state-handling bug; GPU device-side assert crash, not a malformed-input bug) in vLLM V1 rejection sampling: sample_recovered_tokens_kernel in vllm/v1/sample/rejection_sampler.py can emit a recovered token id >= vocab_size (in the verified Qwen3 trace, recovered_token_ids[0] = 151936 == vocab_size) when all valid entries in the boundary/last tile have zero (post-clamp) probability: the tiled loop loads out-of-vocab entries with other=0.0 for both prob and inv_q so their score (prob * inv_q = 0.0) is eligible to win the per-tile tl.max over out-of-vocab padding, and recovered_id = v + local_id lands in the padded region. That OOV recovered token is then treated as the request's live next token: vllm/v1/spec_decode/eagle.py prepare_next_token_ids_padded converts the out-of-vocab value to -1 (INVALID_TOKEN_ID), set_inputs_first_pass writes that -1 back into the live drafter input_ids row, and the embedding/attention path consumes it -> CUDA error: device-side assert triggered -> engine worker death. Reachable remotely via a frontend-legal speculative workload (structured outputs + overlap + cancellation) and via the public gRPC Generate/Abort request surface; aborts concurrent requests and DoSes other clients until worker restart. Affected >= 0.17.1 (first release containing the flawed tiled rewrite), fixed 0.24.0.
