round6_research.bug_semantics: Permission-bypass / incorrect authorization (CWE-863) in rtk's PreToolUse rewriting hook: the permission splitter did not conservatively split or reject shell constructs that Bash treats as command-execution boundaries or nested execution. rtk (Rust Token Killer) rewrites commands before they reach an LLM host hook and checks rewritten commands against the user's allow/ask/deny Bash rules (e.g. from .claude/settings.json). split_on_operators (src/discover/lexer.rs) tokenizes and splits only on `&&`, `||`, `;` and `|` (quote-aware), and src/hooks/permissions.rs checks each segment against deny/ask rules, auto-allowing when no rule fires or an allow rule matches. Constructs split only by Bash - embedded newlines, background `&`, subshell `( )`, command substitution `$(...)` and backticks, process substitution `<(...)`, and fd-dup redirects `>&file` - were treated as part of a single segment, so a command beginning with an allowed prefix such as `git` could hide a second command behind one of these constructs (e.g. `git log; ...` variants that are not split, or `git log $(curl ...|sh)`). rtk rewrite still returned exit code 0, and the hook emitted permissionDecision "allow" with the rewritten command still containing the hidden command, which then executed without the confirmation/denial the permission rules intended. CVSS 7.8 HIGH, CWE-863, published 2026-06-23, fixed in 0.42.2.
round6_research.evidence: CVE-2026-54555 (CWE-863, CVSS 7.8, published 2026-06-23, fixed 0.42.2) - NVD description matches the splitter gap exactly (hidden command behind shell constructs, rewrite exit 0 -> permissionDecision allow). Introducer a9c610a9 (2026-03-13, parent 97b68783): git show a9c610a9:src/permissions.rs contains 'fn split_compound_command' splitting only on &&, ||, |, ; with the comment 'Not a full shell parser - handles common cases'; parent tree has no permissions code (git ls-tree 97b68783:src/permissions.rs -> absent; file count of permission matches = 0), so parent_absent=True. Pre-fix state at v0.42.1: src/discover/lexer.rs split_on_operators splits on &&, ||, ; and pipes only (quote-aware tokenizer), confirming the vulnerable semantics persisted until the fix. Fix commits (both in tag v0.42.2, 2026-06-05 release via PR #2283; verified with merge-base --is-ancestor): cdcdb6863a3df709603dbed0a6205bf16e4e635f (2026-06-03, aesoft/Adrien Eppling) decomposes compound commands on newline, background & and subshell ( ), adds contains_unattestable_construct for command/process substitution and fd-dup redirects, and never auto-allows unattestable segments (defers to host); companion ce362970e5752bacfd3a356c7fa122fea94ff0b2 rejects `>&file` redirect auto-allow. Marker scans (grep -icE 'co-authored|assisted-by|anthropic|claude|copilot|codex|openai|grok|generated with|mastra|gemini|bard') on introducer and both fix commits hit only product-context words ('Claude Code', 'Gemini/Cursor', 'Copilot CLI' host names in subjects/bodies) - no AI co-author or generation trailers anywhere; authors are human accounts (florian@bruniaux.com, aeeppling@users.noreply.github.com).
round6_research.flaw_origin: The permission-check mechanism on rewrites was created by commit a9c610a9afedd748c8184ecb18911598a943da0e (2026-03-13, Florian BRUNIAUX <florian@bruniaux.com>, 'fix(hook): respect Claude Code deny/ask permission rules on rewrite', fixes #260): adds src/permissions.rs (332 lines) whose split_compound_command splits on `&&`, `||`, `|`, `;` only - the doc comment says 'Not a full shell parser - handles common cases' - and rewires src/rewrite_cmd.rs so exit 0 = allow (auto-approve rewrite), exit 2 = deny, exit 3 = ask. Before this commit the hook auto-allowed every rewritten command with no rule checking at all (no permission code in the parent 97b68783: no src/permissions.rs and zero permission-related files), so a9c610a9 is the minimal atomic introducer of the vulnerable splitter-and-auto-allow behavior. The splitter moved to src/discover/lexer.rs (split_on_operators, added 2026-03-29 f3217a46) and was hardened multiple times (e.g. 40c9dbc7 'require all segments to match allow rules', 2026-04-11), but the construct gaps (newline, &, `( )`, $(), <(), >&) that the CVE describes survived until 0.42.2.
round6_research.reasoning: Step 1: the flaw is a permission-splitter gap (CWE-863) in rtk's rewrite hook: incomplete splitting of Bash constructs plus auto-allow semantics let a hidden command ride an allowed prefix into the emitted permissionDecision-allow command. Step 2: decomposition - the splitter-and-check flow first appears in a9c610a9 (2026-03-13); its parent has zero permission code (before that, the hook allowed everything with no rule check, so there was no splitter to bypass), making a9c610a9 the minimal atomic introducer; the later lexer refactors and segment-matching hardening are re-implementations of the same pattern, and the construct gaps the CVE names persisted unchanged until the fix. Step 3: markers - the introducer and the two v0.42.2 fix commits carry no AI co-authorship/generation signals (hits are the project's own product vocabulary: Claude Code/Gemini/Cursor/Copilot are the LLM hosts rtk integrates with, not authorship attributions); introducer authored by a human with Signed-off-by. Human-authored code introduced the vulnerable splitter: verdict = NOT_AI. fix_sha = cdcdb686 (primary decomposition/defer fix), with ce362970 as the companion construct fix in the same release.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Environment CRD PodSpec injection leading to node escape and cluster takeover: Environment.spec.runtime.podSpec / spec.builder.podSpec pass through unvalidated; MergePodSpec (pkg/executor/util/merge.go) propagates HostPID/HostIPC/HostNetwork/SecurityContext/ServiceAccountName/hostPath volumes into generated Deployments by poolmgr/newdeploy/buildermgr. Three compounding flaws: (1) Environment.Validate only checks container naming, never host namespaces/privileged/hostPath; (2) validating webhook (pkg/webhook/environment.go) registered verbs=create only, so a kubectl apply then kubectl patch bypasses admission; (3) unconditional dangerous-field forwarding at the merge layer. A tenant with environments.fission.io create/update RBAC gets a privileged pod with host-root mount, reads cluster CA private key, signs kubelet certs -> full cluster takeover.
round6_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-wmgg-3p4h-48x7/CVE-2026-50545 (fix v1.24.0, PR #3391 companion #3390; OSV GIT fixed=ce617120) details the 3 flaws. Fix e484df84 (2026-05-23, Sanket Sudake, PR #3391) adds ValidatePodSpecSafety (new pkg/apis/core/v1/podspec_safety.go) called from Environment.Validate and FunctionSpec.Validate, extends webhook marker to verbs=create;update, and strips host namespaces/SA/hostPath at the merge layer; companion 8fa79941 (PR #3390) drops builder SA token. BIC trace: git log -S Runtime.PodSpec/MergePodSpec -> first appearance d5785393 (PR #1106, 2019-05-29) which adds Runtime.PodSpec to typefields.go, creates pkg/executor/util/merge.go MergePodSpec forwarding SecurityContext + Volumes + NodeSelector etc., and wires newdeploy.go/gp.go call sites; parent 49f9944 lacks PodSpec (grep rc=1) and MergePodSpec (grep rc=1). c7d448ca (2021-02-23, PR #1932) later added HostPID/HostNetwork/HostIPC/ServiceAccountName forwarding, same unvalidated design. Webhook added 9a07d7d9 (2022-11-13, neha_gupta) with verbs=create only; validation.go lineage (7a7d15b5 2018 -> 11f9ef10 move) never validated podspec security fields. Authors/committers: Vishal Biyani (author), Ta-Ching Chen (committer) for BIC; all human, no Co-Authored-By/assisted trailers; fix by Sanket Sudake, no AI markers (grep 0 hits).
round6_research.flaw_origin: introduced_by_passthrough: the Environment podspec passthrough + MergePodSpec forwarding were added without any security validation; the CRD field, merge logic and call sites all arrive in one commit
round6_research.reasoning: The minimum atomic introducer of the vulnerable behavior is d5785393 (Add kubernetes podSpec support in fission spec), authored by Vishal Biyani, committed by Ta-Ching Chen, both named human maintainers, June 2019 — well before AI coding assistants. The immediate parent lacks the podspec passthrough entirely. Later commits (c7d448ca field extensions, 9a07d7d9 webhook with create-only verbs) extend or fail to constrain the same design, but do not constitute the initial vulnerable behavior. round6_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated command injection (CWE-78) in the Dynamic Proxy Configuration Filename handling of Coolify < 4.0.0-beta.451: NewDynamicConfiguration::addDynamicConfiguration() and DynamicConfigurationNavbar::delete() build shell commands from the user-controlled filename and run them on the managed server via instant_remote_process() without any escaping - 'test -f $file && echo 1 || echo 0', "echo '{base64}' | base64 -d > {$file}" (later tee variant), and 'rm -f {$proxy_path}/dynamic/{$file}' (delete) - so an authenticated user with server update permission can inject shell metacharacters via the filename and execute arbitrary commands on the server (RCE). Fix PR #7375 adds validateShellSafePath($file, 'proxy configuration filename') before use and escapeshellarg() around every interpolation of the file path.
evidence: Identity: OSV CVE-2025-66212 = GHSA-q7rg-2j7p-83gp, 'Coolify Vulnerable to Authenticated Remote Code Execution via Command Injection in Dynamic Proxy Configuration Filename', repo github.com/coollabsio/coolify, GIT range introduced 0 / fixed 96bfc145 (v4.0.0 #9818) and d9ec1054 (v4.0.0-beta.451 #7369 release merges); cvelistV5 record confirms affected coollabsio coolify, references GHSA-q7rg-2j7p-83gp, PR #7375, release v4.0.0-beta.451, research repo 0xrakan/coolify-cve-2025-66209-66213; cvss 9.4

Fix = PR #7375, merge commit 31e2ac49 (2025-11-27, Andras Bacsai; parents e60e74ac9 + 281a7062; branch commits 0073d045f initial hardening + 281a7062 enhanced validation): diff adds validateShellSafePath($file,'proxy configuration filename') and escapeshellarg() in NewDynamicConfiguration.php (test -f / tee lines) and DynamicConfigurationNavbar.php (rm -f line), plus validation of database names (BackupEdit, DatabaseBackupJob, Postgresql General) and file paths (LocalFileVolume) - the sibling injection sites of the 66209-66213 series

Introducer 154b1b05 (2024-02-22, Andras Bacsai <andras.bacsai@gmail.com>, 1 parent 4d88638d) created the feature: NewDynamicConfiguration.php + DynamicConfigurationNavbar.php + DynamicConfigurations.php as new files; pre-fix code was 'test -f $file' / 'base64 -d > {$file}' / 'rm -f {$proxy_path}/dynamic/{$file}' with $file built from unvalidated $this->fileName; parent tree contains none of these files (grep of parent ls-tree for dynamic/proxy shows only unrelated proxy UI/actions), so immediate-parent absence holds and the commit is the atomic introducer

round6_research.bug_semantics: Information disclosure via missing cache-control headers and client-side session checks (CWE-384 session fixation-adjacent / missing Cache-Control): tutor-open-edx (overhangio/tutor) 20.0.2 does not emit Cache-Control: no-store/no-cache headers from the LMS web proxy (nginx config pre-2021, Caddyfile after) and does not add client-side session hardening, so after logout a local user can press the browser Back button and still see cached PII from the previous authenticated session without reauthentication (local attacker, CVSS 3.1 3.3 LOW).
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-gq25-78jf-v78c / CVE-2025-65681 / PYSEC-2025-219 (published 2025-11-26, severity LOW CVSS 3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N, last_affected 20.0.2, no fixed version; only references are the PoC repo Rivek619/CVE-2025-65681, docs.tutor.edly.io and pypa advisory). PoC: log in, view account settings PII, log out, press browser Back -> PII still shown, no cache-control headers and no client-side session checks. Repo forensics: git log --diff-filter=A -- tutor/templates/apps/caddy/Caddyfile -> 728ef966 (2020-09-17, v11.0.0) which is the first Caddyfile; its parent d3c842c8 already had nginx templates (lms.conf etc.); git log --diff-filter=A -- nginx/config/lms.conf.templ -> 3170541f (2017-09-19); git log --diff-filter=A -- nginx/lms.conf -> bdd1a41f (2017-07-03) which is a root commit (rev-list --max-parents=0 --count = 1, no parent field). git show bdd1a41f:nginx/lms.conf has no cache-control/no-store (grep exit 1); git grep -in 'no-store|no-cache|cache-control' HEAD -- tutor/templates/apps/caddy/ -> no matches; git log --all -S 'no-store' -- tutor/templates -> empty. Caddyfile at HEAD only has static-asset expires rules (expires 31536000s for pipelined files), no no-store on HTML/session pages. 057aead0 (v20.0.3) and bd82a68d (v20.0.4, 'security: add upstream security patch' = GHSA-rh64-vc2h-7wfj edx-platform CourseLimitedStaffRole patch) are unrelated to this advisory.
round6_research.flaw_origin: bdd1a41f ':sunrise:' (2017-07-03, root commit of the repo, founder Regis Behmo) is the atomic introducer: it created nginx/lms.conf (the LMS web-server template) with no Cache-Control/no-store headers and no session-related cache directives; the omission persisted through the nginx era (lms.conf.templ), the Caddy transition (231bbbfe 2021-10-14), and is still absent at HEAD (Caddyfile has no cache-control/no-store directives; only static-file expires rules exist). The vulnerable behavior's first writer is the 2017 human-authored root commit; parent absence is trivially satisfied (root commit). round6_research.bug_semantics: Authentication bypass in generic opaque-token validation (internal/auth/generic/generic.go): validateOpaqueToken decodes the RFC7662 introspection response into introspectResp and passes iss to validateClaims, whose issuer check is `if a.issuer != "" && iss != "" { if iss != a.issuer { reject } }`; when the OAuth provider omits the optional iss field, iss defaults to empty string, the condition short-circuits false and the issuer check is skipped silently, so tokens issued by unauthorized/unintended third-party IdPs are accepted.
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-wcpr-6g7x-p44r (published 2026-06-18) describes exactly the validateOpaqueToken/validateClaims issuer-skip; CVE-2026-11718 details identical (equivalent record). Fix commit 1d8df0df ('fix(auth/generic): enforce issuer presence in opaque token validation (#3360)', 2026-06-04, single parent 5f0304f7) rewrites the block to `if iss == "" { reject missing issuer }` and `if iss != a.issuer { reject }`, plus discoverOIDCConfig issuer-presence check; fix predates advisory publication. Introducer c924701a (single parent 9d34f9e1) is ancestor of the fix (git merge-base --is-ancestor exit 0); git grep -c validateOpaqueToken c924701a^ -- '*.go' => exit 1 (absent at parent); blame of the condition at 1d8df0df^ traces to c924701a. All commits by Wenxin Du, markers 0 on introducer and fix.
round6_research.flaw_origin: design flaw in new feature commit c924701a ('feat(auth): support opaque token validation for generic authService (#2944)', 2026-04-09): the commit first wrote both validateOpaqueToken and validateClaims (git log --reverse -S 'func (a AuthService) validateClaims' -> c924701a), including the over-permissive issuer condition that treats missing issuer as 'no check needed'.
round6_research.reasoning: The minimum atomic introducer of the vulnerable behavior (opaque-token introspection path accepting tokens when issuer is absent) is c924701a: it created validateOpaqueToken, validateClaims, and the flawed `a.issuer != "" && iss != ""` skip-condition in one commit, with neither function present at its parent. records.details:
# Consensus Divergence in V5 Transparent SIGHASH_SINGLE With No Corresponding Output

## Summary

Zebra failed to enforce a ZIP-244 consensus rule for V5 transparent transactions: when an input is signed with `SIGHASH_SINGLE` and there is no transparent output at the same index as that input, validation must fail. Zebra instead asked the underlying sighash library to compute a digest, and that library produced a digest over an empty output set rather than failing. An attacker could craft a V5 transaction with more transparent inputs than outputs that Zebra accepts but `zcashd` rejects, creating a consensus split between Zebra and `zcashd` nodes.

A previous fix ([`GHSA-cwfq-rfcr-8hmp`](https://github.com/ZcashFoundation/zebra/security/advisories/GHSA-cwfq-rfcr-8hmp)) addressed a closely related case in the same area of the code, but did not cover this specific one.

## Severity

**Critical** - This is a Consensus Vulnerability that could allow a malicious party to induce network partitioning, service disruption, and potential double-spend attacks against affected nodes.

Note that the impact is currently alleviated by the fact that currently most miners run `zcashd`.

## Affected Versions

Zebra 4.4.0.

## Description

Verification of transparent transactions inherits the Bitcoin Script verification code in C++. Since it is consensus-critical, this code is called from Zebra through a foreign function interface (FFI), with a Rust callback that computes the sighash for each input being verified.

ZIP-244 §S.2a marks two situations as consensus failure for V5 transparent signatures:

1. The signed hash type is not one of the six canonical values; and
2. The hash type is `SIGHASH_SINGLE` (alone or combined with `ANYONECANPAY`) and the input has no transparent output at the same index.

`zcashd` enforces both rules: its `SignatureHash` raises an exception, and `CheckSig` catches it and fails the script. A previous fix (`GHSA-cwfq-rfcr-8hmp`) added the first rule to Zebra's V5 sighash callback. The second rule, however, was not added — Zebra's callback forwarded the request to `librustzcash`'s ZIP-244 implementation, which handles an out-of-range `SIGHASH_SINGLE` output index by hashing an empty output set rather than refusing to produce a digest. As a result, Zebra would compute a well-defined sighash for the missing-output case and accept any signature that verified against it.

An attacker could exploit this by:

- Constructing a V5 transaction with two or more transparent inputs and fewer transparent outputs;
- Signing an input whose index has no matching `vout` entry with `SIGHASH_SINGLE` (`0x03`) or `SIGHASH_SINGLE|ANYONECANPAY` (`0x83`), using the digest Zebra computes;
- Broadcasting the transaction, or a block containing it, to the network.

Zebra would verify the transaction's transparent script and accept the transaction (and any block containing it), while `zcashd` would reject both, splitting Zebra nodes from the rest of the network.

## Impact

**Consensus Failure**

- **Attack Vector:** Network.
- **Effect:** Network partition/consensus split.
- **Scope:** Any affected Zebra node.

## Fixed Versions

This issue is fixed in Zebra 4.4.1.

## Mitigation

Users should upgrade to Zebra 4.4.1 or later immediately.

There are no known workarounds for this issue. Immediate upgrade is the only way to ensure the node remains on the correct consensus path and is protected against malicious chain forks.

## Credits

Zebra thanks @sangsoo-osec, @zmanian, and @fivelittleducks for finding and reporting the issue.

git show 1ec1078e^:zebra-script/src/lib.rs has no corresponding-output guard; the fix adds version >= 5, SignedOutputs::Single, input_index >= outputs().len(), return None, plus 2-input/1-output regression tests including ANYONECANPAY.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Zebra's v5 transparent script verification accepted SIGHASH_SINGLE when the input index had no corresponding transaction output. The Rust sighash callback computed a digest from the empty output case, while consensus requires script verification to fail.

The callback introduced the missing-output behavior because it did not enforce the v5 SIGHASH_SINGLE index rule before hashing.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Query injection in Redis vector store filter expressions (CWE-943 improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic): RedisFilterExpressionConverter.stringValue() concatenates user-controlled filter values directly into the RediSearch TAG block @field:{VALUE} (and TEXT group) without escaping RediSearch-special characters, so a crafted filter value can alter the structure of the generated RediSearch query (TAG field query injection). Affects spring-ai-redis-store 1.0.0<1.0.5 and 1.1.0<1.1.4.
evidence: GHSA-44f4-gvwj-6qg3 / CVE-2026-22744: RedisFilterExpressionConverter inserts user-controlled string filter values into the @field:{VALUE} RediSearch TAG block without escaping; affected org.springframework.ai:spring-ai-redis-store 1.0.0<1.0.5 and 1.1.0<1.1.4; cited fix commit 707e990c9152aabb9c9226053725efa2ada72223, releases v1.0.5/v1.1.4

round6_research.bug_semantics: Information disclosure / proxy restriction bypass (CWE-345 insufficient verification of data authenticity, CWE-441) in Rack::Sendfile: variation() falls back to env['HTTP_X_SENDFILE_TYPE'] and map_accel_path() reads env['HTTP_X_ACCEL_MAPPING'], both directly from client-supplied request headers. An attacker can send 'x-sendfile-type: x-accel-redirect' plus a crafted 'x-accel-mapping' header; the middleware then emits an X-Accel-Redirect response that the nginx-style proxy follows as an internal request not subject to proxy-level access controls, bypassing protection of internal endpoints. Fixed by ignoring HTTP_X_SENDFILE_TYPE from requests, only reading HTTP_X_ACCEL_MAPPING when x-accel-redirect is explicitly configured with no app-level mappings, and using \A instead of ^ for mapping anchors.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR, CWE-639) in Spree's CanCanCan Ability class (core/app/models/spree/ability.rb): the line `can :manage, ::Spree::Address, user_id: user.id` grants guest users manage rights over ANY Address whose user_id matches. For guests, `user` is an unsaved `Spree.user_class.new` object, and `user.id` is nil; CanCanCan's hash-condition check with nil user_id does not actually constrain results, so any unauthenticated caller can read/edit other guest users' address records by manipulating the Address ID on the storefront address book endpoints (e.g. /addresses/{addressId}/edit), disclosing/altering personal data without credentials.
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-3ghg-3787-w2xr / CVE-2026-22589 (Spree <4.10.2, <5.0.7, <5.1.9, <5.2.5): 'Root Cause: Faulty authorization check in CanCanCan Ability class: - can :manage, ::Spree::Address, user_id: user.id + can :manage, ::Spree::Address, user_id: user.id if user.persisted?; the user object in Spree::Ability class for guest users is a Spree.user_class.new object.' Fix commit 4c2bd62326fba0d846fd9e4bad2c62433829b3ad (PR #13422, 2026-01-08, Damian Legawiec) adds `if user.persisted?` to the line. Introducer diff (486dc893) removed the block checks and added `can :manage, Address, user_id: user.id`; parent c3fdc85f retains only the block form. OSV fixed refs 62e41d24e3f0b982f632d935b19291ecc967c42c etc. are version-bump commits for the 4.10.2/5.x.y releases. Advisory data also carried in rubysec/ruby-advisory-db (entry added 2026-01-09 in 81853a77), which is only the data carrier, not the affected code.
round6_research.flaw_origin: The vulnerable hash-condition form `can :manage, Address, user_id: user.id` (later namespaced ::Spree::Address) was introduced by 486dc8939b79ba670f0e29f990e3a59588b6a80d (2020-12-21, Damian Legawiec, 'Use simple SQL for Addresses permissions'), which replaced the previously guest-safe block conditions (`can :manage, Spree::Address do |address| address.user == user end` + `can :create, Spree::Address do |_address| user.id.present? end`, added 2019-05-29 in 7b0a928a). The guest user semantics (user ||= Spree.user_class.new, unpersisted) existed since the Ability class's original design, so the 2020 rewrite is the first writer of the exploitable check.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Arbitrary file upload (CWE-434, CWE-602; CVSS 8.9 High) in Budibase <= 3.24.0: the attachment upload endpoint uploadFile (packages/server/src/api/controllers/static/index.ts) never enforces the extension restrictions configured on the Form 'attachment' field, which are applied only client-side. Server-side validation was limited to a block-list check gated by '!env.SELF_HOSTED' (skipped entirely in self-hosted deployments) plus, from 2026-02-03, active-content (svg/html etc.) checks restricted to PUBLIC users (isPublicUser). An authenticated low-privilege 'App User' can proxy-modify the upload request (extension .svg/.html/.php/.exe, double extensions, spoofed MIME) and store arbitrary files, enabling stored XSS (SVG/HTML with script), SSRF (external URL references) and malware distribution; files are served back under /attachments/.

OSV GIT range: introduced 0, last_affected a00f2b9467b083cc6b0fa2e482695fce982e519c (= release 3.24.0, 2026-01-09). Verified in clone (budibase/budibase): uploadFile at a00f2b94 checks only '!env.SELF_HOSTED && InvalidFileExtensions.includes(extension)' (block-list in packages/shared-core/src/constants/index.ts: 7z/action/apk/app/bat/... no html/svg); at fix parent 0dc4a75e the added ACTIVE_CONTENT checks (extension set html/htm/svg/svgz/xhtml/mhtml/shtml + MIME text/html, image/svg+xml + detectActiveContent) are wrapped in 'if (isPublicUser)' and the block-list is gated 'isPublicUser || !env.SELF_HOSTED'. Fix 1ef9af20 (Peter Clement <peterclmnt@gmail.com>, 2026-05-11, 'Block active content attachment uploads', single parent 0dc4a75e) removes the isPublicUser gate so active-content checks apply to all users and extends sets (js/jse/mjs/wasm, application/javascript etc.); adds spec test 'should reject active content for builder uploads'. Introducer chain: 8cb716df created the controller with unvalidated uploadFile (function body verified at that rev; git log --diff-filter=A confirms file birth there; parent 43a2be32 has no such file -> parent_absent=true); f1aa32e4 (2023-10-27) introduced the !environment.SELF_HOSTED-gated allow-list, b4cb9796 (2023-11-21) converted to block-list, ca2f40b2/3b3305f0 (2026-02-03) added public-user-scoped active-content checks. round6_research.bug_semantics: CVE-2026-54249 / GHSA-h7p7-w5gc-xj3w (PYSEC-2026-3692/3693, published ~2026-06, reporter via GitHub): UI adapters (Vercel AI and AG-UI) reconstruct file parts from client-submitted message history and forward them to model providers. FileUrl parts were validated against a scheme allowlist (allowed_file_url_schemes), but UploadedFile references - which point at a file by provider file ID or cloud-storage URI (s3://, gs://) - were forwarded with NO validation. The provider resolves an UploadedFile with server-side identity (IAM role / service account / provider API key), so a client that crafts message history containing an attacker-chosen UploadedFile can read arbitrary objects in the server's provider/cloud account (confused deputy / broken access control, CWE-284/863). Affected 1.65.0-1.105.0 and 2.0.0b1-b5; fixed in 1.106.0/2.0.0b6 by validating/dropping UploadedFile refs on client-submitted messages the same way file URLs are validated.

Its Vercel adapter diff adds the vulnerable inbound path: FileUIPart.provider_metadata {file_id, provider_name, vendor_metadata, identifier} is load_provider_metadata()'d and reconstructed into UploadedFile(file_id=..., provider_name=...) with NO allowlist/validation, plus the outbound dump path (UploadedFile -> FileUIPart with provider_metadata) enabling round-trip. Since the model provider resolves the UploadedFile using server-side credentials, the client-submitted reference is honored with the server's IAM/service-account/API-key authority. records.details:
## Impact

The admin tables for `PaymentMethods`, `Currencies` and `Carriers` exposed inline toggles and per-record actions (enable, disable, edit, delete) that were rendered for any authenticated panel user without checking the corresponding per-action permission. A low-privilege user could:

- Disable every payment method on the store, blocking checkout.
- Disable or alter the default currency, changing displayed prices and the exchange rate basis.
- Disable carriers, breaking shipping rate computation at checkout.

The impact is a full denial of checkout and pricing integrity loss, reachable by any authenticated user.

## Patches

Fixed in `v2.8.0`. Each toggle and per-record action now requires its matching permission (`edit_payment_methods`, `edit_currencies`, `edit_carriers`).

Upgrade via:

```bash
composer require shopper/admin:^2.8
```

## Workarounds

None. Upgrade to `v2.8.0`.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Out-of-bounds read / native crash in rdiscount via signed length truncation (CVSS 3.1 5.9, AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H): Ruby String lengths larger than INT_MAX are passed unguarded from RSTRING_LEN(text) (a long) into mkd_string(char *buf, int len, ...), and the parser stores remaining input length in a signed int (`struct string_stream { const char *data; int size; }`) whose read loop (`if (!in->size) return EOF; --in->size;`) never terminates for a negative size, causing the parser to read past the end of the Ruby string buffer. Reachable via RDiscount.new(input).to_html and .toc_content; DoS on deployments parsing attacker-controlled multi-GB markdown.
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-6r34-94wq-jhrc (2026-04-06, alias CVE-2026-35201, 'rdiscount has an Out-of-bounds Read'): affected RubyGems rdiscount introduced 1.3.1.1, fixed 2.2.7.4; references commit b1a16445e92e0d12c07594dedcdc56f80b317761. Verified in clone github.com/davidfstr/rdiscount (284 commits, oldest 2008-05-29): fix b1a16445e92e0d12c07594dedcdc56f80b317761 ('w <w@mac.lan>', 2026-03-16, 'Guard against oversized markdown input before calling mkd_string', Co-authored-by: David Foster) adds rb_rdiscount__text_len() raising rb_eArgError when RSTRING_LEN(text) > INT_MAX before the mkd_string(RSTRING_PTR(text), (int)text_len, flags) calls at ext/rdiscount.c:97 and :136; its parent 921379e93a320061fbcee468a6dad3cebe718ab7 still contains the unguarded mkd_string(RSTRING_PTR(text), RSTRING_LEN(text), flags) at both sites. Blame trace of the call pattern reaches the root commit 7c232af20fff48173dd1f2e9a93cd28e9984fd7b (Ryan Tomayko <rtomayko@gmail.com>, 2008-05-29, 'initial commit of discount ruby extension at 1.2.6'): ext/discount.c:29 mkd_string(RSTRING(text)->ptr, RSTRING(text)->len, flags), ext/mkdio.c struct string_ctx {char *data; int size;} + strget 'if (!in->size) return EOF; --in->size;' and mkd_string(char *buf, int len, int flags); intermediate 110dce91817ce8f4b9e740e1a989522ab3a5ca30 (Johan Sorensen, 2009-01-31) only renamed RSTRING(text)->(ptr|len) to RSTRING_PTR/LEN without adding guards. Root commit has no parent (introducer_parent_absent true). No AI markers on any commit in the chain: all authors are human with personal/GitHub emails (rtomayko@gmail.com, johan@johansorensen.com, w@mac.lan, david@dafoster.net); no noreply@anthropic.com/claude emails, no 'Generated with Claude Code', no claude.ai links.
round6_research.flaw_origin: The unguarded truncation of Ruby string length to a signed int before the native parser is present from the repo's ROOT commit 7c232af20fff48173dd1f2e9a93cd28e9984fd7b (Ryan Tomayko, 2008-05-29, 'initial commit of discount ruby extension at 1.2.6'), which vendored the Discount C library: ext/discount.c:29 calls mkd_string(RSTRING(text)->ptr, RSTRING(text)->len, flags) and ext/mkdio.c defines struct string_ctx { char *data; int size; } with the size==0-terminated strget loop. The design flaw (int length, no upper bound checks) originates in the upstream Discount C library (David Parsons) predating RDiscount; the signed-int stream machinery and the unchecked int parameter were never reviewed/guarded in RDiscount's own history (284 commits, 2008-2026).
round6_research.reasoning: The flaw - truncating a Ruby long string length into a signed int before native parsing, with a parser read loop that only stops at size==0 - is a design property of the vendored Discount C library that shipped in RDiscount's very first commit in 2008 (pre-AI era) and persisted with no guards for 18 years. The atomic introducer is the root commit 7c232af, authored by a human (Ryan Tomayko) importing upstream C code by David Parsons; no AI signal exists anywhere in the 284-commit history or on the fix. The 2026 fix is a simple human-authored length guard. Verdict NOT_AI.

round6_research.bug_semantics: LibreChat JSON injection via iconURL in chat POST (CWE-80, PXSS / remote resource inclusion): a client-supplied iconURL parameter in the chat/conversation POST was accepted by zod conversation parsing (TConversationSchema.iconURL) and persisted on conversations/messages; when a chat is shared, viewers' browsers load the stored iconURL resource (a 'tracker' URL), leaking privacy. Fixed in v0.8.1 by stripping iconURL from client conversation input in parseCompactConvo (packages/data-provider/src/parsers.ts) and deriving it server-side only from model-spec config in api/server/middleware/buildEndpointOption.js.
round6_research.evidence: CVE-2025-66450 (GitHub_M cna, CWE-80): 'In versions 0.8.0 and below, when a user posts a question, the iconURL parameter of the POST request can be modified by an attacker. The malicious code is then stored in the chat which can then be shared to other users. When sharing chats with a potentially malicious tracker, resources loaded can lead to loss of privacy for users who view the chat link... fixed in version 0.8.1' (OSV GIT record, published 2025-12-11; aliases GHSA-84vx-vmcf-xgpp, which 404s in the GitHub global advisory API but is referenced by the CVE). Fix commit 6fa94d3eb8f5779363226d10dccf8b01a735744c (#10753, 2025-12-01, Danny Avila, human, no AI markers): strips iconURL in parseCompactConvo ('const { iconURL: _clientIconURL, ...conversationWithoutIconURL } = conversation') and derives iconURL from modelSpecs server-side in buildEndpointOption; advisory also lists dependency-bump 6fa94d... sibling b288d81f5a4625403bc880e93059d90d9aa51fe3 (npm audit fix) as a second fixed event. git log -S iconURL: schemas.ts first touched by 0e50c07e3 (parent has none); parsers.ts only touched by the fix itself (pre-fix leak went through generic schema.parse); messages.js iconURL persistence later (88f4ad7c4 #6903, 22642df40 #14631). 0e50c07e3 is a GitHub squash of PR #2578 (~100 sub-commits, no Co-authored-by trailer), author Danny Avila <danny@librechat.ai>, committer GitHub <noreply@github.com> (squash button, not an AI marker), no claude.ai/codex/xAI links, no [AI] prefixes - nothing in cve-analyzer source_policy.py marker list matches. commit ca8c212c0 (#13125, later hardening of the same code) is post-advisory and irrelevant. SHA256 scheme re-verified: h(['CVE-2025-66450']) == alias-651866dfc9be71ed691ad264 (24-hex truncation; the previously used 28-hex truncation was wrong, all class ids are 24 hex).

round6_research.bug_semantics: Credential disclosure via HTTP redirect: UploadKerberosHub (machinery/src/cloud/kerberos_hub.go, was KerberosHub.go) sends the Hub credentials as custom headers X-Kerberos-Hub-PrivateKey / X-Kerberos-Hub-PublicKey (plus X-Kerberos-Hub-Region etc.) on requests to config.HubURI+paths, using a bare &http.Client{} with no CheckRedirect policy. net/http follows cross-host redirects automatically and only strips the standard sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie, WWW-Authenticate) on host change; custom-named headers are forwarded verbatim, so if the configured HubURI redirects (e.g. compromised/malicious endpoint or misconfigured URL), the private Hub key is disclosed to the redirect target host. Fix 51f1a52 strips the two credential headers whenever the redirect target host differs from the original request host.
round6_research.evidence: Advisory: GHSA-h5gx-45rj-2h5j (published 2026-07-02, repository_identity github.com/kerberos-io/agent, fix_sha 51f1a52e170f21c1264c6de1dc781d5b5e2a5d09 from cohort-v1/advisory-candidates-heldout-20260731-v1/public_fix_references.jsonl); alias manifest class alias-e41b15bd0d784d4258557e70 confirms members [CVE-2026-50192, GHSA-h5gx-45rj-2h5j, GO-2026-5890] with analysis_subject CVE-2026-50192. Introducer abeeb9520471f11eba59ea9e10c0e98b7ada4e0b (2023-06-23, author/committer Cedric Verstraeten <cedric@verstraeten.io>, single parent 6aed20c466784368a7374e8773fba1111deb2043, not a squash merge) added machinery/src/cloud/KerberosHub.go (125 lines) containing UploadKerberosHub: req.Header.Set('X-Kerberos-Hub-PublicKey', config.HubKey), req.Header.Set('X-Kerberos-Hub-PrivateKey', config.HubPrivateKey), client := &http.Client{} for both HEAD and POST. Parent-absence verified: parent tree (ls-tree) has no KerberosHub.go (only Cloud.go, Dropbox.go, KerberosVault.go, S3.go, TestFile.go) and git log -S 'X-Kerberos-Hub-PrivateKey' --reverse first occurrence is abeeb95; file later renamed KerberosHub.go -> kerberos_hub.go (b5f5567). Author/committer identical human dev (repo founder), message 'make region editable through ENV + add new upload function to upload to Kerberos Hub', no trailers, no Co-Authored-By, no AI-tool markers on introducer or on fix commit (tonghuaroot, Signed-off-by only).
round6_research.flaw_origin: Introducer abeeb95 created UploadKerberosHub in one commit: HEAD+POST requests carry X-Kerberos-Hub-PublicKey/X-Kerberos-Hub-PrivateKey set from config.HubKey/config.HubPrivateKey and are sent via client := &http.Client{} (no CheckRedirect), so the full vulnerable combination (custom credential headers + default redirect-following client) existed from the first write of the function.

Due to an error in sed command parsing, it was possible to bypass the Claude Code read-only validation and write to arbitrary files on the host system.

Users on standard Claude Code auto-update will have received this fix automatically. Users performing manual updates are advised to update to the latest version.

Thank you to Adam Chester - SpecterOps for reporting this issue!

round6_research.bug_semantics: OpenClaw stale policy enforcement for queued node actions (Fixes < 2026.3.22, CVE-2026-35648, GHSA-wj55-88gf-x564): the gateway queues foreground node commands that fail with NODE_BACKGROUND_UNAVAILABLE (on iOS nodes) as PendingNodeAction entries holding command + paramsJSON + idempotencyKey, then hands them to the node on the next wake/pull (invokeWake) via listPendingNodeActions without re-validating the queued command against the CURRENT command allowlist (resolveNodeCommandAllowlist + declared commands from the node's connect params). Policy is checked only at enqueue/direct-invoke time (isNodeCommandAllowed in node.invoke), so when an operator tightens the allowlist or a node's declared command set between enqueue and delivery, previously-approved-but-now-forbidden queued commands are still delivered to the node and executed. Fix (ec2c6d83b9f5f91d6d9094842e0f19b88e63e3e2, PR #46815) adds resolveAllowedPendingNodeActions which re-runs isNodeCommandAllowed against the current allowlist + declaredCommands at delivery time and drops/clears disallowed entries before responding.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Path traversal / arbitrary file read in nltk.data.load via URL-encoded path separators and traversal segments in nltk: resource URLs. The unsafe-path regex (_UNSAFE_NO_PROTOCOL_RE) is applied only to the raw (encoded) resource string, then url2pathname() percent-decodes it when resolving to a filesystem path, a decode-after-check (TOCTOU-style) flaw. Payloads like nltk:%2fetc%2fpasswd or corpora/..%2f..%2fetc/passwd pass the filter and decode to a real absolute/traversal path allowing arbitrary local file reads. Fixed in 3.10.0-rc1 / 3.10.0.
evidence: Atomic introducer 51ceb7517 (Steven Xu, 2014-07-12, native git commit no trailers) added url2pathname() percent-decoding to the resource-resolution path in nltk/data.py find(): changed p=os.path.join(path_, resource_name) to p=os.path.join(path_, url2pathname(resource_name)) at data.py ~582 and the same for zipfile. Parent e8c09039f joined path_ with the raw resource_name (no decode), verified via git show parent:nltk/data.py showing os.path.join(path_, resource_name) with no url2pathname. This created the decode-after-check TOCTOU: encoded traversal %2f..%2f passes any raw-form filter and is later decoded to a filesystem path.

The incomplete raw-form-only check (_UNSAFE_NO_PROTOCOL_RE/_reject_unsafe_no_protocol) was later layered on in 4f9ecd278 (hyperps, 2025-11-20, human) but added checks on the encoded form only; this hardening did not introduce the exploitability (parent 51e0480a8 had no check and no nltk/pathsec.py at all, yet encoded traversal was already reachable via the url2pathname decode). decode-after-check is therefore a property introduced by 51ceb7517, not by the later hardening.

Direct fix 7df10e6ef (Ziyu Lin / LinZiyuu, 2026-06-06, PR #3575) adds urllib.parse.unquote decode + re-application of the safety checks in normalize_resource_url() and find(), centralising into _assert_no_encoded_bypass; parent 4a820afa5 remains vulnerable. Fix parent 4a820afa5 verified.

Introducer 51ceb7517 has no AI markers (author/committer Steven Xu, no trailers, 2014 pre-AI). The fix 7df10e6ef adds a 'Co-authored-by: Copilot Autofix powered by AI' trailer and an AI description, but this AI marker is on the remediation only and does not indicate AI authorship of the vulnerable introduce.

Advisory PYSEC-2026-2078 / GHSA-p4gq-832x-fm9v / CVE-2026-54293 ranges introduced 0, fixed 3.10.0-rc1/3.10.0, consistent with a long-standing (introduced 0) flaw first made exploitable by the 2014 decode commit.

round6_research.bug_semantics: CVE-2026-31975 / GHSA-gv8f-wpm2-m5wr (@siteboon/claude-code-ui <1.25.0, CWE-78 primary + CWE-1188/CWE-287, CVSS 4.0 8.7): Unauthenticated RCE via WebSocket shell injection. The server's WebSocket /shell handler builds a shell command by string-interpolating client-supplied message fields and runs it via node-pty: shellCommand = `cd "${projectPath}" && ${command}` (plus provider branches interpolating sessionId/initialCommand), spawned as pty.spawn('bash', ['-c', shellCommand], { cwd: os.homedir() }). projectPath, sessionId and initialCommand come from the untrusted WS 'init' message with no validation (sessionId interpolated into e.g. `claude --resume ${sessionId} || claude`, and --resume argument not even quoted in the claude branch). Auth is bypassable: JWT secret defaults to the hardcoded string 'claude-ui-dev-secret-change-in-production' committed in server/middleware/auth.js (CWE-1188/287), and in IS_PLATFORM mode authenticateWebSocket(null) auto-returns the first DB user, so any client can forge/omit the token; the shell endpoint then yields arbitrary command execution on the host (full RCE). Fix 12e7f074 (merge of fork PR, v1.25.0): validate projectPath (path.resolve + existence) and sessionId (safe pattern), move project path out of the shell string into pty cwd, replace hardcoded JWT with per-installation auto-generated secret (app_config table) with 7d expiry, and add DB-backed WS auth validation.
round6_research.evidence: Identity: cases-pD.jsonl advisory_ids [CVE-2026-31975, GHSA-gv8f-wpm2-m5wr] hashes exactly to alias-6c5ddf890b3d1b049ab2eef5 (verified sha256). OSV: GHSA-gv8f-wpm2-m5wr = CVE-2026-31975 (mutual aliases), CWE-78 (+CWE-1188, CWE-287 in GHSA), CVSS 4.0 8.7, package @siteboon/claude-code-ui, fixed 1.25.0; CVE affected ranges list two fixed commits: 8af72570 (chore(release): v1.25.0 tag commit) and 12e7f074 ('Merge commit from fork', Simos Mikelatos, 2026-03-10). round6_research.bug_semantics: Sandbox escape in smolagents LocalPythonExecutor (local_python_executor.py) via dunder method calls (CWE-78/CWE-94, CVSS 3.1 6.4 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:H/A:L, JFSA-2025-001434277, requires prompt injection). evaluate_call's ast.Attribute branch resolves a called method with raw `getattr(obj, func_name)` without any dunder-name check, unlike evaluate_attribute (raises on __x__ attribute access) and unlike the getattr builtin (remapped to nodunder_getattr). Payload: `func.__getattribute__('__class__')` -> `type.__getattribute__(function_class,'__bases__')[0].__subclasses__()` -> subprocess.Popen -> arbitrary command execution in the sandboxed 'local' Python environment.
round6_research.evidence: Identity exact: OSV CVE-2025-9959 maps to huggingface/smolagents GIT range fixed at 420eaebf2b7ebc1461b5b669f8af1bef1b9bd00e (that SHA is only the v1.21.0 release-bump commit; the real code fix is 6a42a87755d73c68f629eba946002de7ddca5078, PR #1551, 2025-08-04, Natann <142202920+nnfrog@users.noreply.github.com>, 'Enhance local Python executor security by blocking dunder calls', Co-authored-by: Albert Villanova del Moral). Fix adds ALLOWED_DUNDER_METHODS=['__init__','__str__','__repr__'] and, in evaluate_call's callable fallback, raises 'Forbidden call to dunder function' for func.__name__ starting+ending with '__' unless in static_tools or the allowlist; its tests parametrize the exact escape (`'string'.__dir__()`, `func.__getattribute__('__class__')` -> `type.__getattribute__(...,'__bases__')[0]` -> `__subclasses__()` -> subprocess.Popen). git blame at fix parent attributes lines 780-783 (Attribute-branch resolution `func = getattr(obj, func_name)`) to f3dcf1f, and git log -L 780,783:... shows f3dcf1f as sole writer (file creation in the repo-restructure commit; --diff-filter=A across all refs finds no other creation). Pre-fix tree confirmed dunder guards exist only in evaluate_attribute (line 341) and nodunder_getattr remap, not in the call branch. AI-marker scan (copilot|claude|chatgpt|gpt-|codex|aider|co-authored|generated|gemini|llm) on introducer f3dcf1f and fix 6a42a877: 0 hits; the fix's 'Co-authored-by: Albert Villanova del Moral' is GitHub's standard human co-author trailer for a merged contributor PR. Repo history is the linear HF smolagents mainline (original repo restructured Dec 2024; no pre-existing interpreter file).
round6_research.flaw_origin: First writer: f3dcf1f01307120c922666a5075e33d7728ff3a7 'Initialize repo structure.' (2024-12-06, Aymeric Roucher <aymeric.roucher@gmail.com>) creates agents/python_interpreter.py (later renamed src/smolagents/local_python_executor.py) including evaluate_call's `elif isinstance(call.func, ast.Attribute): ... func = getattr(obj, func_name)` branch with no dunder guard. git log -L across the full history of those lines shows only f3dcf1f ever writing them. Immediate parent dfd9609c26ccadfb6165576bf285054e738e2a95 'Initial commit' (2024-12-05) contains only LICENSE, no interpreter file -> parent_absent=true. Subsequent dunder-attribute hardening (ba7baee09c8591631b48499a108e369df2c2423d '#979 Forbid access to all dunder attributes by default' 2025-03-14; 808eab650964dcdabd94203d62f4822f7b3f84bd 'Disable dunder attribute through getattr' 2025-04-11; 33a942e62b6fbf6a35d41f1c735bda2d64c163d0 '#1375 Prevent submodules through indirect attribute access' 2025-05-26; 277b742 '#1180 star-pattern import authorization') patched only the attribute/getattr side; git log --all -S 'Forbidden call to dunder' returns only the fix commit, i.e. no earlier dunder-call check was ever regressed - the call-path gap existed since the file's creation.

round6_research.bug_semantics: SSRF: outbound webhook destination policy bypass. validate_webhook_url (alerts/service_backends/webhook_security.py) parsed webhook URLs with urllib.parse.urlparse while the actual request was sent with requests.post (requests/urllib3 stack); for malformed URLs containing backslashes and @ the two parsers disagree on where the authority ends / which hostname is the real target, so a URL that passes the allow/deny checks can connect to a different host (loopback/private/non-allowlisted). Introduced together with the webhook destination policy feature.
round6_research.evidence: OSV CVE-2026-44502/GHSA-fp53-qcf8-2xx2 (PYSEC-2026-2405): GIT range introduced '0' fixed 940d2df6 (2.1.3). Repo cloned to .ai-slop/state/repos/bugsink_bugsink. Alias hash verified = pair {CVE-2026-44502, GHSA-fp53-qcf8-2xx2} via pool advisory-repos-since-2025-05.json. 940d2df6 is merge (parents 06bd3d4 9ade871) 'Fix parsing misalignment'; real fix commits 0c12a53 'Harden webhook URL validation parsing' (re-parses via requests.Request(...).prepare().url + urllib3.util.parse_url, strips bracket IP literals; parent 06bd3d4) and fc4b576 'Reject non-RFC characters in webhook URLs' (parent 0c12a53), both 2026-04-30. Vulnerable file alerts/service_backends/webhook_security.py created by 5c8e709 'Enforce webhook destination policy with DNS/IP/CIDR validation' (2026-03-07, Klaas van Schelven; parent 8719ddd; file absent in parent confirmed via git cat-file -e rc!=0). Before 5c8e709 there was no outbound destination validation at all (no allowlist in parent tree), so the bypassable validation first appears in 5c8e709. First writer of the vulnerable validation is the commit that created webhook_security.py and safe_post.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Privilege escalation via API abuse of the global user invite/onboarding flow (CWE-269): the POST /api/global/users/onboard endpoint (controller onboardUsers) sits in the builderOrAdminRoutes group, and the workspaceBuilderOrAdmin middleware's hasBuilderPermissions() is satisfied by creators (shared-core hasBuilderPermissions returns user.builder?.global || hasAppBuilderPermissions || hasCreatorPermissions). A Creator-level user - who has no UI permission to invite users - can therefore POST an InviteUsersRequest array with userInfo.admin.global=true, userInfo.builder.global=true, and arbitrary userGroups; the invite payload (including smuggled admin/builder/group fields) is forwarded verbatim to the invite cache, and on acceptance inviteAccept() materializes the invited user as a global admin assigned to any group, enabling full workspace/organization takeover.
round6_research.evidence: OSV CVE-2026-25040 / GHSA-4wfw-r86x-qxrm: 'In versions up to and including 3.26.3, a Creator-level user ... can manipulate API requests to invite new users with any role, including Admin, Creator, or App Viewer, and assign them to any group.' GIT range events: introduced '0', last_affected c5c46d3562dfe6d5e368e36ee016114c563c6bcc; no fixed event. POC (user-attachments/files/22066135) shows a Creator POSTing to /api/global/users/multi/invite with body [{"email":...,"userInfo":{"admin":{"global":true},"builder":{"global":true},"userGroups":["gr_..."]}}] and receiving 200 OK with the user pending in Owner UI. At 3.26.3 (c5c46d35) the single/multi invite routes are under adminRoutes, but POST /api/global/users/onboard is under builderOrAdminRoutes (standard.ts: builderOrAdminRoutes = endpointGroupList.group(auth.workspaceBuilderOrAdmin)) and workspaceBuilderOrAdmin grants creators because hasBuilderPermissions = builder?.global || hasAppBuilderPermissions || hasCreatorPermissions (shared-core/src/sdk/documents/users.ts). onboardUsers() with isEmailConfigured() delegates to inviteMultiple() then userSdk.invite(), which stores userInfo verbatim into the invite cache (worker/src/sdk/users/users.ts); inviteAccept() later reads info.admin.global / info.builder / info.userGroups to build the user. Route permission change from adminOnly to builderOrAdmin happened in introducer 61ed62e6c4 (git show diff: /api/global/users/invite '-auth.adminOnly' '+auth.builderOrAdmin'; multi/invite same; +POST /api/global/users/onboard auth.builderOrAdmin). round6_research.bug_semantics: Auth bypass / signature-wrapping (CWE-347): ruby-saml validates Digest over Nokogiri/libxml2 canonicalization output with no validity check; on invalid XML input libxml2 canonicalization can silently return an empty string, so digest and signature are computed/compared over the empty canonical form, letting a crafted response pass Digest/Signature validation.
round6_research.evidence: Introducer 5e7f13e1757217a2ed3a5e87bda46481eaf872a7 (Stephen Touset <stephen@touset.org>, 2012-10-11 12:40:57 -0700) rewrote lib/xml_security.rb digest check: `hashed_element = document.at_xpath(...)`; `canon_hashed_element = hashed_element.canonicalize(canon_algorithm, inclusive_namespaces).gsub(...)`; `hash = digest_algorithm.digest(canon_hashed_element)` - no check that canonicalize returned a valid node; parent 2d3d46c02d2523fa84cf6258a1938635fcfe721f used `canoner.canonicalize` (XML::Util::XmlCanonicalizer external gem, lib/xml_security.rb lines 80-82), so the libxml2 path is absent at the parent. The behavior survived decaffeination-free through v1.12.4 (v1.12.4 lib/xml_security.rb:344-376). Fix: security PR #750 'security_fix_1.18.0' released as v1.18.0: e9c1cdbd0f9afa467b585de279db0cbd0fb8ae97 (Sixto Martin <sixto.martin.garcia@workato.com>, 2025-03-12, 'Fix vulnerabilities: CVE-2025-25291, CVE-2025-25292: SAML authentication bypass via Signature Wrapping attack allowed due parser differential') added XMLSecurity::BaseDocument.safe_load_xml with strict Nokogiri parsing and malformed-doc rejection (xml.errors non-empty raises) into cache_referenced_xml used by validate_signature, so canonicalization no longer runs on invalid XML and cannot yield the empty form; advisory-referenced commit acac9e9cc0b9a507882c614f25d41f8b47be349a is the sibling CVE-2025-25293 DOS fix from the same PR (references in GHSA-x4h9-gwv3-r4m4 are misattributed to that commit).
round6_research.flaw_origin: Digest/signature verification over Nokogiri canonicalize() output without empty-result or malformed-input checks first written 2012-10-11 in 5e7f13e 'Add support for canonicalization-algorithm detection' (Stephen Touset), which replaced the external XmlCanonicalizer gem with Nokogiri's libxml2 c14n for the hashed element and SignedInfo; the libxml2-empty-canonicalization failure mode the advisory describes is a property of exactly that switch. (A behavioral ancestor computing digests over canonicalized output with no empty check existed since 2011 via XmlCanonicalizer, 25d3d32, but libxml2 was not involved.) The pattern persisted unchanged through v1.12.4 (v1.12.4:lib/xml_security.rb:376 canon_hashed_element = hashed_element.canonicalize(...)) until the 1.18.0 security work.
round6_research.reasoning: The libxml2/Nokogiri canonicalization path whose silent empty-string result enabled the digest/signature bypass was first written 2012-10-11 by human author Stephen Touset (then onelogin/Zendesk ruby-saml maintainer) with no AI markers (pre-AI era, empty body, no trailers); the fix commits e9c1cdbd and acac9e9cc by Sixto Martin (Workato, 2025-03-12) likewise carry no co-author/AI trailers and predate any AI-assisted security commit here. Closed causal chain; no AI involvement in introducer or fix.

records.details:
Due to an overly broad allowlist of safe commands, it was possible to bypass the Claude Code confirmation prompts to read a file and then send file contents over the network without user confirmation. Reliably exploiting this requires the ability to add untrusted content into a Claude Code context window.

Users on standard Claude Code auto-update received this fix automatically after release. Current users of Claude Code are unaffected, as versions prior to 1.0.24 are deprecated and have been forced to update.

Thank you to https://hackerone.com/wunderwuzzi23 for reporting this issue!

round6_research.bug_semantics: Path traversal in Mako's TemplateLookup.get_template(): a URI starting with '//' (e.g. //../../../../etc/passwd) bypasses the directory-traversal check. root cause: inconsistency between two slash-stripping implementations - Template.__init__ strips ONE leading '/' with if/slice (self.uri[1:]), while TemplateLookup.get_template() strips ALL leading '/' via re.sub(r'^/+', ''). After get_template strips all slashes the path resolves to a file outside the template root via posixpath.join, and Template.__init__'s normpath+startswith('..') check is bypassed because only one '/' was stripped. Allows arbitrary file read when app passes untrusted input to get_template(). Fixed in 1.3.11.
round6_research.evidence: class_id hash verified: sha256('CVE-2026-41205\nGHSA-v92g-xgxw-vvmm\n')[:24]==743a4af32ce20e764942e208 (pair brute-forced from cohort-v1 bucket sqlalchemy/mako, 8 advisory ids; census class-repo-precise maps to github.com/sqlalchemy/mako). GHSA-v92g-xgxw-vvmm: path traversal via double-slash URI prefix in TemplateLookup; ECOSYSTEM introduced 0, fixed 1.3.11; GIT fix pointers e05ac619 (real fix) and 217822b5 (1.3.11 release bump). Fix e05ac61989a7fb9dd7dcde6cfd72dc48328719a3 (2026-04-14, Mike Bayer, Fixes #434) changes u_norm = self.uri[1:] (one-slash strip) to self.uri.lstrip('/') in mako/template.py. Introducer 5cd508ffe0d7eaadd6516fc35137c93d1d6577a9 (2011-09-27, Mike Bayer, ticket:174) added the one-slash-strip normpath traversal check; parent 0e42388ff8825bd7ea356d4b963a4b33ce9d6e22 had no such check (git show parent template.py shows only module-directory path normalization, no u_norm/traversal block). get_template()'s all-slash strip (re.sub(r'^/+', '')) predates it (mako/lookup.py, moved to package c. 2010). AI-marker grep count 0 on both introducer and fix messages.
round6_research.flaw_origin: The one-slash-strip traversal check in Template.__init__ was first written 2011-09-27 by Mike Bayer in 5cd508ffe0d7eaadd6516fc35137c93d1d6577a9 (ticket:174, 'A Template is explicitly disallowed from having a url that normalizes to relative outside of the root'). The commit added the u_norm = self.uri; if u_norm.startswith('/'): u_norm = u_norm[1:]; os.path.normpath + startswith('..') check; parent 0e42388ff8825bd7ea356d4b963a4b33ce9d6e22 had no such check (pre-existing module-directory path used its own single-slash strip). The inconsistency is that TemplateLookup.get_template() (mako/lookup.py) already stripped ALL leading slashes (re.sub, present since the pre-1.0 package move c. 2010), so the 2011 one-slash-strip protection is bypassable with a '//' prefix. Fix e05ac61989a7fb9dd7dcde6cfd72dc48328719a3 (2026-04-14, Mike Bayer, 'Fix path traversal via double-slash URI prefix in TemplateLookup', Fixes #434) changes the one-slash strip to self.uri.lstrip('/'), making both paths strip all slashes consistently; 217822b5 is the 1.3.11 release commit. No squash decomposition needed.
round6_research.reasoning: The incomplete traversal protection was written in 2011 by human maintainer Mike Bayer when adding the 'cannot be relative outside of the root' check (ticket:174) - it used an inconsistent one-slash strip that diverged from the older get_template all-slash strip, creating the double-slash bypass. The 2026 fix is also by human maintainer Mike Bayer with no AI markers. The flaw is a hand-written security-check inconsistency in a pre-AI-era library; no evidence of AI authorship at introducer or fix, verdict NOT_AI.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Cross-domain token exposure: when a pull/registry request receives 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header, server/auth.getAuthorizationToken sends the user's signed auth token request to the realm URL parsed from that header without validating the realm host against the original request host. A malicious model server (e.g. /api/pull from an attacker-controlled HTTPS host) can set realm=https://registry.ollama.ai/v2/token and capture valid registry authentication tokens, bypassing access controls.
round6_research.evidence: OSV CVE-2025-51471 (aliases GHSA-x9hg-5q6g-q3jr, GO-2025-3824; href PR #10750 and gecko.security writeup). GIT range in OSV is degenerate (introduced==last_affected a7835c671615d71280ca7dba7264bd05a4f90915, which is actually an unrelated gguf-padding commit) — ignored. PR #10750 (geckosecurity, proposed fix) was closed unmerged; real fix 7601f0e93e53858f09136a7e4ccf674a9b4580bd 'server: reject unexpected auth hosts (#13738)' (2026-01-16, Bruce MacDonald) adds 'if redirectURL.Host != originalHost' validation in getAuthorizationToken (server/auth.go:59-61) and threads originalHost through call sites (images.go, upload.go); semver fixed after 0.9.6. git blame at fix parent shows realm parse (parseRegistryChallenge, images.go:1030-1036) and token request written by be989d89; parent bea683e3 has no WWW-Authenticate/realm auth handling in server/ (grep: no matches).

round6_research.flaw_origin: First writer of the vulnerable behavior: commit 8a9b896721f479d7babc4bb5920536e8124a1797 '[BUGFIX] Change requests to write to Header to ensure StaticFileCache is working' (2021-11-01, Tim <tim@fruit-lab.de>, single parent d906b21078acf58c55f506de4b16ea050e827e10, no trailers, Resolves #837) which switched BOTH sides of the crawl metadata channel in one commit: GuzzleExecutionStrategy.fetchUrlContents changed 'return unserialize($contents)' with $contents from $response->getBody()->getContents() to 'return unserialize($response->getHeaderLine("X-T3Crawler-Meta"))', and CrawlerInitialization middleware changed from writing serialized crawl data into the response BODY ($response->getBody()->write(serialize(...))) to $response->withHeader('X-T3Crawler-Meta', serialize(...)). records.details:
Due to a path validation flaw using prefix matching instead of canonical path comparison, it was possible to bypass directory restrictions and access files outside the CWD. Successful exploitation depends on the presence of (or ability to create) a directory with the same prefix as the CWD and the ability to add untrusted content into a Claude Code context window.

Users on standard Claude Code auto-update received this fix automatically after release. Current users of Claude Code are unaffected, as versions prior to 1.0.24 are deprecated and have been forced to update.

Thank you to Elad Beber (Cymulate) for reporting this issue!

round6_research.bug_semantics: Insecure Direct Object Reference (CWE-639) in get_execution_details: GET /executions/{execution_id} returns execution records (task inputs, outputs, metadata, temporal task tokens) with no developer/tenant ownership check. Router has no x_developer_id dependency (sibling routes like get_task_details require Depends(get_developer_id)); the query filters only WHERE execution_id = $1.
round6_research.evidence: Alias verified: sha256('CVE-2026-67348\nGHSA-42mr-mcg5-367r\n') -> 7621e50cf056eb0ede65e97f. GHSA-42mr-mcg5-367r (NVD CVE-2026-67348, published 2026-07-30, HIGH, IDOR via /executions/{execution_id}, issue julep-ai/julep#1615). Introducer commit 639e80ec 'feat(agents-api): cozo queries for tasks (#352)' (2024-06-06, Diwank Singh Tomer) added @router.get('/tasks/{task_id}/executions/{execution_id}') handler get_execution(task_id, execution_id) with no x_developer_id, calling get_execution_query(task_id, execution_id); parent 170c301b has no execution-details route (only create/status-with-developer-id/transitions-with-developer-id routes). Later relaxation: e270602f (2024-08-03) rewrote model to get_execution(*, execution_id) adding comment 'Executions are allowed direct GET access if they have execution_id'; 0f6e0612 (2024-08-13) refactor created the bare GET /executions/{execution_id} get_execution_details router. Last pg-based query (1bed444f^) still WHERE execution_id = $1 with no developer filter. Endpoint deleted by 3.0 rewrite 'cleanup repo' 1bed444f (2025-06-19, anasalatasiuni). No security patch commit exists; VulnCheck's referenced commit 5371a620 is a docs merge PR #1533 (2026-03-13), not a fix. round6_research.bug_semantics: Path traversal (CWE-22) in the ishayoyo/excel-mcp MCP server (versions up to 1.0.2): the read_file and write_file tools take caller-supplied filePath/outputPath and resolve them with path.resolve(filePath) with no workspace containment, then read (fs.readFile) or write (fs.writeFile) that path; '../' sequences and absolute paths escape the working directory, giving arbitrary file read/write on the host (limited by process privileges; extension-gated to .csv/.xlsx/.xls). Exploitable by any MCP client (or over the network if the server is exposed via SSE/HTTP). Disclosure via GitHub issue #6 (June 2026), with report of in-the-wild exploitation.
round6_research.evidence: Advisory identity: cases file gives CVE-2026-10278 + GHSA-vgmg-2m2p-qqqj (OSV records empty for both ids; NVD/GitHub advisory confirm path traversal in unknown function of src/index.ts affecting read_file/write_file via filePath/outputPath, versions 1.0.0-1.0.2, disclosure via issue #6). Introducer: single root commit (git rev-list --all --max-parents=0 => 1), b33ded8e (2025-06-21, author==committer ishayoyo <ishay.almuly@gmail.com>, 0 parents => parent_absent trivial), contains readFileContent with unresigned path.resolve(filePath) + fs.access + fs.readFile (verified in intro snapshot; write_file absent in intro). Write side: 8b07c88a (same author, parent 2557ac55) adds writeFile with path.resolve(outputPath) + fs.writeFile; write_file count at parent = 0. AI markers: git log -1 --format='%B' b33ded8e | grep -icE 'gpt|copilot|claude|codex|gemini|co-auth|ai-assisted|\[ai\]' = 0 (raw 0); same for 8b07c88a = 0. Fix: 940f43961db7283eb545141efd5f8e324c481caf (2026-08-22, ishayoyo, single parent 5cdd3953ca5ea53f24219ea19fc9afff986cfc1e, 'Harden file path handling and CSV output; refresh dependencies') introduces src/utils/security.ts resolveSafePath() backing all 10 path.resolve sites with opt-in EXCEL_MCP_WORKSPACE_ROOT containment (lexical post-resolve, symlinks not followed) plus CSV formula-injection guard; released as 1.1.0 (fdf3eb08771a391262207c601bb5a7a9ee92ad29, 2026-08-22) => direct_fix_sha == fix_sha. NOTE: the fix commit body carries an explicit AI co-author trailer 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>', i.e. the FIX is AI-co-authored, but per methodology AI fix != AI introducer.
round6_research.flaw_origin: The repo root commit b33ded8e20e99086bcf5bb62c2d2b12956192553 (2025-06-21, ishayoyo <ishay.almuly@gmail.com>, 'Add initial implementation of Excel/CSV MCP server') is the first writer of the vulnerable behavior: excel-csv-mcp/src/index.ts readFileContent() does const absolutePath = path.resolve(filePath); await fs.access(absolutePath) and reads any path supplied by the tool caller, with only an extension check, no traversal/containment logic. The write side (writeFile with outputPath -> path.resolve -> fs.writeFile) was added the same day in 8b07c88a1e962107a1be8300dc41a9d4be5bac34 ('Enhance Excel-CSV MCP Server with write and export functionalities', same author; write_file absent at its parent 2557ac55f3b21538d03e2d6b9f128d43ffe7a5c3). All 10 path.resolve sites in the file tools remained uncontained until the 1.1.0 hardening.
round6_research.reasoning: The minimum atomic introducer of the vulnerable uncontained path handling is the root commit b33ded8e (2025-06-21) by project owner ishayoyo, with the write/export side added same-day by the same author in 8b07c88a; both have zero AI markers (raw 0, no trailers). round6_research.bug_semantics: CWE-347 Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature (CVSS 4.0 7.7, reviewed high): Deno node:crypto AES-128/256-GCM authentication tags are never validated; the new early-exit in Decipheriv#final() ('if (!this.#needsBlockCache || this.#cache.cache.byteLength === 0) { op_node_decipheriv_take(...); return ...; }') takes and discards the DecipherContext WITHOUT calling r#final, so the GCM tag computed by decipher.finish() is never compared with setAuthTag(); GCM degrades to CTR (integrity lost, AAD checks ineffective), tampered ciphertext or wrong keys silently accepted (PoC: decrypt of empty ciphertext with wrong key returns no error). Affects deno >=1.46.0 <2.1.7 and deno_node >=0.102.0 <0.125.0.
round6_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-2x3r-hwv5-p32x/CVE-2025-24015 fetched from api.github.com (reviewed, CWE-347, ec:deno >=1.46.0 <2.1.7 first patched 2.1.7; ec:deno_node >=0.102.0 <0.125.0 first patched 0.125.0; published 2025-06-04; credits reporter canislupaster; references name introducer commit 0d1beed2e3633d71d5e288e0382b85be361ec13d plus fixes 4f27d7cdc02e3edfb9d36275341fb8185d6e99ed and a4003a5292bd0affefad3ecb24a8732886900f67). GitHub API commit objects: 0d1beed two-line Co-Authored-By: Luca Casonato <hello@lcas.dev>, PGP-verified, single parent 2f6da40bd609ebda8f30d748427d325d80e58274. denoland_deno clone archaeology (NUMA-pinned, blobless): git log --reverse -S 'op_node_decipheriv_take' -- ext/node/ yields exactly two commits: 0d1beed (2024-08-08, Divy Srivastava <dj.srivastava23@gmail.com>) as the add and 4f27d7cd (2025-01-20, Divy Srivastava, 'fix(ext/node): GCM auth tag check on DechiperIv#final (#27733)') as the remove; git grep 'op_node_decipheriv_take' at parent 2f6da40b -- ext/node/ → RC=1 (absent); pre-introducer Decipheriv#final() at parent executes op_node_decipheriv_final unconditionally (GCM branch computes decipher.finish() tag and compares with auth_tag, throwing 'Failed to authenticate data' on mismatch). Fix 4f27d7cd (parent e4a16e91fa3e3753547919332a61dba221403725) deletes op_node_decipheriv_take, moves the early-return AFTER op_node_decipheriv_final, and adds cipher.rs guard 'if input.is_empty() && !matches!(self, Aes128Gcm(_) | Aes256Gcm(_)) { return Ok(()); }' so GCM empty-input finals still run the tag check; adds assertThrows regression test. a4003a52 is the identical cherry-pick to the 2.1.x branch (committer crowlkats, 2025-01-21) that shipped in 2.1.7. Neither introducer nor fixes carry any AI co-author/agent trailers (no Amp, Copilot, agent bots).
round6_research.flaw_origin: commit 0d1beed2e3633d71d5e288e0382b85be361ec13d (PR #24940 'fix(ext/node): add CipherIv.setAutoPadding()', 2024-08-08, Divy Srivastava) refactored Decipheriv#final() in ext/node/polyfills/internal/crypto/cipher.ts: in order to support autoPadding it hoisted the empty-input/stream-mode early return BEFORE op_node_decipheriv_final and added op_node_decipheriv_take (ext/node/ops/crypto/mod.rs + cipher.rs + lib.rs) that discards the context without tag verification; for GCM (needsBlockCache=false) every final() with empty leftover thus skipped the auth-tag check that the pre-existing code always performed
round6_research.reasoning: The advisory itself names the introducer commit, and -S archaeology confirms 0d1beed2e is the sole first writer of the tag-skipping short-circuit (single-parent feature commit, parent clean of the vulnerable op). The pre-existing code path always verified the GCM tag at final(); the new op_node_decipheriv_take early-exit removed that verification for GCM/stream-mode and empty-input finals in the same commit that added setAutoPadding support. Author Divy Srivastava (Deno core maintainer, littledivy) with human co-author Luca Casonato; no AI markers on flawed lines or on the human-authored fix; flaw predates the AI-assisted era of the project. Closed causal chain: AI not implicated.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Two command-injection flaws in the stata-mcp Stata automation tools. (A, CVE-2026-31040/GHSA-jpcj-7wfg-mqxv, fixed v1.13.0): the stata_do tool executes user/LLM-supplied Stata do-files with no content validation; Stata's shell-escape directives ('!cmd' on a new line, 'shell cmd') run OS commands, enabling command execution through crafted do-file content. (B, GHSA-4p62-hqp5-g644, fixed v1.17.3): the log_file_name parameter of stata_do was interpolated unvalidated into a Stata command string f'log using "{log_file}", replace ...' where log_file = log_file_path / f'{log_name}.log'; crafted input with quotes/newlines/command separators causes command injection inside Stata (CWE-78).

Marker scans (0 hits) on 8d21a24, 0b5dbfd, 52413ce, e6f9459. Repo cloned as sepinetam_mcp-for-stata (pre-rename name SepineTam/mcp-for-stata).

round6_research.bug_semantics: CWE-340 predictable identifier leading to GCS bucket squatting (CVSS 4.0 score 7.7, high): Vertex AI Experiments save_model (google/cloud/aiplatform/metadata/_models.py) auto-generates the staging bucket name as project + '-vertex-staging-' + location whenever no uri or staging_bucket is configured, then creates the bucket if it does not exist. round6_research.bug_semantics: macOS policy-bypass (CWE-863): ClearanceKit's opfilter Endpoint Security filter treats any process with an EMPTY Team ID but non-empty Signing ID as an Apple platform binary. An unprivileged attacker can ad-hoc sign a binary with an Apple-baseline-allowlisted signing identifier (codesign -f -s - -i 'com.apple.mds') and read any FAA-protected path, because the forged process matches platformBinary/Apple entries in the global allowlist and FAA policy rules. Advisory states the correct signal is es_process_t.is_platform_binary.
round6_research.evidence: Introducer 91a438cb (2026-03-07, Craig Bass <craig@madetech.com>) carries the explicit trailer 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>'; its diff adds appleTeamID='apple' sentinel and 'let resolvedTeamID = teamID.isEmpty ? appleTeamID : teamID' in checkFAAPolicy (lines 106-110 of Shared/FAAPolicy.swift). Parent e1d4a7c4 has only the naive 'rule.allowedTeamIDs.contains(teamID)' with no empty-ID resolution (verified via git show of parent file, grep shows no appleTeamID/resolvedTeamID), so the vulnerable behavior is absent at parent -> first writer confirmed. Subsequence propagation commits are also AI-marked: 9497550112 and b04d0a31 and 36ed307 all carry 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6'; 39258c3e is authored by copilot-swe-agent[bot]. Fix bef65348 (2026-04-12, 'Use is_platform_binary to identify Apple platform processes') replaces the heuristic with es_process_t.is_platform_binary in the ES adapter layer and an 'anchor apple' SecRequirement check for startup enumeration, removes downstream teamID.isEmpty fallbacks from FAAPolicy/JailRule, is on main (merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD verified), and corresponds to patched release v5.0.5-beta-bef6534 (tag exists; advisory patched_versions >= 5.0.5, vulnerable <= 5.0.4). Fix commit itself also carries the Claude Sonnet 4.6 co-author trailer (fix-side marker only, does not change the verdict).
round6_research.flaw_origin: Introduced 2026-03-07 in 91a438cb 'Add one-click allow from deny events; introduce apple team ID sentinel': checkFAAPolicy() resolves ANY empty team ID to the sentinel 'apple' (let resolvedTeamID = teamID.isEmpty ? appleTeamID : teamID) before matching allowedTeamIDs / allowedAncestorTeamIDs, so an ad-hoc-signed binary (empty team ID, arbitrary signing ID) satisfies rules whose team constraint is 'apple'. The flawed empty-team-ID heuristic was then propagated across the codebase: 9497550112 (2026-03-15) global allowlist with platformBinary entries matched by teamID.isEmpty; 39258c3e (2026-03-20, copilot-swe-agent[bot]) ancestry rules; b04d0a31 (2026-03-26) normalised empty+nonempty-signingID to 'apple' at every acquisition point (ProcessTree, ProcessEnumerator, ESProcessRecord, ESInboundAdapter), with follow-up 36ed307 switching platformBinary matching to teamID == 'apple'. The advisory's described flaw exists from 91a438cb onward.

round6_research.bug_semantics: SQL injection and path traversal in the extract_to_json MCP tool of src/entry.py (CWE-89 / CWE-22): the tool builds the query via f-string interpolation of the user-supplied table_name ('query = f"SELECT * FROM {table_name};"') with no identifier validation, and writes results to a user-supplied output_filename via open(output_filename, 'w') with no path sanitization, so an untrusted MCP client can inject SQL (e.g., table_name like 'x; DELETE FROM users; --') and write JSON files to arbitrary filesystem paths via traversal sequences ('../../../../tmp/evil'). CVSS 3.1 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L (no auth required, remote). Fixed in change a5580cb by validating table_name with isidentifier(), bracket-quoting the identifier in the SQL, basename()-stripping output_filename, and anchoring writes to the database directory.

Parent a82de1dd8fb3a46b9ec2b62358fbda9a6530b31e: file contains 0 occurrences of resolveByEmail (git show a82de1dd:.../identity-resolution.service.ts | grep -c resolveByEmail = 0) - vulnerable behavior absent in parent (parent_absent=true). round6_research.bug_semantics: Secrets exposure / improper masking (CWE-200 info disclosure, CVSS 4.0 AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:L 5.1): the deprecated import path 'airflow.sdk.execution_time.secrets_masker' (kept for backward compatibility with providers) redirects mask_secret() to the single-process implementation in airflow.sdk._shared.secrets_masker. That implementation only masks secrets inside the task subprocess; the supervisor process, which actually writes the task logs, never receives the masking instructions, so secrets (including values from the Airflow config file / connections / variables) appear in plain text in DAG run logs UI. The correct supervisor-aware mask_secret lives in airflow.sdk.log. Fix redirects the deprecated path's mask_secret to airflow.sdk.log.mask_secret and switches the deprecation warning class to DeprecatedImportWarning.
round6_research.evidence: OSV GHSA-j86x-fwp2-qh7v (= CVE-2025-66236, PYSEC-2026-8); summary: 'Apache Airflow: Secrets from Airflow config file logged in plain text in DAG run logs UI'; details: before 3.2.0 the security model / workload isolation was under-documented; fixed in 3.2.0; primary reference https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/58662. PR #58662 (merged as 0afe6d3, 2025-11-26, milestone 3.1.4, cherry-pick 65f7af9 to v3-1-test + 9c26db9 via #58726) titled 'Mask secrets properly when using deprecated import path': 'The deprecated import path airflow.sdk.execution_time.secrets_masker was redirecting mask_secret() to a single-process implementation that only masked secrets in the task subprocess. This caused secrets to not be masked in logs because the supervisor process (which writes logs) did not receive masking instructions... The compatibility shim now redirects mask_secret to the supervisor aware implementation in airflow.sdk.log that properly masks secrets in both the task and supervisor processes.' Diff of 0afe6d3 modifies only task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/execution_time/secrets_masker.py (+9/-1): adds 'from airflow.utils.deprecation_tools import DeprecatedImportWarning', changes warnings.warn to DeprecatedImportWarning, and in __getattr__ adds a special case: if name == 'mask_secret': from airflow.sdk.log import mask_secret; return mask_secret. partial_wave.bug_semantics: DNS cache poisoning in hickory-recursor: DnsLru stores records keyed by each record's own (name,type) and cache_response() chains ANSWER+AUTHORITY+ADDITIONAL sections into one insertion; the bailiwick filter uses the zone context of the NS pool that serviced the lookup (e.g. 'poc.'), so an AUTHORITY NS record for a sibling zone (victim.poc. NS ns.evil.poc.) passes is_subzone('poc.', 'victim.poc.') and is cached under (victim.poc., NS), hijacking future lookups in victim.poc. to the attacker's nameserver.

partial_wave.flaw_origin: crates/recursor/src/lib.rs cache_response() record-level caching design; recursor crate created by 0ef848ff 'add the recursor crate' (Benjamin Fry, 2022-02-13); DnsLru keyed-by-record insertion and NS-pool zone-context bailiwick filtering present from the start (all published recursor versions affected per advisory).
partial_wave.reasoning: Record-level cache design with zone-context bailiwick written by human (Benjamin Fry 2022); fix by human (David Cook 2025). No AI-authored commit on the flaw path. Verdict NOT_AI.
