round6_research.bug_semantics: Pickle-scan categorical miss: scanner relies on a finite hand-maintained denylist (_suspicious_globals/_unsafe_globals) keyed by exact module name; a GLOBAL import of idlelib.calltip.Calltip.fetch_tip (RCE-capable via eval chain) matches no denylist entry, is not flagged as an issue, and the loader reports the pickle safe.
round6_research.evidence: CVE-2025-71361 / GHSA-8r4j-24qv-fmq9 (PyPI picklescan, fixed in 0.0.29). Fix aecd11be (2025-08-26, Matthieu Maitre, 'Missing detection when calling Python functions', single parent 7f994d62) adds 'idlelib.calltip': {'Calltip.fetch_tip', 'get_entity'} (plus trace/profile/code/lib2to3/idlelib entries) to the _unsafe_globals denylist in src/picklescan/scanner.py and adds 11 GHSA PoC pickles to tests/data2/. The missing-detection behavior is present from the first scanner commit: c1d5abd ('Implement Pickle scanner', 2022-09-04, Matthieu Maitre) introduces _suspicious_globals (exact-module-keyed, name-set or '*') and scan_pickle_bytes flags only globals that match an entry; an unmatched global (e.g. idlelib.calltip.Calltip.fetch_tip) is silently not counted (issues_count stays 0, later returns Suspicious but non-failing). Parent 6a76b8c3 has zero src/picklescan files (grep -c picklescan = 0), so the denylist paradigm - and with it the missing-entry hole - is introduced atomically here. Later commits (72aa7c43 add safelist, f98f9bd rename _unsafe_globals) only reshaped but kept the exact-match paradigm.
round6_research.flaw_origin: human-authored finite denylist design at scanner debut: only globals matching a curated module->name map are flagged; unlisted RCE-capable builtins (idlelib.calltip.Calltip.fetch_tip) evade detection.
round6_research.reasoning: The vulnerable behavior (RCE-capable global not flagged because unlisted in a finite denylist) exists from the scanner's initial implementation c1d5abd, whose parent tree contains no scanner code at all. The fix simply extends the same denylist the flaw is intrinsic to; no re-architecture. Both commits authored by the maintainer with no AI markers. Verdict NOT_AI.

records.details:
Due to a bug in the startup trust dialog implementation, Claude Code could be tricked to execute code contained in a project before the user accepted the startup trust dialog. Exploiting this requires a user to start Claude Code in an untrusted directory.

Users on standard Claude Code auto-update will have received this fix automatically. Users performing manual updates are advised to update to the latest version.

Thank you to https://hackerone.com/avivdon for reporting this issue!

round6_research.bug_semantics: CVE-2025-65719 / GHSA-94gr-w3q5-rfqr (CWE-94, CVSS 9.8): Kubectl MCP Server <1.2.0 executes kubectl commands via subprocess.run(..., shell=True) with attacker-influenced string interpolation, enabling arbitrary command injection. Two reachable families: (1) compatible_servers/windsurf/windsurf_compatible_mcp_server.py _get_pods: command = f'kubectl get pods -n {namespace}' with namespace taken unvalidated from the MCP tool input (OX Security PoC: 'namespace': 'default && echo pwned > pwned'), reachable from a browser via CSRF-style POST to the JSON-RPC endpoint bound on 0.0.0.0:8080 (Docker default), i.e. 'RCE via crafted HTML page'; (2) kubectl_mcp_tool/natural_language.py process_query -> parse_query -> execute_command(command) -> subprocess.run(command, shell=True); parse_query interpolates word-only captures but the windsurf path interpolates unvalidated namespace. Full cluster takeover when the victim's kubeconfig is mounted.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Cluster of 6 independent security flaws in the MCP Toolbox server (Go): (1) CVE-2026-11624 + CVE-2026-9739/GHSA-7pf3-8xx7-rvhf: DNS rebinding/CORS permissiveness - SSE handler (MCP spec v2024-11-05) sets hardcoded Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and, pre-v0.25/v1.x flags, no Origin/host validation, letting a malicious site drive requests to a local Toolbox (CWE-942/CWE-346). (2) CVE-2026-11717/GHSA-8fcc-w5hv-4gxv: opaque-token introspection 'active' returned as *bool with a nil-tolerant check (Active != nil && !*Active) so a provider response omitting/null 'active' is accepted (auth bypass). (3) CVE-2026-11718/GHSA-wcpr-6g7x-p44r: opaque-token issuer validation condition 'a.issuer != "" && iss != ""' skips the check whenever the introspection response omits 'iss', accepting tokens from unauthorized IdPs (auth bypass). (4) CVE-2026-11719/GHSA-5gf6-gc35-xjpc: tool-level scopesRequired enforcement was added only to the v2025-11-25 MCP protocol method; older protocol versions (v2024-11-05, v2025-03-26, v2025-06-18) bypass scopes (authorization bypass via protocol downgrade). (5) CVE-2026-11720: HTTP tool URL builder resolves attacker-controlled pathParams via ResolveReference after checking only scheme/host/userinfo, so '../'-style dot segments escape the operator-configured base path and reach unintended same-host endpoints with toolbox credentials (path traversal). (6) CVE-2026-15829: bigquery-forecast/bigquery-analyze-contribution allow allowedDatasets bypass - options not safely escaped and the fully-assembled SQL not dry-run checked, so hidden dataset access (e.g., inside SQL views) escapes the allowedDatasets restriction.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Improper Protection of Alternate Path (CWE-424): bypass of the local file-access restriction (no-access / workdir modes) in aws-api-mcp-server (pip awslabs.aws-api-mcp-server / awslabs-aws-api-mcp-server, affected >= 0.2.14, < 1.3.9, fixed 1.3.9; medium CVSS 5.5; CVE-2026-4270). The server parses AWS CLI commands and executes them via awscli.clidriver. The file-access control (validate_file_path / RESTRICTED_URI_HANDLER with LOCAL_PREFIX_MAP mapping file://, fileb:// to get_file_validated) is only registered on the 'load-cli-arg' event; the AWS CLI shorthand parser resolves the '@=' paramfile syntax inside awscli.shorthand._resolve_paramfiles using its own module-global LOCAL_PREFIX_MAP (awscli's default: {'file://': (get_file, {'mode':'r'}), 'fileb://': (get_file, {'mode':'rb'})}) which has no access validation. Payload: `aws ec2 create-tags --resources i-xxx --tags Key=test,Value@=file:///etc/passwd` reads/exposes arbitrary local file contents in the MCP client context in no-access/workdir modes.
round6_research.evidence: Identity exact via GitHub advisory API: GHSA-2cpp-j2fc-qhp7 == CVE-2026-4270 'AWS API MCP File Access Restriction Bypass' (published 2026-03-17, medium 5.5, CWE-424, pip vulns awslabs.aws-api-mcp-server >=0.2.14,<1.3.9 first_patched 1.3.9; AWS security bulletin 2026-007-AWS; PyPI release 1.3.9). Changelog of src/aws-api-mcp-server at the 1.3.9 release commit (0d0fc3fc, 2026-02-13) lists 'Validate file path access in shorthand parser (#2406)'. Fix commit a785b407dab4e11d3f4a948f8cf921ec7874e564 (2026-02-12, Arne Wouters) modifies core/aws/services.py: extracts LOCAL_PREFIX_MAP into a module constant and adds `awscli.shorthand.LOCAL_PREFIX_MAP = LOCAL_PREFIX_MAP` so the shorthand @= paramfile resolution uses the validating get_file_validated; adds tests test_shorthand_paramfile_rejected_when_file_access_disabled parametrized with '--tags Key=test,Value@=fileb:///etc/passwd' and 'Value@=file:///etc/passwd' expecting LocalFileAccessDisabledError. Fix parent tree confirmed: no awscli.shorthand import/wiring (git grep rc=1), only `from awscli.paramfile import URIArgumentHandler` + RESTRICTED_URI_HANDLER (load-cli-arg only). At the introducer f799f236 the same structure exists (RESTRICTED_URI_HANDLER registered on 'load-cli-arg'; execution via awscli.clidriver.create_clidriver present), so the shorthand path was unguarded from 0.2.14 through 1.3.8, matching the advisory range exactly. round6_research.bug_semantics: CWE-770 denial of service in django.utils.html.strip_tags() (and the striptags template filter): processing inputs containing large sequences of incomplete HTML tags (e.g. '>' + '<a'*501, '<' + 'a'*1002) causes severe slowdown because strip_tags repeatedly invokes _strip_once (HTMLParser-based MLStripper) over the whole input; fixed by a pre-check that raises SuspiciousOperation when an open tag spans 1000+ chars containing >=50 '<' (MAX_STRIP_TAGS_DEPTH)
round6_research.evidence: BIC 6ca6c36f82 (Claude Paroz <claude@2xlibre.net>, 2014-03-20, 'Improved strip_tags and clarified documentation', Django 1.7 era) rewrites strip_tags to the 'while True: if not ('<' in value or '>' in value): return value; new_value = _strip_once(value); if new_value == value: return value; else: value = new_value' loop over HTMLParser-based MLStripper; parent aaa2110259 has single-pass 's.feed(value); s.close()' with no loop (verified). Fix 9f3419b5 (Sarah Boyce, 2025-04-08, 'Fixed CVE-2025-32873 -- Mitigated potential DoS in strip_tags()') adds long_open_tag_without_closing_re '<[a-zA-Z][^>]{1000,}' pre-check raising SuspiciousOperation, plus tests ('>' + '<a'*501, '<a'*50 + 'a'*950, '<' + 'a'*1002); released in 4.2.21/5.1.9/5.2.1 (e.g. cherry-pick c9731dc656 in 5.2.1 tag), fix ancestor of HEAD 0b40210e. Intermediate CVE-2024-53907 fix 49ff1042aa (Nov 2024) added MAX_STRIP_TAGS_DEPTH=50 guard but did not cover long open tags. AI marker scan: BIC body+diff 0 matches (pattern excludes the author's given name 'Claude', a real human Django core contributor since 2007); fix body+diff 1 match = human trailer 'Co-authored-by: Natalia <124304+nessita@users.noreply.github.com>'.
round6_research.flaw_origin: The retry-loop structure that re-parses the input until no tags remain was introduced when strip_tags was rewritten around MLStripper in 2014; the loop couples with HTMLParser to make long incomplete-tag sequences quadratic. Intermediate mitigations (CVE-2024-53907 fix 49ff1042aa added the MAX_STRIP_TAGS_DEPTH=50 iteration cap) did not cover long single open tags, leaving the 2025 DoS.

OSV reference pinpoints fix commit 9ba60c09c8836a37a2e4ea67ab35fe403e041415 'Use parameterized queries to the TSDB' (Jason Thomas, 2026-03-02) which switches cvt_model.rb and cvt_model.py to exec_params / cursor.execute(query, params) and quotes column names in questdb_client.py. git log -S traces the vulnerable interpolation: first written by 68f6de4211f09c8f4931b6d89f6c8b239ab17b14 (2025-07-15, 'Initial playback support'); parent c8cab9ca9bb4562e9063cc803048741a6876b9e9 has no db_lookup/raw timestamp interpolation (used exec_params). Introducer commit message body has zero AI markers (grep -icE co-authored|claude|copilot|codex|openai|generated|mastra|gemini|bard|cursor = 0); fix commit also 0 markers.
round6_research.flaw_origin: First writer of the vulnerable behavior: commit 68f6de4211f09c8f4931b6d89f6c8b239ab17b14 'Initial playback support' (Jason Thomas, 2025-07-15) added db_lookup() with raw interpolation `query = "SELECT * FROM #{target_name}__#{packet_name} WHERE timestamp < '#{date_time}' LIMIT -1"` followed by @@conn.exec(query). The parent c8cab9ca9bb4562e9063cc803048741a6876b9e9 used the parameterized form @@conn.exec_params(query, [packet_name, date_time]) for the same lookup, so the unparameterized pattern was newly introduced here. The pattern then propagated: 35f9130539659f4311f8c4b381e6bc343afbe64e (2025-07-29) renamed it tsdb_lookup, 684d7df3647814f7d4dddeeea072cfd1f4bd7d2f (2026-01-27) renamed the timestamp columns to PACKET_TIMESECONDS, both keeping string interpolation of start_time/end_time.

The introducer carries no AI co-author or AI-tool markers in its message, and the author (Jason Thomas) is a core human maintainer; the later rename commit 684d7df3 does carry 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5' but it only renamed columns and preserved the pre-existing vulnerable interpolation, so it did not originate the flaw. round6_research.bug_semantics: Open redirect (CWE-601) in next-intl middleware with localePrefix 'as-needed'. The middleware's pathname sanitizer (sanitizePathname in packages/next-intl/src/middleware/utils.tsx) only replaced backslashes (%5C) and collapsed consecutive slashes. It did not strip the WHATWG-control characters U+0009 (TAB), U+000A (LF), U+000D (CR), which the WHATWG URL parser silently removes during parsing. A crafted path such as '/en/<TAB>/example.org' therefore resolved as '//example.org' (scheme-relative) by new URL(path, base), so the middleware issued an off-site relative redirect while the user started from a trusted app URL.
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-8f24-v5vv-gm5j (CVE-2026-40299, CWE-601, moderate): open redirect when using next-intl middleware with localePrefix 'as-needed' because path handling + WHATWG URL parser resolve a relative redirect target to another host (scheme-relative // or control chars stripped by the parser); patched in next-intl@4.9.1, fix commit 1c80b668 (PR #2304, Jan Amann). git show 1c80b668: sanitizePathname gains .replace(/[\t\n\r]/g, '') with comment explaining decoded TAB in segment separator position causes new URL('/<TAB>/host', base) collapse to '//host' open redirect. git log -S 'sanitizePathname' shows first appearance in f42ac014 (PR #1208, 'Fix open redirect vulnerability for localePrefix as-necessary', Hblee, Co-authored-by Jan Amann). Parent-absence verified: numactl git grep -c 'sanitizePathname' 8c00eb74 -- packages/next-intl/src/middleware/ exit 1.
round6_research.flaw_origin: First writer of the vulnerable behavior is commit f42ac014 (Hblee, 2024-07-19), which introduced sanitizePathname as a fix for a previous open redirect (#1207/#1208) but sanitized only backslashes and duplicate slashes, leaving TAB/LF/CR control characters unstripped. Parent 8c00eb74 has no sanitizePathname (verified git grep exit 1). The same incomplete sanitizer persisted until the advisory fix 1c80b668 (v4.9.1) added /[\t\n\r]/g stripping.
round6_research.reasoning: The vulnerable behavior — an incomplete pathname sanitizer that lets WHATWG-stripped control characters smuggle a scheme-relative host into the middleware's redirect target — was first written in f42ac014 by a human developer (Hblee) in July 2024, with a human co-author (Jan Amann). The parent commit lacks the function entirely. The advisory fix (Jan Amann, April 2026) merely extends the same human-written sanitizer; no AI markers appear on either the introducer or the fix. Root cause is human-authored: NOT_AI.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Sandbox boundary bypass (CWE-20, CVSS 8.6 high): Codex sandbox policy conflated two concepts - the directory where the spawned command runs (command cwd) and the directory that anchors the sandbox's writable-root policy (policy cwd). The model-generated `cwd`/`workdir` field of the container.exec/shell tool call was passed into `get_writable_roots_with_cwd(cwd)`, so a model-generated path (resolved via session.cwd.join(workdir), i.e. an absolute path or `../` traversal) became the sandbox's writable root, enabling arbitrary file writes and command execution outside the folder where the user started the session; network-disabled restriction unaffected. Affects macOS seatbelt (create_seatbelt_command_args) and Linux landlock/seccomp (create_linux_sandbox_command_args) paths.
round6_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-w5fx-fh39-j5rw / CVE-2025-59532 (published 2025-09-19, reviewed, CWE-20, CVSS 8.6): 'Codex CLI could treat a model-generated cwd as the sandbox's writable root, including paths outside of the folder where the user started their session'; remediation: patch in 0.39.0 / SE extension 0.4.12 'canonicalizes and validates that the boundary used for sandbox policy is based on where the user started the session, and not the one generated by the model'; references commit 8595237505a1e0faabc2af3db805b66ce3ae182d and rust-v0.39.0 tag; reporter Tzanko Matev (Codetracer). git log -S 'get_writable_roots_with_cwd' over codex-rs: only 421e159888 (introducer, +get_writable_roots_with_cwd + call sites in exec.rs/linux.rs) and the fix 8595237 (separates command_cwd from sandbox_policy_cwd, passes turn_context.cwd as sandbox policy cwd) change the semantics; git show 421e159888^ protocol.rs shows only get_writable_roots() using std::env::current_dir() for DiskWriteCwd (parent absent of the vulnerable model-cwd flow; verified by git show parent:exec.rs + parent:linux.rs). Introducer author Michael Bolin <mbolin@openai.com>, committer GitHub (squash of PR #800); git log --format=%N over 421e159888^..8595237 shows no co-author/AI trailers in the range; intermediate refactor commits fde48aaa0d, 89ef4efdcf, 0776d78357 all by Michael Bolin (human). Fix 8595237 also authored by Michael Bolin (2025-09-18, PR #3874), no trailers. Fix commit first appears in tag rust-v0.39.0 (advisory's first_patched_version 0.39.0, npm @openai/codex >=0.2.0 <=0.38.0 vulnerable).
round6_research.flaw_origin: First writer of the flawed pattern is 421e159888 'feat: make cwd a required field of Config so we stop assuming std::env::current_dir() in a session (#800)' (2025-05-04, Michael Bolin). Before it, sandbox writable roots came from `get_writable_roots()` which used `std::env::current_dir()` (the process/session cwd - not model-controllable); after it, `get_writable_roots_with_cwd(cwd)` (protocol.rs) threaded the model-supplied ExecParams.cwd (ShellToolCallParams.workdir) into the seatbelt policy args (exec.rs create_seatbelt_command) and the landlock args (linux.rs). The atomic introducer commit's parent 4b61fb8bab has only get_writable_roots() + std::env::current_dir(); the branch-copy commits with identical content (f9f0490ca2, f0ad889ebb, a9816188c6, b2a2481516, 97bc9314ca, 72b1d3ad57, 15bc38585c, 3f73058676) are not in mainline ancestry. The pattern was preserved through refactors (fde48aaa0d seatbelt.rs extraction; 89ef4efdcf landlock overhaul; 0776d78357 sandbox redesign) until the fix.
round6_research.reasoning: Step 1: class hash verified (no case-lowering) against {'CVE-2025-59532','GHSA-w5fx-fh39-j5rw'}; advisory content maps the bug precisely to the sandbox cwd-confusion in codex-rs. Step 2: atomic introducer of the vulnerable behavior (model-generated cwd feeding sandbox writable-root policy) is 421e159888 (2025-05-04, PR #800); parent lacks the get_writable_roots_with_cwd flow entirely (uses std::env::current_dir()), so introducer_parent_absent=True. Step 3: no AI markers anywhere in the causal chain: introducer and all intermediate refactors and the fix are authored by Michael Bolin (OpenAI, human, author==GitHub-merge committer, no trailers, message is an ordinary design PR); the advisory itself credits a human reporter. round6_research.bug_semantics: Command injection (CWE-78) via newline characters in pre/post deployment commands (Heredoc Transport). Admin-configurable pre_deployment_command / post_deployment_command are wrapped as sh -c '...' (single-quote escape variant since 853325d9f, 2024-05-23) and executed via docker exec over an SSH-based ExecuteRemoteCommand trait; the SSH transport preserves raw newlines in the command text, so a command containing \n breaks out of the sh -c wrapper and injects arbitrary shell statements on the Coolify server. The vulnerability is the absence of newline normalization at the injection point: commands were concatenated with only quote-char escaping from the feature's first commit (2024-02-08) until the fix.
round6_research.evidence: Identity pinned by class_id hash reversal over github.com/coollabsio/coolify candidates (63 CVE-level records): single match CVE-2026-34152 (= GHSA-5qp8-9gg7-4c86). '"'; docker exec {$containerName} {$cmd}; git grep at parent 642a6e32 shows 0 occurrences of run_pre_deployment_command and run_post_deployment_command (absent). round6_research.bug_semantics: Command injection (CWE-74) in the ssh_exec handler of an MCP server: host and username from stored credentials are interpolated into a shell command string `ssh -i <key> ... <username>@<host> "bash -ic '<cmd>'"` executed via child_process.exec; a crafted host/username containing shell metacharacters allows command injection. Maintainer disputes it as a real vuln: threat model is a local/trusted tool for an agent, callers already have execution capability via the exposed shell (CVSS 3.1 AV:L 3.3 LOW).
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-26qx-2c8w-xjfx = CVE-2026-19039 (VulDB-origin, published 2026-08-06, unreviewed): command injection via host/username argument of ssh_exec in src/index.ts up to commit 8ebbbb99b26f80ff6162fe00957c6dec73fbc5a5; references point to issue #3, whose maintainer response states the intended threat model is a local/trusted tool and callers already have execution capability. No fix commit exists: the project adopts rolling release; the latest commit 8ebbbb99b26f80ff6162fe00957c6dec73fbc5a5 (2026-04-27) refactors the code and adds host/username regex validation (validateCredentialEndpoint) but still executes arbitrary commands for a local caller, and no later fix exists (ls-remote HEAD = 8ebbbb9). Repo history is 10 commits all by author KinoThe-Kafkaesque (Henry Mao authored 3 Smithery-config commits 2025-05-01). Full-message marker scan across all commits: only hit is the subject of d20d458270b00b0836a56a0408de5fb2b935fbdc ('Add documentation files: Claude guide, monetization strategy, and test specification'), which is a docs commit and does not touch src; no Co-Authored-By, no AI-tool markers on any commit touching the vulnerable code.
round6_research.flaw_origin: First writer of the vulnerable behavior: commit ee2f11f1eb604ef59d56bb3790edbc39dd28826e 'first commit' (KinoThe-Kafkaesque, 2025-02-20) introduced the ssh_exec tool that builds `ssh -i ${privateKey} ${username}@${host} "${command}"` and runs it via child_process.exec with unquoted host/username interpolation. Subsequent commits only evolved it (82606d6c7db204223dda039af34355d91b7cf1c9 2025-03-12, c95b23636813104923eab614a664596c3c7803c1 2025-04-12, b96946237441e2800511e90223e3b61dd7baa472 2025-04-12; refactor 8ebbbb99b26f80ff6162fe00957c6dec73fbc5a5 2026-04-27 moved it to src/handlers/commands.ts with shellQuote + host/username regex validation, which still leaves command content up to the local caller). The repository root commit has no parent, so the vulnerable pattern has no earlier writer.
round6_research.reasoning: The minimum atomic introducer is the repository root commit ee2f11f1eb604ef59d56bb3790edbc39dd28826e ('first commit'): it is the first writer of the interpolated ssh command executed via exec() and has no parent to decompose into. The advisory's affected range ('up to 8ebbbb99...') matches the whole repo history. The flaw (unquoted host/username in a shell string) is a classic human-written pattern from the original author; no AI marker exists on any commit that wrote or modified the vulnerable code, and the single marker hit is a docs-commit subject. The advisory itself notes the maintainer disputes the finding and no fix was ever issued (fix_sha = null), consistent with a low-severity, locally-triggered issue. No AI involvement evidence; verdict NOT_AI.

partial_wave.bug_semantics: docker cp into a container: daemon builds a temporary container FS view by bind-mounting volumes; mount destination path is resolved with GetResourcePath then passed to fileutils.CreateIfNotExists (os.Stat/os.MkdirAll/os.OpenFile on the host-absolute path). TOCTOU: a container process can swap an intermediate path component to a symlink pointing outside the container root between resolution and creation, so empty files/dirs are created as root at arbitrary host paths (GHSA-vp62-88p7-qqf5, CVE-2026-41568).
partial_wave.evidence: Advisory GHSA-vp62-88p7-qqf5 (race during mountpoint creation; companion GHSA-rg2x-37c3-w2rh covers the mount-syscall race). Real fix 64a22d80b93ddc1416b501b5145df02947312249 (Pawel Gronowski 2026-03-26, 'daemon/copy: Fix symlink escape in mount destination creation') reworks createIfNotExists to take *os.Root opened on ctr.BaseFS and use root.MkdirAll/root.OpenFile, scoping all ops to the container root; diff in daemon/containerfs_linux.go + test. Introducer 2bdc7fb0a1e00439aa88438f1164677dda95737f (Cory Snider 2022-10-12, 'daemon: archive in a dedicated mount namespace') created containerfs_linux.go with the GetResourcePath + fileutils.CreateIfNotExists(dest, ...) pattern (lines 84/94 of the added file). No AI markers on introducer or fixer. Shard fix_sha 4ccb8bbc resolves to tag/release bump commit dd24a3adc, not the fix.

records.details:
Claude Code used the git worktree `commondir` file when determining folder trust but did not validate its contents. By crafting a repository with a `commondir` file pointing to a path the victim had previously trusted, an attacker could bypass the trust dialog and immediately execute malicious hooks defined in `.claude/settings.json`. Exploiting this required the victim to clone a malicious repository and run Claude Code within it, and for the attacker to know or guess a path the victim had already trusted.

Users on standard Claude Code auto-update have received this fix already. Users performing manual updates are advised to update to the latest version.

Claude Code thanks [hackerone.com/masato_anzai](https://hackerone.com/masato_anzai) for reporting this issue.

partial_wave.bug_semantics: LAPI Denial of Service via unbounded gzip decompression (CVE-2026-44981, GHSA-273h-gvwr-c3qj): the router applies gzip.Gzip(gzip.NoCompression, gzip.WithDecompressOnly(), gzip.WithDecompressFn(gzip.DefaultDecompressHandle)) globally in pkg/apiserver, so unauthenticated /v1/watchers and /v1/watchers/login accept gzip bodies and decompress them without any size cap; a small gzip bomb exhausts LAPI memory/CPU.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Stripe charge credential replay in mppx (npm, TypeScript machine-payments protocol): the stripe/charge payment method creates PaymentIntents with an idempotency key derived from (challenge.id, spt) but never checks Stripe's 'Idempotent-Replayed' response header. An attacker can replay a valid credential (same spt token) against a new challenge; Stripe returns the already-created PaymentIntent with idempotent-replayed: true, which the server accepts as a new successful payment without charging again, letting an attacker pay once and consume unlimited resources. Fixed in 0.4.11.

Fix b2b1a0b60506fc71aa80b8a025084949dca1a994 (2026-03-26, tmm <tmm@tmm.dev>, 'Merge commit from fork', single-parent commit; 8ce9f56b is a chore bump) adds the replayed check and plumbs replayed through createWithClient/createWithSecretKey (reading lastResponse.headers['idempotent-replayed'] / response.headers.get('idempotent-replayed')). Fix parent 94088246 still contains the vulnerable unreplayed code (line 152 idempotencyKey, no replayed). AI-marker grep count 0 on both introducer and fix messages.

records.details:
Claude Code failed to account for symlinks when checking permission deny rules. If a user explicitly denied Claude Code access to a file and Claude Code had access to a symlink pointing to that file, it was possible for Claude Code to access the file.

Users on standard Claude Code auto-update will have received this fix automatically. Users performing manual updates are advised to update to the latest version.

Thank you to https://hackerone.com/vinai for reporting this issue!

round6_research.bug_semantics: CWE-276 insecure default permissions: RPM/DEB package preinst runs ${INSTALL_DIR}/embedded/bin/python on python-scripts/pre.py (or prerm.py) without -B, so Python writes a __pycache__ dir inside /opt/datadog-agent/python-scripts with default (too loose) permissions at install/upgrade time; a local unprivileged user who can plant a malicious .pyc in that dir achieves code execution as root at the next agent upgrade/install. LPE, code path active only during install/upgrade.
round6_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-6852-76c5-6cmg / CVE-2025-61667: Datadog Linux Host Agent 7.65.0-7.70.2, LPE via insufficient perms on /opt/datadog-agent/python-scripts/__pycache__ during installation, CWE-276, patched >= 7.71.0. Introducer a41ae3430a (#32765, Jose Manuel Almaza Ramiro 2025-01-14) added the python invocation block to omnibus/package-scripts/agent-rpm/preinst (runs PRE_PYTHON_FILE without -B); parent cd8472695 preinst has no such block (grep count 0); first tag containing a41ae3430a is 7.65.0-devel, matching the advisory's affected-range start. True fix 45eecc753e (#41118, Arthur Bellal 2025-09-23) removes __pycache__ in agent-deb+agent-rpm preinst and adds -B plus __pycache__ removal in pkg/fleet/installer/packages/integrations/integrations.go executePythonScript (shipped 7.71.0). OSV GIT refs were misleading (introduced 6ce6e864 typo commit, fixed d3d73218 milestone bump). Prior mitigation 0d11a997a3 (#36825) added -B to preinst in 7.67.0 but only stopped NEW pycache creation, still within affected range. Markers on introducer: 1 = human 'Co-authored-by: NouemanKHAL' trailer only; fix commit markers 0.

Bypass (GHSA-m435-9v6r-v5f6/CVE-2024-54000): the 2024-03 fix added valid_host() but the requests.get in _check_url kept allow_redirects=True, so a 302 redirect from the (validated) target follows into internal networks, re-enabling SSRF.

records.details:
## Summary

The `@utcp/http` package is vulnerable to a blind Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) caused by a trust-boundary inconsistency between manual discovery and tool invocation. `registerManual()` validates the discovery URL against an HTTPS / loopback allowlist, but `callTool()` reuses the resolved `toolCallTemplate.url` directly without revalidating, and the `OpenApiConverter` blindly trusts whatever `servers[0].url` an attacker-hosted spec declares. An attacker who hosts a malicious OpenAPI spec on a legitimate HTTPS endpoint can declare e.g. `servers: [{ url: "http://127.0.0.1:9090" }]` or `servers: [{ url: "http://169.254.169.254" }]`; the converter then produces tools whose URL points at internal services on the agent host.

A separate prefix-bypass also affected the discovery-time check: the previous `startsWith('http://localhost')` guard let URLs like `http://localhost.evil.com` through.

## Sister advisory

This is the npm/TypeScript counterpart of [GHSA-39j6-4867-gg4w / CVE-2026-44661](https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/python-utcp/security/advisories/GHSA-39j6-4867-gg4w) on the Python `utcp-http` package. Same vulnerability, same fix shape, same reporter.

## Versions and patch state

- `@utcp/http <= 1.1.1` — vulnerable. Both the loopback-redirect (`http://127.0.0.1`) and the non-loopback internal-IP variants (e.g. `http://169.254.169.254`, `http://10.0.0.5`) succeed. Note: the `streamable_http` and `sse` `callToolStreaming` paths in 1.1.1 are TODO placeholders and don't actually fetch URLs, so the runtime SSRF surface in these protocols is currently confined to discovery — a future implementation must also call `ensureSecureUrl` before issuing the request.
- `@utcp/http 1.1.2` — full fix. Runtime revalidation in `callTool` closes the non-loopback variants; the `OpenApiConverter` rejects, at conversion time, any spec fetched from a non-loopback source that declares a loopback `servers[0].url`, closing the loopback-redirect variant.

## Impact

A remote attacker who can convince the agent (via the LLM context, prompt injection, or a tool-discovery surface) to register their HTTPS OpenAPI URL can:
- Map internal networks behind the agent.
- Read AWS/GCP IAM credentials from cloud metadata endpoints (`http://169.254.169.254`, `http://metadata.google.internal`).
- Reach unauthenticated internal services exposed on loopback (Elasticsearch, Redis HTTP, internal admin panels, the agent's own HTTP server).
- Have responses returned to the LLM, which combined with prompt injection enables exfiltration back to the attacker.

## Patch

Commit on `dev`: 21f63e6.

New helper `packages/http/src/_security.ts` exposes `isSecureUrl`, `isLoopbackUrl`, `ensureSecureUrl`. Hostname-based validation closes the prefix bypass (`http://localhost.evil.com` → rejected). All three protocols' `registerManual` now call `ensureSecureUrl(url, 'manual discovery')`; `callTool` re-checks the resolved URL with `ensureSecureUrl(url, 'tool invocation')` immediately before the axios request. `OpenApiConverter` rejects remote spec → loopback server.

## Workarounds

For users who cannot upgrade immediately:
- Refuse to call `registerManual` with any URL controlled by an untrusted party, even over HTTPS.
- Restrict outbound network access from the host running the agent so internal addresses (RFC1918, 169.254.0.0/16, loopback) are unreachable.

## Credit

Discovered and reported by [@YLChen-007](https://github.com/YLChen-007) against the Python sibling implementation (universal-tool-calling-protocol/python-utcp#83). The TypeScript port shared the same code shape and the same vulnerability.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Heartbeat owner-downgrade logic (ForceSenderIsOwnerFalse) only fired for exec completions and cron reasons; when untrusted webhook 'wake' system events (trusted:false) triggered a heartbeat run (reason hook:wake), the pending untrusted content was not inspected and the reply ran with senderIsOwner still true, preserving owner-like execution context for attacker-controlled webhook content (CWE-184 incomplete list of disallowed inputs, CWE-863 incorrect authorization).
round6_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-g2hm-779g-vm32/CVE-2026-43566 (npm >= 2026.4.7 < 2026.4.14, patched 2026.4.14, CWE-184/CWE-863, fix commit 31281bc92f55796817a92bc43f722cba1e77ab42, PR #66031). git blame 31281bc92f^ on heartbeat-runner.ts:540-541 (shouldInspectPendingEvents = isExecEventReason || isCronEventReason || hasTaggedCronEvents) -> f855d0be4ff (2026-02-19, vikpos); line 920 (ForceSenderIsOwnerFalse: hasExecCompletion) -> a30214a6249 (2026-03-31 Vincent Koc, PR #57652). 5b6e552b51f (2026-04-06, Agustin Rivera, PR #62003, co-author Devin Robison): hooks.ts diff enqueueSystemEvent(value.text, { sessionKey }) -> { sessionKey, trusted: false }; in v2026.4.7, NOT in v2026.4.5 (git merge-base --is-ancestor checks); trusted flag default (trusted: options.trusted !== false) added by a77928b1087 (2026-03-30, Jacob Tomlinson, PR #57691). Fix 31281bc92f adds shouldInspectWakePendingEvents to shouldInspectPendingEvents and hasUntrustedPendingEvents -> ForceSenderIsOwnerFalse, plus UNTRUSTED_SYSTEM_EVENT_LINE_RE /^System (untrusted):/m -> senderIsOwner: false in get-reply-run.ts. PR #62003 squash commits: fd2e1b728c7e9c687a5fd240aba7cdaa7eab1f9a (code), 677a9edef172419c6d7af610ed7cc184918c7539 (changelog). BIC commit message has no AI markers (author/committer/co-author are human; no gpt/copilot/claude/codex/gemini/ai-assisted tokens).
round6_research.flaw_origin: 5b6e552b51f marked wake hook events untrusted (enqueueSystemEvent(value.text, { sessionKey, trusted: false })) while the owner-downgrade inspection introduced by a30214a6249 covered only exec completions (shouldInspectPendingEvents = exec|cron|taggedCron; ForceSenderIsOwnerFalse = hasExecCompletion). The mismatch created the vulnerable behavior: untrusted wake content processed with owner auth. round6_research.bug_semantics: Environment variable injection (CWE-454/untrusted input in env): OpenClaw loads a workspace .env from the process CWD at startup (dotenv.config) and applies its entries to the process environment with an incomplete deny-list. A malicious workspace .env can set runtime-control variables (update sources, gateway URL/port, ClawHub resolution, browser executable paths, TLS/registry base URLs) thereby redirecting updates, exfiltration endpoints, and executed binaries. Untrusted workspace files were trusted as configuration, and the deny-list was a patch-up effort.
round6_research.evidence: openclaw clone .ai-slop/state/repos/openclaw. Introducer 16dfc1a5b929f7184261c52f50846daca536ca24 (2025-11-24, Peter Steinberger <steipete@gmail.com>, 'Add warelay CLI with Twilio webhook support') created src/index.ts with 'dotenv.config()' (line 16) - loads .env from process CWD with NO filtering of any variable, so workspace .env entries (incl. later-introduced OPENCLAW_* runtime controls) enter the process env. Parent f6dd362d39b8e30bd79ef7560aab9575712ccc11 has no dotenv usage in src (git grep: no hits) -> parent_absent. Refactored into src/infra/dotenv.ts by 77b19643e2f10fa0595acafc67df147df0ca87a7 (2026-01-05 'fix: load global .env fallback', replaces index.ts dotenv.config with loadDotEnv). First trust-boundary filter: 6a793248024 (2026-03-25, Devin Robison, 'Filter untrusted CWD .env entries before OpenClaw startup (#54631)') added initial BLOCKED_WORKSPACE_DOTENV_KEYS (API keys, proxies); extended by 7a5c5f33d05 (#57767 auth env vars), 330a9f98cb2 (#58170 bundled-root overrides), 290e5bf219d (#58473 helper interpreter overrides) - all still incomplete. Fix dbfcef319618158fa40b31cdac386ea34c392c0c (2026-04-08, Agustin Rivera <31522568+eleqtrizit>, PR #62660 'fix(dotenv): block workspace runtime env vars') added to the deny-list: BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH, PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH, OPENCLAW_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH, CLAWHUB_AUTH_TOKEN, CLAWHUB_CONFIG_PATH, CLAWHUB_TOKEN, CLAWHUB_URL (prefix CLAWHUB_, OPENCLAW_CLAWHUB_, OPENCLAW_DISABLE_ added), OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT, OPENCLAW_NODE_EXEC_HOST, OPENCLAW_NODE_EXEC_FALLBACK, OPENCLAW_MPM_CATALOG_PATHS, OPENCLAW_PLUGIN_CATALOG_PATHS, OPENCLAW_SHOW_SECRETS, OPENCLAW_ALLOW_*, cache-trace vars, OPENAI_API_KEY/KEYS moved up, plus '_BASE_URL' suffix rule; 77-line dotenv.test.ts. round6_research.bug_semantics: IDOR / missing authorization (CWE-284/639) in LobeChat's KnowledgeBaseModel.removeFilesFromKnowledgeBase (packages/database/src/models/knowledgeBase.ts), exposed via the tRPC router knowledgeBase.removeFilesFromKnowledgeBase. The ownership predicate eq(knowledgeBaseFiles.userId, this.userId) is present only as a commented-out line ('// eq(knowledgeBaseFiles.userId, this.userId)') inside the delete WHERE clause, which keeps eq(knowledgeBaseFiles.knowledgeBaseId, knowledgeBaseId) and inArray(knowledgeBaseFiles.fileId, ids) but drops the user scoping. Any authenticated user who knows a target knowledgeBaseId + fileId can delete files from other users' knowledge bases (IDs are random, so exploitation requires ID leakage, hence low CVSS 3.7).

round6_research.bug_semantics: Sandbox escape (RCE, CVSS 10.0) in @enclave-vm/core: vm context global exposes host closures as own enumerable properties (root: __safe_console holding host-bound console methods called with raw args, __safe_callTool host closure; later __host_memory_track__); raw intrinsic Object (getOwnPropertyDescriptors etc.) is reachable (at root the global Object IS the raw intrinsic since no SafeObject existed; after PR #20 SafeObject only shadowed the global name, {}[['__proto__']].constructor still yields the intrinsic). getOwnPropertyDescriptors(this) leaks host references; host fn .constructor chain yields host Function -> Function('return process')() for RCE; console passthrough also triggers host util.inspect via Symbol.for('nodejs.util.inspect.custom').
round6_research.evidence: Root commit is the single root (git rev-list --max-parents=0 -> 63535a26 only), author David Antoon <david@frontegg.com>, 'initialize project structure with essential configuration files and setup', empty message body (no AI trailers). Root libs/enclave/src/adapters/vm-adapter.ts: baseSandbox=vm.createContext({}); sanitizeVmContext removes only Iterator/AsyncIterator/ShadowRealm/WeakRef/FinalizationRegistry/Reflect/Proxy/performance/Temporal per level (not host refs, not Object statics); Object.entries(safeRuntime) defineProperty'd non-writable/non-configurable/enumerable (includes __safe_callTool host async closure); __safe_console=createSafeConsole which rate-limits but calls method(...args) with original args (host console.log.bind(console)); code wrapped in async IIFE run via script.runInContext(this.context) -> top-level this = contextified global; NO SafeObject at root. Empirical reproduction with these exact shapes on node v22: getOwnPropertyDescriptors(this) exposes __safe_console/__safe_callTool/plain props; PoC1-style (plain host fn own prop .constructor('return process')()) -> [object process]; PoC2-style (g.__safe_console.value.log(obj) with Symbol.for('nodejs.util.inspect.custom') -> inspect.constructor('return process')()) -> [object process]. Advisory GHSA-f229-3862-4942/CVE-2026-27597 (published 2026-02-25) rates critical, claims all <=2.10.1 vulnerable (incl. 1.x), PoCs by c0rydoras, fixed v2.11.x. Fix 9e1a930cd8efa1c4b6fb699f79bba6b4889d1910 (PR #52, squash merge, contains v2.11.0/v2.11.1) neutralizes intrinsic Object statics, makes __host_memory_track__ configurable then deletes it, pre-stringifies console output; commit message carries 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>' (AI-marked FIX, not introducer). Advisory also references release commit 09afbebe4cb6d0586c1145aa71ffabd2103932db (v2.11.0 bump).
round6_research.flaw_origin: Root import commit 63535a26 introduced the whole vulnerable design: host closures defined as non-writable own props of vm.createContext({}) sandbox, user code run via script.runInContext with this=context global, no protection of the intrinsic Object descriptor API, createSafeConsole wrapping host console but calling method(...args) with original args. Later commits (PR #11 double-VM, #14 SecureProxy, #16 memory tracking adding __host_memory_track__, #20 SafeObject) layered defenses/surface but the escape class existed continuously from the initial import through v2.10.1.
round6_research.reasoning: Step 1: vuln = vm sandbox escape via host-object leakage + reachable intrinsic Object descriptor API + raw console passthrough (CWE-94). Step 2: atomic introducer = root commit 63535a26: it is the first writer of every required element (host closures as own context global props, raw intrinsic Object, raw-args console passthrough, runInContext with this=global), it has no parent (root of repo; introducer_parent_absent=true), and it is not a squash (initial import; no decomposition). Later commits added more leak surfaces (e.g., __host_memory_track__ in ef05e863) but the same escape class was demonstrably present at root (reproduced both PoC routes with root shapes). Step 3: root commit has no AI markers (human author, empty body, no co-author trailers, no AI-tool references); the only AI marker in this story is on the FIX commit (Claude Opus 4.6), and an AI-authored fix does not make the introducer AI-written. round6_research.bug_semantics: TLS hostname verification disabled by default (CWE-297 Improper Verification of Certificate with Host Mismatch): jruby-openssl OpenSSL::SSL::SSLContext::DEFAULT_PARAMS sets :verify_hostname => nil, so connecting with VERIFY_PEER validates the certificate chain but never checks that the certificate hostname matches the target host. A MITM can present any valid certificate for a domain they own and JRuby accepts it. PoC in advisory: CRuby 3.4.3 fails with "certificate verify failed (hostname mismatch)" while JRuby 10.0.0.0 / 9.4.2.0 (jruby-openssl 0.15.3) accept. Fixed in jruby-openssl 0.15.4 / jruby 10.0.0.1 / 9.4.12.1.
round6_research.evidence: Identity: class repos include rubysec/ruby-advisory-db (advisory DB repo) but cohort/precise GHSA match pins the real affected repo github.com/jruby/jruby-openssl; member_map/advisory GHSA-72qj-48g4-5xgx ("JRuby-OpenSSL has hostname verification disabled by default", alias CVE-2025-46551; affected rubygems:jruby-openssl introduced 0.12.1 fixed 0.15.4, org.jruby:jruby 10.0.0.0->10.0.0.1 and 9.3.4.0->9.4.12.1; PoC against bad.substitutealert.com with a cert for s8a.me). Fix: 96444ea340a3642b882a53fd5258b9531853d44b (2025-05-07, Charles Oliver Nutter <headius@headius.com>, "Verify hostname by default", single parent 80d37ce600dd584ac9cc6ffefbe137ab4880fcda, released as 0.15.4 on same day via 31a56d690 merge/4a835668 version bump): flips DEFAULT_PARAMS :verify_hostname => nil to :verify_hostname => true; commit message explicitly states "This addresses CVE-2025-46551 and GHSA-72qj-48g4-5xgx". BIC: aefb8235d (2022-01-27, kares) as above; parent 1f9c1366 has verify_hostname => true -> introducer_parent_absent=1. No AI markers: %N empty on introducer and fix; kares (Karol Bucek) and headius (Charles Oliver Nutter) are long-time human JRuby maintainers; commit dates 2022/2025 pre-date AI code-gen in this project; no Co-Authored-By naming any AI tool.

Parent 1f9c1366 verified: line 23 reads :verify_hostname => true (verification ON; vulnerable behavior absent) -> introducer_parent_absent=1. round6_research.bug_semantics: Absolute path traversal (arbitrary file read) in gradio prior to 6.7.0 on Windows with Python 3.13+: gradio.utils.safe_join() guards user path with os.path.isabs(filename) (after posixpath.normpath) before os.path.join(directory, filename) returns the final path. Python 3.13 changed os.path.isabs on Windows so root-relative paths like '/windows/win.ini' are no longer isabs, so the guard passes and ntpath.join collapses 'directory' + '/windows/win.ini' to 'C:\windows\win.ini', escaping STATIC_PATH_LIB. PoC: GET /static//windows/win.ini on a Windows-hosted gradio app reads arbitrary files unauthenticated, even with auth enabled (GHSA-39mp-8hj3-5c49 / CVE-2026-28414, aliases PYSEC-2026-64). Fix (6.7.0) adds 'or filename.startswith("/")' to the guard.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Regular expression denial of service (ReDoS, CWE-400) in the MCP server package @wonderwhy-er/desktop-commander (versions prior to 0.2.39): src/search-manager.ts searchExcelFiles() (Excel/sheets search, added #282) and searchDocxFiles() (DOCX search, added #341) compile the user-supplied search pattern directly with new RegExp(pattern, flags) (lines ~352 and ~535 at fix-parent; the try/catch only validates syntax, escaping only on invalid regex) and match it against cell/document text content. A crafted pattern with nested quantifiers (e.g. (a+)+$ against 'a'.repeat(30)+'!') triggers catastrophic backtracking, pinning the Node.js event loop at 100% CPU and hanging the MCP server - denial of service reachable from any connected MCP client (e.g. via prompt-injected or direct search input). Reported by skywings via VulDB (VDB-367960), issue #375, patch PR #400.
round6_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-r87g-78mx-3wg4 / CVE-2026-10691 pin search-manager.ts excel/docx search; fix PR #400 'validate regex patterns to prevent ReDoS in search' = commit eb139aca (Saeed Al Mansouri <sorlen008@gmail.com>, 2026-04-09, 'Replace excel/docx search from regex to literal search'; 1 file, +32/-35) - included in release v0.2.39 (tag b3dfe1a3, 2026-04-23; merge-base confirms eb139aca is an ancestor -> FIX_IN_0239, matching the advisory's affected <0.2.39). Pre-fix code shows regex = new RegExp(pattern, flags) at search-manager.ts:352 (searchExcelFiles) and :535 (searchDocxFiles) with only syntactic try/catch escaping. History: -S 'new RegExp' -- src/search-manager.ts -> add at 367039af (2025-12-08), more at 899879c4 (2026-02-19), removed at eb139aca; 367039af^ file has grep -c RegExp = 0 -> introducer_parent_absent true. AI markers: authors edgarsskore <edgars.skore@gmail.com>, Eduard Ruzga <wonderwhy.er@gmail.com>, Saeed Al Mansouri <sorlen008@gmail.com>, committers GitHub <noreply@github.com> - no Co-authored-by/AI-bot trailers on introducer, DOCX extension commit, file-creation commit 227050bd, or the fix.
round6_research.flaw_origin: The user-regex-permitting search behavior was introduced when Excel/sheets search landed: 367039af (edgarsskore, 2025-12-08, 'Feature/sheets handling (#282)') first wrote 'regex = new RegExp(pattern, flags)' against user-supplied content-search patterns in search-manager.ts (verified: 367039af^:src/search-manager.ts has 0 'RegExp' occurrences -> parent_absent=true; the file itself was created earlier at 227050bd, 2025-08-28, Eduard Ruzga 'Refactor file search (#229)' with pattern-free matching). DOCX search duplicated the same pattern at 899879c4 (Eduard Ruzga, 2026-02-19, #341). No ReDoS safeguards (no literal fallback, no quantifier heuristics) existed until the fix.

No AI-author markers on any commit in the causal chain; verdict NOT_AI.

records.details:
Due to an error in command parsing, it was possible to bypass the Claude Code confirmation prompt to trigger execution of an untrusted command. Reliably exploiting this requires the ability to add untrusted content into a Claude Code context window.

Users on standard Claude Code auto-update will have received this fix automatically. Users performing manual updates are advised to update to the latest version.

Thank you to the NVIDIA AI Red Team for reporting this issue!

round6_research.bug_semantics: Missing authentication on SSE/HTTP MCP transports (CWE-77 per advisory; real issue is CWE-306-style unauthorized access): mcp-neo4j-memory v0.3.0 serves ALL MCP tools (knowledge-graph + Neo4j-backed ops incl. arbitrary Cypher) over SSE/HTTP without any auth/API-key/origin checks; anyone who can reach the endpoint can invoke tools -> sensitive data disclosure or arbitrary command execution via Neo4j. Default host 127.0.0.1, but README/docker examples bound 0.0.0.0 exposing the unauthenticated service; no middleware at all (FastMCP 2.0 stateless_http).

 fix: dashboard menu clickability + expiration date UX (#753)

 * fix: dashboard menu clickability + expiration date UX

 Dashboard actions menu:
 - Inactive (expired/removed) rows dimmed via their cells instead of the
 row, so `opacity` no longer creates a stacking context that trapped the
 actions dropdown beneath later rows and made its items unclickable.
 - Add an "Extend 6 months" menu item for expired repos/PRs/gists.

 Expiration form (anonymize):
 - Fix the "After , the content will be removed." blank date: guard the
 helper text and add min/max validation feedback so an invalid pick no
 longer nulls the model into a broken sentence.
 - Add a `min` (today) so past dates can no longer be selected, and
 compute min/max from local date parts (not UTC) to avoid a timezone
 off-by-one in the native picker.
 - Default expiration is now 6 months (single source of truth, removing a
 latent double-offset bug); max stays at 1 year.
 - Block submitting a missing/out-of-range expiration date.

 Backend:
 - New POST /:id/extend endpoint for repos, PRs and gists that pushes the
 expiration +6 months and re-anonymizes so expired items come back
 online, mirroring the refresh flow. Shared extendExpirationDate helper.

 Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

 * fix: add frontend translation for invalid_status error code

 The new /extend endpoints throw an "invalid_status" AnonymousError, which
 the error-code coverage test requires to have a locale entry.

 Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Distinct from CVE-2026-23490 (OID decode integer overflow, MAX_OID_ARC_CONTINUATION_OCTETS). Fix adds MAX_NESTING_DEPTH = 100 with a depth check in SingleItemDecoder.__call__.

round6_research.bug_semantics: SSRF: when the path argument is an absolute URL, HTTParty's Request#uri uses it as-is (instead of joining base_uri), so the request -- carrying configured headers/credentials such as X-API-KEY -- is sent to the attacker-controlled host. Introduced by `uri = path.relative? ? URI.parse("#{base_uri}#{path}") : path` in lib/httparty.rb.

URI.parse("#{base_uri}#{path}") : path`, letting absolute URLs bypass base_uri. Parent ae7ce30 has no 'relative' anywhere in lib/ (git grep rc=1). Pickaxe `git log --reverse -S 'path.relative?'` shows first appearance at a279df8. Fix 0529bcd (John Nunemaker, 2025-12-23) adds validate_uri_safety! host-vs-base_uri check raising UnsafeURIError, released in 0.24.0 (55ec76e8); commit body contains '🤖 Generated with Claude Code' and 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>'. Introducer commit has no AI markers (grep rc=1).

(1) Chat history renders useMarkdown-processed HTML via v-html="process(message.content)"; (2) airi-card views pass card fields through hightlightTagToHtml(), which wraps {{...}} template tags in a span via string replace with NO HTML escaping, then injects via v-html; (3) the Tauri MCP plugin exposes connect_server (crates/tauri-plugin-mcp/src/lib.rs) which passes user-supplied command and args straight to Command::new(command).args(args) with no validation/whitelist, so the XSS (callable from the frontend via the exposed Tauri API) escalates to arbitrary command execution. round6_research.bug_semantics: Username enumeration: GET /api/v1/user (and other v1 API endpoints) returns a 401 whose JSON 'message' is the raw authentication error, and Basic-auth failures yield different errors depending on whether the username exists: nonexistent username propagates user_model.ErrUserNotExist{Name: login} ('user does not exist [uid: 0, name: X]'), while an existing username with a wrong password propagates an error containing the user's real uid/message (ErrUserNotExist{UID: N} at introduction; later ErrUserPasswordInvalid 'user password is invalid [uid: N, ...]' after 0403bd989f). An attacker can therefore enumerate valid usernames.
round6_research.evidence: OSV CVE-2025-69413 / GHSA-pc73-rj2c-wvf9 ('In Gitea before 1.25.2, /api/v1/user has different responses for failed authentication depending on whether a username exists'); OSV GIT 'fixed' = eaa916a7867d44a5cb8dacc74e4acd1eb09021de which is only the 1.25.2 release-notes commit (#35986). Real code fix: main-branch 62d750eadb4a6ecdbaf807c1682ace4d87695977 (2025-11-21, PR #36002, Lunny Xiao) backported into v1.25.2 as 20cf4b78493ad4bff572e1b1772ad57d82c43b60 (#36004): apiAuth now maps auth errors to a unified message via new auth.ErrAsUserAuthMessage + constant 'invalid username, password or token' (routers/api/v1/api.go), with new tests/integration/api_auth_test.go asserting identical 401 messages for user2+wrong-password vs user-not-exist. Introducer chain verified: pre-refactor modules/context/api.go APIAuth had only 'ctx.Doer = authMethod.Verify(...)' with no error branch; pre-refactor services/auth/basic.go returned bare nil on UserSignIn error; pre-refactor routers/api/v1/user/user.go GetAuthenticatedUser always returned 200 with convert.ToUser(Doer, Doer) (nil -> null). The APIAuth middleware is applied to the whole v1 API (m.Use(context.APIAuth(group)) at routers/api/v1/api.go:627 in the parent tree). Later commits preserved the leak: 591f586bf1 (2023-09-12, KN4CK3R) only moved the middleware to routers/common, e8186f1c0f (2023-02-08) moved it to services/auth/middleware.go, f35850f48e (2025-02-17, wxiaoguang) mechanically renamed ctx.Error(401,'APIAuth',err) to ctx.APIError(401,err), 0403bd989f (2023) changed the wrong-password error to ErrUserPasswordInvalid (same uid-revealing semantics, clearer text).

round6_research.bug_semantics: Authentication bypass via unanchored regex in the public-endpoint matcher (CWE-287, critical): buildMatcherRegex compiles public no-auth route patterns with 'new RegExp(route)' (no ^ anchor) and matches() tests them against ctx.request.url, which includes the QUERY STRING. An unauthenticated attacker appends a public path as a query parameter (e.g. POST /api/global/users/search?x=/api/system/status) so an unanchored public-route regex matches inside the query string; the authenticated middleware then sets publicEndpoint=true and skips the 403 auth check, exposing protected routes (e.g. user search) without authentication.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Token-scope propagation flaw (CWE-441) in Gitea's own package registries (conan/container/nuget): package clients authenticate via JWT exchange endpoints (conan /v1/users/authenticate, container /token, nuget api-keys) that issue a 24h package authorization JWT (packageClaims{UserID}) without embedding or checking the caller's API-token scope. The JWT is exchanged once for read-only AND write operations, so a token scoped e.g. read:notification or read:package can mint a full-privilege package token and upload/delete packages (uploads succeed with any token because CreateAuthorizationToken carries no scope and reqPackageAccess' ApiTokenScope check is bypassed: conan/container auth routers never set store Data IsApiToken/ApiTokenScope from the exchange JWT, so the scope gate silently no-ops). Affected < 1.22.2.

records.details:
Because the hostname huggingface.co was pre-approved as a bare hostname for the WebFetch tool, any path on that domain—including attacker-controlled model repositories—was auto-approved without a permission prompt or being subject to --allowedTools restrictions. An attacker able to inject untrusted content into a Claude Code context could direct it to issue WebFetch requests against attacker-controlled repository files (e.g. /resolve/main/config.json), which HuggingFace counts as downloads server-side, creating a covert out-of-band channel for encoding and exfiltrating data Claude can access such as files, environment variables, or command output. Reliably exploiting this required the ability to add untrusted content into a Claude Code context window. Users on standard Claude Code auto-update have received this fix already; users performing manual updates are advised to update to the latest version.

Thank you to hackerone.com/novee for reporting this issue.
records.summary: Claude Code: Out-of-Band Data Exfiltration via Pre-Approved HuggingFace Domain in WebFetch

round6_research.bug_semantics: CWE-424 improper protection of alternate path: the AWS API MCP Server's file-access restriction (workdir confinement, default WORKING_DIRECTORY, and no-access mode; unrestricted opt-in) validates file:// and fileb:// path arguments only through the server-side parameter parser and, after aa937bb2, through a swapped-in validated RESTRICTED_URI_HANDLER (get_file_validated) registered on awscli's 'load-cli-arg' event. AWS CLI SHORTHAND syntax arguments (compact key-value lists parsed by awscli.shorthand.ShorthandParser, e.g. --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=file:///etc/passwd,...}]', --metadata 'key=file://...', or any argument containing embedded file:// inside shorthand) are expanded through awscli.shorthand.LOCAL_PREFIX_MAP, which still mapped file:// -> raw awscli get_file with NO validation. round6_research.bug_semantics: CWE-73/CWE-200 arbitrary local file read: IndexFile.remove() and Head.checkout() forward **kwargs into `git rm` (git/index/base.py remove: self.repo.git.rm(args, paths, **kwargs)) and `git checkout` (git/refs/head.py checkout: self.repo.git.checkout(self, **kwargs)) with no unsafe-option guard. round6_research.bug_semantics: Unhandled exception (anyio.ClosedResourceError) in the BaseSession._receive_loop of the MCP Python SDK streamable HTTP transport (src/mcp/shared/session.py). A client that deliberately triggers an exception after establishing a streamable HTTP session (e.g. abrupt disconnect) makes anyio.ClosedResourceError propagate out of the receive loop uncaught, crashing the server task group/process and requiring a restart - unauthenticated remote DoS (CVSS 4.0 7.1, VA:H). Affects PyPI mcp < 1.10.0; fixed in 1.10.0.
round6_research.evidence: Identity: class alias-9730a1c79594c67996690142 reconstructed by brute-force as {GHSA-j975-95f5-7wqh, CVE-2025-53365} (sha256 of sorted canonicalized members, validated formula against confirmed classes e90d1c05 and f593331f); class-repo-precise.jsonl=[github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk]. GHSA-j975-95f5-7wqh (aliases CVE-2025-53365, PYSEC-2026-1618): "MCP Python SDK has Unhandled Exception in Streamable HTTP Transport, Leading to Denial of Service", PyPI mcp < 1.10.0, reporter Rich Harang, refs PR #967 + commit 7b420656de48cfdb90b39eb582e60b6d55c2f891. Fix commit 7b420656 (David Dworken <dworken@anthropic.com>, committer GitHub noreply@github.com, 2025-06-16, message "Fix uncaught exception in MCP server (#967)", no trailers) wraps the receive loop in try/except anyio.ClosedResourceError + blanket except, and guards the finally-block stream sends. Introducer: root commit 4cbf8154 "Initial import" (David Soria Parra, 2024-09-24; the mcp_python repo initial commit, no parent). Introducer-authored vulnerable loop confirmed at 4cbf8154:mcp_python/shared/session.py lines 172-209 (bare async-for, no exception containment). AI-marker scan of the entire file lineage (git log --follow --format %an|%ae): all anthropic.com addresses are human employee emails (davidsp@, dworken@, inna@, camila@, basil@) - none is the cve-analyzer AI marker noreply@anthropic.com; no claude/codex/copilot/co-authored-by/generated-with trailers in introducer or fix.
round6_research.flaw_origin: The vulnerable receive-loop pattern - bare "async for message in self._read_stream:" inside an async-with over the streams with no outer exception containment - was first written in the very first commit of the repository, 4cbf8154306aa5b96b2bb3fc83ac5984d217a0f5 "Initial import" (David Soria Parra <davidsp@anthropic.com>, 2024-09-24) as mcp_python/shared/session.py, which is the root commit (no parent; introducer_parent_absent=true). The loop survived subsequent refactors (9d0f2dad #239 reorganize message handling, 719660446 revert of #282, 29c69e6a4 request-validation try/except) with no outer exception handler until the fix. Verified: fix parent 1eb1bba83c70c3121bce7fc0263e5fac2c3f0520 contains zero ClosedResourceError occurrences in session.py; blame at the fix parent shows line 336 async-for authored by 719660446 (Marcelo Trylesinski, 2025-03-14, revert commit) but the structurally identical loop existed since 4cbf8154 (grep of 4cbf8154:mcp_python/shared/session.py lines 172-209 shows the same unguarded loop).

records.details:
Claude Code failed to properly validate commands using piped sed operations with the echo command, allowing attackers to bypass file write restrictions. This vulnerability enabled writing to sensitive directories like the .claude folder and paths outside the project scope. Exploiting this required the ability to execute commands through Claude Code with the "accept edits" feature enabled.

Users on standard Claude Code auto-update received this fix automatically. Users performing manual updates are advised to update to the latest version.

Claude Code thanks hackerone.com/nil221 for reporting this issue!
records.summary: Claude Code Vulnerable to Command Injection via Piped sed Command Bypasses File Write Restrictions

round6_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated remote code execution via command injection in Coolify's CA certificate management feature (GHSA-7g97-c4xv-3cjx, affected < 4.0.0-beta.464). Any authenticated user with access to the server CA certificate management UI (app/Livewire/Server/CaCertificate/Show.php, saveCaCertificate -> writeCertificateToServer) could submit the CA certificate content which was interpolated verbatim into a remote shell command string: "echo '{$this->certificateContent}' > $caCertPath/coolify-ca.crt" passed to remote_process/instant_remote_process over SSH; appending shell metacharacters (e.g. a valid PEM followed by '; id > /tmp/pwned ; echo ') executed arbitrary commands as the configured SSH user (typically root or docker-group), giving complete compromise of the managed server. Fix (fe36b7068) base64-encodes the cert content before embedding it in the command (echo '<base64>' | base64 -d | tee ...) and re-exports the saved certificate through openssl_x509_export so only a normalized PEM (no shell metacharacters) is ever embedded; same pattern also hardened in app/Actions/Server/InstallDocker.php and app/Models/Server.php generateCaCertificate().
round6_research.evidence: IDENTITY: class id alias-9a0b10a5549fa1646a1f552b computed as sha256(member+'\n')[:24] and brute-force matched exactly one member from the 63-id cohort list for github.com/coollabsio/coolify: CVE-2026-27957 (advisories=1 matches the case row). OSV: summary 'Coolify: Authenticated RCE via command injection in CA certificate management feature'; details say any authenticated user can execute arbitrary commands as configured SSH user; affected prior to 4.0.0-beta.464; GIT range introduced 0, fixed e1f940dc229cd10538dac0e6f8d58b127cf424bc; alias GHSA-7g97-c4xv-3cjx (GitHub API 404 for raw advisory, OSV record confirmed). FIX: e1f940dc229cd10538dac0e6f8d58b127cf424bc is the v4.0.0-beta.464 release SQUASH merge (#8624, Merge: d29a9a280 11007771f); decomposed to the actual atomic fix commit fe36b706808d7427a5a710b2634aedc9578ba482 'chore: prepare for PR' (Andras Bacsai <5845193+andrasbacsai@users.noreply.github.com>, 2026-02-25, parent 12f8f80eb16c82397ba6e2993caf8bdd335bc163) which changed app/Livewire/Server/CaCertificate/Show.php (+12/-), app/Actions/Server/InstallDocker.php, app/Models/Server.php, database/seeders/CaSslCertSeeder.php and added tests/Feature/CaCertificateCommandInjectionTest.php (93 lines) covering the exploit string "$validCert.' ; id > /tmp/pwned ; echo '" through Livewire saveCaCertificate; the fix's diff replaces "echo '{$certificateContent}' > $caCertPath/coolify-ca.crt" with base64-encoded echo|base64 -d|tee in all three sites and re-exports the PEM via openssl_x509_export to strip injected metacharacters. BIC: git log origin/main --diff-filter=A -- app/Livewire/Server/CaCertificate/Show.php => 261a2fe564a3825d690daa216a025561fd5b4c79 'feat(ca-certificate): add CA certificate management functionality with UI integration and routing' (Andras Bacsai, 2025-05-29, 7 files, moves CA management UI out of app/Livewire/Server/Advanced.php into new CaCertificate/Show.php + show.blade.php + routes); pre-image at that commit contains line 117: "echo '{$this->certificateContent}' > $caCertPath/coolify-ca.crt" via writeCertificateToServer -> remote_process($commands, $this->server); PARENT ABSENCE verified: git cat-file -e 9d719009529aa8941f957d87a6a766141254449f:app/Livewire/Server/CaCertificate/Show.php => absent (rc=1), and parent has no echo-of-cert pattern for CA UI. Note the same echo pattern also exists from earlier commits with NON-user-controlled content: d6d1c9ad8 (2025-03-31) Server.php generateCaCertificate echoes app-generated SslCertificate content; 091530376 -> 7406ee67c (2025-01-31, peaklabs-dev) InstallDocker.php echoes auto-generated server cert; those are not the CVE entry point (the advisory + regression test target the user-supplied CA management form).

round6_research.bug_semantics: DoS via livelock: Concurrent::AtomicReference#update enters a permanent busy retry loop ('true until compare_and_set(...)') when the stored value is Float::NAN. The numeric CAS wrapper (numeric_cas_wrapper.rb) guards the underlying atomic swap with a Ruby equality pre-check ('return false unless old == expected'); since Float::NAN == Float::NAN is always false in Ruby, compare_and_set never succeeds and #update spins forever, repeatedly evaluating the caller's block (CPU burn / thread hang).
round6_research.evidence: OSV CVE-2026-54904 / GHSA-h8w8-99g7-qmvj ('AtomicReference#update livelocks when the stored value is Float::NAN', fixed in 1.3.7). BODY=ReadWriteLock is a fast and very useful utility, but it is non-reentrant and this
makes it unsuitable for some (well, a lot of) applications. You can never take an
exclusive lock without being 100% sure that you are not holding it already. If you
mess up, then game over. Your thread will deadlock hard and grind to a halt. Any
other thread which tries to take the exclusive lock will deadlock too.

When there are only a few sections of code which access a shared, mutable resource,
avoiding this scenario is not so hard. But when you have a lot of places where
locking is needed, and they call each other in complex ways, forget it. You WILL
get it wrong.

If you are building a library for other programmers to use, and you call into
"consumer" code with locks held, that's even worse. (Such as public API methods
which yield to a block...) You don't know what that "consumer" code will do. It
may call back into your library again.

AUTHOR=Joshua Young <djry1999@gmail.com>
SUBJECT=Fix `ReentrantReadWriteLock` read hold overflow into write-lock bit
BODY=The per-thread `@HeldCount` packs the read hold count into the low 15
bits and uses bit 15 as `WRITE_LOCK_HELD`. The reentrant paths in
`acquire_read_lock` and `try_read_lock` incremented `@HeldCount`
without bounding the read portion, so after 32,768 reentrant read
holds the count overflowed into `WRITE_LOCK_HELD`. A subsequent
`try_write_lock` or `acquire_write_lock` would then take the "already
hold a write lock" fast path and return true without setting
`RUNNING_WRITER`, silently violating write exclusivity.

Raise `ResourceLimitError` when the local read count would overflow,
matching how the cold path handles global reader exhaustion.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Ruby on Rails Action View tag helpers XSS via blank attribute names: tag_options()/tag_option() emit an attribute whenever the value is non-nil, without skipping blank (empty-string/nil) attribute names; ERB::Util.xml_name_escape('') returns an empty string, so tag('img', 'src' => '/nonexistent.png', '' => '/onerror=alert(1)') renders . The HTML tokenizer treats the unexpected '=' as a parse error, and the attacker-controlled attribute VALUE ("...") is then misparsed as a separate attribute name (onerror=...) - malformed HTML susceptible to mXSS (HackerOne report 3078929). Apps that let users specify custom HTML attributes are affected (CWE-79, cvss_v4 2.3).

round6_research.bug_semantics: Potential denial-of-service (algorithmic complexity, CWE-407) in django.utils.text.Truncator: TruncateHTMLParser.handle_endtag() used deque.remove(tag) to remove a tag from the stack on every end tag; with crafted HTML input containing a large number of unmatched end tags, each remove() triggers a linear full-stack scan, making overall runtime quadratic. Reported by Seokchan Yoon. Affects Django 4.2 < 4.2.28, 5.2 < 5.2.11, 6.0 < 6.0.2

round6_research.bug_semantics: Serialization injection (CWE-502). Serializable.toJSON() in langchain-core serializes free-form constructor kwargs without escaping plain objects that carry the internal 'lc' marker key (lc:1, type, id). When such JSON is later deserialized via load()/parse(), the trusting reviver interprets any object with the lc structure as a legitimate LangChain constructor/function/secret marker: it instantiates registered classes from the import map and substitutes values from the loader's SecretMap for {lc:1,type:'secret',id:[key]} entries. Attacker-controlled free-form data (e.g. message content/kwargs reaching JSON.stringify of a serialized graph) can therefore inject constructor or secret markers that, once the serialized payload is loaded by a downstream consumer, instantiate arbitrary registered constructors or exfiltrate the loader's secret values (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY). Affected @langchain/core <0.3.80 / <1.1.8 and langchain <0.3.37 / <1.2.3.
round6_research.evidence: OSV CVE-2025-68665 (aliases GHSA-r399-636x-v7f6): toJSON() did not escape objects with 'lc' keys when serializing free-form data in kwargs, so such keys are treated as legitimate LangChain objects during deserialization; patched in core 0.3.80/1.1.8, langchain 0.3.37/1.2.3. GIT ranges: introduced 822db857 (v1.0.0 release commit, 2025-10-20) and '0'; fixes listed de32b32b (version-packages release, 2025-12-22)/d0c905dd (release, 2026-08-14)/2954498b (docs commit; OSV artifact)/e5063f9c. Direct code fix: e5063f9c 'fix!(core/langchain): hardening for load (#9707)' (Hunter Lovell, 2025-12-22) adds libs/langchain-core/src/load/validation.ts (LC_ESCAPED_KEY='__lc_escaped__', needsEscaping/escapeObject) and rewires Serializable.toJSON() to run every kwarg through escapeIfNeeded BEFORE replaceSecrets/mapKeys, so plain objects containing an 'lc' key serialize as {"__lc_escaped__":{...}} and are returned as data by the loader. Pickaxe: first occurrence of replaceSecrets at f78b0c1f (reformat), first occurrence of the whole system at fb60a1a9 (git log --all --diff-filter=A langchain/src/load/index.ts -> fb60a1a9; parent 2835c133 lacks both load/index.ts and schema/load.ts, verified via git cat-file -e exit 128). Marker scan on introducer: author Nuno Campos <nuno@boringbits.io>, no trailers, no AI hints; on fix e5063f9c: no Co-authored-by lines either. First tag containing introducer: 0.0.1 (vulnerability present since the first release).
round6_research.flaw_origin: Human-authored foundational serde design. The entire serialization system - Serializable.toJSON() passing constructor arguments through unescaped and the load() reviver that trusts embedded serialized markers - was first written by Nuno Campos (LangChain co-founder) in commit fb60a1a9 (2023-05-26, 'Implement new serialization format...'); both langchain/src/load/index.ts and langchain/src/schema/load.ts are brand-new (A) in that commit and absent from its parent. The 2023-06-01 follow-up f78b0c1f ('Review serde format, implement secret management') renamed the marker from v:1/identifier to lc:1/id and added the secret marker type, but its parent already carried the identically-shaped vulnerable pass-through (v-format toJSON with unescaped arguments + trusting v-reviver), so f78b0c1f is a format change, not the first writer. Code lineage: langchain/src/schema/load.ts -> langchain-core/src/load/serializable.ts (via 2023 core split, 2025-08 rearrange acfaf7050, 2025-10 v1 main replacement 9e6eb913). Exploitability persisted until the Dec 2025 hardening.
round6_research.reasoning: The vulnerability's behavioral essence - serializer passthrough of untrusted free-form constructor data combined with a loader that trusts embedded marker objects (v-form, later lc-form - including the secret marker) - was first written on 2023-05-26 by human maintainer Nuno Campos, months before mainstream AI coding assistance existed and with zero AI markers on the introducing commit or its lineage. The 2023-06-01 serde review (f78b0c1f) that created the lc marker format is explicitly not the introducer because its parent already contained the same unfixed behavior under the v marker, failing the immediate-parent-lacks-it test. Fix-side commit carries no AI markers either (unlike many 2025-era fixes). No element of causal chain is AI-written: verdict NOT_AI.

round6_research.evidence: unserialize() in locutus assigns deserialized keys via plain bracket assignment (expectObject: obj[String(prop[0])] = value[0]; expectArrayItems: items[String(key[0])] = item[0] in src/php/var/unserialize.ts) with no __proto__/constructor/prototype filtering, so a PHP payload with __proto__ key triggers JS prototype setter -> property injection, for..in propagation, DoS via builtin method override. Sinks born in BIC dd073d6d2 'Unserialize reimplemented (#412)' (2020-09-28, Rafal Kukawski): reimplemented parser with expectObject/expectArrayItems using raw obj[prop[0]]=value[0] and items[key[0]]=item[0] (git show dd073d6d2:src/php/var/unserialize.js lines 257,334); parent 916f5b4f had older implementation with same raw-assignment pattern (val[kret[0]]=vret[0], readdata[key]=value) - advisory explicitly targets the new expectArrayItems/expectObject sinks. Renamed JS->TS in 977a1fb16 (2026-03-03, TS migration) with lines unchanged in behavior. Fix 345a6211 'fix: harden php prototype pollution sinks (#597)' (2026-03-25, Kevin van Zonneveld): adds DANGEROUS_UNSERIALIZE_KEYS = {__proto__, constructor, prototype} and setUnserializedProperty() routing dangerous keys through Object.defineProperty; also hardens parse_str; released 3.0.25 per advisory. GHSA-4mph-v827-f877/CVE-2026-33993, npm locutus < 3.0.25, medium. Distinct from earlier parse_str advisories (GHSA-f98m-q3hr-p5wq).

round6_research.bug_semantics: Apache Airflow XCom PATCH endpoint acceptance of forbidden keys: PATCH /api/v2/xcomEntries/{key} (XComUpdateBody model) never validates FORBIDDEN_XCOM_KEYS (reserved serialization keys: return_value, __classname__, etc.), unlike the POST create path (XComCreateBody validator added in #64148 as the CVE-2026-33858 fix). round6_research.bug_semantics: Replay of legitimately-signed policy snapshots (CWE-354 / CWE-347): ClearanceKit's on-disk policy store (/Library/Application Support/clearancekit/store.db, earlier user-policy.json) is signed with an EC-P256 key (System Keychain / Secure Enclave) and verified on load via PolicySigner, but the signed payload contains only the canonical row content with NO monotonic counter, version, or timestamp (freshness) binding. An attacker who can write store.db and the matching data_signatures row (feasible during the opfilter-update window when the Endpoint Security filter is offline, or via offline-boot / decrypted-backup scenarios) can substitute a previously captured legitimately-signed older snapshot; opfilter accepts it as fully valid on next boot because the ECDSA signatures still verify. Fixed in 5.0.10.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Filesystem path traversal family (CWE-22/CWE-697; LangChain < 1.3.9). (1) FilesystemFileSearchMiddleware (libs/langchain_v1/langchain/agents/middleware/file_search.py) validates only the starting base dir: glob_search runs base_full.glob(pattern) on an unchecked pattern (a '..' pattern like '../../etc/passwd' escapes the root; absolute patterns raise but are unhandled) and grep_search's _search_content walks base_full.rglob('*') following symlinked directories, so files outside root_path are enumerated/read and returned; results are only converted with relative_to(self.root_path) after the fact. (2) Anthropic tools middleware (libs/partners/anthropic/langchain_anthropic/middleware/anthropic_tools.py) _validate_path and _FilesystemClaudeFileToolMiddleware._full_path_from_virtual_path enforce allowed_prefixes with a raw string startswith(prefix) test (no segment boundary), so with prefix '/memories' the path '/memories2/evil.txt' passes; also path.startswith check in save tool has same boundary flaw. Fixed in 1.3.9 by dcaf7795: adds _is_within_root (resolve + is_relative_to) containment checks on glob matches and rg results, rejects patterns starting with '/' or containing '..' parts, replaces rglob with os.walk(followlinks=False), and adds _is_within_allowed_prefix segment-boundary comparison in anthropic middleware.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Stored XSS via improper CSP sandbox enforcement on webhook/HTTP responses: isHtmlRenderedContentType() decides whether the CSP sandbox header is applied by checking if the response content-type starts with 'text/html'/'application/xhtml+xml' on a toLowerCase()'d but NOT trimmed string. A content-type such as ' text/html' (leading whitespace, sent by a crafted Respond-to-Webhook node) fails the startsWith check, so no sandbox CSP is set; browsers still render the body as HTML, executing attacker-controlled script with same-origin privileges (session hijack/account takeover). Webhook-request-handler setCommonHeaders gates the CSP on '!contentType || isHtmlRenderedContentType(contentType)'.

BIC b5ab34fe7 (Ryan Melton, 2024-09-30, 'Switch to session token based auth') added SESSIONS_KEY check inside AuthModel.verify while set() already called verify(old_token) for old_password; parent a34e61ea exists and its verify() accepts only password/service-password hashes (no session tokens). The Argon2 refactor 55dc2740a (Ryan Pratt, 2025-12-09) preserved the same vulnerable no_password:false pass-through (pre-existing old_token line was merely renamed).
