round6_research.bug_semantics: Open redirect via protocol-relative (network-path) redirect target in google_sign_in gem (basecamp/google_sign_in, lib/google_sign_in/redirect_protector.rb). ensure_same_origin only origin-checks targets that match QUALIFIED_URL_PATTERN (scheme-required, \A#{URI::DEFAULT_PARSER.make_regexp}\z); any other non-blank target passes validation, and browsers resolve '//attacker.com/path' as a network-path reference, so proceed_to=//attacker.com after OAuth completes redirects the user off-site. Empirically verified with ruby -ruri: '//evil.com/path' =~ make_regexp => nil (so pre-2025-08-22 code raised no Violation), and '//evil.com/path' =~ URI::DEFAULT_PARSER.regexp[:ABS_PATH] => 0 (so the 2025-08-22 ABS_PATH allowance also admitted it).
round6_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-5jch-xhw4-r43v / CVE-2025-58067 (reported via HackerOne by muntrive, published 2025-08-29): google_sign_in gem < 1.3.1 open redirect via protocol-relative URI. Introducer 13dafac86203a8b1359070b6ea63caf23ab2e4ad (George Claghorn, 2018-08-29): git show confirms file creation with check 'target.blank? || (target =~ QUALIFIED_URL_PATTERN && origin_of(target) != origin_of(source))', raise Violation only then; parent cb62598697df70babff808582dd368de8ed729e3 has no lib/google_sign_in/redirect_protector.rb (parent-absence verified). Ruby empirical test: URI::DEFAULT_PARSER.make_regexp does NOT match '//evil.com/path' => no Violation => redirect allowed since 2018. Intermediate: a0548a604fb17e4eb1a57029f0d87e34e8499623 (2025-08-22) rewrote ensure_same_origin to allow 'target =~ URI::DEFAULT_PARSER.regexp[:ABS_PATH]' (empirically: '//evil.com/path' =~ ABS_PATH => 0), keeping the hole open in v1.3.0. Fix branch flavorjones/handle-invalid-paths: 9fd0605c87fdebb38682ab06323868b5e282ce0d (2025-08-28, first write of 'URI(target).host.nil? && !target.start_with?(//)' guard; verified ancestor of merged tip), refactored into c1b9c4d852104b41aac4fe667d8e29da6f908083 (2025-08-28, 'refactor: extract methods to give them names', url_origin?/absolute_path? with same guard), merged as PR #75 by e97aef4626b1bcbd2c6f01f7dd25f12ac855d4cc (Mike Dalessio, 2025-08-29); version bump e7f2a9ab59fe38020781560e8989f9697ace75c2 -> v1.3.1 same day. round6_research.bug_semantics: Potential SQL injection in FilteredRelation column aliases on PostgreSQL (django 4.2<4.2.27, 5.1<5.1.15, 5.2<5.2.9): a suitably crafted dictionary expanded as **kwargs into QuerySet.annotate()/alias() can smuggle a '$'-containing FilteredRelation alias; PostgreSQL columns aliases allow '$', and aliases are passed into join SQL unquoted, so attacker-controlled alias reaches raw SQL. Follow-up gap to CVE-2025-57833 (which banned '.' in aliases via Query.check_alias but not '$').
round6_research.evidence: OSV CVE-2025-13372 (aliases GHSA-rqw2-ghq9-44m7, PYSEC-2025-104): SQL injection in FilteredRelation column aliases on PostgreSQL, affected 4.2<4.2.27, 5.1<5.1.15, 5.2<5.2.9, reported by Stackered; OSV GIT fixed events point at release commits 5948e6657f/6ef1f6fbe3/c14b756185. Actual code fix: mainline 5b90ca1e75 (Jacob Walls, 2025-11-17, 'Fixed CVE-2025-13372 -- Protected FilteredRelation against SQL injection in column aliases on PostgreSQL', follow-up to CVE-2025-57833, reviewed by Simon Charette & Mariusz Felisiak) adds SQLCompiler.quote_name_unless_alias override in django/db/backends/postgresql/compiler.py raising ValueError when '$' in alias; backports 479415ce52 (5.2.x), 9c6a5bde24 (5.1.x), f997037b23 (4.2.x); no AI markers on fix messages. Introducer 01d440fa1e (2017, human, no co-author/AI markers) wrote the FilteredRelation alias plumbing; prior validation commits also human (93cae5cb2f CVE-2022-28346, 5171171709 CVE-2025-57833).
round6_research.flaw_origin: Vulnerable behavior originated with the FilteredRelation API itself: commit 01d440fa1e6b5c62acfa8b3fde43dfa1505f93c6 (Fixed #27332 -- Added FilteredRelation API for conditional join (ON clause) support, Nicolas Delaby, 2017-09-22) first let user-supplied alias strings flow into join clause SQL without quoting. Immediate parent 3f9d85d95cab228fd881ea952c707022e9e3bdf3 contains no FilteredRelation code (verified absent), so this is the minimum atomic introducer; later check_alias() validation (CVE-2022-28346 fix 93cae5cb2f, extended to add_filtered_relation by CVE-2025-57833 fix 5171171709) incompletely closed the gap, leaving '$' permitted, which CVE-2025-13372 then banned.
round6_research.reasoning: The injectable alias path is 2017-era Django ORM feature code by a human core contributor; the incomplete character-set bans ($) were human-authored security follow-ups, and the 2025 fix is a human security-team commit with no AI markers. None of the introducer, the intermediate validation commits, or the fix carry AI signatures -> NOT_AI.

partial_wave.bug_semantics: Merge node SQL query mode: user-supplied SQL query is executed via alasql (db.exec(query)) with no restriction on code-execution constructs; alasql supports CREATE FUNCTION, REQUIRE/yy.Require, utils.require and JavaScript engine so an authenticated user with workflow create/edit permissions can execute arbitrary code and write arbitrary files on the n8n server. Later hardening only blocked file FROM/INTO/engine handlers (79f1cca9af0, 9ce3ac092cf, 70c573c8822) but left code-exec vectors open until the final fix froze alasql.fn/yy and disabled utils.require/REQUIRE/yy.JavaScript.

File at n8n@2.9.2 (vulnerable) still calls db.exec(query) with only disableAlasqlFileAccess() which blocks file handlers but leaves CREATE FUNCTION/REQUIRE/utils.require/yy.JavaScript code-exec open. Fix: 062644ef786 (chore: Bundle 2026-W7 #26214, 2026-02-25, ancestor of n8n@2.9.3) adds disableUnsafeAccess/freezeAlasql freezing alasql.fn and yy, disabling utils.require, yy.Require.prototype.execute, yy.JavaScript and REQUIRE fn handler; prior partial hardening commits were human (Michael Kret #20858, mfsiega #24082/#24907).
partial_wave.flaw_origin: Merge node v3 overhaul (#9528) introduced the combineBySql mode writing db.exec(query) directly on user-controlled query text with zero sandboxing; alasql's file/code-exec capabilities were fully reachable from day one.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Missing hostname canonicalization: loopback classification used exact match h === "localhost" without stripping trailing dots, so a hostile remote-CDP discovery response returning localhost. (absolute-form, resolves to loopback) bypassed the remote-CDP loopback protection and let a non-loopback profile pivot the follow-up connection onto a localhost-resolving endpoint (CWE-20/CWE-639).
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-fh32-73r9-rgh5/CVE-2026-41372 (severity medium, affected <=2026.4.1, patched >=2026.4.2) lists fix commit 9c22d636697 (PR #59236, 2026-04-02): adds canonicalHost = normalizedHost.replace(/\.+$/, "") before the === "localhost" check in parseHostForAddressChecks (src/gateway/net.ts). git log -S "h === "localhost"" -- src/browser/cdp.ts (reverse chronological, tail): first appearance is bd8a0a9f8f4 "feat: add remote CDP browser support" (2026-01-01, author Peter Steinberger), which added isLoopbackHost to cdp.ts (lines 22-31) with exact-match h === "localhost" (plus 127.0.0.1/0.0.0.0/::1/:: variants), used by normalizeCdpWsUrl. Parent 73d0e2cb81 has src/browser/cdp.ts (git ls-tree blob 2d2c5523d2) but git grep for h === "localhost" in it returns rc=1 (absent). Raw commit content has no trailers, no Co-Authored-By, no AI markers. The check itself was first written in 208ba02a4a6 (config.ts, clawd browser control) but only reached a security decision on the CDP host path with remote CDP support (bd8a0a9f8f4).
round6_research.flaw_origin: isLoopbackHost exact-match check written into the remote-CDP path (src/browser/cdp.ts) in the remote CDP browser support commit; pattern copied from the same-named helper in src/browser/config.ts from the earlier clawd browser control commit, which predates remote CDP discovery and is not the advisory path. Later commits (8d75a496bf5 centralize utilities #12926, 28b8101eef7 IPv6 loopback auth, b02b94673f4 dedupe flows) only moved/reformed the same non-normalizing check into parseHostForAddressChecks (src/gateway/net.ts) where the fix landed.
round6_research.reasoning: Atomic introducer of the vulnerable behavior (loopback classification of CDP hosts without trailing-dot canonicalization, feeding the remote-CDP protection decision) is bd8a0a9f8f4 by Peter Steinberger; the identical flawed exact-match pattern predates it in config.ts (208ba02a4a6) but that path is not reachable by the advisory attack (requires remote CDP discovery). Parent verified absent of the check. Fix author mappel-nv with human co-author Jacob Tomlinson (NVIDIA colleague; Co-authored-by trailer is not an AI-tool marker). No AI authorship signal anywhere on the introduces; closed causal chain to a human developer.

round6_research.bug_semantics: TracingMiddleware: arbitrary server-side file read. round6_research.bug_semantics: Denial of service via improper handling of length-parameter inconsistency (CWE-770 / CWE-20): MemoryFileUploadHandler.new_file() activates the in-memory upload path based solely on the declared Content-Length ('self.activated = content_length <= settings.FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE'). In ASGI deployments Content-Length is not guaranteed to reflect the actual body size (absent with Transfer-Encoding: chunked, or understated), so an unauthenticated attacker can upload an arbitrarily large file that is buffered fully in memory (bypassing FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE and the memory-budget expectation), causing service degradation / DoS. Affects Django 5.2 (<5.2.14) and 6.0 (<6.0.5); fixed 2026-05-05 security release.
round6_research.evidence: Identity: hash reversal over plan pool -> {CVE-2026-5766, GHSA-w26r-rmm8-9c29} (aliases PYSEC-2026-54, BIT-django-2026-5766; PyPI django introduced 5.2/6.0, fixed 5.2.14/6.0.5; advisory: ASGI requests with missing/understated Content-Length bypass FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE, reported by Kyle Agronick). Fix: 5a89e341 (2026-03-24, Jacob Walls, 'Fixed CVE-2026-5766 -- Enforced DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE in MemoryFileUploadHandler on ASGI.', with human Co-authored-by Natalia/nessita): replaces the header-based gate with an actual stream-size determination (seek to end, fall back to Content-Length only for non-seekable streams), backports ad8f9e19 [6.0.x] and 2ec27eda [5.2.x]; committed 6 weeks before the 2026-05-05 security release with docs/tests. No AI markers (regex) on fix or its message. Introducer d725cc97 (2008-07-01): FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE-gated in-memory handler activation first written here; 2008 django core commit by human (Jacob Kaplan-Moss), pre-AI; parent verified to lack file and any equivalent gating. All three commits (d725cc97, 5a89e341, backports) contain only human trailers.
round6_research.flaw_origin: Introduced by d725cc97 (2008-07-01, 'Fixed #2070: refactored Django's file upload capabilities.', Jacob Kaplan-Moss): this commit created django/core/files/uploadhandler.py and with it the MemoryFileUploadHandler activation gate 'if content_length > settings.FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE: self.activated = False' (later 'self.activated = content_length <= FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE'), i.e. the first writer of the behavior of trusting the Content-Length parameter to decide memory-vs-temp buffering. The immediate parent ef76102e lacks the file entirely (cat-file 128 -> introducer_parent_absent=true) and its pre-refactor wsgi.py used CONTENT_LENGTH only to size a LimitedStream (django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:165-170), not as a memory-vs-disk decision input; file-scoped pickaxe -S 'FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE' on uploadhandler.py returns only d725cc97 plus two 2008 svn branch merges (0e8710d5, bc3d6b49, non-original). The ASGI request path added in Django 3.0 (2019) later made the header untrustworthy (reachability change), but did not rewrite the flawed gate; the gate stood unchanged until the 2026 fix.
round6_research.reasoning: The flawed behavior - gating in-memory upload buffering on the untrusted Content-Length parameter - was first written in 2008 by a human Django core developer (Jacob Kaplan-Moss) in the upload-handler refactor (#2070); parent verifiably lacks both the file and equivalent logic. It survived byte-similar for 18 years and was fixed in 2026 by human core developers with no AI markers. ASGI adoption (2019) changed reachability, not the flawed logic's authorship -> NOT_AI.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Command injection in the git-mcp-server MCP tool suite: tool logic files (git_add, git_init, git_clone, git_cherry_pick, git_rebase, etc.) build shell command strings by interpolating user-controlled inputs (targetPath resolved from input.path, filesArg, branch names, messages, etc.) and execute them via promisified child_process.exec. Because exec runs through the shell, shell metacharacters (|, >, &&, ;, $(...)) in inputs are interpreted, so a malicious or prompt-injected MCP client gains arbitrary command execution as the server user. Representative line: `const command = \`git -C "${targetPath}" add -- ${filesArg}\`; await execAsync(command)`. Fixed in v2.1.5.

round6_research.bug_semantics: DoS (process crash, std::terminate) on SBI POST /namf-evts/v1/subscriptions (EventExposure) when request body lacks the 'subscription' field. Chain: auto-generated model from_json (AmfCreateEventSubscription) does unguarded j.at("subscription") -> throws nlohmann::detail::out_of_range; generated handler create_subscription_handler catches std::exception and calls handleParsingException, which is noexcept and rethrows via 'throw ex;' (ex bound to const std::exception&, so the rethrow slices to static type std::exception); the catch(nlohmann::detail::exception&) inside therefore never matches -> exception escapes noexcept -> std::terminate -> whole AMF process dies -> DoS. CWE-20, CVSS 7.5, advisory credits PoC from swallele/Vulnerability verified against oai-amf v1.4.0 (json_dos_poc.py).
round6_research.evidence: Introducer: 50003832 'First version for AMFEventExposure API/Impl' (2021-08-16, Tien-Thinh Nguyen <Tien-Thinh.Nguyen@eurecom.fr>) created src/sbi/amf_server/api/SubscriptionsCollectionDocumentApiEventExposure.cpp whose create_subscription_handler contains nlohmann::json::parse(request.body()).get_to(amfCreateEventSubscription) and handleParsingException(const std::exception& ex) const noexcept { try { throw ex; } catch (nlohmann::detail::exception& e){...} } (git log -S 'throw ex' -> only 50003832). Parent dc968a36 (2021-08-16, same author, 'Add new model data for EventExposure') created model src/sbi/amf_server/model/AmfCreateEventSubscription.cpp with from_json = j.at("subscription").get_to(...) and validate(); verified 0 EventExposure api/impl files at dc968a36^ and 0 at 50003832^ (introducer_parent_absent). Handler was dead code at 50003832 (AMFApiServer.hpp had no EventExposure member); wiring ddcaaab0 'Associate EventExposure with AMF App' (2021-08-16) + impl a4d4a12e (2021-09-06, same author) made the vulnerable route reachable; at v2.0.1 the route is served by the HTTP1 Pistache server (amf_http1_server.cpp: m_subscriptionsCollectionDocumentApiImplEventExposure->init()), and at HEAD the HTTP1 server (started whenever support_features.http_version==1, the default) still wires it with the unmodified vulnerable handler. Fix: 8ec08786 'fix: Improve stability and robustness of AMF' (2026-07-22, Tien-Thinh Nguyen; parent 89e15886 verified to lack parse_json_body; git log -S 'parse_json_body' -> only 8ec08786) adds never-throw sbi_helper parse_json_body and refactors amf_http2_server.cpp EventExposure subscriptions route (returns BAD_REQUEST instead of crashing); not in any release tag (v2.1.0-v2.2.1), consistent with advisory affected 'AMF<=v2.0.1' because the HTTP2 route (only available post-v2.0.1) already caught std::exception -> 400 without crashing pre-fix. No AI markers on introducer chain (git log --format=%N empty for dc968a36/50003832/ddcaaab0/a4d4a12e; all Tien-Thinh Nguyen, EURECOM, 2021, pre-AI-assistant era for this project).
round6_research.flaw_origin: Auto-generated OpenAPI Generator code: (1) generated model accessors use unguarded nlohmann .at() (throws out_of_range on missing key) in from_json; (2) generated Pistache handler's handleParsingException rethrows a reference in a noexcept function, string-slicing the concrete nlohmann exception to std::exception so its own catch clauses can never match. Introduced with the first EventExposure API/model code (2021).
round6_research.reasoning: The minimum atomic introducer of the vulnerable behavior is 50003832 (first writer of the crashable handler: unguarded parse().get_to() + exception-slicing rethrow in noexcept), with the unguarded model from_json (dc968a36) as co-introduced component; parent-absence verified at both. The 2026 fix commit 8ec08786 carries explicit 'Assisted-by: Claude Sonnet 4.6 / Claude Opus 4.6 / ChatGPT Codex 5.4' trailers, but AI involvement on the fix side never flips a verdict; the flawed code was written by a human in 2021. round6_research.remaining_gap: Advisory scope '<=v2.0.1' matches release timing (HTTP2 route only exists post-v2.0.1 and was non-crashing pre-fix), but the HTTP1 Pistache EventExposure route remains wired with the unchanged vulnerable generated handler at HEAD for http_version==1 deployments; whether maintainers consider HTTP1 deprecated/unsupported is not documented in the advisory. round6_research.bug_semantics: Branch deletion permission bypass after merging a pull request (CWE-284 improper access control): when a PR is merged with 'delete branch after merge' set (form.DeleteBranchAfterMerge), both the web handler (routers/web/repo/pull.go MergePullRequest -> deleteBranch) and the API handler (routers/api/v1/repo/pull.go MergePullRequest) call repo_service.DeleteBranch on the HEAD repo with no write-permission check on that repo. DeleteBranch (services/repository/branch.go) only checks default-branch and protected-branch status, never whether the acting user can write to the head repo. A user who can merge a PR into the base repo (write on base) but has no write access to the head repo (e.g., the PR head is a fork owned by another user) can then delete the head branch in that fork. The pre-existing manual delete-branch-after-merge button (CleanUpPullRequest in routers/web/repo/pull.go) DID enforce perm.CanWrite(models.UnitTypeCode) on the head repo; the automatic path added by #16049 skipped that check entirely. Fixed by extracting repo_service.CanDeleteBranch (perm.CanWrite(unit.TypeCode) plus default/protected checks) and gating both merge flows on it.
round6_research.evidence: OSV GHSA-rrcw-5rjv-vj26 (aliases CVE-2025-68940, GO-2025-4267, BIT-gitea-2025-68940): summary 'Gitea doesn't adequately enforce branch deletion permissions after merging a pull request', CVSS 3.1 AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N, Go package code.gitea.io/gitea, SEMVER range introduced 0, fixed 1.22.5; refs PR go-gitea/gitea#32654, release v1.22.5. Fix commit 17053e953f697ba21e067f1ad7715b18e07e273b (Lunny Xiao, 2024-12-03, 'Fix delete branch perm checking (#32654)') extracts repo_service.CanDeleteBranch — adds access_model.GetUserRepoPermission + perm.CanWrite(unit.TypeCode) on top of the default/protected-branch checks — reuses it inside DeleteBranch, gates the web and API delete-after-merge blocks on CanDeleteBranch, skips deletion for agit flow (pr.Flow != PullRequestFlowGithub), and adds integration test 'merging with no permission to delete branch'; backported as 0d1fc2b2e9 (#32707) into v1.22.5. Verified: fix is ancestor of HEAD; introducer 78118a3b02 is ancestor of fix; introducer parent 46a4c683 has no DeleteBranchAfterMerge (git grep -c exit=1) so delete-after-merge cannot be triggered before #16049.
round6_research.flaw_origin: Introduced by commit 78118a3b029ee4eb140d47be22e86df17253a786 (2021-07-13, Jimmy Praet <jimmy.praet@telenet.be>, 'Add checkbox to delete pull branch after successful merge (#16049)') which added the DeleteBranchAfterMerge handling to both web and API MergePullRequest paths, calling repo_service.DeleteBranch on the head repo without the head-repo write-permission check the pre-existing manual CleanUpPullRequest path performed. Verified at the immediate parent 46a4c6835daf4642074bb1a18a3210b03a64259b: git grep -c DeleteBranchAfterMerge (repo-wide and in routers/api/v1/repo/pull.go) exits 1 (absent), and the parent CleanUpPullRequest enforces GetUserRepoPermission(headRepo, user) + perm.CanWrite(models.UnitTypeCode) before deleting. git log -S DeleteBranchAfterMerge --all confirms 78118a3b02 as the oldest commit containing the string. Introducer is a single-parent commit (git cat-file -p shows 1 parent), not a squash/merge.
round6_research.reasoning: Atomic introducer of the vulnerable behavior is 78118a3b02 (#16049, 2021-07-13): it is both the first writer of the automatic delete-branch-after-merge code path (web and API) and the commit that dropped the head-repo write check that the manual CleanUpPullRequest path retained. Parent 46a4c683 is clean (feature absent, exit=1), so no earlier commit introduced this gap. The commit is authored by human maintainer Jimmy Praet with a human co-authored-by trailer (Andrew Thornton); marker regex' single hit is that human trailer, i.e., zero genuine AI signals. The fix (#32654, Lunny Xiao, 2024-12-03) restores authorization, only reaches v1.22.5 via backport, and carries no AI markers either. No AI authorship anywhere on the vulnerable lines; the flaw is a classic human-designed feature gap (new convenience feature omitted the authorization check the adjacent manual path had).

round6_research.bug_semantics: Arbitrary code execution from fork pull requests via insecure CI workflow (CWE-94 / GitHub Actions pwn-request class). .github/workflows/ci.yml triggers on pull_request_target (privileged context with repository-write GITHUB_TOKEN, permissions: pull-requests: write) and job2 'Lint Markdown' checks out the untrusted PR head (actions/checkout ref: github.event.pull_request.head.sha) and runs 'run: npx markdownlint-cli ${{ needs.job1.outputs.markdown_files }} --ignore node_modules' where both the executed script (npx resolves node_modules/.bin/markdownlint-cli from the attacker's checkout) and the interpolated filename list are attacker-controlled. A malicious fork PR can execute arbitrary code with the workflow's write permissions: steal credentials/steps context, post comments, push code, create releases.
round6_research.evidence: Identity resolved by hash reversal: size-1 match CVE-2026-22869 in the 2-id pool {CVE-2025-68952, CVE-2026-22869} (case metadata advisories=1). Direct fix commit 102a864d by Cole Murray (2026-01-12, parent a1efe01a): splits lint-markdown into its own workflow using pull_request (read-only, no secrets) instead of pull_request_target, pins markdownlint-cli@0.43.0, upgrades checkout@v4/github-script@v7/paths-filter@v3; message documents attack vector (malicious node_modules/.bin/markdownlint-cli in fork PR executes under repo-write token). Introducer f6dd4268: root commit (no parents), author=committer CamelAIorg <camel@eigent.ai>, 2025-07-29, message 'initial commit', no trailers, no AI markers; ci.yml at that commit verified to contain on: pull_request_target, permissions pull-requests: write, and job2 with head.sha checkout + markdownlint run. round6_research.flaw_origin: Repo-founding workflow design. The vulnerable ci.yml (pull_request_target trigger + job2 checking out the PR head sha and executing markdownlint on PR-controlled filenames) was present in the very first commit of the repository, f6dd4268 (2025-07-29, root commit by the CamelAIorg organization account, camel@eigent.ai). partial_wave.bug_semantics: Use-after-free (CWE-416) in the MSL decoder: ReadMSLImage/ProcessMSLScript parse the script from the input blob held by the MSL image (msl_image->blob) via a libxml2 push parser, but the MSL coder had the default CoderBlobSupportFlag so the caller could hand it a live in-memory blob whose lifetime is not tied to the parser; script-triggered image list operations can free the blob memory while the SAX parser is still consuming it, yielding a use-after-free (crash reported via Magick.NET reading MSL from byte arrays).
partial_wave.evidence: GHSA-5r4x-w6p5-222q / CVE-2026-46523 (2026-05, Magick.NET, fixed 14.13.1): use-after-free in MSL decoder. Fix 4d92249c84 (2026-05-13, Cristy, message = advisory URL) is a one-liner in RegisterMSLImage: entry->flags^=CoderBlobSupportFlag (coders/msl.c:7588); since AcquireMagickInfo defaults flags to CoderAdjoinFlag | CoderBlobSupportFlag (MagickCore/magick.c:188) the XOR removes blob support, and GetMagickBlobSupport()/OpenBlob then route blob inputs through a temp file instead of parsing from live blob memory (MagickCore/blob.c:835, 2543). The MSL coder has parsed script chunks from the blob via xmlParseChunk since the repository root commit 3ed852eea (2009-09-05, cristy, initial import, human; coders/msl.c:7527-7540 at root). No AI markers.
partial_wave.flaw_origin: The MSL coder was written in the original import parsing the script straight from the blob stream with no temp-file indirection; the 2026 fix clears CoderBlobSupportFlag (flags^=) so GetMagickBlobSupport() returns false and blob inputs are spooled to a stable temporary file before parsing, decoupling blob lifetime from the XML parser.
partial_wave.reasoning: The blob-lifetime hazard in the MSL coder was written by human maintainer cristy in the original 2009 import. NOT_AI.

round6_research.bug_semantics:
Reflected XSS in the OAuth callback page (CWE-79): create_callback_html() in src/fastmcp/client/oauth_callback.py composes the callback HTML page via f-string interpolation of message, title, and server_url with no HTML escaping (e.g., the template contains
{message}
and Connected to: {server_url}). The /callback route handler reads the error and error_description query parameters and passes f'OAuth Error: {error}
{error_desc}' as the message, so GET /callback?error= on the localhost callback server executes attacker-controlled JS in the callback page's origin (reflected XSS, CVSS 4.0 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:P/SC:L/SI:L). A malicious OAuth authorization server can trigger it automatically by returning the crafted URL in authorization_endpoint, which the client then opens in the browser. Fixed in 2.13.0 by adding html.escape() to the shared UI helpers (utilities/ui.py create_page/create_status_message/create_info_box/create_detail_box) and removing the raw {server_url} interpolation.
round6_research.evidence: OSV GHSA-mxxr-jv3v-6pgc (aliases CVE-2025-62800, PYSEC-2026-1364): PyPI package fastmcp, ECOSYSTEM range introduced 0, fixed 2.13.0; summary 'FastMCP vulnerable to reflected XSS in client's callback page'; CVSS 4.0 AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:P/VC:N/VI:N/VA:N/SC:L/SI:L/SA:N; refs github.com/jlowin/fastmcp/pull/2090 and commit 2a20f54617a37213ed83894a8c2f0ac38a2e83a3. Advisory PoC: start an OAuth client with the callback server, then GET http://localhost:1337/callback?error=<img/src/onerror=alert(window.origin)>; also triggerable via a malicious authorization_endpoint returned by a rogue auth server. Verified in the repo clone: c438987d (file creation) already contains the unescaped {message}/{title}/{server_url} template and the error/error_description wiring; fix 2a20f54617 is ancestor of HEAD; introducer c438987d is ancestor of fix; parent 67c36b0c has no create_callback_html (exit=1).
round6_research.flaw_origin:
Introduced by commit c438987d4ea93305ff64790132bfb870c453e91c ('Add callback server', 2025-05-30, Jeremiah Lowin) which created src/fastmcp/client/oauth_callback.py: create_callback_html already embedded message/title/server_url unescaped (verified at c438987d: template line
{message}
, and the handle_callback route wiring error/error_description query params straight into create_callback_html's message argument). Immediate parent 67c36b0c110667d041d98bc74488e15fa3e5e1df has no create_callback_html anywhere (git grep -c exit=1). Single-parent commit (git cat-file -p shows 1 parent), not a squash/merge. The unescaped sink persisted through later refactors (b46d4934 'Add comprehensive OAuth 2.1 authentication system with WorkOS integration (#1327)' moved the page construction into utilities/ui.py helpers which also interpolated without escaping) until PR #2090.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Broken Access Control (IDOR/BOLA, CWE-284/CWE-639). In FastGPT's chat auth helper authChatCrud, the team-token authentication path (spaceTeamId+teamToken) validates only the team token via authTeamSpaceToken and never verifies that the requested appId belongs to that team. A valid team token from ANY authenticated team combined with a foreign appId grants cross-tenant access and execution of private AI application workflows (authenticated user of team A executes / reads chats of team B's apps). The credential check was dropped in the V4.8.14 rewrite of chat context execution: pre-rewrite code bound chat.teamId === spaceTeamId; post-rewrite, chat lookup is MongoChat.findOne({appId, chatId, outLinkUid}) with no team filter, and with no chatId the function returns a fully authorized teamDomain response for an unchecked appId.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Missing authorization (CWE-862): owner-enforced slash commands (/send, /config, /debug) executable by any sender on channels with wildcard or empty allowFrom (e.g. allowFrom ['*']) when no explicit commands.ownerAllowFrom is configured. Gate: isAuthorizedSender = commandAuthorized && isOwner, where isOwner = !isWhatsAppSurface || allowAll || ownerList.length === 0 || senderE164 in ownerList; with a wildcard allowFrom the owner candidate list is empty (entries '*' are filtered out), so ownerList.length === 0 / allowAll make isOwner true and the command passes. Affects released versions <= 2026.4.20; fixed 2026.4.21.

[]).filter(e => e && e !== '*'). Parent-absence: git grep 'ownerList.length === 0' and 'isOwner' at parent 1bad96aa2b rc=1 (no owner gate concept; isAuthorizedSender = commandAuthorized). Release-line port 995febb7b1e811ff6a1df5b18c22de94103f4c9f (same subject); f788c88b is docs/release-notes only. round6_research.bug_semantics: Path traversal in EverOS POST /api/v1/memory/add ingestion endpoint (CVE-2026-58499 / GHSA-c795-2g9c-j48m, affected <= 1.0.0, fixed 1.0.1). The per-message sender_id field was a plain unvalidated str (min_length=1) in src/everos/entrypoints/api/routes/memorize.py (MessageItemDTO), unlike app_id/project_id which already enforced the path-safe charset + reserved-token rejection (PathSafeId AfterValidator). During user-memory extraction, sender_id flows to owner_id/scope_id, and BaseDailyWriter._resolve_path joins it directly into the episode markdown path: <memory_root>/<app>/<project>/users/<scope_id>/episodes/episode-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md, written by MarkdownWriter via anyio.Path(...).mkdir + os.replace with no containment check. A sender_id containing ../ sequences therefore directs the write outside the memory root, letting an unauthenticated caller create or overwrite .md files at any location writable by the server process, with partially attacker-influenced content. Fix (a10cdcd, v1.0.1, PR #290): (1) sender_id now uses PathSafeId with pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9_.@+-]+$ plus . / .. token rejection; (2) defense-in-depth MarkdownWriter._ensure_within_root in core/persistence/markdown/writer.py rejecting any write target resolving outside memory root (covers write and append read-modify-write paths), raising PathTraversalError mapped to HTTP 400; regression tests added (test_memorize_route_validation.py, test_writer.py).

round6_research.bug_semantics: Replay-protection bypass / verified replay identity drift (CWE-294/CWE-345) in the Plivo V2 webhook verification path (extensions/voice-call/src/webhook-security.ts): validatePlivoV2Signature authenticates base-URL-without-query + nonce, but the replay-protection key was derived from the FULL verificationUrl including the query string (plivo:v2:sha256Hex(verificationUrl + nonce)), so unsigned query-only variants of the same signed request mint a new verifiedRequestKey and are treated as fresh verified work instead of replays. An attacker holding one valid captured signed request can re-submit arbitrary query-only variants to re-trigger verified side effects. CVSS 4.0 6.9 (VI:H). Fixed in v2026.3.23.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Role-restriction bypass / missing authorization check (CWE-863; GHSA-4phw-6824-6cfp = CVE-2026-33551, CVSS 3.1 3.5 LOW, NVD published 2026-04-10, OSSA-2026-005 reported 2026-04-07 by Maxence Bornecque of Orange Cyberdefense; affects keystone >=14.0.0 <26.1.1 and ==27.0.0/28.0.0/29.0.0, first_patched 26.1.1): keystone application credentials carry an 'unrestricted' flag (originally 'allow_application_credential_creation'); a RESTRICTED app credential may only be used for operations its limited role set (e.g. reader) permits, and its token records auth method 'application_credential'. The EC2 credential endpoints (POST /v3/users/{user_id}/credentials/OS-EC2, DELETE /v3/users/{user_id}/credentials/OS-EC2/{credential_id}) predate application credentials (keystone/contrib/ec2/controllers.py since 2012) and never received the _check_unrestricted_application_credential guard that the application-credential create/delete endpoints had from the start. Their only enforcement is the pre-existing policy identity:ec2_create_credential = RULE_ADMIN_OR_OWNER, which any token owner passes for their own IDs. An authenticated user holding only a reader role but owning a restricted app credential can authenticate with it and mint EC2/S3 credentials bound to the FULL parent user; those EC2 credentials carry the parent user's complete S3 permissions, bypassing the role restriction (reader escalates to full-user S3 access). The fix adds the unrestricted guard to EC2 create/delete and tightens both policies to a new ADMIN_OR_MEMBER_AND_CRED_OWNER rule so reader-role tokens can no longer mutate EC2 credentials at all.

partial_wave.bug_semantics: In DuplexFramingMiddleware, SingletonFramingMiddleware, and RawStream, the framing handshake read loops invoked PipeReader.ReadAsync without checking readResult.IsCompleted or passing a cancellation token. When a client closed the connection after sending only the preamble, subsequent ReadAsync calls returned synchronously with an empty buffer and IsCompleted=true; because buffer.Length == 0, the inner loop was skipped and the outer loop spun in a 100% CPU infinite loop ignoring handshake timeouts.

records.details:
### Summary

A vulnerability in the Linux kernel's algif_aead subsystem (CVE-2026-31431, "copy.fail") allows an unprivileged container workload to corrupt arbitrary file page-cache pages via the AF_ALG crypto interface and splice(). On Talos Linux, this vulnerability can be chained into a complete node compromise: an attacker who can schedule a pod on a worker node can, without any elevated Kubernetes permissions, achieve arbitrary code execution as root on the host (by poisoning a binary inside a privileged pod, or poisoning a binary which runs with elevated privileges like a CNI binary), access host filesystem, including node secrets.

The exploit does not require kernel debugging, race conditions, or any prior privileges beyond the ability to create a pod.

### Impact

An attacker with the ability to deploy a Kubernetes pod on an affected node can:

1. Corrupt the page-cache of /usr/sbin/nft in the containerd snapshot layer shared between the attacker's pod and the kube-proxy DaemonSet. Because containerd reuses XFS page-cache pages across overlayfs mounts sharing the same lower layer, the corruption is immediately visible to all containers using that image layer — including privileged system DaemonSets.
2. Execute arbitrary code inside kube-proxy — a privileged DaemonSet running on every node with all Linux capabilities (privileged: true) and host network access — the next time kube-proxy invokes nft as part of its nftables reconciliation loop (typically within seconds).
3. At this point, an attacker achieved code execution inside a privileged pod, which allows to escape to the host.
4. Same attack can be planted by infiltrating other binaries running as privileged, for example a CNI plugin.

### Patches

Upgrade to Talos v1.13.0 or Talos v1.12.7 which ships Linux kernel 6.18.25. The kernel fix for CVE-2026-31431 (algif_aead in-place optimization revert) was committed upstream in Linux 6.18.22 and is included in all Talos releases from v1.13.0 and Talos 1.12.7 onwards.

### Workarounds

There are multiple workarounds available based on the situation, but we really recommend to upgrade.

#### Option 1 - Change kernel arguments

Add a kernel argument with `initcall_blacklist=algif_aead_init` by upgrading Talos to the same version.

> Note: this either requires setting `machine.kernel.extraKernelArgs` if using BIOS based boot or upgrading with a new image from factory/imager generated image by setting the extra kernel args. See [Boot Assets](https://docs.siderolabs.com/talos/v1.13/platform-specific-installations/boot-assets)

#### Option 2 - Deploy all workload pods with a seccomp profile denying creating `AF_ALG` socket creation

`patch.yaml`

```yaml
machine:
 seccompProfiles:
 - name: copy-fail-block.json
 value:
 defaultAction: SCMP_ACT_ALLOW
 syscalls:
 - names:
 - socket
 action: SCMP_ACT_ERRNO
 args:
 - index: 0
 value: 38
 op: SCMP_CMP_EQ
```

Apply this patch to all machines in the cluster and set this for all the pod spec:

```yaml
...
spec:
 securityContext:
 seccompProfile:
 type: Localhost
 localhostProfile: profiles/copy-fail-block.json
```

#### Option 3 - Block the syscall in runtime with a eBPF program

See [copy-fail-blocker](https://github.com/cozystack/copy-fail-blocker), this can be applied to a running system without a reboot, but it has to run before any other workloads are scheduled after a reboot.

### References

* https://copy.fail/
* https://xint.io/blog/copy-fail-linux-distributions
* https://github.com/theori-io/copy-fail-CVE-2026-31431
* https://github.com/Percivalll/Copy-Fail-CVE-2026-31431-Kubernetes-PoC

round6_research.bug_semantics: Transport-security flaw (CWE-319) in the OpenClaw Android gateway client: non-loopback remote gateway endpoints were accepted and connected over cleartext ws:// (the scheme picked 'wss' only when a TLS config was present, with no loopback/emulator exemption logic and no TLS requirement for remote hosts), and the client sent STORED gateway credentials (token/password loaded from SecurePrefs) over that unencrypted connection. Discovery beacons or forged setup codes could thereby steer the client onto an attacker-controlled cleartext remote endpoint, disclosing stored credentials in plaintext. Affected <= 2026.4.1 (npm openclaw), fixed >= 2026.4.2.
round6_research.evidence: Identity: member_map pin CVE-2026-40045 + GHSA-83f3-hh45-vfw9 (OSV valid: 'OpenClaw: Android accepted cleartext remote gateway endpoints and sent stored credentials over ws://'; npm openclaw <= 2026.4.1 affected, >= 2026.4.2 fixed; fix commit a941a4fef9bc43b2973c92d0dcff5b8a426210c5 'require TLS for remote Android gateway endpoints'; thanks @zsxsoft). Fix: a941a4fe (2026-04-02, Agustin Rivera/eleqtrizit, #58475) adds GatewayHostSecurity.kt with isLoopbackGatewayHost() (localhost, 127.x, ::1, emulator 10.0.2.2) and enforces it in three places: ConnectionManager.resolveTlsParams returns required-TLS (expectedFingerprint null, allowTOFU false) for any non-loopback endpoint; GatewayConfigResolver.parseGatewayEndpoint returns null (rejects) for non-loopback cleartext (ws://) input including scanned setup codes (resolveScannedSetupCode now validates decoded URL via parseGatewayEndpoint); GatewaySession internal URL building switched to buildGatewayWebSocketUrl. Co-authors: Devin Robison (NVIDIA, human) - no AI trailers on the fix. round6_research.bug_semantics: CWE-400/770 (resource exhaustion, CVSS 7.5): Rack::QueryParser parses query strings and application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies by splitting on & and iterating every key-value pair into a Hash (parse_query/parse_nested_query -> _normalize_params) with NO upper bound on the number of parameters and no total bytesize limit, so a single crafted request with hundreds of thousands of parameters consumes excessive memory and CPU, stalling or crashing the Rack server (full DoS). The earlier key_space_limit partial mitigation (capping total parameter-key bytes at 65536, 2011) was determined ineffective (nested params bypassed it) and was neutralized in 2022, leaving parsing fully unbounded until the 2025 fix added RACK_QUERY_PARSER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT/ PARAMS_LIMIT (defaults 4MB and 4096) and QueryLimitError.
round6_research.evidence: rubysec advisory gems/rack/CVE-2025-46727.yml (GHSA-gjh7-p2fx-99vx, 2025-05-08): 'Rack::QueryParser parses query strings and application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies into Ruby data structures without imposing any limit on the number of parameters'; patched ~>2.2.14, ~>3.0.16, >=3.1.14; links fix commits 2bb5263b/3f5a4249/cd6b70a1. (2) Guard-removal chain restoring the fully unbounded state: 5b9d09a8 (2011-12-13, Evan Phoenix) added key_space_limit=65536 key-bytes check; 5e6e9446 (2022-01-25, Jonathan Rochkind, 'Deprecate key_space_limit') turned it into a no-op (limit 'didn't actually prevent an attacker... didn't actually do anything useful'); a5762cf6 (2022-09-10, Samuel Williams, 'Remove deprecated code. (#1966)') deleted the remnants - no param-count or bytesize guard whatsoever afterwards. (3) Fix: 2bb5263b (2025-05-06, 'Merge commit from fork', author Jeremy Evans, committer+Co-authored-by Samuel Williams) adds check_query_string with params_limit 4096 + bytesize_limit 4MB (env-overridable) and QueryLimitError (=ParamsTooDeepError alias), incl. round6_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated remote code execution in Spree < 0.60.2 via the product search functionality. GET /?search[send][]=eval&search[send][]=Kernel.fork%20do%60<cmd>%60end (metasploit module spree_search_exec, exploit-db 17941, joernchen@phenoelit disclosure 2011-10-05): products_controller builds @searcher = Spree::Config.searcher_class.new(params); Spree::Search::Base#prepare calls @product_group.from_search(params[:search]) when params[:search] is present; ProductGroup#from_search iterates raw (scope_name, scope_attribute) pairs into add_scope, which stores ProductScope {name => scope_name.to_s, arguments => [*args]} with NO name validation; ProductScope#apply runs Product.send(self.name, *self.arguments) - so an attacker-controlled scope name is dispatched via Ruby send on Product with attacker-controlled args, reaching arbitrary method invocation (send/eval/system etc. CVSS v2 9.0, v3 9.8, v4 10.0 per rubysec advisory). Fixed in 0.60.2 by rejecting scope names matching /eval|send|system|[^a-z0-9_!?]/ in ProductGroup#add_scope.
round6_research.evidence: Class identity: case metadata (advisories: 2) CVE-2011-10019 + GHSA-97vm-c39p-jr86, repo field rubysec/ruby-advisory-db (advisory source); code repo spree/spree (clone .ai-slop/state/repos/spree_spree, HEAD 4ea38937). rubysec advisory gems/spree/CVE-2011-10019.yml: 'RCE in search function via search[:send][]: e.g. /?search[send][]=eval&search[send][]=Kernel.fork...' , patched >= 0.60.2, refs metasploit spree_search_exec + exploit-db 17941. v0.60.1 vulnerable flow verified in-tree: core/app/controllers/products_controller.rb (@searcher = Spree::Config.searcher_class.new(params)), core/lib/spree/search/base.rb (#prepare -> from_search(params[:search]) if params[:search]), product_group.rb (from_search each_pair -> add_scope raw name; add_scope builds ProductScope(:name => scope_name.to_s) - no filter), product_scope.rb apply: Product.send(self.name, *self.arguments). Fix commit 453f4078e1c694b8a8ff11a118c9fb4474b56e85 (2011-10-04, parent 24455e9e) 'Added scope_name filtering': add_scope raises ArgumentError when scope_name matches /eval|send|system|[^a-z0-9_!?]/; also changed Product.search -> Product.metasearch; tag v0.60.2 contains it (range v0.60.1..v0.60.2 ~9 commits, others unrelated). Introducer: git log -S 'Product.send(self.name' --all -> first writer 05de3d6909d7134da35d1d78189c82add79f08be which CREATED core/app/models/product_scope.rb (line: Product.send(self.name, *self.arguments)) and core/app/models/product_group.rb with from_search/add_scope (git log -S 'from_search' --all also starts at 05de3d6909); git cat-file -e 0ecbaab999:core/app/models/product_scope.rb -> rc=128 (absent at parent, first-appearance-in-history confirmed by pickaxe order). git grep from_search at 05de3d6909: only the definition (no callers yet - HTTP wiring added later, before 0.60.1, in the same unguarded form; the shipped+metasploit'd attack surface is 0.60.1, whose primitive traces to 05de3d6909; fix touched the exact primitive site).

The entire vulnerable primitive (from_search + unvalidated add_scope + Product.send dispatch) first entered the repository atomically in the refactoring commit that created core/app/models/product_group.rb and core/app/models/product_scope.rb; HTTP wiring (products_controller params[:search] -> searcher -> from_search) was added between 2010-06 and 0.60.1, but the unguarded dispatch point remained untouched until the scope_name filtering fix landed 15 months later.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Information disclosure (CVE-2026-44653, CVSS 6.5, CWE-200/CWE-522): in LibreChat <= 0.8.3, GET /api/mcp/servers and GET /api/mcp/servers/:serverName returned the full MCP server config objects, including decrypted admin-managed secrets (apiKey.key and oauth.client_secret), to any authenticated user with only MCP USE or VIEW permission - including viewers of a shared MCP server who do not own it. The responses were raw registry/parsed configs with zero redaction, so non-owners could exfiltrate the underlying provider/API credentials. Fixed in 0.8.4 by redacting secrets from all server responses and validating configs.

records.details:
A vulnerability in Claude Code's project-load flow allowed malicious repositories to exfiltrate data including Anthropic API keys before users confirmed trust. If a user started Claude Code in an attacker-controller repository, and the repository included a settings file that set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to an attacker-controlled endpoint, Claude Code would issue API requests before showing the trust prompt, including potentially leaking the user's API keys.

Users on standard Claude Code auto-update have received this fix already. Users performing manual updates are advised to update to the latest version.
records.summary: Claude Code Leaks Data via Malicious Environment Configuration Before Trust Confirmation

round6_research.bug_semantics: CWE-345/CWE-20 content-type verification bypass: ActiveStorage::DirectUploadsController#blob_args permits an arbitrary client-supplied metadata hash (permit(metadata: {})), and ActiveStorage::Blob stores internal state flags 'identified'/'analyzed'/'composed' in that same metadata store (store :metadata, accessors:, coder: JSON). A direct-upload client can therefore set identified/analyzed to skip MIME detection and analysis, uploading arbitrary content while claiming a safe content_type, defeating validations that rely on Active Storage's automatic content-type identification. Fixed by filtering PROTECTED_METADATA = %w(analyzed identified composed) out of user metadata in Blob.create_before_direct_upload!. Affected < 7.2.3.1 / 8.0.4.1 / 8.1.2.1.
round6_research.evidence: Advisory CVE-2026-33173/GHSA-qcfx-2mfw-w4cg (published 2026-03-23, fix date 2026-01-07). Internal use of the metadata store for flags predates it: 'identified' flag stored in metadata since c2ba530c43 (2018-01-15, George Claghorn, 'Extract content types from blob data') and 'composed' since 79a5e0b759 (2019-08-16, Gannon McGibbon, 'Add ActiveStorage::Blob.compose') - but flags were not client-writable until bb148d822. Fix: 707c0f1f41f067fdf96d54e99d43b28dfaae7e53 (main) adds PROTECTED_METADATA = %w(analyzed identified composed) + filter_metadata (metadata.without(...)) called in create_before_direct_upload!; backports 8fcb934caadc79c8cc4ce53287046d0f67005b3e (8.0) and d9502f5214e2198245a4c1defe9cd02a7c8057d0 (7.2), same patch, message explicitly states 'metadata is an entirely user controlled blob ... round6_research.flaw_origin: Human-authored feature commit: 2020 PR #40662 by Tahsin Hasan broadened the direct-upload strong-parameters permit to accept an arbitrary metadata hash, unintentionally exposing internal metadata flags to clients. round6_research.reasoning: The vulnerability decomposes to one atomic change: accepting a client-supplied metadata hash on direct uploads (bb148d822). Before it, strong parameters filtered a hash-valued metadata param to empty, so internal flags (identified/analyzed/composed) living in the same metadata store could not be forged remotely; after it, a direct-upload client can set them and skip MIME detection/analysis, enabling content-type claims to bypass verification (exactly what the fix's own commit message describes). The 2018/2019 commits that began storing flags in metadata were not vulnerable by themselves - they only became an issue once the controller exposed the hash, and the fix filters in Blob.create_before_direct_upload! (the code path bb148d822 feeds). Author Tahsin Hasan, 2020-11-28, no AI markers; the fixing commits (Jean Boussier, 2026) also carry no AI markers. Fully human causal chain: NOT_AI.

round6_research.bug_semantics: SQL injection (CWE-89) in QuerySet.filter()/exclude()/get() and Q() via a crafted '_connector' keyword argument (dictionary expansion). round6_research.bug_semantics: Rack::Multipart parser buffers non-file form fields (parts without a filename) entirely in process memory as Ruby Strings with no size cap; a single multi-hundred-MB text field in a multipart/form-data request exhausts worker memory (CWE-400 uncontrolled resource consumption, DoS). File parts are streamed to Tempfiles; the unbounded in-memory path is only for non-file fields, from the parser's first commit to 2025.
round6_research.evidence: Census/class-repo-precise resolve the class to github.com/rack/rack (class 'repo' is the rubysec metadata registry). OSV CVE-2025-61771 GIT range: introduced '0', fixed 2.2.19/3.1.17/3.2.2. Introducer: git log --reverse -S 'Multipart' -- lib/rack/utils.rb => 4fe5360a 'Make Rack::Request read multipart form data', Christian Neukirchen <chris@...> (project creator), 2007-02-28; diff shows module Multipart with `body = ''` / `body = Tempfile.new('RackMultipart') if filename` / `body << buf.slice!(0, i)` - the vulnerable in-memory accumulation verbatim. Parent 758f9287: git grep -i 'multipart' at parent rc=1 (no multipart code anywhere); no part-buffering patterns in utils.rb (rc=1). Atomic: parser created wholesale in this single commit, no earlier decomposition possible. AI markers: none (2007 commit, plain message + darcs-hash, no trailers; author is the human creator of Rack). Fix: 589127f4/d869fed6/e08f78c6 (identical 'Fix denial of service vulnerbilties in multipart parsing', Jeremy Evans, 2025-09-15, one per maintained branch) add BOUNDARY_START_LIMIT (16KB), MIME_HEADER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT (64KB) and update_retained_size enforcing BUFFERED_UPLOAD_BYTESIZE_LIMIT (default 16MiB) on BufferPart (non-file) bodies; verified in v3.2.1..v3.2.2 diff; 4c4ea296/8d141b30/bce149b1 are patch version bumps (2025-10-07).
round6_research.flaw_origin: Original 2007 design by Rack's creator: the first multipart parser (lib/rack/utils.rb, module Utils::Multipart) did `body = ''` for non-file parts vs `body = Tempfile.new('RackMultipart') if filename` for file parts, then accumulated every non-file body via `body << buf.slice!(...)` with no bound. The asymmetric buffering-without-limit is the flaw, present since inception (OSV GIT range introduced '0').
round6_research.reasoning: The vulnerable behavior (unbounded in-memory buffering of non-file multipart fields) was introduced at the very creation of Rack's multipart parser in 2007 by the project's founder, ~15 years before AI coding assistants existed; no AI authorship markers and none possible for this commit. Per the no-inference rule and marker absence: NOT_AI. This is a long-standing design limitation (CWE-400) only recognized as a vulnerability in 2025 when the maintainers added size caps.
round6_research.remaining_gap: None material. The advisory's plain-text '2 MiB' cap figure differs from the implemented default BUFFERED_UPLOAD_BYTESIZE_LIMIT=16MiB, but the mechanism (retained in-memory non-file body cap) matches the reported vulnerability; exact cap value does not affect the introducer analysis.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Command-line injection on Windows when executing batch files (CWE-77): Windows CreateProcess implicitly spawns cmd.exe when the target is a .bat/.cmd file, so arguments passed unquoted by Deno.Command.spawn()/node:child_process compatibility (e.g. args: ['&calc.exe']) are interpreted by cmd.exe as additional commands. The flaw is that Deno allows direct execution of batch files with user-supplied arguments and no quoting/rejection; fixed in 2.5.2 by rejecting .bat/.cmd execution on Windows outright ('Use a shell to execute .bat or .cmd files' error) in ext/process/lib.rs compute_run_cmd_and_check_permissions. Affects all Deno versions up to 2.5.1 (born-flawed behavior).
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-m2gf-x3f6-8hq3 / CVE-2025-61787 (published 2025-10-08): 'Deno is Vulnerable to Command Injection on Windows During Batch File Execution', affected up to 2.5.1, fixed 2.5.2, references PR #30818 and commit 8a0990ccd37bafd8768176ca64b906ba2da2d822 (git branch --contains -> main). Fix diff: ext/process/lib.rs adds #[cfg(windows)] rejection of cmd.extension() == bat/cmd in compute_run_cmd_and_check_permissions with ProcessError::SpawnFailed PermissionDenied, plus tests/unit/command_test.ts rejectBatAndCmdFiles asserting PermissionDenied for new Deno.Command('test.bat', {args:['&calc.exe']}). BIC: `git log -S 'std::process::Command'`/'-S Command::new' earliest hit = 48bf4062e4359674e1a417100eb76a6347e77fc1 (2018-11-16, 'First pass at running subprocesses (#1156)', Bert Belder): +629 lines adding js/process.ts (deno.run with args), src/ops.rs Run op (+141), src/permissions.rs run permission, src/resources.rs process resource; parent 9b702da9e has no subprocess spawn code. `git log --follow --diff-filter=A -- ext/process/lib.rs` shows the file lineage: cli/ops.rs split at e6c349af9 (2019-08-14) -> later moves into ext/process/lib.rs, with no intermediate change to batch-file handling. Introducer parent-absent: no process execution existed before 48bf4062e in this repo's history.
round6_research.flaw_origin: Born-flawed behavior of Deno's subprocess feature: the first commit implementing process spawning (deno.run with args) executes arbitrary program paths with arguments passed straight through to the OS, which on Windows means batch files are routed through cmd.exe with injectable metacharacters. The implementation commit predates and outlives multiple refactors (cli/ops.rs -> cli/ops/process.rs via split up ops.rs (#2753) -> ext/process/lib.rs), none of which changed the Windows batch-file handling until the 2025 fix.
round6_research.reasoning: Step 1: GHSA-m2gf-x3f6-8hq3 describes Windows cmd.exe implicit-spawn injection for .bat/.cmd when args are unquoted; the vulnerable behavior is Deno's direct process spawn of arbitrary paths including batch files. evidence: Introduced 2007-02-28 by 4fe5360acf4f1aa680ee00df589bba10b0b56634 (Christian Neukirchen <chneukirchen@gmail.com>, 'Make Rack::Request read multipart form data', darcs-era import): Utils::Multipart.parse_multipart loop 'until head && buf =~ /.../; if !head && i = buf.index("\r\n\r\n") ...; c = input.read(...); buf << c' buffers the part header without any size limit
Parent 758f928783ea935dd082414bb783bdde8a6df68e contains 0 occurrences of parse_multipart (absence verified via git grep on parent tree), so 4fe5360a is the first writer of the vulnerable behavior

Vulnerable behavior persisted through refactors: 6674f365 (2009), 24d51253 (2011, split to lib/rack/multipart/parser.rb), 8987a0cb/351027ac/a1585b11/7f3b3d43 (2015-08-28 Aaron Patterson evented parser), 534ef35b (2018-07-24 Nick Adams StringScanner rewrite introducing @sbuf.scan_until(/(.*?\r\n)\r\n/m)) - none added a header size cap

round6_research.bug_semantics: RCE via arbitrary git config in the Git node (CWE-829, critical): the 'Add Config' operation passes workflow-controlled free-form key/value straight to simple-git's addConfig -> 'git config --local <key> <value>'. A malicious workflow can set core.hooksPath to a directory inside the cloned repository that contains a 'pre-commit' hook; Git then executes that hook as a local system command during subsequent Git operations (commit/clone/pull), giving arbitrary command execution on the n8n host.
round6_research.evidence: Identity: member_map pin alias-dbf8e9cb -> CVE-2025-65964 + GHSA-wpqc-h9wp-chmq (published 2025-12-08, critical, CWE-829; affected >=0.123.1 <1.119.2, patched 1.119.2). BIC 3667b0dd01 (2021-06-05, Jan <janober@users.noreply.github.com>, ':sparkles: Add Git node (#1820)') is the file/feature birth: introduces Git node incl. the addConfig branch 'const key = this.getNodeParameter('key'...); ... await git.addConfig(key, value, append)' (Git.node.ts:265-278) with zero validation; immediate parent ea9f956f has no Git node dir (ls-tree) and zero 'addConfig' hits in packages/nodes-base (git grep exit 1); single-parent commit; %N trailers empty. A network attacker (MITM, adjacent) can intercept and harvest vCenter administrator credentials (used to authenticate), then access vCenter. CVSS 3.1 9.3 (AV:A/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N). Fixed in v0.16.0 by making TLS behaviour user-configurable (creds.SkipTLS + creds.CACert with Validate(), new pkg/vmware/tls.go).

round6_research.bug_semantics: Active Storage proxy-mode DoS via Range requests (CWE-789 uncontrolled memory allocation, CVSS 6.6 moderate): ActiveStorage::Blobs::ProxyController#show -> send_blob_byte_range_data parses the client Range header with Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges and, for a single range, loads the ENTIRE requested byte range into memory via blob.download_chunk(range) before send_data. A large or unbounded Range header (e.g. bytes=0-) makes the server allocate memory proportional to file size, allowing remote unauthenticated memory-exhaustion DoS in proxy delivery mode. Fixed by capping total range size to ActiveStorage.streaming_chunk_max_size (default 100MB): ranges whose sum exceeds the cap now get 416 range_not_satisfiable. Affected activestorage <7.2.3.1, >=8.0.0.beta1 <8.0.4.1, >=8.1.0.beta1 <8.1.2.1.
round6_research.evidence: Introducer fcc46228c626b02f7ace689843dbbcf400d118df (2021-08-05, Tom Prats <tprats108@gmail.com>, 'Squashed commit of the following' = PR #42493 'Add Active Storage support for byte ranges'; single parent 7f5ebc4b43030f99dc06cb79fd3b3ad3faa3af6e, verified absent: git grep for send_blob_byte_range_data/get_byte_ranges in parent activestorage tree returns 0) created activestorage/app/controllers/concerns/active_storage/streaming.rb with send_blob_byte_range_data: ranges = Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges(range_header, blob.byte_size); single-range branch does data = blob.download_chunk(range) and send_data(data, ...) - entire requested range materialized in memory with no cap (bytes=0- yields whole-file allocation); multi-range branch concatenates all chunks into one String (data << chunk), unbounded sum. Pre-squash sub-commits (b9553e3698a7af5105171f9d63bd7b89cbb7e2c3 'Added Active Storage support for byte ranges' 2021-06-23 etc.) are not present in any reachable ref (git cat-file: could not get object info), so the squash is the minimum atomic introducer; commit message contains only human Co-authored-by: Rafael França. Fix 2cd933c366b777f873d4d590127da2f4a25e4ba5 (2025-12-02, Gannon McGibbon <gannon.mcgibbon@gmail.com>, 'Configurable maxmimum streaming chunk size', [CVE-2026-33174] [GHSA-r46p-8f7g-vvvg]) is the advisory-referenced patch on 8-0-stable/8-0-sec; identical cherry-picks 42012eaaa88dfc7d0030161b2bc8074a7bbce92a (8-1-sec) and 8159a9c3de3f27a2bcf2866b8bf9ceb9075e229b (7-2-sec). Diff: replaces the blank check with ranges_valid?(ranges) returning false unless ranges.blank?||ranges.all?(&:blank?) AND ranges.sum { |r| r.end - r.begin } < ActiveStorage.streaming_chunk_max_size (new mattr_accessor default 100.megabytes, configurable via config.active_storage.streaming_chunk_max_size in engine.rb), returning head(:range_not_satisfiable) on overflow; adds 'Byte Range is too big' / 'too big overall' tests (bytes=0- under 1KB cap -> 416) + CHANGELOG + configuring.md entry. AI markers: introducer fcc46228 body grep count 1 = 'Co-authored-by: Rafael França <rafael@franca.dev>' (human core-team co-author, counts 0); fix 2cd933c366 / 42012eaa bodies 0 markers each. records.summary: VM2 Has a WASM Sandbox Escape

advisory_research.source_boundary: Advisory semantics and release boundary are known from local GHSA data; the affected Claude Code implementation is not public, so atomic introducer, parent absence, fix hunk, and causal AI role remain unverified.

dossier.bug_semantics: Node 25+/V8 WebAssembly.JSTag lets wasm try_table/catch catch JS exceptions, bypassing vm2 transformer's JS-only catch instrumentation (handleException); host exception escapes sandbox via externref (err.name=Symbol() triggers host TypeError on err.stack access). vm2 inherits host WebAssembly global by omission; fix deletes WebAssembly.JSTag in sandbox.
dossier.evidence: clone /tmp/blocked57_clones/patriksimek__vm2: git show 1fbdeff743d48fb1416964777f5947057f6f1295 --stat => lib/setup-sandbox.js +20, test/vm.js +38, single parent f2d9cfe942b88ed639ef4e530dec4d4961498fed; git grep -c 'JSTag' f2d9cfe9 -- lib/ => 0 hits (parent absence proven); git log --all -S 'JSTag' => 1fbdeff is first code commit (others docs 408fc85/d1ab748/10c4b22/d329f1f and JSPI fix 6915fa4); git show 1fbdeff^:lib/setup-sandbox.js | rg 'WebAssembly|JSTag' => only comment line 46, no sandbox exposure code; lib/bridge.js lib/transformer.js lib/main.js at parent have zero WebAssembly/JSTag refs; git show -s --format=%B 1fbdeff | rg -i 'co-authored|claude|gpt|anthropic' => no hits; setup-sandbox.js created in 2353ce6 (2022-02-08) without JSTag/wasm-catch code
dossier.reasoning: Mechanism and direct fix fully closed: human-authored single-commit fix with parent absence and regression PoC tests. But source-to-sink cannot be closed inside vm2: JSTag capability is introduced by Node/V8 (Node 25+), and no vm2 commit ever wrote the vulnerable line - the sandbox inherits the host WebAssembly global by omission. Per instruction 'do not misattribute V8 external code to vm2' and fail-closed protocol, there is no vm2 atomic introducer with parent absence; classifying the external V8/Node commit as vm2's introducer would be misattribution.
dossier.remaining_gap: No vm2 atomic introducer exists for the exposed capability (flaw is omission vs V8-provided WebAssembly.JSTag, Node 25+); authoritative V8/Node introducer commit is outside repo and unverifiable here; cannot decompose 'omission' into a vm2 BIC without misattributing external code

ai_marker.note: 1fbdeff and 408fc855 are single-parent Patrik Simek commits with no Co-Authored-By/Claude/Copilot/Cursor/GPT trailers. A later Claude Opus trailer on c950166 (WebAssembly.Memory cap) is a different GHSA and not causal here. Human author on the fix is not used as BIC proof.

JSTag is a Node/V8 host global (docs: ~Node 23; fix comment: Node 25+), not a vm2-implemented tag.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Open redirect (CWE-601) in the basecamp/google_sign_in gem (Google Sign-In for Rails) < 1.3.0: RedirectProtector#ensure_same_origin validates the persisted post-auth redirect URL (flash[:proceed_to]) with QUALIFIED_URL_PATTERN = /\A#{URI::DEFAULT_PARSER.make_regexp}\z/, and Ruby's RFC2396 URI regexp accepts malformed URLs containing control characters (e.g. 'https://basecamp.com\n\r@\n\revil.com'), so the same-origin comparison passes server-side while browsers strip the control chars and navigate to the attacker origin. Chained with a session-cookie injection (required only when flash is stored in a cookie) this redirects a just-authenticated user off-origin and can leak the OAuth token/authentication info. Fixed in v1.3.0 (PR #73): ensure_same_origin now allows only a well-formed same-origin URL or an absolute path (ABS_PATH without host / no '//' prefix) and raises Violation otherwise; follow-up 9fd0605/c1b9c4d hardened against double-slash net-paths.
evidence: rubysec advisory gems/google_sign_in/CVE-2025-57821.yml (2025-08-27): title 'Google Sign-In for Rails allowed redirects to malformed URLs', gem google_sign_in, patched >=1.3.0, cvss_v3 4.2, credited muntrive via HackerOne; requires flash stored in session cookie to be exploitable; references GHSA-7pwc-wh6m-44q3, commit a0548a60, commit 85903651, PR #73, release v1.3.0
Product repo basecamp/google_sign_in cloned (HEAD e7f2a9ab 'version bump to v1.3.1', 2025-08-29, Mike Dalessio)

Fix a0548a60 (2025-08-22, Mike Dalessio <mike@37signals.com>, 1 parent 44f572a5): 'Prevent redirects to malformed URLs' rewrites ensure_same_origin to allow only (qualified URL with equal origin) or ABS_PATH, raising Violation otherwise; adds tests 'disallows URL target that is not a valid URL' ('https://basecamp.com\n\r@\n\revil.com') and 'disallows URL target that is blank'; merged via PR #73 merge commit 85903651 (2025-08-26, GitHub); release v1.3.0 tag 2025-08-27; no AI markers in fix messages

Introducer 13dafac (2018-08-29, George Claghorn <george.claghorn@gmail.com>, committer GitHub, 1 parent cb625986) 'Switch to server-side OAuth 2.0': creates redirect_protector.rb as a new file with QUALIFIED_URL_PATTERN = /\A#{URI::DEFAULT_PARSER.make_regexp}\z/ and 'if target =~ QUALIFIED_URL_PATTERN && origin_of(target) != origin_of(source) raise Violation' - the permissive regexp is the bypass root; immediate parent tree has zero redirect/protector files (grep exit 1), so immediate-parent absence holds

Only pre-fix change to the check: ce1b950 (2019-03-22, Rosa Gutierrez <rosa.ge@gmail.com>, human, no markers) added 'target.blank? ||' - a hardening, not the writer of the vulnerable comparison; QUALIFIED_URL_PATTERN line unchanged 2018-2025 (git show 44f572a5 pre-fix content identical in the vulnerable line)

round6_research.bug_semantics: Unsafe pickle deserialization allowing arbitrary (zero-byte) file creation via the logging.FileHandler gadget (CWE-502): picklescan's blocklist in src/picklescan/scanner.py (_unsafe_globals) blocked RCE-focused modules (os, subprocess, builtins, ctypes, functools.partial, _io.FileIO, etc.) but did not cover the Python standard library logging module. An attacker can craft a pickle whose __reduce__ returns (logging.FileHandler, ('evil.log',)); on deserialization the handler opens the file in append mode, creating a zero-byte file at an arbitrary path when it does not exist, with no overwrite of existing content. Since scanning occurs on untrusted pickle input, this yields filesystem pollution / logic disruption (e.g., planting lock files the application checks, DoS), though not direct RCE. Fixed in 1.0.1 by adding logging.FileHandler to _unsafe_globals (plus a regression fixture tests/data2/logging_FileHandler.pkl).
round6_research.evidence: OSV GHSA-m7j5-r2p5-c39r (aliases CVE-2026-56304, PYSEC-2026-225): PyPI package picklescan, ECOSYSTEM range introduced 0, fixed 1.0.1; summary 'picklescan vulnerable to arbitrary file create using logging.FileHandler'; CVSS 4.0 AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N (E:P); refs github.com/mmaitre314/picklescan/pull/60, commit 4d9bc9cd34bca8672dad3481cd4556d5ba747156, pypa/advisory-database PYSEC-2026-225.yaml. PoC: pickle __reduce__ returning (logging.FileHandler, ('evil.log',)) creates a zero-byte file; verified in the clone that fix 4d9bc9cd adds logging.FileHandler to _unsafe_globals in src/picklescan/scanner.py and bumps version to 1.0.1, with new fixture tests/data2/logging_FileHandler.pkl and test coverage; fix is ancestor of HEAD; introducer c1d5abd is the file creation commit and ancestor of fix; parent 6a76b8c3 has no _unsafe_globals (exit=1).
round6_research.flaw_origin: Introduced by commit c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e ('Implement Pickle scanner', 2022-09-04, Matthieu Maitre) which created src/picklescan/scanner.py and its initial _unsafe_globals blocklist; the blocklist enumerated dangerous modules (os, subprocess, builtins, ctypes, functools, httplib, _io.FileIO, numpy f2py etc.) but did not include logging.FileHandler, so the deserialization safety check would not flag the FileHandler gadget. Variant 2 (evaluate_augassign): the dunder-attribute block exists only in evaluate_attribute/nodunder_getattr, but get_current_value (augassign read) and set_value (plain assignment) use raw getattr()/setattr(), so obj.__code__ += trap reads __code__ via __radd__ interception and victim.__code__ = evil overwrites function bytecode -> RCE. round6_research.bug_semantics: Command injection (CWE-78) in the PostgreSQL database healthcheck: app/Actions/Database/StartPostgresql.php builds Docker healthcheck 'test' as shell-form ['CMD-SHELL', "psql -U {$this->database->postgres_user} -d {$this->database->postgres_db} -c 'SELECT 1' || exit 1"] (originally ['CMD-SHELL', 'pg_isready', '-d', $database->postgres_db]). Docker CMD-SHELL joins the elements into a /bin/sh -c string, and postgres_user/postgres_db are user-controlled database settings, so an authenticated user who can create/edit a PostgreSQL resource injects shell commands executed as root inside the database container. Fix converts to exec-form ['CMD', 'psql', '-U', ..., '-d', ..., '-c', 'SELECT 1'] which bypasses the shell.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Cleartext interception (CWE-319, related STARTTLS stripping) in django.core.mail.backends.smtp.EmailBackend: EmailBackend.open() assigns self.connection = connection_class(host, port, ...) and only then calls starttls(context=...) / login(...) inside a try/except OSError that swallows the error when fail_silently=True. On a failed STARTTLS handshake (e.g. a mitm/on-path attacker, or a server that refuses upgrades) the exception is suppressed but self.connection stays set to the partially-initialized raw SMTP socket; subsequent send_messages() reuses that cleartext connection (open() sees self.connection truthy and returns False), so email content is transmitted in cleartext. Affects Django 5.2 < 5.2.15 and 6.0 < 6.0.6 (earlier unsupported series likely also affected per advisory). Reported by Kasper Dupont.
round6_research.evidence: Identity: class hash verified sha256('CVE-2026-7666\nGHSA-mm6v-q8q9-pgcf\n')[:24] == alias-df4fbf1117cd31daf99f8e2c (pair recovered from PYSEC-2026-200.yaml aliases; repo-precise mapping class-repo-precise.jsonl assigns to django/django). Advisory PYSEC-2026-200 / GHSA-mm6v-q8q9-pgcf (published 2026-06-03): SMTP EmailBackend fails to prevent reuse of a partially-initialized connection after a failed STARTTLS handshake when fail_silently=True, enabling on-path attackers to read email via cleartext interception; fixed 5.2.15/6.0.6. Fix df887f5019 (2026-04-30, Jake Howard <git@theorangeone.net>, 'Fixed CVE-2026-7666 -- Delayed setting SMTP connection until fully configured.', thanks Kasper Dupont, reviews Jacob Walls + Natalia Bidart): refactors open() to build the connection into self._partial_connection, runs starttls() and login() on it, and only assigns self.connection once fully configured; on OSError with fail_silently the _partial_connection is closed (new _close_connection() helper) and reset so the broken cleartext socket is never reused; close() also extended to abandon partial connections. Backports: afd82a5449 [6.1.x], 625a670c46 [6.0.x], 4e47d2b800 [5.2.x]. Introducer verification: aba5389326 diff shows smtp.py as a new file (git show --stat: django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py | 103 ++++) containing 'self.connection = smtplib.SMTP(...)' before 'self.connection.starttls()' inside bare 'except: if not self.fail_silently: raise'; parent has no backends dir / starttls refs. AI marker grep (co-authored|assisted-by|anthropic|claude|copilot|codex|openai|generated|mastra|gemini|bard|cursor): introducer aba5389326 = 0; fix df887f5019 = 0; backports afd82a5449/625a670c46/4e47d2b800 = 0 each. Authors: introducer Russell Keith-Magee (Django co-founder, human, 2009); fix Jake Howard (human); backports applied by Natalia Bidart (human).
round6_research.flaw_origin: minimum atomic introducer is commit aba5389326372be43b2a3bdcda16646fd197e807 (2009-11-03, Russell Keith-Magee <russell@keith-magee.com>, 'Fixed #10355 -- Added an API for pluggable e-mail backends.'): created django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py (new file, 103 lines) with the exact vulnerable pattern: 'self.connection = smtplib.SMTP(self.host, self.port, local_hostname=DNS_NAME.get_fqdn())' then 'if self.use_tls: self.connection.ehlo(); self.connection.starttls(); self.connection.ehlo()' inside 'try: ... except: if not self.fail_silently: raise' — connection stored on self before STARTTLS, and a suppressed TLS failure leaves the cleartext connection set. round6_research.bug_semantics: Django ASGIRequest normalizes ASGI header names following WSGI conventions (hyphens mapped to underscores, or prefixed HTTP_, see corrected_name = 'HTTP_%s' % name.upper().replace('-', '_')), so a spoofed header named with underscores (e.g. X_FORWARDED_HOST instead of X-Forwarded-Host) collides with its hyphenated twin even when proxies strip the hyphenated form; remote header spoofing. Fixed by ignoring all header names containing '_' in ASGIRequest (as Daphne does).
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-mvfq-ggxm-9mc5 / CVE-2026-3902 (reported by Tarek Nakkouch): ASGI header spoofing via underscore/hyphen conflation; fixed in 6.0.4, 5.2.13, 4.2.30. Mainline fix caf90a971f (Jacob Walls, 2026-01-22, 'Fixed CVE-2026-3902 -- Ignored headers with underscores in ASGIRequest') adds 'if "_" in name: continue' to the header loop in django/core/handlers/asgi.py (backports 1cc2a7612f/5.2.x, a623c39828/6.0.x, 4412731aa6/4.2.x). The vulnerable normalization loop (name.decode('latin1'); 'HTTP_%s' % name.upper().replace('-','_')) debuted with the ASGI handler in a415ce70be (2019-04-12, Andrew Godwin, 'Fixed #30451 -- Added ASGI handler and coroutine-safety'); its parent cce47ff65a has no django/core/handlers/asgi.py at all (git ls-tree | grep: rc=1), so introducer_parent_absent=true. round6_research.bug_semantics: Denial of service (CWE-400) on the user-memories API: POST /api/memories and PATCH /api/memories/:key in api/server/routes/memories.js accept arbitrarily large key/value strings with no payload-size limit (no express.json({limit}) middleware) and no per-field length validation -- only non-empty-string checks. round6_research.bug_semantics: Reflected XSS (CWE-79) in the AI Playground OAuth callback handler: site/ai-playground/src/server.ts onStart() customHandler interpolates result.authError (sourced from the OAuth callback's error_description query parameter) directly into an inline <script> tag: `<script>alert('Authentication failed: ${result.authError}'); window.close();</script>`. An attacker crafts a malicious OAuth redirect link; on click, arbitrary JS executes in the victim's session context, exposing chat history, LLM interactions, and connected MCP servers. A later partial mitigation (#788, JSON.stringify) escaped quotes but not '</script>' breakout, so the flaw persisted until the advisory fix.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Improper cross-namespace reference validation (CWE-863 / CWE-284) in the Function admission webhook: specification.spec.package.packageref.namespace and specification.spec.environment.namespace were never validated, while Secret and ConfigMap references were. Introduced 0, fixed in fission 1.24.0. Companion advisories in the same era: GHSA-cvw6-gfvv-953q (Package webhook), GHSA-vjhc/GHSA-gc3j (cross-ns refs in Package + KubernetesWatchTrigger), GHSA-gx55 (PodSpec fields) - same 2026-05 hardening batch.

blocked106.flaw_semantics: Open5GS NRF NFM handler (src/nrf/nrf-sm.c nrf_state_operational, OGS_SBI_SERVICE_NAME_NRF_NFM / NF_INSTANCES resource): for any non-GET/OPTIONS method the DEFAULT branch looks up nf_instance via message.h.resource.component[1] (the {nfInstanceId} path segment) and, when absent, falls into the PUT branch that calls ogs_sbi_nf_instance_add()/ogs_sbi_nf_instance_set_id() with a NULL id. round6_research.bug_semantics: Denial of service (engine crash) via invalid regex in structured output (guided decoding) in vllm-project/vllm (case repo pypa/advisory-database; actual vulnerable repo vllm-project/vllm). With the default v1 guided-decoding backend 'auto' (DecodingConfig.backend = 'auto' if VLLM_USE_V1 else 'xgrammar'), a request with guided_regex (e.g. '[.*') goes through validate_xgrammar_grammar, whose xgr.Grammar.from_regex raises ValueError -> auto fallback switches backend to 'guidance' WITHOUT validating the grammar; the invalid regex then reaches llguidance compilation inside the engine worker and raises an uncaught exception, crashing the vLLM server (ReDoS-style DoS, PYSEC-2025-55: 'Version 0.8.0 up to but excluding 0.9.0 have a Denial of Service (ReDoS) that causes the vLLM server to crash if an invalid regex was provided while using structured output'). Fix restores validation on the fallback path so the request is rejected with HTTP 400 (test test_invalid_regex in the fix commit uses guided_regex=r'[.*').

round6_research.bug_semantics: Stack-based buffer overflow in the GDAL netCDF driver (frmts/netcdf/netcdfsg.cpp): scanForGeometryContainers() and SGeometry_PropertyScanner::open() read the CF_SG_GEOMETRY attribute into fixed-size stack buffers (char c[NC_MAX_CHAR] / char buf[NC_MAX_CHAR+1]) via nc_get_att_text() without checking the attribute length first, so an oversized geometry attribute in a crafted NetCDF file overflows the stack and can achieve code execution on the server (also the attrf() helper reads into a fixed 257-byte stack buffer without length validation). Affects GDAL 3.1.0 through 3.13.0; fixed in 3.13.1.
