round6_research.bug_semantics: Mattermost interactive button callbacks could run action handlers (button-click dispatch to the agent) before normal sender authorization/allowlist checks completed. The interaction handler verified only an HMAC context token (_token) and then dispatched as a system event + synthetic inbound message, so a crafted callback could invoke an action without going through the channel's sender/allowlist authorization path (unauthorized action execution). Fixed by adding an optional authorizeButtonClick callback in createMattermostInteractionHandler and wiring monitorMattermostProvider to route callback authorization through authorizeMattermostCommandInvocation.
evidence: GHSA-8883-9w57-vwv6 / CVE-2026-35652: Mattermost interactive callback dispatch could run action handlers before normal sender authorization checks; affected <2026.3.22, fixed >=2026.3.22; fix commits a47722de7e3c and 630f1479c44f (release tag).

Direct fix a47722de7e3c (Vincent Koc, 2026-03-15, PR #46787 'Integrations: tighten inbound callback and allowlist checks') adds authorizeButtonClick callback to createMattermostInteractionHandler in extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/interactions.ts and wires monitorMattermostProvider in monitor.ts to route callback authorization through authorizeMattermostCommandInvocation (sender + allowlist).

Atomic introducer 136ca87f7bb2f3b764548d8a897fa35c3debc81d (Tony Dehnke, 2026-03-05, 'feat(mattermost): add interactive buttons support (#19957)') created extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/interactions.ts with createMattermostInteractionHandler verifying only the HMAC _token and then dispatching button-click via system event + dispatchButtonClick, with no sender allowlist authorization check before dispatching.
Immediate parent 9741e91a64c does not contain extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/interactions.ts (parent_absent=true), so the un-authorized dispatch behavior first appears in 136ca87f7bb.
Introducer is a squash merge (PR #19957) with author Tony Dehnke and co-authors tonydehnke + mukhtharcm; commit body has no AI/[AI]/codex/claude markers and no AI-generated attribution.

partial_wave.bug_semantics: GHSA-38f7-945m-qr2g (CVE-2026-32887): effect's MixedScheduler batches fiber continuations and drains ALL accumulated tasks inside a single microtask/timer callback (starveInternal), so the Node.js AsyncLocalStorage context active during that callback belongs to whichever request first triggered the drain cycle, not the request owning the resumed fiber; under concurrent RPC load (e.g. Next.js + Clerk auth() inside Effect fibers via toWebHandlerRuntime), a fiber can read another request's session, causing cross-request authentication/session confusion (CWE-362).
partial_wave.evidence: Advisory GHSA-38f7-945m-qr2g (2026-03-20) pins the root cause to Scheduler.ts MixedScheduler.starveInternal draining all queued continuations in one callback; fixed in effect 3.20.0. git log -S 'starveInternal' -- '*Scheduler.ts' finds first write at 5f14f523df (2022-05-31, Michael Arnaldi, 'chore: improve scheduling'), which replaces the single-thunk defaultScheduler with a module-level scheduled {running,tasks} + starve/starveInternal batching loop - the exact flawed pattern; the code survives ed79588f9d (2023-09-29 'integrate preconstruct, unify package structure') which moves it to packages/effect/src/Scheduler.ts as MixedScheduler. Fix 8798a8432 (2026-03-15, Michael Arnaldi, 'fix(effect): isolate scheduler runners per fiber (#6124)', changeset 'Fix scheduler task draining to isolate AsyncLocalStorage across fibers') introduces per-fiber SchedulerRunner instances via SchedulerRunner.cached WeakMap so each fiber gets its own drain cycle, and also updates workerRunner/RpcClient/RpcServer to pass the fiber. round6_research.bug_semantics: CWE-287/CWE-346/CWE-639 CRITICAL: gateway JWT-session bypass and :authority injection via the unauthenticated router hair-pin path. The ext_proc MCP router (HandleNoneToolCall) honors an attacker-supplied 'mcp-init-host' header on any initialize-method request and rewrites the upstream :authority to the attacker-chosen target, gated ONLY by a single shared 'router-key' header compared against RouterAPIKey. That shared value is (a) a hardcoded literal fallback 'secret-api-key' (cmd/mcp-broker-router/main.go, flag --mcp-router-key / env MCP_ROUTER_API_KEY) and (b) in controller-managed deployments hex(sha256(MCPGatewayExtension.UID)[:16]) passed via --mcp-router-key=... in the container argv - a non-secret value readable by anyone with get on the resource. A caller knowing/deriving the key can route to ANY backend listener registered with the gateway (incl. external services), bypassing the broker's signed x-mcp-authorized capability filter and the JWT session model. A TODO comment at the check site ('look to use a signed key possible the JWT session key') documents the author's awareness that the static key design was weak.
round6_research.evidence: OSV GHSA-g53w-w6mj-hrpp (2026-05-19, GO-2026-5390, CVSS 4.0 9.3, CWE-287/346/639): 'Authority-injection and JWT/session bypass via the unauthenticated router hair-pin "router-key" / "mcp-init-host" path'; fixed 0.7.0; references fix commit 60520792. (1) Introducer: git pickaxe -S 'mcp-init-host'/'secret-api-key'/'router-key' all point to b72493ac (2025-11-17, craig <cbrookes@redhat.com>, 'draft use extrnal session store use client based init handle session timeout') as the earliest commit: it adds the hairpin initialize path in internal/mcp-router/request_handlers.go (HandleNoneToolCall reads 'mcp-init-host', compares 'router-key' header to s.RoutingConfig.RouterAPIKey, then headers.WithAuthority(remoteInitializeTarget); 400-reject on mismatch) and the --mcp-router-key flag with hardcoded default goenv.GetDefault('MCP_ROUTER_API_KEY', 'secret-api-key') in cmd/mcp-broker-router/main.go (also adds defaultJWTSigningKey='default-not-secure' fallback for session JWTs). Immediate parent 1a1cae85 verified free of all three strings (git grep exit 1 each). Single-parent plain commit (rev-list --parents shows only 1a1cae85), not a squash. (2) Shaping commits, same author: 2eb62131 (2025-11-24 'pass through headers') refines the block (RoutingKey const, unsets router-specific headers before forwarding); f996170e (2026-02-06 'Base of the move to an operator based deploy') makes the controller emit --mcp-router-key=<key> via routerKey(mcpExt) = hex(sha256(UID)[:16]) (internal/controller/broker_router.go), exposed in pod argv and derivable by anyone with get on the MCPGatewayExtension (3df0937c keeps it, 'ensure rbac is synced and kept upto date'). round6_research.bug_semantics: Open redirect (CWE-601, medium) in the OIDC flow: correctOIDCUrl() derives the final redirect host/protocol from unvalidated request headers - 'actualHost = forwardedHost || requestHost' (X-Forwarded-Host / Host) and X-Forwarded-Proto - and rewrites the callback/consent redirect URL whenever the target host differs or is localhost; in deployments where the reverse proxy forwards client-supplied X-Forwarded-* headers as-is, an attacker injects an arbitrary host (e.g. X-Forwarded-Host: google.com) and victims are sent to a malicious domain (phishing, credential harvesting, session fixation).
round6_research.evidence: Identity: member_map pin alias-eb8ef389 -> CVE-2025-59426 + GHSA-xph5-278p-26qx (published 2025-09-24, medium, CWE-601; @lobehub/chat <1.130.1, fixed 1.130.1; advisory names src/app/(backend)/oidc/consent/route.ts using correctOIDCUrl with vulnerable header-derived host). BIC 0ed73685 (2025-07-30, Arvin Xu <arvinx@foxmail.com>, 'fix: fix desktop auth redirect url error (#8597)') creates src/utils/server/correctOIDCUrl.ts (61 lines) with 'const actualHost = forwardedHost || requestHost' and 'correctedUrl.host = actualHost' - zero host validation; immediate parent f92b86b1 has no correctOIDCUrl anywhere (git grep exit 1; its only x-forwarded-host hit is an outgoing header to the embedded oidc-provider, not redirect derivation); single-parent commit, %N trailers empty. round6_research.bug_semantics: CWE-178: Windows-compatible env override keys (e.g. `ProgramFiles(x86)`) could bypass the system.run approval binding. The execution path normalized env overrides with `normalizeHostOverrideEnvVarKey` (accepts `PORTABLE_ENV_VAR_KEY` plus the Windows-compat `WINDOWS_COMPAT_OVERRIDE_ENV_VAR_KEY` = /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_()]*$/), while the approval-binding path computed the expected env hash with strict `normalizeEnvVarKey(rawKey, {portable:true})` (rejects keys with parentheses). A Windows-compatible override key like `ProgramFiles(x86)` therefore never entered the approval binding's envHash/envKeys, so an approved system.run command could execute with an attacker-chosen env override that was not represented in (and thus not approved as part of) the binding. Approved-command env integrity bypass (medium).
round6_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-98ch-45wp-ch47 (published 2026-04-02, medium, no CVE; npm pkg openclaw, affected <=2026.4.1, patched >=2026.4.2) pins Fix Commit 7eb094a00d80e9f6bf0e62f2c45d3b88ff67c04d = squash of PR #59182 (author pgondhi987/Pavan Kumar Gondhi, Co-authored-by Devin Robison). Fix changes src/infra/system-run-approval-binding.ts: normalizeSystemRunEnvEntries switches from `normalizeEnvVarKey(rawKey,{portable:true})` to `normalizeHostOverrideEnvVarKey(rawKey)` and matchSystemRunApprovalEnvHash gains a fail-closed APPROVAL_ENV_BINDING_MISSING branch; src/infra/host-env-security.ts exports normalizeHostOverrideEnvVarKey (1-line). Introducer of the divergence: 7abfff756d6c68d17e21d1657bbacbaec86de232 (Josh Avant, 2026-03-20, PR #51207 'Exec: harden host env override handling across gateway and node') added WINDOWS_COMPAT_OVERRIDE_ENV_VAR_KEY and normalizeHostOverrideEnvVarKey (accepting `ProgramFiles(x86)`-style keys) to the execution path only; parent 7abfff756d6^ has neither the regex nor the function (grep count 0), while the approval binding created earlier in 4894d907faa7540ca8b6835f561a6dd3ea824b77 (Peter Steinberger, 2026-02-26) kept strict portable normalization. Introducer/fix parents and the fix commit all clean of AI markers (marker scan 0). v2026.4.1-252-g7eb094a00d8 confirms fix is 252 commits after v2026.4.1, in 2026.4.2.
round6_research.flaw_origin: human-authored security refactor (Josh Avant, PR #51207) that hardened the execution path with a broader Windows-compatible env-key normalization while the earlier human-authored approval-binding path (Peter Steinberger, 4894d907f) kept strict portable normalization; the two paths drifted (no AI markers on any relevant commit)
round6_research.reasoning: The vulnerability is a normalization drift between the system.run approval-binding path (strict portable env-key normalization, dropping keys with parentheses) and the execution path (Windows-compatible normalization that accepts them). The first commit that created that divergence is 7abfff756d6c68d17e21d1657bbacbaec86de232, which introduced normalizeHostOverrideEnvVarKey + WINDOWS_COMPAT_OVERRIDE_ENV_VAR_KEY only on the execution side (parent provably lacks both). Its author is human (Josh Avant) with no AI markers; every commit in the relevant chain (2cdbadee1f8, f202e73077a, e80c803fa88, 4894d907f, 10481097f8e, 84a50acb553, 7abfff756d6, and the fix 7eb094a00d8) scans clean. The fix is authored by a human as well. No evidence of AI involvement in introducing or fixing the flaw, hence NOT_AI.

round6_research.bug_semantics: CWE-78 OS command injection in @rtk-ai/rtk-rewrite 1.0.0 OpenClaw plugin (openclaw/index.ts): before_tool_call hook takes exec tool's `command` param and passes it to execSync(`rtk rewrite ${JSON.stringify(command)}`); JSON.stringify double-quotes the value but leaves $() and backticks unescaped, and /bin/sh expands them inside double quotes, so a crafted command executes arbitrary OS commands with plugin/gateway privileges (GHSA-fqgj-m2gp-mr3q; reported by EQSTLab, published 2026-06-23; CVSS 8.8/6.3).
round6_research.evidence: Advisory id resolution: case class alias-ee17d78131801e7d4322df40 = sha256('CVE-2026-55249\n') (single-id hash matched only CVE-2026-55249; the GHSA-fqgj-m2gp-mr3q+CVE pair hashes to alias-c15a4ae25, so the class kept the CVE alone). Introducer 56160d83 (squash-merge of PR #358, author Alex <a.neyman17@gmail.com>, committer GitHub, 2026-03-18) is the first commit of openclaw/index.ts; git show 56160d83:openclaw/index.ts contains `import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'`, line 19 execSync('which rtk'), line 29 `execSync(`rtk rewrite ${JSON.stringify(command)}`)` in tryRewrite(), and the before_tool_call hook reading event.params?.command (lines 52-56) — the full source->sink chain. Git log --follow confirms no earlier commit touched the file. Parent 4d799b0 exists (git cat-file -e rc=0). Trailers on introducer: Signed-off-by + Co-authored-by Patrick szymkowiak (human); no AI markers (author/committer/trailers scanned). Fix commits 1bb17f4 and f525ceec (identical fix, author aesoft/Adrien Eppling, 2026-06-03, both on develop, no trailers): replace execSync with execFileSync('rtk',['rewrite',command]) — no shell, closes the injection. Fix side carries no AI markers either, and AI fix would not flip verdict.
round6_research.flaw_origin: Introduced with the plugin itself: commit 56160d83 created openclaw/index.ts containing the execSync template-string sink (line 29) and execSync('which rtk')(line 19). The in-PR refactor replaced 60+ regex rewrite rules with a single `rtk rewrite` execSync call, so the vulnerable sink is present in the very first commit of the file; no prior commit wrote the sink.
round6_research.reasoning: The vulnerable behavior (shell-backed execSync of an attacker-influenced command string) was written by human author Alex in PR #358; all authorship signals on the introducing commit are human. The plugin is an AI-agent integration, but that is product context, not authorship evidence. Closed causal chain: introduced 56160d83, fixed 1bb17f4. NOT_AI.

round6_research.bug_semantics: First-use privilege escalation during device pairing (CWE-269/287): OpenClaw bootstrap setup codes were NOT bound to the intended device role and scopes. issueDeviceBootstrapToken() issued a token without any role/scope profile, and verifyDeviceBootstrapToken() never compared the redeeming role against an allowed set - it simply merged the requesting role/scopes into the record (entry.roles = mergeRoles(entry.roles, role)) and returned ok:true as long as token/deviceId/publicKey were present. A bootstrap setup code (designed for onboarding a node) could therefore be redeemed with any role (e.g. a privileged hub role), enabling privilege escalation during first-use pairing. Fix shipped in v2026.3.22+ (npm patched >=2026.3.22); reported by @tdjackey.
round6_research.evidence: Identity: member_map pin CVE-2026-41386 + GHSA-gg9v-mgcp-v6m7 (GHSA: "OpenClaw: Unbound bootstrap setup codes allow privilege escalation during pairing", high severity, npm openclaw <=2026.3.13-1 vulnerable, >=2026.3.22 patched, first stable tag v2026.3.22, fix commit listed DIRECTLY as a600c72ed7d0045a27f58bf031d2b36ecb0141c9 (2026-03-22T23:57:15-07:00), thanks @tdjackey). Fix: a600c72e (2026-03-22, Peter Steinberger, "fix: bind bootstrap setup codes to node profile", single parent 4580d585ffa43d8b3fc2b71ead902f07db38f513): issueDeviceBootstrapToken() now takes roles/scopes params (normalized; default roles=["node"], scopes=[]); records store roles/scopes; verifyDeviceBootstrapToken() fails closed (bootstrap_token_invalid) when record has no roles or requested role/scopes set differs from issued profile (sameStringSet); setup-code.ts issues codes with PAIRING_SETUP_BOOTSTRAP_ROLES=["node"] + empty scopes; tests added (50 lines device-bootstrap.test.ts, 10 setup-code.test.ts, device-pair/index.test.ts +4). BIC: bf89947a (2026-03-12, Peter Steinberger) as above; parent absent of file + token refs -> introducer_parent_absent=1. No AI markers: %N trailers empty on introducer, fix, and intermediate 1803d16d; all authors (Peter Steinberger, Robin Waslander, Mariano, Val Alexander) human identities; no Co-Authored-By naming any AI tool on relevant commits.
round6_research.flaw_origin: Atomic introducer: commit bf89947a8e9ec5d278b71a8c438ce414dd04a2d6 (2026-03-12, Peter Steinberger <steipete@gmail.com>, single parent 9cd54ea8824462b876733471132f2bd7b8c1b0b0, no trailers, "fix: switch pairing setup codes to bootstrap tokens") created src/infra/device-bootstrap.ts with issueDeviceBootstrapToken() (no roles/scopes in issued record; the DeviceBootstrapTokenRecord type already allowed optional roles/scopes but issue never set them and setup-code.ts called it with ONLY baseDir) and verifyDeviceBootstrapToken() which accepted whatever role/scopes the redeeming device requested, merging them into the record - i.e. first writer of the unbound setup-code flow the advisory pins. Parent 9cd54ea verified: src/infra/device-bootstrap.ts absent (git ls-tree 0 hits) and no issueDeviceBootstrapToken/bootstrapToken references anywhere in src (git grep 0 hits) -> introducer_parent_absent=1. Predecessor caveat: the setup-code pairing flow itself predates - src/pairing/setup-code.ts born 599c890221f0226d1369a38e031b8e55abde5d31 (2026-02-16, Mariano, human) - but the token-based unbound bootstrap mechanism (advisory-pinned) is atomic to bf89947a. Intermediate 1803d16d5cec (2026-03-13, Robin Waslander "fix(auth): make device bootstrap tokens single-use to prevent scope escalation") hardened single-use but did NOT bind role/scopes; the role-binding gap persisted until the advisory fix.
round6_research.reasoning: The advisory-pinned vulnerability (bootstrap setup codes unbound to role/scopes, redeemable for arbitrary role = first-use privilege escalation) is atomic to the human-authored 2026-03-12 commit bf89947a (Peter Steinberger) which introduced the token-based bootstrap flow with issue lacking role binding and verify accepting any requested role; parent verified to have no such code. The fix (a600c72e, also Peter Steinberger, human) binds codes to node profile fail-closed. No AI markers on any relevant commit -> NOT_AI.

blocked106.flaw_semantics: Blind SSRF (CWE-918) in Knowage-Server < 8.1.37: user-supplied URLs are fetched server-side without any host/address validation. Two REST sinks: (1) GET /restful-services/ckan-management/download?url=... -> CkanHelper.DownloadCkanDataset -> downloadAndSaveFile -> ProxyClientUtilities.getTarget(fileURL).request().get(InputStream.class) (response written to server file, replayToClient); (2) GET /restful-services/1.0/geo/getWMSlayer?layerURL=... -> GeoResource.getWMSlayer builds finalWMSUrl = layerURL + '?' + query and fetches it via new URL(finalWMSUrl).openConnection() under a trust-all SSLContext. Attacker cannot reliably read responses but can drive requests to arbitrary internal hosts/paths (internal-network scan oracle). Advisory GHSA-m6x8-wh9v-6jxp; sibling CVE-2025-55007 identical text; patched in 8.1.37.

round6_research.bug_semantics: OpenStack Keystone privilege escalation via unrestricted application credentials chained with trusts (OSSA-2026-015, CVE-2026-43000, Closes-Bug #2148477). An attacker holding a member role can create an application credential with unrestricted=True and then create/use a trust that delegates victim roles: keystone/trust/controllers.py (_check_unrestricted) only blocked trust create/delete when the token's auth methods contained 'application_credential' AND application_credential['unrestricted'] was False (or when the context was admin it returned early), so an UNRESTRICTED application credential could manage trusts, including delegating the victim's admin role to the attacker's identity (trustor validation passes because the impersonated token carries the victim identity). Fix (14a1447) replaces the restricted-only check with _check_application_credential() which blocks ALL application credentials (restricted and unrestricted) on ALL trust operations (create/delete/list/get/list-roles/get-role) unless the new opt CONF.security_compliance.allow_insecure_application_credential_trust_escalation is set. Affected: >=14.0.0 <27.0.2, >=28.0.0 <28.0.2, >=29.0.0 <29.0.2.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (CWE-79) escalating to Remote Code Execution (CWE-94) in the Dive MCP-host desktop app: the Mermaid diagram renderer src/views/Chat/preview/mermaid.tsx calls mermaid.initialize({ securityLevel: 'loose', ... }), overriding the library's safe default. With securityLevel loose, Mermaid renders HTML labels and javascript: URLs in diagram nodes, so a diagram originating from an untrusted source (a malicious MCP server configuration injected through the LLM/MCP tool pipeline) can execute arbitrary JavaScript when the node is rendered or clicked. round6_research.bug_semantics: Path traversal in Active Storage DiskService (CWE-22, CVSS 8.0): ActiveStorage::Service::DiskService#path_for (activestorage/lib/active_storage/service/disk_service.rb) joins the blob key directly onto the storage root ('File.join root, folder_for(key), key') with no validation that the resolved path stays inside root; a blob key containing '../' segments (used by apps passing user input as keys) lets an attacker read, write, or delete arbitrary files on the server via the disk service (upload/download/delete and the DiskController HTTP endpoints). Fixed in 7.2.3.1 / 8.0.4.1 / 8.1.2.1.
round6_research.evidence: ruby-advisory-db gems/activestorage/CVE-2026-33195.yml (published 2026-03-23) lists three fix commits: 4933c1e3b8c1bb04925d60347be9f69270392f2c / 9b06fbc0f504b8afe333f33d19548f3b85fbe655 / a290c8a1ec189d793aa6d7f2570b6a763f675348, all 'Prevent path traversal in ActiveStorage DiskService' (2026-03-13) by Mike Dalessio (main + 7.2/8.0 backports; no trailers). Fix rewrites path_for: raises ActiveStorage::InvalidKeyError on blank keys, on dot segments ('.','..'), on Encoding errors, on null bytes (ArgumentError), and enforces 'path.start_with?(File.expand_path(root) + "/")'; DiskController rescues InvalidKeyError as not_found/422. Introducer metadata: author AND committer David Heinemeier Hansson (direct commit, not squash), 2017-07-01 pre-LLM era, no AI markers, commit message 'No need to normalize since we generate our own keys'. History chain verified via -S 'normalize(key)' and -S 'File.join root, folder_for(key), key' (only the 2026 fix touches the final string). Advisory patched ranges match 4933c1e3 origin (main) with branch backports.
round6_research.flaw_origin: The unvalidated key join 'File.join(root, folder_for(key), key)' in path_for was first written by ce44746ea3a98fab1af65c75ec32eeadd67b1b5f 'No need to normalize since we generate our own keys' (2017-07-01, David Heinemeier Hansson) as an immediate follow-up to the Active Storage (then 'Active File') initial implementation: the file-creation commit d30231e983c019fbe3fcd6a2a06a461fefa58dab (2017-07-01 00:04) created lib/active_file/sites/disk_site.rb with path_for calling 'normalize(key)' (a helper that did not exist at that commit — only normalize_key existed), and ce44746e (00:13, same day) removed the normalize call, leaving the raw key joined into the filesystem path with no containment check. Parent 3959d32aa09206518f4c1ea2cd96fa62be383dcd still has 'File.join(root, folder_for(key), normalize(key))' (verified). The 'folder_for' key prefixing ('[key[0..1], key[2..3]].join("/")') never limited traversal since '../<segment>' keys still escape. File renamed over time: lib/active_file/sites/disk_site.rb → activestorage/lib/active_storage/service/disk_service.rb (2017-08 renames), same code.
round6_research.reasoning: The vulnerable raw-key path join was written on 2017-07-01 by Rails creator David Heinemeier Hansson while bootstrapping Active Storage — nine years before AI coding assistants existed; the only key-filtering helper (normalize_key) was added and dropped within the same hour by the same human author. The 2026 fix is by human Rails security maintainer Mike Dalessio with no AI markers. No AI involvement possible on either side; verdict NOT_AI.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Permission bypass (contradictory global flags): 'deno run --allow-read --deny-read main.ts' results in read allowed even though deny should be stronger; same for all global --allow-* / --deny-* pairs. Cause: the fast-exit permission check skip_check_if_is_permission_fully_granted! macro calls UnaryPermission::is_allow_all(), which returned true whenever granted_global is set and the flag/prompt denied LISTS are empty, but ignored the deny-GLOBAL fields (flag_denied_global / prompt_denied_global). With --allow-read --deny-read both set at global scope, granted_global=true and flag_denied_global=true but the lists stayed empty, so is_allow_all() short-circuited the check to Ok(()) and never consulted the deny state. 'Nonsensical combination of flags' per advisory, likely low real-world impact.

Starting in version 1.41.3... fixed 2.1.13/2.2.13/2.3.2'). GIT range: introduced 0d7662e1 (release 1.41.3, 2024-03-14, denobot version-bump — the first released vulnerable version, not the code introducer), fixed 5b85bdaf (2.1.13 release), introduced 2968816863 (2.2.0 release bump, 2025-02-19), fixed 0117f27a (2.2.13), introduced 61574bb9 (2.3.0 release bump, 2025-04-30), fixed 7b74f385 (2.3.2); refs PR #22894 and PR #29213. Introducer version of is_allow_all: 'self.granted_global && self.flag_denied_list.is_empty() && self.prompt_denied_list.is_empty()' — missing flag_denied_global/prompt_denied_global. blocked106.flaw_semantics: Broken access control (CWE-287) in the HestiaCP Panel Cronjobs editor (web/edit/server/hestiaweb/index.php, reads/writes /var/spool/cron/crontabs/hestiaweb): the admin guard `if ($_SESSION["userContext"] !== "admin" && $user_plain === "$ROOT_USER")` references $ROOT_USER, which is undefined in the web context (web/inc/main.php defines only $user_plain and $_SESSION["ROOT_USER"]), so it interpolates to an empty string, `$user_plain === ""` is always false, and the redirect never fires for non-admin users. round6_research.bug_semantics: Path traversal / arbitrary file write in the @mobilenext/mobile-mcp MCP server (< 0.0.49, patched 0.0.49). An attacker (via prompt injection from a malicious website/document) can make the AI write/overwrite files outside the workspace, e.g. ~/.bashrc, ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, .config files. round6_research.bug_semantics: Insufficient verification of data authenticity (CWE-345/642): Bonjour/DNS-SD TXT records are unauthenticated attacker-influenced metadata, yet OpenClaw CLI routing consumed TXT-provided host/port hints (tailnetDns, lanHost, gatewayPort) as fallbacks when actual service resolution (SRV/A/AAAA via dns-sd -L) failed to yield a resolved host/port. records.details:
Claude Code's sandbox did not prevent sandboxed processes from creating symlinks pointing to locations outside the workspace. When Claude Code subsequently wrote to a path within such a symlink, its unsandboxed process followed the symlink and wrote to the target location outside the workspace without prompting the user for confirmation. This allowed a sandbox escape where neither the sandboxed command nor the unsandboxed app could independently write outside the workspace, but their combination could write to arbitrary locations, potentially leading to code execution outside the sandbox. Reliably exploiting this required the ability to add untrusted content into a Claude Code context window to trigger sandboxed code execution via prompt injection.

Users on standard Claude Code auto-update have received this fix automatically. Users performing manual updates are advised to update to the latest version.

Claude Code thanks hackerone.com/philts for reporting this issue.
records.summary: Claude Code: Sandbox Escape via Symlink Following Allows Arbitrary File Write Outside Workspace

round6_research.bug_semantics: Forwarding-header spoofing bypass of gateway.trustedProxies client-origin detection (CWE-290, CVSS 3.1 6.5): when gateway.trustedProxies is configured, the gateway derives the client origin from X-Forwarded-For without validating per-hop values or skipping loopback hops, so an attacker can inject a spoofed loopback hop (e.g. 127.0.0.1) that is accepted as the client origin, weakening downstream canvas-auth and auth-rate-limit decisions that treat loopback as local/trusted.
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-844j-xrrq-wgh4 / CVE-2026-35656 (published 2026-03-26, reporter @lintsinghua, severity medium, CVSS 3.1 6.5 / 4.0 6.3) names fix commit fc2d29ea926f47c428c556e92ec981441228d2a4; advisory code-level confirmation: src/gateway/net.ts now ignores loopback forwarded hops before trusted-proxy client resolution. Fix diff adds 'if (isLoopbackAddress(hop)) continue;' in the resolvedForwardedClientIp right-to-left loop (3 insertions in net.ts). git log --reverse -S 'isTrustedProxyAddress' and -S 'trustedProxies' first hit e6e71457e0c; parent 2684a364c grep of resolveGatewayClientIp|isTrustedProxyAddress = 0 matches; rev-list --parents shows e6e71457e0c is single-parent (not a squash). Config wiring (types.gateway.ts, zod-schema.ts, docs) added in the same commit.
round6_research.flaw_origin: Commit e6e71457e0c (fix: honor trusted proxy client IPs, PR #1654, 2026-01-25) is the first writer of trusted-proxy-aware client origin resolution: it added isTrustedProxyAddress/resolveGatewayClientIp to src/gateway/net.ts and wired gateway.trustedProxies into auth.ts, server-http.ts, ws-connection/message-handler.ts, openai-http.ts, openresponses-http.ts, tools-invoke-http.ts. Its parseForwardedForClientIp returns the leftmost XFF entry (split(',')[0]) with no per-hop validation or loopback skip, so a spoofed loopback entry is returned as the client origin. Parent 2684a364c has zero occurrences of resolveGatewayClientIp/isTrustedProxyAddress (git grep -c rc=1) and its pre-existing forwarded-header handling (auth.ts isLocalDirectRequest/hasTailscaleProxyHeaders) only DETECTS proxies fail-closed, never derives client origin from XFF. 8877bfd11ec (2026-02-21) rewrote the walk to right-to-left returning the first non-trusted hop, still without loopback skip - that is the exact code shape the advisory fix patches (via be7f825006d rename to resolveForwardedClientIp), but the vulnerable behavior itself originates in e6e71457e0c.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Header-injection / parsing ambiguity (CWE-20): the HTTP header parser accepted null bytes and control characters (0x00-0x08, 0x0B-0x1F, 0x7F) in header values instead of rejecting them per RFC 9110 s5.5-5. Both parser backends were permissive: the pure-Python HeadersParser performed NO value-side character validation (only header-NAME charset via HDRRE and length limits), and the C parser (llhttp in lenient mode, default since aiohttp 2.0) accumulated values verbatim via on_header_value callbacks with no CTL check. Consequences: a server can send response header values that aiohttp's client interprets differently from what a reverse proxy / other parser understood (e.g. request.url.origin() disagreeing with the raw Host header), enabling header/request smuggling-style security bypasses. records.details:
When using Claude Code with Yarn installed, Yarn config files can trigger code execution when running yarn --version. This could lead to a bypass of the directory trust dialog in Claude Code, as plugins and yarnPath could be executed prior to the user accepting the risks of working in an untrusted directory. Users on standard Claude Code auto-update will have received this fix automatically. Users performing manual updates are advised to update to the latest version.

Thank you to Benjamin Faller, Redguard AG and Michael Hess for reporting this issue!

round6_research.bug_semantics: ReDoS (CWE-1333) in Sinatra's ETag conditional-request parsing: the etag/etag_matches? helpers split the attacker-controlled If-Match / If-None-Match headers with the regex split( /\s*,\s*/ ); on Ruby < 3.2 String#split with that pattern is super-linear for crafted input (e.g. long whitespace/comma runs), causing CPU-bound DoS on any app using the etag method. Fixed in Sinatra 4.2.0 by commit 3fe8c38dc405586f7ad8f2ac748aa53e9c3615bd (2025-10-08, PR #2121): list.to_s.split(/\s*,\s*/) -> list.to_s.split(',').map(&:strip). Ruby >= 3.2 fixed the underlying split behavior (bugs.ruby-lang.org/19104), which is why the advisory only affects older Rubies.

round6_research.bug_semantics: SQL injection introduced by the 1.2.6 rewrite of the JDBC adapter's execute/to_sql wiring in lib/arjdbc/jdbc/adapter.rb: execute() was re-routed through a gsub('?') bind-substituting to_sql with an inverted ActiveRecord version check (MAJOR < 3 instead of >= 3), causing double '?' bind substitution so user-supplied values were not safely parameterized/quoted before reaching the database (issue #322; 1.2.6 yanked).
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-5qw5-wf2q-f538 / OSVDB-114854 (RubyGems activerecord-jdbc-adapter, vulnerable >= 1.2.6, fixed 1.2.8, advisory dated 2013-02-25 by rubysec, no CVE). Introducer: 0ca61530 ('re-invent execute to log (sql) name correctly based on AR version avoid substitute_binds completely and backport to_sql for everybody', 2013-01-30, kares, single parent d2b78c08) rewrites adapter.rb: removes the secure `execute(sql,name,binds)` that did `sql = substitute_binds(sql, binds)` (single then-current substitution), and installs version-conditional execute() methods routing through `to_sql(sql, binds)` (forall AR majors) plus a backported bind-substituting to_sql guarded by `if ActiveRecord::VERSION::MAJOR < 3` (inverted: the AR>=3 branches got the non-substituting path while the substituting to_sql was wired only where not needed). Result: double '?' bind substitution / unparameterized user input reaching JDBC (issue jruby/activerecord-jdbc-adapter#322, reported by @ebeigarts; 1.2.6 yanked, README note commit e24bfdb4). Parent d2b78c08 still contains the old safe execute() with substitute_binds. Fix series: 31e6aa75 (= 3d6fe4a8 on 1-2-stable, 2013-02-08) flips the version check to `MAJOR >= 3`; 9bdf8b09 (2013-03-12) removes the second bind-consumption path (`copy = binds.dup` -> direct shift) closing the remaining raw-CRUD double bind ('re-closing #322'); both land by tag v1.2.8 (aa59dd86).

round6_research.bug_semantics: Format injection / arbitrary file write (CWE-73) in the Edit Image node (n8n-nodes-base EditImage): the node's Format option was passed unvalidated to gmInstance.setFormat(options.format) (GraphicsMagick CLI wrapper) and interpolated into the output binary's fileExtension, mimeType ('image/'+format) and fileName (split('.').join + '.' + format). A crafted format value (reachable via an expression in the options.format parameter by any authenticated user able to run workflows) causes the image library to write bytes to a path outside the node's working directory. The 'type: options' dropdown (bmp/gif/jpeg/png/tiff) is not a security boundary because n8n parameters accept expression values at runtime. CVSS 4.0 7.7 (AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H); fixed in n8n 1.123.67 / 2.31.5 / 2.32.1 (2026-07-22).
round6_research.evidence: GHSA-xmc9-4f2h-jf9c (no CVE alias; published 2026-07-22, reporter simonkoeck; npm n8n <1.123.67, 2.0.0-rc.0..<2.31.5, 2.32.0..<2.32.1; GHSA references commit f69dfc6dd2178a14ea1624d2e1d403c2e755042f). n8n release process squashes weekly merges into bundles (n8n-assistant[bot], cherry-picked from private n8n-private) - the security fix entered all lines 2026-07-22 via 1.x bundle 1cd2c5fb22a906058cc083c3af2d561ce7f4332d (#34679), main 2.x 2222fe3a6c886a9059f28e1b6d4bdb10ee420624 (#34680), 2.31.x f6cb6cf3ab177c3740a5ef624b89bae5165405a1 (#34688), 2.32.x f69dfc6dd2178a14ea1624d2e1d403c2e755042f (#34692) (same batch as the GHSA-cj9h-qx8g-pq2g fix). Fix diff in f69dfc6dd2: EditImage.node.ts adds const VALID_IMAGE_FORMATS = new Set(['bmp','gif','jpeg','png','tiff','tif','webp']) and validateImageFormat(format, node) which throws NodeOperationError 'Invalid image format: ...' for non-whitelisted or non-string values; the vulnerable line 'gmInstance = gmInstance!.setFormat(options.format as string)' becomes 'gmInstance = gmInstance!.setFormat(format)' after validation; new tests 'should reject an unsupported string format' ('pdf'/123) assert setFormat is not called. Vulnerable behavior origin: d201cc3dd7fe8a27952bd7beeb1c1a227ea47aee (2020-05-27, Jan Oberhauser, ':zap: Make it possible to change output image format, quality and name') added the format option and the unvalidated pass-through (gmInstance.setFormat(options.format), fileExtension/mimeType/fileName interpolation); parent 0091f5311431ebecd0ee40ded6215ddbb57dce14 has no setFormat / format handling in EditImage.node.ts (verified). Later commits (766f74c782 directorize 2021-11-17, a7bb1463fb) only moved the file. Marker scans on introducer and intermediate commits: 0 AI markers; fix bundles carry batch-level Co-authored-by trailers including 'Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>' plus humans (Charlie Kolb, Guillaume Jacquart, Stephen Wright, ...) covering dozens of PRs per bundle, not attributable to the EditImage fix author.
round6_research.flaw_origin: Design gap introduced with the Format option itself, 2020-05-27: when 'Make it possible to change output image format, quality and name' added the format/quality/fileName options, no whitelist or validation was applied to the format string before it reached gm.setFormat and the derived output file attributes. The unsanitized string sink persisted through later refactors (directorize 2021-11-17, binaryPropertyName changes) unchanged.
round6_research.reasoning: The vulnerable behavior - an unvalidated format string passed to GraphicsMagick's setFormat and used to derive output file attributes - was first written on 2020-05-27 by Jan Oberhauser (human maintainer), well before the coding-agent era, with zero AI markers on the exact vulnerable lines. The flaw is the original design of the Format option (no whitelist), not something introduced by AI code or an AI refactor. round6_research.bug_semantics: Missing authentication (CWE-306, CVSS 8.1 High) in HTTP transport mode: ApiKeyMiddleware fails open - requests carrying no client API key are unconditionally forwarded to the next handler (server.py:1427), so the downstream HTTP client falls back to the server operator's NETLICENSING_API_KEY env var (client.py:30 api_key_ctx default) and uses it to authenticate every upstream call to the NetLicensing REST API. An unauthenticated network attacker can invoke any MCP tool (incl. destructive deletes) as the operator. Fixed in 0.1.6: /mcp requires x-netlicensing-api-key header or Authorization: Bearer, else 401; /health stays unauthenticated.
round6_research.evidence: OSV GHSA-x9vc-9ffq-p3gj (alias CVE-2026-54446, PYSEC-2026-3490): fixed 0.1.6, ref commit fbbb1d5ff88eb5400ec933a84e75601ebee48927, ref tag 0.1.6; fix verified ancestor of tag 0.1.6. Fix diff: server.py ApiKeyMiddleware rejects missing/empty keys with 401 except /health; test_auth_middleware.py added. Parent absence: git grep -c ApiKeyMiddleware / call_next(request) at 81f799ac^ both exit=1. BIC is root commit (no parent exists); vulnerable behavior (unauthenticated HTTP mode + env-key client fallback) present in initial tree (client.py line 21 os.getenv NETLICENSING_API_KEY, server.py mcp.run streamable-http).
round6_research.flaw_origin: Root commit 5a2d3f07dc4979e7ea512ad49e25ef1f1532024a (2026-03-16, R.Brown <ready.brown@hotmail.de>, 'NetLicensing MCP server - initial commit') created HTTP streamable transport (mcp.run(transport='streamable-http')) with no authentication whatsoever, while client.py anchors api_key_ctx default to os.getenv('NETLICENSING_API_KEY') - so any unauthenticated HTTP request is served using the operator's upstream API key. round6_research.bug_semantics: CWE-200/CWE-201 environment-variable exfiltration. Git.polish_url() (git/cmd.py, v3.1.50 lines 907-925) unconditionally runs os.path.expandvars(url) on its input on the non-Cygwin branch, and Repo._clone() (reached via public Repo.clone_from()/Repo.clone(), git/repo/base.py:1407-1418) passes the polished post-expansion URL to the git clone subprocess after running the unsafe-protocol check on the raw URL. An attacker who controls the clone URL (standard 'import repo from URL' pattern in CI/git hosts/dependency scanners) can embed $NAME/${NAME} tokens that are expanded server-side from the process environment and then transmitted to the attacker-named host via DNS/HTTP request, exfiltrating secrets such as AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or GITHUB_TOKEN. Secondary aggravator: check_unsafe_protocols() runs pre-expansion, so an env var whose value begins with ext:: could bypass the unsafe-protocol filter (requires env-write precondition).

round6_research.bug_semantics: Insecure deserialization / arbitrary class reconstruction leading to RCE in LangGraph Checkpoint's JsonPlusSerializer (libs/checkpoint/langgraph/checkpoint/serde/jsonplus.py, versions <=2.1.2). loads() = json.loads(data, object_hook=self._reviver); _reviver treats any dict with lc:2/type:constructor/id as instructions to importlib.import_module the module named by id, getattr the class/method, and call it with attacker-controlled args/kwargs (cls(*args, **kwargs) / method(*args, **kwargs)). Malicious payloads (e.g., constructors such as subprocess.Popen or os-level classes with attacker-controlled args) yield code execution when deserialized. By default the serializer prefers msgpack, but dumps_typed fell back to the 'json' type whenever msgpack serialization failed (e.g., illegal Unicode surrogates), so json-mode payloads reach the vulnerable loads() path. Fixed in checkpointer 3.0.0 (commit c5744f583, PR #6269: removed untyped loads/dumps and restricted deserialization to an allow list).

records.details:
Claude Code failed to properly validate directory changes when combined with write operations to protected folders. By using the `cd` command to navigate into sensitive directories like `.claude`, it was possible to bypass write protection and create or modify files without user confirmation. Reliably exploiting this required the ability to add untrusted content into a Claude Code context window.

Users on standard Claude Code auto-update received this fix automatically. Users performing manual updates are advised to update to the latest version.

About
Claude Code thanks hackerone.com/nil221 for reporting this issue!

round6_research.bug_semantics:
1-click Remote Code Execution (CWE-94, GitHub advisory severity HIGH, CVSS 3.1 10.0 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N) in the Eigent desktop agent. The renderer executes untrusted document previews with full Electron privileges: the main BrowserWindow is created with webSecurity:false + nodeIntegration:true + webviewTag:true (electron/main/index.ts ~717/796/798); the preload exposes generic ipcRenderer.invoke plus executeCommand (ipcMain.handle('execute-command') at electron/main/index.ts:319 spawns an arbitrary command string in the main process); protocol.handle('localfile') (index.ts:948) serves arbitrary local files as text/html; and FileReader.openFile (electron/main/fileReader.ts) parses downloaded csv/xlsx/docx/pptx into unescaped HTML (e.g. html += `${cellValue}`, `
  • ${text}
    • `), rendered in src/components/Folder/index.tsx via dangerouslySetInnerHTML (line ~287) or iframe src=localfile://+encodeURIComponent(content). Clicking a file chip in chat renders attacker-controlled file content as HTML/JS in the privileged renderer, enabling executeCommand RCE. Advisory's vulnerable range 0.0.60, patched 0.0.61; the publisher (Wendong-Fan, published 2025-12-26) lists no credits/reporter. Advisory is imprecise: v0.0.60..v0.0.61 contains no security fix; the real fix landed in v0.0.72.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Improper validation of uploaded-file validity in MISP's module/import file-upload path (app/Controller/EventsController.php): the guard condition `(isset($fileupload['error']) && $fileupload['error'] == 0) || (!empty($fileupload['tmp_name']) && $fileupload['tmp_name'] != 'none') && is_uploaded_file(...)` suffers an operator-precedence flaw (&& binds tighter than ||) so `error == 0` alone satisfies the check and is_uploaded_file() is never consulted; an attacker-supplied tmp_name (any readable local path) is then passed to FileAccessTool::readAndDelete(), enabling file read/deletion outside genuine uploads.
round6_research.evidence: Identity: cases-pC.jsonl lists repo misp/misp with advisory_ids CVE-2025-66384 + GHSA-863h-c4v7-h5fv. OSV CVE-2025-66384: 'app/Controller/EventsController.php in MISP before 2.5.24 has invalid logic in checking for uploaded file validity, related to tmp_name'; GIT range introduced 0, fixed 6867f0d3157a1959154bdad9ddac009dec6a19f5 (and merge 1b4f6b3bf93b8933f04d3fd78ed565c1bbfb9d9d). Fix commit: 'fix: [security] fix invalid check for uploaded file validity - Thanks to Raphael Lob from NATO Cyber Security Center' (iglocska, 2025-10-28), +10/-1 in EventsController.php rewriting the condition to require (!isset(error)||error==0) && (!empty(tmp_name)&&tmp_name!='none') && is_uploaded_file(tmp_name). Pickaxe -S on the exact vulnerable snippet across app/Controller/EventsController.php yields exactly two writers: 1f1c8c814 (2016, introduced) and f720706a4 (2022 refactor, logic preserved). Introducer metadata: author/committer Iglocska <andras.iklody@gmail.com>, 2016-08-01, subject 'new: First revision of the new import system'; AI-marker grep on %B = 0 hits; f720706a4 %B also 0 hits. Parent 2d3b3aa7728be55a16c1e90da2bbaf2dedcd388b's EventsController.php contains 0 '$fileupload' occurrences => block absent => introducer_parent_absent True. Release checks: git merge-base --is-ancestor 6867f0d3 v2.5.24 => YES; v2.5.23 still contains the vulnerable is_uploaded_file check => confirmed affected-before-fixed.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Denial of service / uncontrolled memory consumption (CWE-400) in Spring AI pdf-document-reader: a maliciously crafted PDF processed by ForkPDFLayoutTextStripper triggers unreasonable memory allocation, OOM-ing the host. Two attacker-controlled allocation vectors: (1) per-character writing builds each line via completeLineWithSpaces() which concatenates SPACE_CHARACTER one char at a time ('line += ' loop, O(n^2) char copies) for a length derived from the PDF page width (lineLength = pageWidth/OUTPUT_SPACE_CHARACTER_WIDTH_IN_PT -> unbounded); (2) text-position parsing computes numberOfLines = floor(textYPosition - previousTextYPosition)/height from attacker-controlled coordinates (tiny heights / huge gaps -> huge counts) and createNewEmptyNewLines() materializes that many TextLine objects, each triggering the per-line allocation. Affected spring-ai-pdf-document-reader 1.0.0-1.0.5 (fixed 1.0.6) and 1.1.0-1.1.4 (fixed 1.1.5).
round6_research.evidence: Identity: member_map pin CVE-2026-40980 + GHSA-26gg-9gv2-v27j (OSV valid: 'Spring AI Vulnerable to OOM by attacker-controlled PDF ... handled by ForkPDFLayoutTextStripper'; spring-ai-pdf-document-reader 1.0.0-1.0.5 fixed 1.0.6, 1.1.0-1.1.4 fixed 1.1.5). SUBJECT=Reject HTTPS proxies when libcurl lacks HTTPS-proxy support (#3626)
BODY=The cURL handlers fail closed on an effective https:// proxy (from the proxy
option or the environment) unless the installed libcurl is 7.52.0 or newer
built with HTTPS-proxy support, throwing a RequestException before any bytes
reach the wire. Without the guard, libcurl before 7.50.2 silently downgrades
such a proxy to a plaintext HTTP proxy, and 7.50.2 through 7.51 (and builds
without the feature) fail only later at connect time.

The proxy scheme is matched against the literal "://" prefix rather than with
parse_url(), whose scheme detection is not anchored to the start of the string.

Reject HTTPS proxies when libcurl lacks HTTPS-proxy support (#3626)
The cURL handlers fail closed on an effective https:// proxy (from the proxy
option or the environment) unless the installed libcurl is 7.52.0 or newer
built with HTTPS-proxy support, throwing a RequestException before any bytes
reach the wire. Without the guard, libcurl before 7.50.2 silently downgrades
such a proxy to a plaintext HTTP proxy, and 7.50.2 through 7.51 (and builds
without the feature) fail only later at connect time.

round6_research.bug_semantics: Expression sandbox escape (RCE): the tournament VM (output-compatible riot-tmpl rewrite used as n8n's expression sandbox) lists ArrowFunctionExpression under the 'Do nothing' branch of jsVariablePolyfill, so a free identifier in a concise arrow body (e.g. () => process) is never routed through polyfillVar into the data context and reaches native evaluation, allowing crafted workflow expressions with arrow functions to escape the sandbox and execute system commands on the host. Fixed (2.31.5/2.32.1) by routing concise arrow-function bodies through polyfillVar via a new ArrowFunctionExpression custom patcher.
round6_research.evidence: advisory GHSA-gv7g-jm28-cr3m (published 2026-07-22): 'n8n: Expression sandbox escape via arrow-function bodies enabling command execution', fixed in 2.31.5/2.32.1, references commit f69dfc6dd2. Fix tokens verified in packages/@n8n/tournament/src/VariablePolyfill.ts via `git log --all -S 'concise arrow body'` (hits only 2222fe3a6c master bundle, f6cb6cf3ab 2.31.x backport, f69dfc6dd2 2.32.x backport): new ArrowFunctionExpression custom patcher (if parent.body === path.node -> polyfillVar) plus case 'ArrowFunctionExpression' moved from the 'Do nothing' switch list into the customPatches dispatch. Introducer verified via `git log --follow -- packages/@n8n/tournament/src/VariablePolyfill.ts` -> earliest commit 98e24baf64; `git show --stat 98e24baf64 -- packages/@n8n/tournament/` shows all 25 package files added (7215 insertions); `git ls-tree -r 98e24baf64^ --name-only | grep -c tournament` = 0; file content at 98e24baf64 has ArrowFunctionExpression under the '// Do nothing' comment (line 177) and no custom patcher for it. `git log 69c86333b..2222fe3a6c` = only 2222fe3a6c (master is bundle-linearized; individual fix PR commit not public). VariablePolyfill.ts absent from pre-98e24baf64 tree; no equivalent sandbox file existed earlier (only unrelated ArrowFunctionExpression uses in eslint plugin rules and workflow-sdk validators).
round6_research.flaw_origin: Born-flawed: the flaw is part of the @n8n/tournament expression-sandbox design as first imported into the monorepo. VariablePolyfill.ts (with ArrowFunctionExpression in the 'Do nothing' switch list and no custom patcher) was added in its entirety at the package-move commit; the immediate parent tree contains no tournament paths and no pre-existing equivalent sandbox code in this repo. Pre-import history of the external @n8n/tournament package (v1.0.7) is not available in this clone.
round6_research.reasoning: Step 1: GHSA-gv7g-jm28-cr3m describes sandbox escape via arrow-function bodies -> command execution; the mechanism is the missing polyfill routing for concise arrow bodies in tournament's VariablePolyfill.ts (CWE-94). Step 2: BIC decomposition - VariablePolyfill.ts and the whole tournament sandbox entered n8n-io/n8n at 98e24baf64 (2026-04-29, package move into monorepo); the vulnerable configuration (ArrowFunctionExpression listed as 'Do nothing', causing free identifiers like process in () => process to bypass the data-context polyfill and resolve natively) is present byte-for-byte in that import, and the parent ca5320a7ed has no tournament code, so the import commit is the minimal atomic introducer; it is a single-parent PR squash whose constituent commits are not in the repo (external @n8n/tournament v1.0.7 pre-history unavailable), so no further decomposition is possible. Step 3: AI assessment - the introducer is authored by a human (Matsu, real n8n engineer) with no AI markers; nothing in the import commit signals AI authorship of the flawed switch-list placement. The fix was shipped privately (CAT-series security process) and lands only via bundle commits; the aggregated Claude/Cursor trailers on the master bundle are spread across 16 unrelated PRs and are not attributable to the fix itself. No positive AI signal on the causal chain -> NOT_AI.
round6_research.remaining_gap: Pre-import history of @n8n/tournament (v1.0.7, external package) could not be examined - no clone/source available; if that history were available, the BIC would likely be an earlier commit in the tournament repo. Also the individual fix PR commit is not public, so fix authorship is inferred from bundle co-authors (Charlie Kolb) rather than a direct commit.

blocked106.flaw_semantics: Improper access control (CWE-284/200) in share views: ShareService.getViewRecords() passes the client-supplied `projection` query parameter straight through to recordService.getRecords() (`projection: query?.projection ?? filteredFields.map(f => f.id)`). The default projection lists only the view's non-hidden fields, but a crafted projection of arbitrary field IDs overrides the mask, so an anonymous share visitor can read hidden column values from GET /api/share/:shareId/view/records by supplying hidden field IDs (enumerable from share metadata).
